  ```
  * thread #3, stop reason = EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x4010000000000000)
    frame #0: march_incrc + 48        (runtime/march_runtime.c — atomic ldadd into a bad pointer)
    frame #1: go$apply$4104 (closure inside Stats.mean's fold)
    frame #2: Stats.mean + 104
    frame #3: DataFrame.eval_agg + 608
    frame #4: go$apply$2583 / $lam19634$apply$2580
    frame #5: DataFrame.apply_group_by + 520
    frame #6: bench_groupby + 292
  ```
  The faulting address (`0x4010000000000000`) has the shape of a tagged/erased immediate being dereferenced as if it were a heap pointer — the same RC-misclassification *class* as the sort-family crashes (`bench/heapsort.march` et al., "heapsort RC underflow" below), but a **distinct call site**: this one is reached through `DataFrame.eval_agg`'s `Mean` aggregation path calling `Stats.mean` (`stdlib/stats.march`) inside a per-group fold, not through `Sort`'s heap/merge internals. Repro: `march --compile bench/dataframe_bench.march -o /tmp/df && /tmp/df` (exit 139); `march bench/dataframe_bench.march` (exit 0, prints all 4 benchmark sections including correct GroupBy output — `cat_0`..`cat_4`, 200 rows each, mean values `47.5`..`51.5`). Needs investigation starting from why a value flowing into `Stats.mean`'s internal fold closure is misclassified as owning a heap pointer specifically under the `DataFrame`→`eval_agg`→per-group-closure call shape — not yet root-caused to a specific `perceus.ml`/`borrow.ml` site. Added to the oracle's `known_divergence` list (`test/test_oracle.ml`) so the conformance sweep stays green while this is open.

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18 session 3, `lib/tir/llvm_case.ml` `branches_match_niche_shape`).** NOT an RC bug at all — a **representation-decode hijack via ctor-name ambiguity** in emit_case's TVar-erased NICHE recovery. `lower_match` mints nested sub-pattern scrutinees with `unknown_ty`, so the inner `case row of Row(fp)` in `from_rows_widen`'s `Cons(Row(first_pairs), rest)` reaches emit_case typed `TVar` and the niche recovery identifies the type by ctor NAME — with `List.exists`: ANY niche-shaped typedef owning the ctor committed the niche decode. Stdlib `Csv`'s `ptype CsvRow = CsvEof | Row(List(String))` is niche-shaped and owns a `Row` ctor, so it hijacked the decode of the BOXED single-ctor `DataFrame.Row = Row(List((String, Value)))`: the niche identity path bound the box POINTER itself as `first_pairs`, whose header tag (0) read as `Nil` → 0 builders → `DataFrame(Nil)` → `row_count 0` — silently, no crash, no ASAN signal (the box is valid memory), interp correct. Explains every observation: `summarize`/`inner_join` collapse identically (same head-Row match); the isolated repros P4/P5/P6 passed because their `Row` was ENTRY-module (registered bare → sub-scrutinee resolves concretely → recovery never fires); the runtime-RC-trace plan was unnecessary — the ASAN-clean + tag-0-reads-as-Nil signature pointed to the Boxed-vs-Niche mismatch class ([[project_bytes_boxed_runtime_abi]]'s sibling; the Bytes fix `43e2c69a` disciplined the NEWTYPE recovery but the NICHE recovery kept `List.exists`). **Minimal repro (P9/`test/native/niche_ctor_ambiguity.march`):** a nested-module `type Row = Row(List(Int))` matched `Cons(Row(fp), rest)` — `len=2` interp, `len=0` compiled; the emitted `.ll` showed the inner decode as `icmp eq ptr, null` (niche) instead of a tag switch. **Fix:** `branches_match_niche_shape` now collects ALL candidate owner typedefs (every variant type whose ctor set contains all the branch ctor tags) and commits to the niche decode only when they ALL classify niche-shaped — mirroring `newtype_recovery_payload`'s all-owners ambiguity discipline; any ambiguity keeps Boxed (the status quo). Genuine niche matches that list a distinguishing ctor set (e.g. both `CsvEof` and `Row`, as every csv.march match does) are unaffected — their only owner is the real niche type. **Verified:** `gb.march` Groups: 2 == interp; `bench/dataframe_bench.march` AND `examples/dataframe_basic.march` now byte-IDENTICAL to interp end-to-end (group_by 5 groups + correct means, inner_join 800, summarize 4) — both PRUNED from the oracle `known_divergence` list (DataFrame divergences now ZERO). Regressions: `test/native/niche_ctor_ambiguity.march` (mechanism) + `test/native/dataframe_groupby_count.march` (user-facing) + oracle anchors.

  **UPDATE 2026-07-18 (session 2) — recovered the FULL prior analysis + RULED OUT the nested-fn-param hypothesis for THIS (float-free) manifestation.** The lost `c6599af9` commit (whose typecheck fix restored item 32) parked a deep DataFrame investigation; its analysis (recovered from `git show c6599af9:specs/todos.md` lines 59-64) root-caused the ORIGINAL FLOAT crash to THREE stacked layers, the key one being **Layer 2 (`lib/tir/lower.ml`, nested-fn param typing):** a nested `fn go(lst : List(a), acc : Int)` gets its ANNOTATED param types via `lower_ty` (the NAME tvar family, `TVar "a"`) while the body's span-derived types use the typechecker's NUMBERED family (`TVar "_2006"`), so mono's ELetRec local-subst (matched against param types) never covers the body's tvars. Top-level fns are fixed via `Lower_decls.ty_from_tc_or_ann` (prefer span, fall back to annotation only on `TVar "_"`); nested `ELetFn`/`ELam` (lower.ml ~762 / ~631) do the OPPOSITE (prefer annotation). The prior 3-part fix's piece (a) [span-preferring nested params] FIXED the float crash but INTRODUCED a `Groups: 0` regression (attributed to a stale span type breaking group-key hashing) and was reverted; recommended proper fix was to make the typechecker record accurate nested-fn param-span types first. **BUT: the typechecker ALREADY records ELetFn param-span types (typecheck.ml ELetFn ~5284, added post-analysis), and applying `ty_from_tc_or_ann` to BOTH `ELetFn` AND `ELam` in this session left the float-free `gb.march` at `Groups: 0` unchanged** — so the nested-fn-param typing (Layer 2) is NOT the root cause of the current float-free wrong-answer. Both speculative lower changes reverted (no surviving diff). **The float crash the prior analysis targeted is now separately FIXED by the item-45 runtime float-boxing fix** (a different root), which is why the bench reaches group_by at all. **Remaining precise state:** a runtime RC drop of the head-`Row`'s `List((String,Value))` payload between construction in `apply_group_by`'s `List.map(group_pairs, closure)` (instrumented payload=2) and consumption in `from_rows_widen`'s `Cons(Row(first_pairs),_)` head-match (instrumented first_pairs=0). `from_rows_widen`'s own TIR is CLEAN (no TError/mistype; `first_pairs : List((String, Value))`). No ASAN signal. Isolated repros P4/P5/P6 all pass. **Next: a dedicated runtime RC-watch session** (MARCH_WATCH rc-hook / MARCH_DEBUG_PERCEUS on the specific closures — filter_col_by_indices_df / eval_agg_exprs' nested `go` / the `List.append(key_pairs, agg_pairs)` in the map closure) to catch exactly where the payload's rc hits 0. The closure captures `df`/`group_cols`/`agg_exprs` as heap FVs; the `key_pairs = List.zip(group_cols, key_vals)` aliasing-without-dup hypothesis is still unconfirmed but is the leading suspect.

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18, `lib/tir/cprop.ml`).** Root cause: a copy-propagation / `strip_scrut_decrc` NAME-DESYNC. When `Beta_adt` (pre-Perceus) collapses the static outer `Cons`, the head constructor becomes an owned-local `case` scrutinee bound through a copy alias (`let $f = $head`). Perceus emits the arm's ownership `dec_rc $f`, which `llvm_case.ml`'s `strip_scrut_decrc` is supposed to convert into a shallow free that IncRC's the extracted fields (so freeing the head box keeps the still-live extracted heap field alive). But cprop then copy-propagated the scrutinee ATOM (`case $f` → `case $head`) while — by design (`cprop.ml` never rewrites `EDecRC` operands, to protect RC counts) — leaving `dec_rc $f` untouched. `strip_scrut_decrc` matches the arm's ownership dec BY NAME against the scrutinee (`$head`), so the desynced `dec_rc $f` was no longer recognized, the compensating field-IncRC was skipped, and freeing the head deep-freed the still-live extracted field → `RC underflow (rc was 0)`. Same C1-class under-refcount as the 2026-07-11 map-key fix, but caused by cprop desyncing the names rather than dec ordering. **Fix:** cprop's `ECase` case now keeps the scrutinee un-substituted whenever an arm's leading dec-run contains a `dec_rc` of the original scrutinee var (`branch_leads_with_dec`), preserving the scrutinee↔arm-dec name link `strip_scrut_decrc` relies on. Strictly more conservative (a few un-propagated scrutinee copies); no existing post-Perceus snapshot shifted (cprop is post-Perceus). Verified: `p2` / 3-Row / tuple-payload variants interp==compiled; `p2b`/`p3`/`--no-opt` controls unchanged; regression `test/native/nested_cons_ctor_heap.march` + oracle anchor + `test/snapshots/*/nested_cons_ctor_heap`; full gate green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 31 / codegen 421 / stdlib 809 / oracle 0 un-triaged); RC benchmarks unchanged (tree_transform 104857600 / list_ops 333333666666 / binary_trees depth-16 131071). NOTE: this does NOT fix the DataFrame group_by/join empty-result bug above — that is a distinct bug (dynamic list, no static-Cons collapse, no ASAN signal), confirmed still `Groups: 0` after this fix.

  ~~Nested `Cons(Ctor(heap_field), rest)` match miscompiles to an RC underflow (compiled abort) when the optimizer statically collapses the outer `Cons` (2026-07-18).~~ Minimal repro (`p2.march`): `type Row = Row(List(Int))`; `let rows = Cons(Row(Cons(1, Cons(2, Nil))), Cons(Row(Cons(3, Nil)), Nil))`; `match rows do Cons(Row(fp), rest) -> println(int_to_string(List.length(fp))) | Nil -> ... end`. Interp prints `2`; compiled `--opt 2` aborts `march: RC underflow (rc was 0)`. **Bisected:** (a) `--no-opt` compiles+runs correctly; (b) building the list dynamically from a function so the optimizer can't fold the `Cons` (`p2b.march`) works at `--opt 2`; (c) a single `Row` matched directly (`P1`) works; (d) `Cons(Box(Int), rest)` with a SCALAR inner field (`P3`) works. So the trigger is specifically: an outer `Cons` whose head is a statically-known constructor wrapping a HEAP field, matched with a nested pattern, where the optimizer's case-of-known-constructor collapse fires. **Mechanism — CONFIRMED localized to a post-Perceus Opt pass (2026-07-18).** The post-Perceus snapshot (Lower→Mono→Defun→Perceus, no Opt) is CORRECT and matches the working `--no-opt` binary: it keeps the full nested `case rows of Cons($f527,$f528) -> dec_rc rows; case $f527 of Row($f529) -> dec_rc $f527; … let fp = $f529 in …`, where every `dec_rc` is a Perceus SHALLOW-free that transfers ownership of the extracted children to their bindings (the `dec_rc $f527` before `let fp` is fine BECAUSE the shallow free moves `$f529`'s reference to `fp`). But a post-Perceus Opt pass — the case-of-known-constructor collapse (`Beta_adt`, and/or the `Opt.run` fixed-point's cprop/inline that folds the static outer `Cons(head, tail)` literal into direct `$head`/`$tail` lets and DCEs the outer Cons alloc) — rewrites this into `case $headRow of Row($f) -> dec_rc $headRow; let rest = $tail in dec_rc rest; let fp = $f in …use fp…` and in doing so breaks the shallow-free ownership-transfer accounting, yielding an RC underflow at runtime (`rc was 0`). So the fix belongs in whichever Opt pass collapses the outer `Cons`: it must preserve Perceus's shallow-free semantics (the folded-away `dec_rc rows` transferred head+tail ownership; after the fold, head/tail are owned directly and their own `dec_rc`s plus the inner field extraction must stay balanced — the collapse currently double-accounts the head Row's field). `--dump-tir` (post-Opt) shows the broken form; the post-Perceus snapshot shows the correct form — the diff between them IS the offending pass. Repro at scratchpad `p2.march`; `p2b.march` (dynamic list, opt on) / `p3.march` (scalar inner field) / `--no-opt` are the passing controls.

### Recently fixed
- ✅ **Compiled-only wrong value: a builtin call (`int_to_string`, `math_sqrt`, ...) fed a scalar bound by a tuple/constructor pattern read the raw tagged bits instead of the untagged value (2026-07-22)** — found auditing `specs/lang/pattern-matching.md`. Minimal repro: `match f() do Some((top, rest)) -> println(int_to_string(top)) ... end` where `f() : Option((Int,Int))` returns `Some((3,9))`. Interpreted prints `3` (correct); compiled printed `7` = `(3<<1)|1`, the raw low-bit-tagged immediate encoding of `3`, read verbatim as if it were already an untagged `i64`. Confirmed NOT specific to nesting-inside-a-constructor — a plain top-level `match f() do (top, rest) -> int_to_string(top) end` (no `Some` at all) hit the identical bug; a `let (top, rest) = f()` destructuring-let was unaffected (different lowering path, binds `top` at its concrete `i64` type directly). **Root cause:** every `ECase`-bound field (tuple OR ADT constructor field) is loaded via the uniform ptr-slot convention (`llvm_case.ml`) — scalars are low-bit-tagged `(n<<1)|1` at construction and read back as generic `ptr`, meant to be conditionally untagged (`Llvm_ctx.coerce "ptr" "i64"`, an `ashr`) at the point of use. The generic `EApp` call-argument-coercion path (`llvm_emit.ml`, ~line 1975) only performed that coercion against `ctx.top_fn_param_tys` — populated for user-defined fns/externs only. Compiler builtins (`int_to_string`, `math_sqrt`, `float_abs`, `tcp_listen`, ~50 more with a native `i64`/`double` C parameter, per `lib/tir/llvm_builtins.ml`'s `declare_sig` table) were never in that table, so an argument arriving as `ptr` (from any tuple/ADT scalar field) flowed uncoerced into the builtin's native scalar parameter — the raw tagged bits landed in the parameter register unchanged. Verified in the emitted LLVM: `call ptr @march_int_to_string(ptr %ld31)` against a declaration of `declare ptr @march_int_to_string(i64 %n)` — a type-mismatched call that clang/LLVM silently accepted (both types are pointer-width) rather than erroring, so the tag bits reached the C function as the raw integer argument. **Fix:** `lib/tir/llvm_builtins.ml` — added `builtin_param_llvm_tys`, deriving each builtin's parameter LLVM types by parsing its own `declare_sig` text (the same string already used for the preamble `declare` line — one source of truth, no new hand-maintained table to drift). `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`'s `EApp` argument-coercion fallback now also consults this when `top_fn_param_tys` has no entry, coercing each arg to the builtin's declared param type exactly as it already does for user fns. Verified: original repro, plain top-level tuple match, 3-tuple payload, 2-level-nested tuple payload, and a `Float`/`Int` tuple flowing into `math_sqrt`/`float_to_string`/`int_to_string` all now match interpreted output compiled. (`let Some((top, rest)) = f()` — bare constructor pattern in a block `let` — does not parse in March; confirmed not a viable alternative repro shape.) Full suite green: compiler 527 / eval 238 / codegen 438 (1 unrelated skip: cross TLS+gzip linux/amd64, no sysroot) / stdlib 780 quick (2 TIR snapshot failures in `run_snapshots.exe`, `tuple_atom_string_arms`/`scrutinee_borrowed_conservatism`, confirmed pre-existing on `main` via file-copy-swap baseline, untouched by this change — this fix never touches TIR/Perceus, only post-Perceus LLVM codegen). Benchmarks (`tree_transform`, `list_ops`, `binary_trees`) compile and run with unchanged output.
- ✅ **General (non-builtin-named) interface impls with a compositional `when` constraint self-dispatched to their OWN body instead of the constrained type's impl — wrong answer interpreted, ICE compiled (2026-07-22)** — found auditing `specs/lang/surface-syntax.md`'s Implementations section against the compiler. Minimal repro: `interface MyEq(a) do fn eq: a -> a -> Bool end`, `impl MyEq(Int) do fn eq(x,y) do x == y end end`, `type Wrap(a) = Wrap(a)`, `impl MyEq(Wrap(a)) when MyEq(a) do fn eq(w1,w2) do match (w1,w2) do (Wrap(x),Wrap(y)) -> eq(x,y) end end end` — the natural, idiomatic shape for ANY compositional interface impl (`Eq(List(a)) when Eq(a)`, `Show(Option(a)) when Show(a)`, etc.), not contrived. **Interpreted:** `eq(Wrap(1),Wrap(1))` panicked `non-exhaustive pattern match: no branch matched (1, 1)` — the inner `eq(x,y)` recursive call re-entered `Wrap`'s OWN `eq` (matching `Int`s against the `(Wrap(x),Wrap(y))` pattern) instead of dispatching by the runtime type of `x`/`y`. Root cause: `lib/eval/eval.ml`'s `DImpl` handling (TWO independent copies — the top-level `eval_decl` arm AND a byte-for-byte duplicate inside `make_recursive_env`, since a source file's single top-level `mod X do ... end` is unwrapped by the PARSER so its decls are processed by the latter, not via `eval_decl`'s own `DMod` recursion) built each non-zero-param impl method as a SELF-RECURSIVE closure (`eval_decl env (DFn (fn_def, sp))`) for every interface except the four builtin-dispatched ones (Show/Eq/Ord/Hash, which already got a non-self-referential closure so recursive calls route through the builtin `eq`/`compare`/`show`/`hash` dispatch instead of back into the impl) — so a GENERAL interface's compositional body silently shadowed its own per-method dispatcher. **Compiled:** `internal compiler error: Failure("interface dispatch fn __march_ifdispatch$MyEq$eq$Int has no runtime-tag rows")` at `lib/tir/llvm_case.ml:847`. Root cause (unrelated code path, same repro): `Lower_state`'s `_iface_methods` dispatch table keys rows by BARE method name only (never by interface), so a user interface's method sharing a literal name with an unrelated interface (here: the compiler's own synthesized primitive `Eq$Int.eq`/`Eq$Float.eq`/… rows, `lib/tir/lower.ml`'s builtin-iface injection block) lands in the SAME bucket; `Mono.try_collision_dispatch` — built for the unrelated case of one interface's impl colliding across two SAME-SHORT-NAME types (the FQN dispatch-identity work, see `project_fqn_impl_dispatch_identity`/`specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-dispatch-identity.md`) — then mistook the two DIFFERENT interfaces' `Int` rows for competing impls of one ambiguous type and tried to build a runtime constructor-tag switch over a bare `Int` (no ADT tags to switch on), hence "has no runtime-tag rows". Confirmed NOT the same bug class as the FQN work despite sharing `llvm_case.ml`'s dispatch-fn codegen: this repro has zero same-short-name type collisions. **Fix (interpreter, `lib/eval/eval.ml`):** general-interface impl methods now build a non-self-referential closure the same way Show/Eq/Ord/Hash already did, over an environment where the method name is bound to its per-(iface,method) dispatcher (created idempotently — reused if an earlier impl of the same method already built one — so this is independent of impl declaration order); the `make_recursive_env` duplicate is deleted outright and now delegates to `eval_decl`, removing the drift hazard that let this exact fix land in one copy but not the other. **Fix (compiler, `lib/tir/lower.ml`):** `collect_iface_impls` now qualifies bare self-referencing calls inside a GENERAL (non-Show/Eq/Ord/Hash) interface impl body to `"Iface.method"` — reusing the qualified-key row `collect_iface_impls` already registers per impl — so the call resolves only against that interface's own rows and never collides with an unrelated interface's same-named method; builtin-named interfaces are excluded (their primitive rows are registered under the bare name only, so qualifying would leave e.g. `Eq(List(a))`'s recursive `eq` on an `Int` element unresolved — verified no regression: `[1,2,3] == [1,2,3]`/`Some(1) == Some(1)` still work both backends). Verified: the minimal repro plus declaration-order reversal (`Wrap` impl declared BEFORE `Int`'s), three-level nesting (`Wrap(Wrap(Wrap(Int)))`), and a two-constraint `when` clause (`impl MyEq(Pair(a,b)) when MyEq(a), MyEq(b)`) all print the correct answer on BOTH backends. Full suite: compiler 527 / eval 238 / codegen 438 / stdlib 780 (quick) — all green; snapshots 31 (2 pre-existing failures, `tuple_atom_string_arms`/`scrutinee_borrowed_conservatism` at the perceus stage, confirmed present on an unmodified baseline via file-copy A/B swap, unrelated to this fix).
- ✅ **Interpreter WebSocket connections flapped disconnected within ~0s of an idle read — non-blocking accept-loop socket mode leaked into the blocking WS handler (2026-07-21)** — found chasing a `forge scroll.serve` repro where the notebook UI loaded once then immediately flipped to "disconnected — retrying in Ns" in a tight loop, and a raw curl WS handshake got an instant server-initiated `Close(1001, "going away")` with no client-side close ever sent. The 2026-07-07 `run_http_event_loop` fix (see entry below) put every accepted client socket in non-blocking mode (`set_nonblock client_sock`) so its multiplexed HTTP accept loop never stalls, and its own comments claimed the WS-upgraded connection "becomes WS-owned and blocking, exactly as before this fix" — but no code ever cleared the non-blocking flag at the WS handoff (`http_run_pipeline_and_respond`, `lib/eval/eval.ml`). `ws_recv_frame`'s blanket `try ... with _ -> close_gone` then caught the resulting `Unix.Unix_error(EAGAIN|EWOULDBLOCK, "recv", _)` from `Unix.recv` on any read that raced ahead of the client's next frame — including, under the right timing, the very FIRST post-handshake read — and silently reported it as the peer closing the connection. Verified with a controlled Python WS client (`websockets` lib): pre-fix, a client that connects and sends `{"type":"load"}` gets slammed shut milliseconds later (immediate `EAGAIN` on the next blocking-style `recv`); post-fix, the same connection stays open 60s+ idle and a full `load` → `run` → `poll_run` round trip completes normally with the socket still open afterward. Fix: `Unix.clear_nonblock sock` right before the WS handshake response is written (`lib/eval/eval.ml`, `http_run_pipeline_and_respond`), so every subsequent `ws_recv_exact`/`http_recv_line`-style blocking read actually blocks instead of racing a leftover non-blocking flag. Found and fixed the same bug CLASS in the compiled runtime's thread-per-connection HTTP server (`runtime/march_http.c` `connection_thread`): the keep-alive `SO_RCVTIMEO=10s` socket option set at connection-thread startup was never cleared before handing the fd to the blocking WS closure, so a `--compile`-built WS server would spuriously disconnect an idle client with the same synthesized `Close(1001, ...)` (from `recv_exact`'s undifferentiated `r <= 0` check) after 10s of inactivity instead of instantly — same root cause (an accept-time-scoped socket mode not undone before WS takeover), different timing symptom. Fixed by resetting `SO_RCVTIMEO` to `{0,0}` right before the WS handshake/handoff, mirroring how the C runtime's OTHER server (the evloop variant's `ws_handler_thread`, `runtime/march_http_evloop.c`) already explicitly clears `O_NONBLOCK` before its own handoff — the thread-per-connection path was the one missing an analogous reset. Full suite green (`scripts/run-tests.sh`) except one unrelated pre-existing/flaky failure (`test_compiled_sanitize_clean_exit`, an ASAN altstack-teardown regression test in `runtime/march_scheduler.c`, a file this change never touches). Separately noticed but NOT fixed here (files a distinct follow-up): the server always replies to a WS `Ping` with an empty `Pong` payload (`lib/eval/eval.ml` `ws_send_frame` `VCon ("Pong", _) -> (0x8A, "")`, and the equivalent in `runtime/march_http.c`) instead of echoing the Ping's payload as RFC 6455 requires — harmless for real browsers (whose native WebSocket API never exposes manual ping/pong to page JS) but would make any WS client/proxy that actively pings and strictly validates the echoed payload (observed with Python's `websockets` client library, which force-closes after two missed pongs, ~40s) misdiagnose the connection as unresponsive; the `WsFrame` stdlib ADT (`stdlib/websocket.march`) would need a payload field added to `Ping`/`Pong` to carry it, a breaking shape change touching both runtimes and every application pattern-matching on those constructors, so it's out of scope for this connection-stability fix.
- ✅ **`string_to_float`/`String.to_float` compiled-only SIGSEGV — Option(Float) Some-cell stored the raw double inline instead of a boxed-float pointer (2026-07-21; `runtime/march_runtime.c` `march_string_to_float`).** Found while auditing `docs/cookbook/strings.md`: `match string_to_float("3.14") do Some(f) -> println(float_to_string(f)) ... end` segfaulted (exit 139) compiled but ran fine interpreted. `Option(Float)` is correctly classified `Boxed` (0.0 aliases niche-None=0, so it can't use the raw-pointer niche encoding other `Option(_)` builtins use — see `Repr.niche_payload_ok`'s `TFloat -> false` arm, already correct). The bug was purely in the hand-written runtime C: `march_string_to_float`'s `Some(f)` cell wrote the raw IEEE-754 double directly at the payload offset, but the LLVM codegen's generic Boxed-ADT ctor convention treats every ctor field slot as pointer-width and, for a `Float` field, loads it as `ptr` then calls `march_unbox_float(ptr)` to recover the double — exactly the convention `native_float_arr_to_list`/`native_float_arr_from_list` already use correctly for `List(Float)` (the earlier float-boxing fix, `runtime/march_runtime.c` ~4389-4425). `march_unbox_float` then dereferenced 3.14's own bit pattern as a heap pointer. Fix: box the payload via `march_alloc_float(f)` and store the resulting pointer at offset 16, matching the established convention. Verified: `Some`/`None`/`0.0` (the exact aliasing case the boxing exists to prevent)/negative floats all correct compiled; full `String.to_float` stdlib path (the real caller, used by e.g. `stdlib/toml.march`) correct; full `dune runtest` (all suites) green, zero regressions. Regression test: `test/native/string_to_float_option.march` + `.expected` (existing `test_string_to_float` in `test/test_codegen.ml` only ever exercised the interpreter via `eval_with_string`, so this compiled-only representation bug was invisible to it).
- ✅ **`Lower_state.resolve_iface_method` was not collision-aware — an ambiguous general-interface call site got baked to whichever impl was registered first at LOWER time, not deferred to Mono's collision dispatch (2026-07-22).** Found as a side effect of a follow-on constructor-module-qualified-identity investigation, independent of and already present before that work (landed as part of the FQN dispatch-identity Stages 1-3 PR below). `resolve_iface_method` (`lib/tir/lower_state.ml`) resolved the callee's concrete type name via `List.assoc_opt tname impls` — first-match, not collision-aware — when two modules declare same-short-name types (e.g. `NA.Thing`/`NB.Thing`) that both `impl` the same interface, `impls` under the bare key `"Thing"` holds both candidates and `List.assoc_opt` silently returned whichever was registered first, baking ONE static impl symbol into the call's `EApp` callee before `Mono.monomorphize`'s collision-aware `try_collision_dispatch` (which generates a correct runtime tag-switch) ever runs. `env.type_map` (the typechecker's own type representation, all this layer has to consult) only carries the type's BARE name — the module-qualified identity is attached later, in the TIR/Mono layer — so this layer has no sound way to pick a winner and must defer. **Note:** for the exact repro shape in the bug report (`speak(NA.mk())`/`speak(NB.mk())` in one `main`), the wrong resolution happened to be masked END-TO-END by an unrelated Mono guard (the interface-method-name-collision check, `mono.ml` ~line 608, added for a different bug — a user fn sharing a name with an interface method) that re-verifies the call's actual argument type against the picked impl's declared parameter type; that incidental self-healing is not a substitute for correct behavior at the lowering layer, and does not cover every call shape (e.g. `ECallPtr` sites with no `fn_table` entry have no such guard). **Fix:** `resolve_iface_method` now dedups `impls` by mangled symbol under the queried `tname` and returns `Some` only when exactly one distinct impl remains — `None` (deferring to Mono) when ≥2, mirroring the `uniq >= 2` gate `Mono.try_collision_dispatch` already uses. Purely collision-conditional: non-colliding call sites are unaffected. TDD: new lower-only unit test `test_ambiguous_iface_call_stays_unresolved_at_lower_time` (`test/test_codegen.ml`, "lower: collision-conditional impl symbols" group) proves BOTH `speak` calls stay as a bare, unresolved `speak(...)` callee post-`Lower.lower_module` (RED pre-fix: both resolved to the SAME `Speak$NB.Thing.speak` symbol). New end-to-end runtime witness `test/native/iface_collision_ambiguous_call.march` (compile-and-run golden, prints `from-A`/`from-B`) — companion to `test/imports/speak_collision_native`, which structurally dodges this exact shape (each call there originates inside the impl's own declaring module). Full suite green: compiler 524 / eval 238 / codegen 438 / stdlib 814 (the one `MARCH_SANITIZE` ASAN-altstack-teardown failure is a PRE-EXISTING environmental hang — confirmed via zombie `sanexit_bin` processes dated hours before this session even started — unrelated and reproduces identically without this change); `test/snapshots/` unchanged. Design context: `specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-dispatch-identity.md`.
- ✅ **FQN dispatch-identity Stages 2-3 COMPLETE — same-short-name types in different modules may each implement ANY interface (not just `Eq`/`Ord`/`Show`/`Hash`), dispatching correctly interpreted AND compiled (2026-07-21).** Builds on Stage 1 (declaring-module coherence key). The Stage-1 relaxation was scoped to the four type-dispatched builtins because a GENERAL user interface then mangled two same-short-name impls to ONE symbol and dispatched on the bare type name — silently running the wrong body compiled (`from-A`/`from-A`). Stages 1-3 close that, **all collision-conditional** (non-colliding programs are byte-identical): a `Collision_set` pass (TIR `lib/tir/collision_set.ml` + an AST-level twin in `lib/eval/eval.ml`) identifies short names declared by ≥2 modules; colliding types then get (1) globally-unique runtime tags, (2) forced uniform Boxed representation, (3) module-qualified mangled impl symbols (`Speak$NA.Thing.speak` vs `Speak$NB.Thing.speak`, `lib/tir/lower.ml`), (4) a generated runtime tag-switch dispatch fn (`__march_ifdispatch$...`, `lib/tir/mono.ml` + `Llvm_dispatch`/`llvm_emit`) that routes an ambiguous bare-typed call site on the value's real ctor tag; the interpreter qualifies `iface_method_tbl` the same way (`lib/eval/eval.ml`). **Flag-day (this task):** `register_impl_shape` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`) drops the builtin-only `iface_native_type_dispatched` gate and the temporary `MARCH_DEV_RELAX_COHERENCE` dev harness entirely, so EVERY interface gets the declaring-module coherence relaxation. Fixture `reject/t82_impl_general_iface_collision` flips to `accept/t89_impl_general_iface_collision` (types corpus now 89 accept / 82 reject, counting Task 6b's re-added `reject/t82_impl_coherence_shared_ctor_double_collision`). First cross-backend runtime witness `test/imports/speak_collision_native` (3-file import fixture, runs `from-A`/`from-B` correctly interpreted AND compiled). **NARROWED RESIDUAL GAP (Task 6b, 2026-07-21):** when two colliding same-short-name types ALSO share a CONSTRUCTOR name (a "double collision", e.g. both `type Thing = Shared | …`), this specific shape is now REJECTED at typecheck (a safe compile error) rather than silently misdispatching — `register_impl_shape` gains a ctor-set-disjointness check that only relaxes coherence when the two colliding types' constructor NAME sets are disjoint. Fixtures: `reject/t82_impl_coherence_shared_ctor_double_collision` (rejected) vs `accept/t89` (distinct ctor names, still accepted). Making these two ACTUALLY dispatch correctly (instead of being rejected) still needs the `ci_module.Type.Ctor` extra qualification layer — tracked as its own OPEN item under P1 below. Design: `specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-dispatch-identity.md` (status now `implemented`).
- ✅ **Lazy-stack-growth SIGSEGV handler gated on `si_code == SEGV_ACCERR`, crashing on MAPERR-reporting Linux (2026-07-21; `runtime/march_scheduler.c` `march_sigsegv_handler`).** Compiled parallel/distributed programs (`List.pmap`/`pfilter` on >1024 elems, msgpack RPC) intermittently SIGSEGV'd (exit 139) on Linux while passing on macOS arm64 — the reported "concurrency" release blocker. **Root cause is NOT a data race** (TSan on native aarch64 Linux found zero races across the pmap and rpc_auto_enroll corpora; the crash reproduces under a single scheduler too). It is the green-thread lazy-stack-growth fault handler: it accepts SIGBUS unconditionally but required `SIGSEGV && si_code == SEGV_ACCERR`, rejecting a legitimate guard-page growth fault whenever the kernel reports it as `SEGV_MAPERR`. **Empirically verified:** an identical `mmap(PROT_NONE)`+access reports `SEGV_ACCERR` (2) on native aarch64 Linux but `SEGV_MAPERR` (1) under emulated/virtualized x86-64 (qemu-user; and, by this signature, some hypervisor/CI VM configs). This exactly explains the macOS-passes/Linux-crashes asymmetry (macOS delivers guard faults as SIGBUS, always accepted) and the flakiness (whether a run's green stack grows past its committed page is timing/data-dependent, perturbed by concurrent scheduling; stack-heavy pmap/msgpack recursion trips it most). **Fix:** classify a stack-growth fault purely by the address-range check (fault addr within the running proc's `[grow_lo, grow_hi)` reservation — the code's own comment already called this "the real safety gate"), for SIGSEGV and SIGBUS alike; drop the `si_code` gate. A genuine wild pointer is outside every proc's growable region and still terminates via `fatal:`; an in-range fault whose mmap is gone fails the mprotect and also terminates. **Validation:** the reproduced crash (emulated x86-64, `List.pmap` 2000-elem parity like adversarial-regression #22, and a 30k-elem × 40-round heavy stress) went 50/50 → 0/50 and 15/15 → 0/15; `rpc_auto_enroll` 0 failures; full driver suite on native aarch64 Linux shows an IDENTICAL pre/post FAIL set (byte-for-byte baseline comparison — zero regressions); `bench/tree_transform` unchanged (change is in the fault handler, not the RC hot path). No perf cost.
- ✅ **impl-coherence now distinguishes same-short-name types by DECLARING MODULE (2026-07-20; FQN dispatch-identity Stage 1).** Two genuinely-distinct ADTs sharing a short name across modules (`AeLib.AeDir` vs `AeLib2.AeDir`) can each declare their own `impl Eq(AeDir)` without a false `Overlapping implementation` — previously both lowered to `TCon("AeDir")` and the coherence check (`register_impl_shape`, `types_overlap`) over-fired. **Fix (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`):** `register_impl_shape` gains `?decl_module` (threaded at the four Pass-1 fold sites); each impl head resolves to a declaring-module identity — qualified head `Mod.T` → the `.`-prefix, bare head → `decl_module` iff `StrMap.mem (decl_module^"."^name) env.types` (empirically verified to hold for both nested modules `NA.Thing` and sibling-file modules `AeLib.AeDir`), else `None` (conservative). `env.impls` entries carry the resolved module as a THIRD tuple element (`ty * span * string option`); two heads overlap only when they do NOT resolve to two DISTINCT concrete modules. **The relaxation is SCOPED to the type-dispatched builtin interfaces (`Eq`/`Ord`/`Show`/`Hash`)** — those dispatch natively through generated ctor-qualified structural functions (`ensure_adt_eq_fn`) and are correct compiled. A GENERAL user interface dispatches on the bare type name in BOTH backends and mangles two same-short-name impls to ONE symbol, so allowing them would SILENTLY run the wrong body compiled (a spike confirmed `from-A`/`from-A`); those collisions stay REJECTED at declaration (`reject/t82_impl_general_iface_collision`) until Stage 3 adds runtime ctor-tag dispatch. The stored `inst_ty` stays BARE so `discharge_constraints` is untouched (avoids the cut-b `expected X but got Mod.X` split). **No codegen/mangling change — goldens + TIR snapshots byte-identical.** Witnesses `accept/t88_impl_distinct_modules` (builtin `Eq`) + `reject/t82_impl_general_iface_collision` (general `Speak`); `reject/t79`/`t80` + `accept/t83`/`t85` unchanged; 3 new `run_compiler` cases. `test/imports/adt_eq_native` drops its blanket `impl Eq(a)` workaround for per-module `impl Eq(AeDir)` (compiles + runs, proving the fix end-to-end). Suite: **compiler 520 / stdlib 810 / snapshots 31 / types 170 (88 accept + 82 reject) / oracle 0 divergences**; the lone `dune @runtest` failure (`native_ffi_result`, expects `nan` gets `bad int`) is PRE-EXISTING and unrelated — `ffi_result.march` has no `impl`s, so the coherence change is provably a no-op for it (filed separately). Design: `specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-dispatch-identity.md`; plan: `specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-coherence-stage1-plan.md`. **Stages 2–3 (interp `impl_tbl` + native runtime ctor-tag dispatch, for the general case) remain open** — part of the broader FQN overhaul below.
- ✅ **Self-referencing block-let shadowing (`let x = x + 5` rebinding the same name) miscompiled on the native AND JS backends while the interpreter was correct (2026-07-10)** — `let x = 10; let x = x + 5; println(int_to_string(x))` printed `15` interpreted but `10` compiled (`--compile`, silently) and folded to `String(10)` under `--target js`; a genuinely non-foldable chain (e.g. `let x = f(x)`) emitted nested `{ const x = (…x…) }` in JS that hit the temporal-dead-zone (TDZ). **Root cause** (`lib/tir/lower.ml`): block-let lowering emitted BOTH bindings under the source name `x` — the post-lower TIR was `let x = 10 in let x = +(x,5) in int_to_string(x)`, structurally correct (proper nesting) but name-ambiguous. The native codegen (`llvm_emit`) copes (it renames colliding alloca slots — verified: `--emit-llvm --no-opt` is correct), but every NAME-BASED TIR pass captures across the shadow: copy-prop/fold (which runs at all `--opt` levels — `opt_enabled` is separate from clang `--opt N`) records `x -> 10` from the OUTER binding and substitutes it into `int_to_string(x)`, whose `x` semantically refers to the INNER binding, folding to `int_to_string(10)`; the inner binding then dies and is DCE'd. The JS `const` emitter independently TDZ-faults on the self-reference. **Fix:** new `Lower_decls.uniquify_fn`, mapped over every function at the end of `Lower.lower_module`, alpha-renames any local binder that SHADOWS a name already in scope to a fresh unique name (`orig ^ "$sh" ^ N`) and rewrites references in the binder's scope — a scope-aware walk over all TIR binding forms (`ELet`, `ELetRec` fn-names+params, `ECase` `br_vars`, `fn_params`). Non-shadowing binders keep their source name, so non-shadowing code is byte-for-byte unchanged (only genuinely-shadowing functions shift). Fixes the whole capture class at once (cprop/fold/inline/dce + the JS `const` emitter) and aligns the compiled backends with the interpreter's lexical scoping. Post-lower TIR is now `let x = 10 in let x$sh1 = +(x,5) in int_to_string(x$sh1)`. New compile-and-run golden `test/native/shadow_selfref_let.march` (single, chained, and match-arm-body shadows; native+JS+interp all print `15 / 70 / 107 / 0`). One intended snapshot shift: `guard_match`'s two guarded arms each bind `n = x` and the guard-fallthrough nesting made the second a genuine shadow → renamed to `n$sh1` (both stages regenerated, behavior-preserving — both bind to `x`). **Suite: 451 compiler / 231 eval / 394 codegen (the lone `task_await_int`/`task_await_ptr` ir-verify-gate failure is PRE-EXISTING — a CWD-dependent tmp-dir emit artifact, reproduces identically with the fix disabled, and the task_await compile-and-run golden passes) / 807 stdlib / 53 test_stdlib_march / 29 snapshots, 0 new failures.** NOTE: the bug report referenced a `mix32` comment + workaround in `stdlib/random.march` and a filed todos entry — neither exists in this tree; `random.march`'s `mix` uses self-referencing `x` shadows directly (unworkaround-ed) and is now correct compiled.
- ✅ **`march_ws_recv` freed an uninitialized (and double-freed a real) `payload` on every WebSocket disconnect → server SIGSEGV crash-loop (2026-07-08)** — found running production `forgepm.org`: the native server crash-looped ~every 12s (593+ SIGSEGV), which surfaced as intermittent Cloudflare 502s. `gdb -p` on the live server (the crash is traffic-triggered — an idle instance never crashes, and a first backtrace on an isolated run misattributed to `Config.e`/`march_process_env`) gave the real stack: `__libc_free(mem=0x12) ← march_ws_recv ← WebSocket.recv ← IslandSocket.ws_loop`. In `runtime/march_http.c` `march_ws_recv`, `payload` was declared partway down the function, but the early `goto closed` paths (2-byte header read, extended-length read, mask read) jump PAST that declaration to the `closed:` cleanup, which does `free(payload)` — so a client that closes before sending a full frame (**every browser WebSocket disconnect**, and the island socket runs BEFORE the request logger so the crash was unlogged) freed an uninitialized stack pointer. A second bug: the mid-payload read-failure path did `free(payload); goto closed;`, and `closed:` freed it again — a double-free. Fix: declare `uint8_t *payload = NULL;` at the very top of the function (before any `goto closed`) and drop the redundant pre-goto `free` (the label owns the free). Verified in production (old binary crashed on the 1st WS disconnect; fixed binary survived 25/25 abrupt disconnects against the live service, 0 restarts). New standalone regression `test/test_ws_disconnect.sh` (like `test_http_native.sh`): compiles `examples/ws_echo.march`, then opens 20 WebSockets and, on half, sends a frame header claiming a payload then closes before sending it (the deterministic double-free path — the uninitialized-free alone is stack-garbage-dependent and can spuriously pass), asserting the server stays up + still serves. GREEN with the fix; the buggy server aborts (double-free) with it reverted.
- ✅ **`forge` registry-dependency resolver — `bastion = "0.2.1"` now fetches + builds (2026-07-08)** — Registry-dep resolution was an explicit placeholder on this branch (a prior session built it but never committed — lost to churn); a bare-string dep `name = "0.2.1"` was silently dropped, so `forge build` errored `Unknown module Bastion`. Re-implemented (`forge/lib/{project,cmd_deps,cmd_build,registry_client}.ml`): `project.ml` parses bare-string and `{ version = "..." }` deps as `RegistryDep`; `cmd_deps.ml`'s `resolve_registry_deps` fetches `<reg>/api/v1/packages/:name` metadata via the embedded `forge_registry.march` `fetch` action, PubGrub-solves (path/git deps pinned as overrides), downloads each release, sha256-verifies against the release checksum (digestif), and extracts with `--strip-components=1` into `~/.march/cas/deps/<name>`; `cmd_build.ml` maps `RegistryDep → ~/.march/cas/deps/<name>/lib`. External commands run under a `fork`+`setsid`+kill-process-group timeout so a hung march→clang child can't orphan. Verified end-to-end against the LIVE registry: a minimal app AND the full **forgepm** app both resolve `bastion = "0.2.1"` (fetch metadata → PubGrub → download 485852 B → sha256 verify → extract) and compile with 0 errors (forgepm binary built). 239 forge tests green (1 pre-existing `qualified-call cycle` failure confirmed unrelated via `git stash`). Commit `d3f705d5`.
- ✅ **`march_tcp_recv_http` returned a bare String / NULL instead of `Result(String,String)` → compiled `forge publish` client PANICKED `non-exhaustive pattern match` (2026-07-08)** — `tcp_recv_http` is declared `Result(String, String)`, but `runtime/march_http.c`'s `march_tcp_recv_http` returned a bare `march_string` on success and `NULL` on every error path — unlike its sibling `march_tcp_send_all`, which wraps in `make_ok`/`make_err`. A bare String / NULL matches neither `Ok` nor `Err` of the boxed `Result`, so a compiled `match tcp_recv_http(...) do Err(e) -> .. | Ok(raw) -> .. end` hit the non-exhaustive fallback and PANICKED — this bit the `forge publish` client's plain-HTTP (`--insecure`) path (`forge_registry.march`): the publish succeeded server-side but the client crashed. Never seen in production because the TLS publish path reads via `read_chunks`, not `tcp_recv_http`. Fix: wrap the success return in `make_ok(result)` and every error path in `make_err(<reason>)`, honoring the declared Result contract (also protects stdlib `http_transport.march`, which matches it the same way). Verified: the `--insecure` fetch now fails GRACEFULLY (`transport: read failed: tcp_recv_http: connection closed …`) instead of panicking. Commit `ed778f10`. **Residual (separate, deeper): the plain-TCP path still can't complete the read over an SSH tunnel (connection-closed) — a `send_plain`/recv-behavior issue distinct from the panic; and a large multipart POST through the Cloudflare tunnel still returns 502 (likely cloudflared re-chunking a body forgepm's Content-Length-only parser can't frame). Production publishing uses the direct/TLS path; these affect `--insecure`/tunneled publishing only.**
- ✅ **Compiled HTTP server capped every request at a fixed 64KB → registry package uploads >64KB got a 413 (2026-07-08)** — `runtime/march_http.c`'s per-connection read buffer was a fixed `CONN_BUF_SIZE = 64 * 1024`; when it filled without a complete request parse, the server returned an immediate 413, bounding the WHOLE request (headers + body) at 64KB. So forgepm (the package registry) rejected any tarball upload larger than 64KB — a 486KB `bastion` publish `413`'d at the buffer (the `forge publish` client then saw the 413 and, through Cloudflare, a 502). Fix: grow the buffer by doubling on demand up to a new `MAX_REQ_SIZE = 32 * 1024 * 1024` cap (one `realloc` in the recv step), only 413 past the cap; sub-64KB requests still start at and stay within 64KB, so the hot path is unchanged and only an overflowing request pays a realloc. Verified live on the deploy droplet: a 600KB POST now reaches the handler (401 for a bad token) instead of 413, and `forge publish` of `bastion` 0.2.1 (485KB, with the islands-dispatch fix) succeeds server-side (registry lists 0.1.0–0.2.1). **Follow-up (not this fix): the `forge publish` client (`registry.march`) panics `non-exhaustive pattern match` parsing the publish SUCCESS response — the publish completes server-side but the CLI reports failure; a client-side response-shape gap to fix separately.**
- ✅ **`--check` type-erasure through an ENTRY-module self-qualified reference (`EntryMod.fn`) — an unannotated (or distinct-tvar-annotated) entry-level fn laundered any type through the qualified name, so a memory-unsafe mismatch typechecked clean (2026-07-08)** — `./_build/default/bin/main.exe --check` exited 0 on `mod Main do fn id(x) do x end  fn need_str(s : String) : Int do string_length(s) end  fn attack() : Int do need_str(Main.id(42)) end end` — an `Int` laundered into a `String` parameter (a memory-safety break); the bare `need_str(id(42))` correctly rejected. All three soundness classes reproduced through `Main.id`: general `Int`→`String`, the `Cap(IO)`→`Cap(Db.P)` proof-cap forge, and an ADT `Box(String)`→`Box(Int)` arg; a nested sibling reference to the entry name (`T.id` from `mod App` inside entry `T`) reproduced too. **Root cause** (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, DFn branch of `check_decl`): the entry module is UNWRAPPED at the combined module's top level, so — unlike a wrapped sibling module, whose public members are re-exported under `Sib.fn` with their real body-checked schemes when the sibling's `DMod` is checked (verified: `Lib.id` from a sibling correctly rejects) — its own top-level fns are only ever seeded by `check_module_core`'s Pass 1b (`prebind_mod_members m.mod_name.txt`) as a bare `Mono (fresh_var 1)` placeholder (`prebind_fn_scheme` returns None for an unannotated fn; a distinct-tvar annotation `fn f(x:a):b` yields an un-body-validated `a -> b` from annotation syntax). That decoupled `?a -> ?b` was never reconciled with the fn's real scheme, so any `EntryMod.fn` reference (produced by desugar's `qualify_module_refs`, or hand-written to disambiguate a shadowing nested local) instantiated it and ERASED the laundered type. The pinned placeholder also over-rejected legitimate polymorphism (`Main.id` used at both `Int` and `String` spuriously failed). **Fix:** the DFn branch now rebinds the entry-qualified name (`current_module ^ "." ^ fn_name`) to `sch`, the scheme `check_fn` validated against the body, so it is exactly as polymorphic as the bare name. Guarded to fire only at the ENTRY level (`cap_qual_prefix = "" && current_module <> ""`: nested/loaded modules already re-export real schemes) and only when the qualified key already exists (`Some _`: a private `pfn` gets no qualified prebind and is untouched; the incremental `check_module_with_env` path never seeds the entry's own top-level fns, so the fix is inert there). Codegen-safe: mono/TIR key on the per-span `type_map`, not this env scheme — `llvm_ir_validity_gate` stays at 0 failures. **Sibling of the still-open link-time finding above** (entry file self-qualifying its own top-level mod name → undefined symbols at link time): same `entry_prefix = "" / cap_qual_prefix = ""` root, but that is a codegen/lowering gap this typecheck fix does not address, so it remains open. New non-vacuous RED→GREEN group `entry_mod_qual_erasure` in `test/test_compiler.ml` (8 cases): the three launder shapes + the C2 distinct-tvar variant + the nested-sibling `T.id` shape (all flip clean→rejected), plus three green guards — `Main.id` at a single type stays clean, `Main.id` used polymorphically at Int AND String is RESTORED to clean (RED pre-fix: placeholder pinning over-rejected), and an annotated `a->a` entry fn stays clean. **Full suite: 451 compiler (+8) / 231 eval / 394 codegen (IR-gate 0 failures) / 805 stdlib / 29 snapshots pass, 0 failures** (`test_stdlib_march`'s lone `global_registry` `unbound variable` failure is pre-existing — identical at HEAD without this change).
- ✅ **A single-field ADT defined in a NON-ENTRY module was constructed boxed but tuple-nested-destructured as a newtype — compiled `Bytes.concat` returned an empty `Bytes` (2026-07-08)** — Compiled `Bytes.concat(a, b)` returned an EMPTY `Bytes` (`Bytes.length`/`to_list` = 0) while the interpreter was correct (5); this emptied depot's Postgres wire packets (`Encode.encode(Startup)` builds them via `Bytes.concat`), hanging forgepm's native PG handshake — the actual deploy blocker (distinct from the mono `go`-collision fix above; the pre-diagnosis conflated them). Root cause in `lib/tir/llvm_case.ml` `emit_case`: a type defined in a non-entry module (a nested `mod`, or any MARCH_LIB_PATH library incl. all of stdlib) is registered in `tm_types` under its MODULE-QUALIFIED name (`lower_mod_decls` prepends the prefix → `Bytes.Bytes`), but that module's own value types reference it BARE (`Bytes`) because the typechecker drops the prefix on same-module references — entry-module types are registered bare, so this only bit non-entry types. Construction (`llvm_emit.ml` EAlloc) and top-level patterns resolve the type by the **bare** name (from the `TypeName.CtorName` ctor key) → `repr_of_ty` misses → **Boxed** (which is ALSO what the C runtime uses — `make_bytes_from_raw`/`bytes_to_raw` build/read `Bytes` as a box with the `List(Int)` at offset 16, and crypto/compress/tcp all depend on that). But `emit_case`'s newtype-recovery path — which fires for a TVar-erased tuple-element sub-scrutinee and identified the type by looking up the owning typedef by CTOR name → the **QUALIFIED** registration — classified it `Newtype`. So `match (b1,b2) do (Bytes(xs),Bytes(ys)) -> …` bound `xs` to the BOX POINTER (Newtype identity) instead of projecting the payload field, and the boxed header (tag 0) then read as an empty `Nil`. Entry-module ADTs registered bare → both sides agreed → worked, which is why it was invisible in single-file/entry tests and only surfaced through stdlib `Bytes`. Fix: make the recovery classify the owning type by the **bare** (last dot-segment) name, exactly as construction and the runtime do — so a non-entry single-field type stays consistently **Boxed** (a genuine entry-module newtype is registered bare, so stripping is a no-op and it still classifies `Newtype`). Keeping `Bytes` boxed is required: the runtime constructs and consumes it boxed pervasively (an earlier attempt to reconcile the names toward `Newtype` in `Repr.find_variant` made compiled `Bytes` a raw list, which then mis-read every runtime-constructed `Bytes` — `tcp_recv_exact`'s PG-handshake buffer decoded as an empty `Nil` → `Bytes.get: index out of bounds`). Minimal repros: nested-`mod` single file (`(Wrap(xs),Wrap(ys))` tuple match → `pair=0` compiled pre-fix, `5` post-fix / interp); `/tmp/bytes_probe.march` (`Bytes.concat` → `tolist_len` 0→5). New compile-and-run regression `test/test_codegen.ml` `nonentry_newtype_repr_codegen` (`test_nonentry_newtype_tuple_destructure_compiled`) — a nested `mod` single-field ADT tuple-destructured must print `5` compiled (RED `0` pre-fix). **Full suite: 443 compiler / 231 eval / 393 codegen / 805 stdlib / 29 snapshots pass, 0 failures; property oracle no new divergences; RC benchmarks unchanged; verified against the live Postgres on the deploy droplet (native forgepm clears the handshake).**
- ✅ **Monomorphization resolved a nested `fn`'s call against the top-level `fn_table`, so a user top-level `go`/`loop`/`aux` captured every stdlib nested helper of the same name — compiled tail-recursive list accumulators returned garbage (2026-07-08)** — A user program with a top-level `pfn go(xs, acc)` reversing a list via `Cons(h, acc)` compiled to a binary where `List.length(r)`/`List.sum_int(r)` returned a garbage pointer reinterpreted as an `Int` (observed `len=4745871568`); the interpreter was always correct (`len=3`), an interpreter-correct / compiled-wrong divergence that blocked the native forgepm deploy (its Postgres wire packets are built with `Bytes.concat` → `list_append_go`, a lifted top-level helper — the same collision emptied every startup packet). Root cause in `lib/tir/mono.ml` `rewrite_calls`: the `EApp`/`ECallPtr` callee is resolved by **bare name** against the module-level `fn_table`, but the recursion into `ELetRec`/`ELet`/`ECase` bodies never tracked which names are bound by a lexically-enclosing nested `fn`. March's stdlib uses the conventional helper name `fn go(...)` inside dozens of functions (`List.length`/`reverse`/`map`/`sum_int`/…); each is normally left un-resolved by mono (`fn_table` miss) and lifted to a distinct `go$apply$N` closure by `Defun`. But the moment ANY top-level `go` exists, `fn_table["go"]` hits, and every stdlib helper's nested `go(...)` call is silently rebound to the user's top-level `go` — the callee body is replaced wholesale, so `List.length` ran the user's reverse-accumulator against an `Int` accumulator and returned junk. Confirmed decisive: renaming the user fn `go`→`myrev` made the bug vanish; the buggy `--emit-llvm` showed `List.length`'s helper mangled to `go$List_Int$List_Int` (the user's mangling) with NO distinct length helper, and `go$List_Int$Int` (length's correct name) appeared in **zero** of the 35 dumped phases — the collision is present from `tir-mono` onward. Fix: thread a `shadowed : SSet.t` set of lexically-bound names through `rewrite_calls`; skip the `fn_table` resolution when the callee name is shadowed (leaving it for `Defun`, exactly as when no collision exists). The set accumulates `ELetRec` function names (in the inner bodies + the ELetRec body + — critically for a MONOMORPHIC helper like `sum_int`, whose block-`fn` lowers to `ELet("go", ELetRec([go], AVar go), go(xs,0))` — the continuation, via the `ELet` binder `v`), and `ECase` `br_vars` (constructor-arg pattern binders). Deliberately does NOT seed function *params* — that would short-circuit the intentional `ECallPtr` erased-type interface-dispatch fallback. New compiled-vs-interpreted regression `test/test_codegen.ml` (`nested_fn_name_collision_codegen`): a top-level `go` reversing `[1..5]` then `List.length`/`List.sum_int` on the result must print `5|15` compiled, matching the interpreter — RED pre-fix (`5|5308956944`) / GREEN post-fix. **Full suite: 443 compiler / 231 eval / 393 codegen (+1) / 805 stdlib / 29 snapshots pass, 0 failures; RC benchmarks unchanged (tree_transform=104857600, list_ops=333333666666, binary_trees depth-16 check=131071).**
- ✅ **`alias Long.Path as Short` inside a non-entry module body → undefined-symbol link failure (2026-07-07)** — `forge build` of forgepm (via bastion) failed to link with `Undefined symbols: _PubSub.subscribe / _PubSub.unsubscribe / _PubSub.unsubscribe_all / _PubSub.broadcast_from`, referenced from `IslandSocket.handle_text`/`ws_loop`. bastion's `mod IslandSocket` declares `alias Bastion.PubSub as PubSub` and calls `PubSub.subscribe(...)`; typecheck resolved the alias fine, but codegen emitted the call as `_PubSub.subscribe` while the definition (in `mod Bastion.PubSub`) was emitted as `Bastion.PubSub.subscribe` — the two names never converged. Root cause: TIR lowering resolves module aliases via `_use_aliases` + `resolve_use_alias` (`lib/tir/lower.ml` / `lower_state.ml`), and there IS a top-level `DAlias` handler — but `lower_mod_decls`, which lowers every NON-entry module (auto-discovered MARCH_LIB_PATH files and nested `DMod`s), had **no `DAlias` case** in its inner decl match (it fell into the `_ -> ()` catch-all). So an `alias` at the entry file's own top level resolved correctly, but the identical alias inside any auto-discovered module body was silently dropped. Minimal repro: `mod AcBase.Target do fn answer() do 42 end end` + a separate lib module `mod AcCaller do alias AcBase.Target as T; fn go() do T.answer() end end` + an entry calling `AcCaller.go()` → `_T.answer` undefined; entry-file aliasing of the same module linked fine — the exact entry-vs-lib asymmetry. Fix: added an order-independent module-alias PREFIX table (`_module_aliases`: short name → full path, e.g. `"PubSub" → "Bastion.PubSub"`) populated by `DAlias` in BOTH the top-level and (newly-added) `lower_mod_decls` handlers, plus a fallback in `resolve_use_alias` that rewrites `Short.member → Long.Path.member` by prefix substitution when every exact-name lookup misses. Prefix rewrite is deliberately order-independent (unlike the existing exact-entry approach, which scans `!fns` and therefore only covers aliases whose target module was lowered first — true for the entry file, processed last, but not for a lib module whose target sibling may be lowered afterward). Exact entries still win when present; the prefix table only backstops. New native golden `test/dune` rule + fixtures in `test/alias_codegen/` (`ac_caller.march` is the non-entry aliasing module; compiled with MARCH_LIB_PATH, run, diffed to `42`) — RED pre-fix (`_T.answer` undefined → clang link failure) / GREEN post-fix. Verified end-to-end: forgepm now compiles+links to a native binary (was the last blocker). **Full suite (complete `dune build`): 443 compiler / 231 eval / 391 codegen / 805 stdlib pass, 0 failures.**
- ✅ **`march check`/`forge build` quadratic hang on multi-hundred-file MARCH_LIB_PATH projects (2026-07-07)** — `march check`/`forge build --target ...` on a large multi-repo project (forgepm + bastion + depot + march_doc, ~200 auto-discovered `.march` files) burned 99.9% CPU for 30+ minutes instead of completing in seconds, confirmed non-deadlocked via `sample <pid>` repeatedly showing `List.mem_472 -> caml_c_call -> caml_compare -> compare_val` as the dominant cost. Root cause: `Typecheck.record_use` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`), called on **every single `EVar`** during `infer_expr` (i.e. once per variable reference in the WHOLE combined program — stdlib + every file pulled in via MARCH_LIB_PATH auto-discovery, since `check_module_core` typechecks all of it as one shared `env`), did `List.iter (fun ie -> if ie.ie_matches name then ...) !(env.import_tracker)` — a full linear scan, with each `ie_matches` itself doing a `List.mem`/polymorphic-`=` scan, over `import_tracker`, a list holding ONE ENTRY PER `use`/`import`/`alias` DECLARATION ACROSS THE ENTIRE PROGRAM (never scoped per-file, only ever appended to). That pairing is O(total-var-refs × total-imports) — genuinely quadratic in project size, dominating everything else in the pipeline (parse/desugar/resolve-imports/stdlib-load were all sub-100ms per `--timings`). Fix: index `import_tracker` entries at creation time (the four `ie_matches` construction sites: `DUse`'s `UseAll`/`UseNames`/`UseExcept`, and `DAlias`) into a new `env.import_idx` — two `Hashtbl`s, `ie_exact_index` (every literal name an entry can exact-match: rebound short names, the bare qualified module/alias name itself) and `ie_prefix_index` (keyed by the first-dot-split "prefix root" of a qualified reference, mirroring `split_qualified`'s existing convention elsewhere in this file) — so `record_use` does two O(1)-average Hashtbl lookups instead of an O(n) scan; the prefix-index path still calls the entry's real `ie_matches` closure to disambiguate (defends against same-root-prefix collisions), so semantics are byte-for-byte preserved, not approximated. Verified via a synthetic scaling harness (many auto-generated modules each `import Shared` + several EVar refs, CAS cache cleared between runs so timings are real, not cache hits): 400 files ~1.2s→~0.6s, 1200 ~8.2s→~1.4s (6x), 2000 ~21.1s→~2.3s (9x), 3000 ~45.5s→~3.7s (12x) — pre-fix time fits ~quadratic (k≈5e-6·n²), post-fix is linear. Separately investigated and ruled out as a distinct bug: a cascade of spurious `Unknown module` errors (e.g. `DateTime`, `UUID`, `IOList`, and in some invocations `Config`) observed when scoping down a killed run — traced NOT to `import_tracker`/`record_use` but to `find_stdlib_dir()` (in both `bin/main.ml` and `lib/modules/module_registry.ml`) failing to locate the bundled `stdlib/` directory when `march`'s compiled binary is invoked from a cwd outside its own source tree AND the binary was built via a partial `dune build <specific-targets>` rather than a full build / `@install` (which is what actually copies `stdlib/` under `_build/default/`) — confirmed by reproducing the exact same cascade with the FIX applied but `_build/default/stdlib` absent, and confirming it disappears with a complete build; this is a pre-existing build/packaging rough edge, not a compiler correctness bug, and is out of scope for this fix (noted here for whoever hits it next). New regression test `test/test_compiler.ml` (`resolver` suite, `Slow`): `test_large_multi_file_check_is_not_quadratic` builds a synthetic MARCH_LIB_PATH (2500 auto-discovered modules each importing a shared module and referencing 30 of its functions) and asserts the check completes under 30s — confirmed RED pre-fix (measured 30.78s, matching the calibration) / GREEN post-fix (~3-5s) by temporarily stashing/restoring the fix. **Full suite (complete `dune build`, no partial-target gaps): 429 compiler (+1) / 231 eval / 391 codegen / 805 stdlib pass, 0 failures** — diffed against a throwaway clean baseline worktree off the same `main` commit (428/231/391/805, also 0 failures with a complete build) to confirm zero regressions and isolate the pre-existing `march: cannot find runtime/march_runtime.c` failures (14-15, non-deterministic count) as an unrelated partial-build artifact that disappears with a full build on BOTH branches.
- ✅ **Interpreter `http_server_listen` — single slow/idle client wedged the whole dev server (2026-07-07)** — The OCaml `http_server_listen` builtin (`lib/eval/eval.ml`, used by `forge run` / plain `march file.march`, NOT the compiled/LLVM path) was fully sequential: `select` only watched the *listening* socket, then `accept`ed exactly ONE client and blocked synchronously inside `handle_http_connection`'s `recv`/`send` for that client's entire request-response cycle before accepting the next. A client that opened the TCP connection but delayed sending bytes (e.g. a WebSocket client pausing before its upgrade request during reconnect backoff) left the interpreter's one thread parked in a blocking `recv()`, starving every other connection — confirmed via `sample <pid>` showing the sole thread inside `camlUnix.recv_1225`, with unrelated routes hanging 90+ seconds. Fixed by replacing the accept loop with a single-threaded, non-blocking, multiplexed event loop (`run_http_event_loop` in `lib/eval/eval.ml`), mirroring the same cooperative-scheduling pattern already used for actor mailboxes (`BlockedOnReceive`/`run_scheduler`): every open connection is a small state machine (`HCReadingRequest` accumulating bytes until a full request is parsed via `http_try_parse_request`, then `HCWriting` draining a queued response), and one `Unix.select` per iteration multiplexes the listen socket plus every live client socket — no connection's `recv`/`send` can block progress on any other connection. WebSocket upgrades are unchanged: once a `WebSocketUpgrade` conn is detected, the handshake is written and `handler_fn` still runs synchronously/blocking on that one connection for its lifetime, exactly as before (this was already the pre-fix behavior post-upgrade and is out of scope — only the plain-HTTP accept-and-parse path was non-blocking-ified). `handle_http_connection` and `http_server_spawn_n` (the fork-based N-request test variant) are untouched. Regression test in `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml` (`test_interp_http_server_idle_client_does_not_block_others`, `Slow`): launches the interpreter as a real subprocess, opens an idle TCP connection that never sends a byte, then opens a second connection that sends a complete request and asserts the response arrives within 1s — confirmed to fail (times out empty at the 2s bound) on the pre-fix code and pass post-fix by temporarily stashing/restoring the fix. Out of scope / follow-up: keep-alive (each connection is currently closed after one response, matching prior behavior), chunked transfer-encoding request bodies (not handled by `http_try_parse_request`, matching prior `Content-Length`-only behavior), and partial-write backpressure is now handled (writes queue and drain non-blocking across iterations) but large response bodies under a persistently-full socket buffer haven't been load-tested.
- ✅ **Channel payloads corrupted every odd Int + every Bool compiled (session-types F1/F2, 2026-07-06)** — a single `Chan.send(c, 43)` / `Chan.recv(s)` round-trip returned `43` interpreted but `21` compiled (`v → (v-1)/2`), and Bool flipped `true→false`; even Ints and heap/String payloads passed by luck (even-aligned). Root cause (IR-confirmed): `march_chan_send(ptr %ep, ptr %val)` is declared with a `ptr` payload slot, but `chan_send` had NO dedicated emit arm in `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml` and fell through the general `EApp` path, which passes the Int payload as a raw untagged `i64` (e.g. `43`). Meanwhile `march_chan_recv`'s returned payload goes through the standard erased-i64 CONDITIONAL-UNTAG restore (`ptrtoint`→`and 1`→`select (ashr x,1) x`) — asymmetric: send stores `43` raw, recv sees low-bit-set and `ashr`s → `21`. Fix: add three additive emit arms (`chan_send`/`chan_choose`/`mpst_send`), placed BEFORE the general `EApp` fallthrough, that coerce the payload/label/value arg via `emit_atom_as ctx "ptr"` (`coerce i64→ptr` = `(n<<1)|1`, the exact inverse of recv's conditional-untag; short-circuits to identity for values already `ptr`, so String/record/ADT payloads pass verbatim). Endpoint/role args stay `ptr`; return type mirrors the general path (`Chan` → `ptr`). Because the arms are ADDITIVE and sit ahead of the shared path, `record_put`/`task_await`/every other builtin is untouched by construction. Mirrors the existing `vault_set`/`actor_reply` precedent arms (same void*-round-trip tag bug). Verified interp==compiled for odd Int (43→44 echo), Bool (`true`→TRUE), String (`ping-pong`), and choose/offer atom-label + Bool (`BRANCH-ok-true`). Un-vacuumed the previously-vacuous session tests: `test_session_eval_send_recv` bumped to an odd payload; two new compile-and-run value assertions in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`session_compile` suite: `compiled odd Int payload round-trips (F1)`, `compiled Bool payload round-trips (F2)`) that RUN the compiled binary and check the printed value — both RED on the pre-fix binary (43→10, true→FALSE) / GREEN after. F3 (MPST compiled segfault), F4–F8 remain open (session-types survey findings). **`scripts/run-tests.sh` full six-runner suite GREEN: 426 compiler (+2 session compile-and-run cases) / 231 eval / 391 codegen / 804 stdlib pass; 29 snapshots pass.**
- ✅ **Compiled `Task.await`/`await_many`/`async_stream` returned double-tagged i64 results (2026-07-06)** — found while restoring the `test/apps/actor_stress.march` stress fixture and compiling it natively. The `Result`-returning `Task.await` family left an `Int` `Ok` payload double-tagged: the thunk trampoline stores `task[3] = (apply_ret << 1) | 1`, and for an `Int` the `apply` fn already returns a tagged scalar (`2*n+1`), so `task[3] = 4*n+3`; `march_task_await` (`runtime/march_runtime.c`) wraps `task[3]` straight into `Ok(...)` and the normal `Ok(n)` destructure untags only once, leaving `2*n+1`. Compiled `Task.await(async(fn () -> 6*7))` → `Ok(85)`, `await_many([10,20,30])` → sum `123` (21+41+61), `async_stream` squares-sum → `2×correct+N`; the interpreter was always correct, and `Task.await_unwrap` was already fixed (commit 291f6b5f) but the `Result`-returning paths — all funnelling through the one `task_await` builtin — never got it. Fixed in `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`'s `task_await` case: for a statically-known `i64` `Task` inner type, strip the extra tag from the freshly-allocated `Ok` payload field (offset 16) with one `ashr` (`4*n+3` is always odd → unconditional shift is the exact inverse of the double-tag). Ptr-payload path left byte-identical (verified the String/List task IR carries none of the new instructions) → zero RC risk. New native compiled-run golden `test/native/task_await_int.march` (+ `.expected`, wired in `test/dune`, run under `MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=1`), RED pre-fix (`85/123/115`) / GREEN post-fix (`42/60/55/99`, matching the interpreter). Also restored `test/apps/actor_stress.march` (stale `=`→`:` `init`/record syntax) as a second native golden `native_actor_stress`. **421 compiler / 231 eval / 391 codegen / 804 stdlib pass** (alcotest unchanged; +2 `test/dune` native golden-diff rules).
- ✅ **Cond-form and `when`-guard arms with binary operators failed to parse (2026-07-06)** — found while live-verifying `specs/lang/pattern-matching.md`. Two or more consecutive cond arms (`match do BoolExpr -> body end`) or match-arm guards (`Pattern when GuardExpr -> body`) whose expression used one of `>=`/`<=`/`==`/`!=`/`&&`/`||`/`++`/`|>`/`+`/`*`/`/`/`%` failed to parse: cond `score >= 90 -> "A"` / `score >= 80 -> "B"` errored "I got stuck here" at the 2nd `>=`; guard `x when x == 1 -> …` / `x when x == 0 -> …` errored "I was expecting `end` to close the match here" at the 2nd guard. A single such arm, or arms using strict `<`/`>` (LT/GT), always worked — which is why it went unnoticed. Root cause in `lib/parser/token_filter.ml`'s `lookahead_is_new_arm`: the contextual-newline filter decides whether the tokens after an arm body's NL start a NEW arm (scan reaches a depth-0 `ARROW`) or continue the current body (depth-0 `NL` first), and it *bailed early to "body continuation"* the moment it saw one of a set of binary-operator tokens (`LEQ/GEQ/EQEQ/NEQ/AND/OR/PLUSPLUS/PIPE_ARROW/PLUS/STAR/SLASH/PERCENT`). That heuristic is correct for a plain `Pattern -> body` arm (a bare pattern can never be followed by `>=`), but WRONG where the thing before `->` is a full boolean expression: the cond form (no scrutinee) and a guard's expression. The early-bail fired *before* the scan could reach the same-line `->`, so the second arm got glued onto the first arm's body. Fix: thread a per-match `ms_is_cond` flag (set by peeking one token after `MATCH` — cond iff `DO` immediately follows — carried on a `pending_match_conds` stack popped in lockstep with `pending_match_depths` at the matching `DO`), and within the lookahead track a `seen_when` flag set at a depth-0 `WHEN`. The binary-operator bail is now suppressed when `is_cond || seen_when`, so the scan continues to the same-line `ARROW`; the structural-keyword bails (`EQUALS/DO/LET/IF/MATCH/FN/PFN/ASSERT`, which guard against a spurious `ARROW` from a nested lambda/construct) stay unconditional. Plain scrutinee-match arms (not cond, no guard) are byte-for-byte unchanged. Multi-line arm-body continuations still terminate correctly at the depth-0 `NL` (verified: a `a == 5` statement on a body-continuation line stays in the body, in both plain and cond matches). 6 new parser regression tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`token_filter_cond_guard_operators` suite): 2+ consecutive `>=`/`==`/`<=` cond arms and 2+ consecutive `==`/`>=`/`<=` guards, each asserting the arms stay SEPARATE (correct `ECond`/`EMatch` branch count, not merely that the module parsed), all RED pre-fix (parse error) / GREEN post-fix. `docs/pattern-matching.md`'s own Cond/Guards examples (which showed the clean paren-free form and thus previously did not parse) now compile and run correctly. **406 compiler (+6) / 230 eval / 389 codegen / 804 stdlib / 29 snapshots pass.**
- ✅ **Compiled `println(:atom)` / `show(atom)` — link failure + typecheck gap for `Show(Atom)` (2026-07-05)** — `println(:ok)` ran fine interpreted (`VAtom a -> ":" ^ a`) but failed to LINK compiled (`Undefined symbols: "_show", referenced from _march_main / _println$Atom`): `Atom` was absent from BOTH `lib/tir/lower.ml`'s builtin `Show` injection (`show_specs`) and `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`'s `builtin_impls`, so a `show(atom)` call resolved to a bare, undefined `show` symbol. Same class as the tuple/`None` `_show` link failures (P1 below) but for atoms. Atoms compile to nameless FNV-1a i64 hashes (`Llvm_ctx.atom_hash`), so `Show$Atom.show` cannot reconstruct `:name` from the runtime value — the fix collects every atom `(hash, name)` seen during codegen (`emit_atom` + `emit_case`, into a new `ctx.atom_names`) and emits a generated `@march_atom_to_string(i64)` switch (returning `march_string_lit(":name")`, mirroring `march_int_to_string`'s RC shape) at module finalization via `Llvm_toplevel.emit_atom_show_table`, gated on the call actually appearing in the emitted IR (robust to the `atom_to_string` body being inlined). Emitted into `ctx.extra_fns` so BOTH the AOT (`emit_module`) and JIT/REPL (`llvm_repl.ml`, all five emitters) finalizers define the symbol in-module — JIT fragments are compiled standalone, so a call with no in-module definition is a clang error. Also added `atom_to_string` to `lib/tir/defun.ml`'s `builtin_names` (else it's treated as an unknown free var → `ECallPtr`, which leaf-detection flags non-leaf → a spurious reduction check in `Show$Atom.show`, breaking `phase4_reduction_codegen` "all-leaf module"). 2 new compiled-parity regression tests in `test/test_codegen.ml` (`iface_impl_mono_codegen` suite): `println(:ok)` and multi-atom `show(:hello)++show(:world_123)`, both RED pre-fix (link failure) / GREEN post-fix, verified interp == compiled; plus a `Slow` REPL/JIT parity test `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml` (`repl_compiler_parity` "atom show", `show(:ok)`/`show(:hello_world)`/`show(:ok)++show(:err)`) pinning the JIT-fragment path that regressed to an undefined `@march_atom_to_string` during the fix. **400 compiler / 230 eval / 387 codegen (+2) / 804 stdlib (+1) / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots pass; generated IR verified clean by `opt -passes=verify`.**
- ✅ **`float_to_string` interpreter-vs-compiled divergence on whole-number Floats (2026-07-05)** — surfaced while writing golden conformance programs for `specs/lang/core-march.md` (Core March spec). The same source `float_to_string(1.0)` printed **three different strings** across backends: `1.` interpreted (`eval.ml` OCaml `string_of_float`, the declared reference semantics), `1` compiled (`runtime/march_runtime.c` used C `%g`, which drops a bare `.0` AND caps at 6 sig-figs), and `1.0` wasm (`runtime/march_runtime_wasm.c`'s hand-rolled formatter). JS (`runtime/march_runtime.mjs`, `toPrecision(6)`) gave `1`. Beyond whole numbers this was a full **precision** divergence too — `float_to_string(0.123456789)` was `0.123456789` interpreted vs `0.123457` compiled (12- vs 6-sig-fig). Decision: **match the reference** (§0/§1 of the spec: `eval.ml` IS the reference, and the golden oracle's contract is compiled == interpreter), i.e. OCaml-style `1.`, rather than changing the interpreter to a conventional `1.0` (which would mutate the reference and every doctest depending on it). Fix reproduces `string_of_float` exactly = `valid_float_lexem (format_float "%.12g" f)`: `runtime/march_runtime.c` now `snprintf("%.12g")` + appends `.` when every char is a digit/`-` (fixes whole-number AND precision divergence, byte-identical to interp); `runtime/march_runtime_wasm.c` trims all trailing fractional zeros to the bare `.` (`1.0`→`1.`; freestanding 6-decimal precision cap for fractional values is a documented deferral); `runtime/march_runtime.mjs` mirrors via `toPrecision(12)` + trailing-dot rule (extreme-exponent fixed-vs-exp notation edge deferred). The REPL/JIT value-display formatters (`lib/jit/repl_jit.ml`'s two `%g` sites) are a distinct value-inspector surface (not the `float_to_string` builtin; pinned by `test/repl_smoke_test.sh`) and are intentionally left — noted as a remaining related inconsistency. Differential test: new golden `specs/lang/golden/g09_float_show.march` (auto-discovered by BOTH `specs/lang/golden/verify.sh` and the `@oracle` sweep `test/test_oracle.ml`), RED before / GREEN after (`9/9` golden match; oracle `g09` MATCH, 0 un-triaged failures). `march_value_to_string` (generic `to_string`) has no float branch — the builtin path funnels solely through `@march_float_to_string`, so this one symbol was the whole compiled surface. `specs/lang/core-march.md` §5 updated (8→9 golden). **400 compiler / 230 eval / 385 codegen / 803 stdlib pass; golden 9/9; oracle 0 un-triaged failures.**

pinned fallbacks if offline) so the soname/ABI matches `debian:bookworm-slim` (`libssl.so.3`/`libcrypto.so.3`/`libz.so.1`), and copies the multiarch `openssl/opensslconf.h` (Debian ships it under `usr/include/<multiarch>/openssl`, not `usr/include/openssl`). **Compiler** (`bin/main.ml`): a `cross_sysroot_dir` resolver (env override `MARCH_CROSS_SYSROOT_<ARCH>`/`MARCH_CROSS_SYSROOT` → cache) with a clear actionable error on cache-miss (names the fetch script;
