- ✅ **Perceus RC use-after-free on cross-module opaque types** — a value whose concrete type isn't propagated across a module boundary (e.g. `let gate = Gate.cast(...)` where `Gate` is an opaque type from another module) keeps an unresolved type-var `'_NNNN` in monomorphic TIR. `needs_rc (TVar _)` returned `false` ("skip RC"), so Perceus never emitted an `EIncRC` for such a heap value; when the binding was consumed twice (e.g. two `Gate.get_change(gate, …)` calls) the first consume freed the box and the second double-freed it (`RC underflow in march_decrc_freed`, bastion `Gate.cast` test). Fix: `needs_rc (TVar _) = true` (`lib/tir/perceus.ml`) — `llvm_ty (TVar _) = "ptr"`, so the value is a heap pointer and must be RC-managed; safe for genuine scalars because RC ops are guarded by `if ty = "ptr"` in llvm_emit and `IS_HEAP_PTR` in the runtime. Mirrors the earlier `TFn` fix. Regression test: `perceus` group "incrc for unresolved-tvar value used twice (cross-module opaque)" in `test/test_march.ml`.

## P1 — High Impact / Near-Term

- [ ] **Actor scheduler has ≥2 unbounded busy-spins that can peg a core at ~100% CPU forever under heavy host oversubscription — NOT live-confirmed, strong hypothesis only (investigated 2026-07-23).** Found while chasing why `test_erased_option_niche_fbip_no_underflow_compiled` (`test/test_codegen.ml:7668`, binary `erasedoptbin`) was observed hung for 3+ hours on a dev machine running several concurrent build/test sessions. `task_wait_done`'s in-scheduler branch (`runtime/march_runtime.c:1985`, what `task_await`/`task_await_unwrap` call) has **no timeout at all** — `while (task[4]==0) { march_sched_yield(); }` — unlike `Actor.call`'s own timed-wait path (`runtime/march_runtime.c:2340-2377`), which correctly bounds itself against `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`. `march_sched_wake`'s `PROC_PARKED` wait (`runtime/march_scheduler.c:1306`) is a second, tighter unbounded spin, justified in-comment as "O(1), extremely short" — true only if the target proc's OS thread is actually scheduled promptly, which isn't guaranteed under oversubscription (each compiled process spawns ~`nproc` scheduler OS threads via `MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS`; several concurrent march processes on one box easily oversubscribes real cores). Once either spin stalls, it adds CPU pressure that plausibly worsens the very starvation that caused it — a self-reinforcing pileup consistent with the multi-hour persistence and with a *different* test binary (`sanexit_bin`) independently observed stuck the same way. `march_sched_wait_idle` (`runtime/march_scheduler.c:1116-1148`) has the same shape but wasn't reached by this repro. **Not reproduced live**: ~160 attempts (200 sequential runs, then ~9 batches of 8 concurrent runs each with a 6s-grace lldb-attach watcher) all completed cleanly — this needs either a live capture or a careful structural fix mirroring `Actor.call`'s wall-clock-deadline pattern without changing `task_await`'s documented wait-forever semantics. Full writeup + reproduction recipe: memory `project_scheduler_unbounded_spin_hangs` (if accessible) or ask for the standalone fix-agent prompt drafted alongside this entry.

- ✅ **FQN dispatch identity — full `ci_module.Type.Ctor` constructor identity COMPLETE (unblocks same-ctor-name double collisions; flag-day 2026-07-22).** The earlier FQN dispatch-identity flag-day (Stages 1-3, 2026-07-21) let two same-short-name types in different modules each implement ANY interface and dispatch correctly in both backends — *provided their constructor NAME sets were disjoint*. When they ALSO share a constructor name (e.g. both `type Thing = Shared | …`), dispatch identity keys on the BARE ctor name (`env.ctors` is bare-keyed), so the value cannot be routed to the right impl. **Task 1 (2026-07-21, this plan) landed:** `add_ctor`'s structural dedup now also compares `ci_module`, so two different modules' identically-shaped ctors (e.g. both a nullary `Shared`) no longer collapse onto one candidate — `env.ctors "Shared"` now retains BOTH declaring modules' `ctor_info`s. This is bookkeeping only: `ci_module` still feeds NO codegen/mangling/dispatch. **Task 2 (2026-07-21, this plan) landed:** constructor RESOLUTION now consumes those retained candidates — `lookup_ctor`/`lookup_ctor_in_type` prefer the candidate whose `ci_module` matches the reference's own lexical current module (instead of "first in the list"), and a bare reference whose candidates span more than one declaring module, with the current module owning none of them, is now a hard `Err.error` (new helper `all_ctor_candidates_named`) instead of silently picking an arbitrary candidate — see `specs/progress.md`. Resolution is now correct and safe, but STILL bookkeeping-only for codegen/mangling/runtime dispatch: this item stays open until a later task in the plan gives constructors a full `ci_module.Type.Ctor`-qualified identity that actually threads through lowering so the double-collision `impl` shape below can be ACCEPTED instead of rejected. **Current stopgap (Task 6b):** `register_impl_shape` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`) REJECTS this specific double-collision shape at typecheck via a ctor-set-disjointness check (safe compile error — `reject/t82_impl_coherence_shared_ctor_double_collision`) rather than silently misdispatching. **NARROWER-THAN-IDEAL SCOPE (final-review note):** the stopgap only reliably rejects 1-level-nested double collisions. For a type nested 2+ modules deep, the disjointness check compares `ci_module` (the FULL dotted prefix, e.g. `"A.B"`) against `decl_module` (only the immediate segment threaded to `register_impl_shape`, e.g. `"B"`), so it finds no module-qualified ctor keys → computes an EMPTY ctor set → the two types look "disjoint" → coherence is RELAXED → that specific (rare) 2+-level double-collision shape would still silently misdispatch. This is false-negative-only (it never falsely REJECTS the common distinct-ctor-name case), so the plan's actual deliverable carries no correctness risk; the real `ci_module.Type.Ctor` fix below closes it. **The real fix** is to give constructors a `ci_module.Type.Ctor`-qualified identity that threads through lowering/mangling/the runtime tag-switch dispatch fn and the interpreter's `iface_method_tbl`, so the two `Shared` ctors get distinct dispatch tags and the double-collision programs actually WORK instead of being rejected. Then flip `reject/t82` to an accept fixture. Design sketch: `specs/plans/2026-07-20-fqn-impl-dispatch-identity.md` ("Residual, documented"); related ctor-identity groundwork `specs/plans/2026-07-17-fqn-type-ctor-identity.md`. **Task 3/4 (native, this plan) landed:** `ECon` lowering and branch-tag lowering in `lib/tir/lower.ml` module-qualify a colliding, shared-ctor-name constructor's global tag via `Lower_state.env`'s `mod_prefix`/`collision_set` fields, both at construction and at pattern-match, so the native backend's double-collision programs now dispatch correctly instead of needing the Task 6b stopgap. **Task 5 (interpreter, this plan) landed:** the interpreter's `VCon` tag IS its entire runtime identity (no separate integer discriminant like native), so `ECon` evaluation and `match_pattern`'s `PatCon` arm now module-qualify a colliding, shared-ctor-name tag as `"<module>.<type>.<ctor>"` (e.g. `"DcA.Thing.Shared"`), collision-conditional (byte-identical bare tag otherwise). Because `module_stack`/`current_doc_prefix` reflect only the single eager upfront `eval_decl` walk (stale by the time a DEFERRED closure body — the common case for any `fn`/`impl` method actually called later — runs), `VClosure` now carries a 4th field: the lexical module prefix captured at closure-CONSTRUCTION time, restored as an ambient `closure_prefix_override` for the duration of that closure's body (`apply_inner`, exception-safe) — this is also how `match_pattern` (a pure function with no `env`/module-context parameter) gets the right qualifying prefix with NO signature change, reading the same global. Register_type_ctors also registers the qualified tag into `ctor_type_tbl`/`ctor_qualified_type_tbl` so `dispatch_type_name_of_value` (general-interface dispatch) still resolves a qualified-tag value. Two additional, narrower-than-`type_collision_set` gates were needed after a full-suite regression sweep found real false positives: (a) only PUBLIC (`type`, not `ptype`) candidates qualify — `stdlib/seq.march` and `stdlib/file.march` each independently declare `ptype Seq(a) = Seq(a)` as a deliberate structural-interop redeclaration (`File.with_lines`'s callback constructs a `File.Seq` fed through `Seq.map`/`Seq.to_list`), not a genuine ambiguity; (b) the short name must ALSO have at least one `impl` block anywhere in the program — `bin/main.exe`'s auto-loaded stdlib prelude means a user's own impl-less marker type (e.g. an MPST test's `type Server = Server` role token) routinely collides BY NAME ALONE with an unrelated stdlib type (`stdlib/http_server.march`'s own `type Server = Server(...)`), and MPST's runtime resolves role names by reading a `VCon` tag as a raw string key, which qualification broke. **Task 5.5 (native, this plan, 2026-07-22) landed:** native's Tasks 3/4 had the SAME over-broad bug the interpreter's Task 5 fixed — they qualified ANY `Collision_set.is_colliding` short name with no visibility / impl-presence filter, breaking the `stdlib/seq.march`+`stdlib/file.march` `ptype Seq(a) = Seq(a)` structural-interop hand-off (confirmed: HEAD compiler `panic: non-exhaustive pattern match`, fixed compiler prints `6`). Fixed by a new narrow `Lower_state.shared_ctor_collision_tbl` (populated by `compute_shared_ctor_collisions`, same PUBLIC-only + impl-presence filters as `eval.ml`'s `compute_type_collision_set`) consulted ONLY by Tasks 3/4's two gates; the broad `env.collision_set` (Task 1/2, impl-symbol qualification) is untouched. Stages 2 (interp) / 3 (native, narrowed by Task 5.5) landed. **Task 6 (flag-day, 2026-07-22, this plan) landed — item COMPLETE:** now that both backends resolve and dispatch the shared-ctor-name double-collision shape correctly, `register_impl_shape` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`) drops BOTH the Task-6b `ctor_sets_disjoint` stopgap AND Task 0's `MARCH_DEV_RELAX_CTOR_COHERENCE` dev harness together — the declaring-module coherence relaxation is now sound unconditionally, no ctor-sharing carve-out. Fixture `reject/t82_impl_coherence_shared_ctor_double_collision` flipped to `accept/t90_impl_coherence_shared_ctor_double_collision` (types corpus now 90 accept / 81 reject). ### Compiler (found while building the Canvas 2D stdlib API, 2026-07-09)

- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15, open-items plan Phase 3.2) — a zero-arg lambda `fn -> body` now satisfies a declared `Unit -> Unit` callback param (the real fix; the earlier `Int -> Unit` workaround at the Done entry below is REVERTED).** Two symmetric halves fixed in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`: (a) `check_expr`'s `ELam` peel accepts a 0-arg lambda checked against `Unit -> T` as a unit-consuming thunk (checks the body against the arrow's result); (b) `infer_app` applies an implicit unit when an empty-parens call `f()` (idx 0) hits a `Unit -> T` value, yielding `T` (the `idx=0` guard preserves partial applications like `g(x)` on `Int -> Unit -> T` — this also fixed `Unit -> T` builtins like `int_max_value()`). The bare-thunk inference path (no expected arrow) is untouched, so `task_spawn(fn -> …)` still works. `stdlib/dom.march`'s Dom callbacks reverted from `Int -> Unit` back to `Unit -> Unit` (docs now say pass `fn -> …`), `runtime/march_dom.mjs` comment updated. Tests: 3 `--check` cases in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`zero_arg_unit_callback`) + a native compile-and-run parity fixture (`test/native/unit_callback_zero_arg.march`), all RED pre-fix / GREEN post-fix across interp/js/native. ORIGINAL FINDING (`task_f422fd93`): `stdlib/dom.march` declares all three callbacks as `cb: Unit -> Unit`. Per `specs/lang/core-march-types.md`'s T-Abs rule, a zero-arg lambda `fn -> body` typechecks to its BODY's result type directly (no arrow wrapper — a "thunk", matching the comment in `test/native/zero_arg_closure_default.march`: "A zero-arg lambda `fn () -> T` is typed as a thunk `T` (its result), not a function"), so it can never unify with an explicitly-declared `Unit -> Unit` arrow type. Minimal repro (typechecks standalone, no Dom/Canvas involved): `fn call_it(cb: Unit -> Unit) : Unit do cb() end` called as `call_it(fn -> once())` fails both at `cb()` ("expected `()` but got `() -> ()`... Did you forget to apply it to its arguments?") and at the call site ("expected `() -> ()` but got `()`... A function was expected here"). At the JS runtime boundary (`runtime/march_dom.mjs`) the callback is invoked as `cb._0(cb)` — genuinely zero additional args — so the ABI does expect a real 0-arg closure; the extern's declared TYPE is simply the wrong shape for what a 0-arg lambda actually produces. No existing test or demo previously called these three functions from March source, so the bug was latent/unnoticed. Discovered building `demo_app/canvas_demo/`, which had to drop its originally-planned `Dom.on_frame` animation loop in favor of a static scene as a result. Fix needs either a typechecker special-case for bidirectional-checking a 0-arg `ELam` against a declared arrow type, or a different (possibly compiler-supported) type spelling for "0-arg closure parameter, later force-called via `cb()`" — see the spawned task for the full investigation brief.

ONLY nested-`PatTuple`-in-block-`let` breaks — so the bug is in the `ELet`/`EBlock` pattern-destructuring lowering path (`lib/tir/lower.ml`), which appears to emit a reference to an inner sub-pattern variable (`a`) without binding it, unlike the `match_pattern`/`EMatch` lowering (which recurses into nested sub-patterns correctly). The golden corpus keeps `g16_tuple_nested.march` on the `match` form to stay green; a nested-tuple-in-`let` golden program should be added once fixed. - ✅ **VERIFIED FIXED 2026-07-17 (already resolved; regression-locked): `>=`/`<=` as an ECond arm condition.** No longer reproducible — a scrutinee-less `match do s >= 90 -> ... s <= 0 -> ... end` parses AND runs correctly on both backends (interp == compiled). The token-filter arm-boundary lookahead now handles the two-char `>=`/`<=` operators before the next arm's `->`. Regression-locked: grammar `parse/p26_cond_arm_ge_le.march` (value-witness, prints A/B/Z/F). Stale note in `golden/g31_cond_middle_arm` corrected. Original diagnosis: **`>=`/`<=` as an `ECond` (scrutinee-less `match do`) arm condition fails to parse.** Found by the Core March golden corpus (Phase 1 Task 7, conditionals). In a `match do cond -> body … end` boolean chain, an arm whose condition uses `>=` or `<=` (e.g. `s >= 90 -> …`) is a parse error, while `>` / `<` (e.g. `s > 89 -> …`) parse fine. Root cause is in the token filter's arm-boundary lookahead (the `->`-scan distinguishing arm boundaries from block continuations gets stuck on the two-char `>=`/`<=` operator before the next arm's `->`). Interpreter and compiler are both unaffected once it parses — a pure front-end (lexer/token-filter) limitation, not a semantics divergence. Workaround: use `>`/`<` with an adjusted threshold. Lower severity (clean workaround) but a real surface-syntax gap worth a token-filter fix.

The token-filter lookahead gap was closed. Stale open marker cleared. ~~`stdlib/global_registry.march:101` — inline `match` as a lambda body in a call argument is a PARSE ERROR, making `GlobalRegistry` unavailable (surfaced 2026-07-08 by the prebind-fix adversarial review; NOT introduced by that fix).** `List.map(kept, fn (kv) -> match kv do (n, _e) -> n end)` — a `fn ... -> match ... do ... end` lambda body used directly as a call argument — fails to `--check`/parse (`-- ERROR -- stdlib/global_registry.march 101 | List.map(kept, fn (kv) -> match kv do (n, _e) -> n end)`). Same token-filter arm-boundary-lookahead limitation class as the `>=`/`<=` finding above and the `match`-RHS/with-binding notes elsewhere: an inline `match` whose arms are newline/paren-delimited inside a lambda inside a call-arg confuses the arm-boundary scan. This is the REAL cause of the long-standing `test_stdlib_march` `global_registry` group failure (18/18 unbound `GlobalRegistry.*`) — the module never parses, so none of its members bind, not a "module-resolution issue" as the 2026-07-06 "Multi-arm `with ... else`" Done entry provisionally guessed. Workaround: bind the `match` to a `let` and return the bound name, or hoist the projection to a named helper `fn` (the parser accepts a `match` as a top-level fn body). Pre-existing; a token-filter fix (or the stdlib workaround) closes it. Not fixed in the prebind-fix batch (out of scope).

### Compiler (found during Core March language-spec typing track, 2026-07-05)

- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-05, commit `f0f5299c`) — `let`-binding type annotations (`let x : T = e`) are parsed but never enforced by the typechecker.** Fix in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`: new helper `infer_let_annotated` (used at both `infer_block`'s `ELet` arm and the tail-position `ELet` arm) resolves `bind_ty` via `surface_ty` and CHECKs the RHS against it with `check_expr` (a proper checking context, so a polymorphic RHS bound at a more specific instance still works, e.g. `let f : (Int) -> Int = fn x -> x`). The annotation is resolved into a scratch error context first; if `surface_ty` can't express it (e.g. a phantom/typestate tag `Handle(Open)` where `Open` is a data constructor, not a type name), it falls back to plain inference — preserving the pre-fix behaviour for grammar-inexpressible annotations so no legitimate program (e.g. the `tag_and_typestate` tests) starts being rejected. Corpus: `reject/t16_let_annot_mismatch` (`let x : Int = "foo"` rejected) + `accept/t21_let_annot_ok`. Unit tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`let_annotations` group). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §4.1 finding 16 (marked RESOLVED). ORIGINAL FINDING: Found by the Core March typing corpus (typing Task 2, tuples/records). The parser accepts a type annotation on a `let` binding and stores it as `Ast.bind_ty`, but `typecheck.ml` never consulted it — `grep -c bind_ty lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml` = 0. The binding's type is fully *inferred* from the RHS and the annotation is silently discarded, so `let x : Int = "foo"` and `let pair : (Int, Int) = (1, 2, 3)` both `--check` at exit 0 (independently confirmed by the typing-Task-2 implementer and reviewer). This is **not a soundness hole** — the inferred type still governs, so a later *use* of `x` at the annotated-but-wrong type is still caught; the annotation is merely decorative rather than a checking context. Lower severity (no miscompile, no crash), but a real enforcement/ergonomics gap: a programmer writing `let x : Int = compute()` reasonably expects the annotation to *check* the RHS against `Int` (a `check_expr env e (surface_ty bind_ty)` at the `ELet` arm, `typecheck.ml` ~:4293), and an annotation that documents-but-doesn't-verify is a footgun. The typing corpus routes around it — the tuple-arity reject (`specs/lang/types/reject/t08_tuple_arity_mismatch.march`) uses a *function-parameter* annotation (which IS enforced via param-vs-arg unification) rather than a `let` annotation to elicit the mismatch. Fix: at the `ELet` arm, when `bind_ty` is present, check the RHS against it (`check_expr`) instead of (or in addition to) inferring, and unify the pattern against the annotated type. A typing-corpus `reject/` program pinning `let x : Int = "foo"` should be added once this is enforced.
- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-05, commit `8cbd6dd2`) — An explicit `when Interface(a)` bound on a generic function parameter is not re-checked at call sites — only enforced when it happens to be violated at the function's OWN declaration (SOUNDNESS bug).** ROOT CAUSE (pinned this task): in `check_fn`'s `when`-clause processing, the constraint argument `a` in `when Eq(a)` was resolved ONLY against `fn_tvars` (signature type-variable names). For an UNANNOTATED value parameter named `a`, `fn_tvars` has no `"a"` entry, so the code minted a FRESH, disconnected placeholder var and attached `CInterface("Eq", …)` to THAT — a variable never unified with the parameter's actual type. The constraint therefore rode on a phantom var: `generalize` quantified it away, and at each call site `instantiate` substituted it with an independent fresh var that never bound to the argument type, so `discharge_constraints` always saw an `Unbound` TVar and skipped it ("still polymorphic"). FIX (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`): when the `when`-clause argument name is not a signature type var, resolve it against the value-parameter binding in `body_env` (`lookup_var`) and attach the constraint to the parameter's own type variable; it then survives generalization onto the scheme, rides through `instantiate` onto the caller's `pending_constraints`, and is discharged at the call site. Falls back to a fresh registered placeholder only when the name is neither a signature type var nor a bound value. SAFETY VALVE verified: bug now rejects (`` `Hue` does not implement interface `Eq`. ``); satisfiable generic constraints still accept interpreted AND compiled (`max(1,2)→2`, `same(1,1)`, `same("x","y")`); unconstrained generics unaffected; full fast suite (408 compiler / 230 eval) + types corpus (39/39) green. NOTE: user-defined `impl Eq`/`derive Eq` on a locally-shadowed ADT name (e.g. `impl Eq(Color)` for a module-local `Color`) is a SEPARATE pre-existing limitation (app-type-namespace collision — `expected \`Color\` but got \`Color\``) that already rejected before this fix and is out of scope. Corpus: `reject/t17_generic_when_constraint_unsatisfied` + `accept/t22_generic_when_constraint_satisfied`. Unit tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`generic_when_constraints` group). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §4.1 finding 15 (marked RESOLVED). ORIGINAL FINDING: Found by the Core March typing corpus (typing Task 6, interface constraints). Repro: `fn same(a, b) when Eq(a) do a == b end` (params left UNANNOTATED, so `a` stays a generic type variable at `same`'s own declaration) then `same(Rood, Rood)`, where `Rood` is a variant of a bare ADT `type Hue = Rood | Bloo` with no `impl Eq(Hue)`, **typechecks at exit 0** — even though a direct `Rood == Rood` (bypassing the `same` wrapper) correctly rejects with `` `Hue` does not implement interface `Eq`. `` Contrast: `fn same(a : Hue, b : Hue) when Eq(a) do a == b end` (params CONCRETELY annotated) correctly rejects at `same`'s own declaration with the identical message — so the constraint is genuinely attached to `same`'s scheme (`check_fn`'s `all_constraints` branch, `typecheck.ml:4752–4757`, folds the `when`-clause's `CInterface` into the returned `Poly` scheme when the type variable isn't otherwise resolved) but is not re-verified when `instantiate` (`typecheck.ml:901–937`) substitutes a concrete type in for that quantified variable at a later call site and pushes the freshly-instantiated constraint onto the caller's `env.pending_constraints` — the caller's own `discharge_constraints` call (`typecheck.ml:4932–5049`) should then see and reject `CInterface("Eq", Hue)`, and does not. Root cause not pinned down (docs-only task, `typecheck.ml` unmodified): likely implicates `generalize`'s fresh-isolated-ref-per-quantified-id copy (`typecheck.ml:845–895`, esp. :866–869) interacting with the ORIGINAL constraint-bearing `TVar` ref captured earlier while processing the `when`-clause (`typecheck.ml:4687–4712`) — both share an integer id (which `instantiate`'s `List.assoc_opt id subst`, :915, keys on), so in principle the constraint should still resolve correctly; something breaks that between the immediate-declaration path (works) and the deferred generic-call path (silently drops). Reproduces identically for a plain ADT value and (separately confirmed) is not `TArrow`/function-value-specific. This is a genuine, if narrow, typechecker SOUNDNESS gap for user-declared `when`-bounds specifically (the four BUILT-IN interface constraints arising from `+`/`==`/`<`/`show` themselves are unaffected — those are always checked at THEIR OWN enclosing declaration, never re-instantiated through an intermediate user-defined polymorphic wrapper function the way `same` is here). Full live-verified repro and analysis in `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §4 finding 15.

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — interfaces/impls declaration checking, Task 4, 2026-07-06)

- ✅ **STAGE 1+2 LANDED 2026-07-17: impl-coherence — overlapping user-vs-user impls (exact AND parametric) are now rejected at declaration (T-ImplCoherent).** `register_impl_shape` (`typecheck.ml`) does a lookup-before-insert keyed on an alpha-normalized structural key (`canonical_impl_key`) of the impl head: a SECOND impl whose head is alpha-equal to an already-registered USER impl for the same interface is a compile error citing the first. `env.impls` now carries the decl span (`(ty * Ast.span) list`) so re-registration across passes (same span) is distinguished from a genuine duplicate (different span). Witnesses: `reject/t79_impl_coherence_duplicate` (two `impl Speak(Dog)`), `accept/t83_impl_distinct_types`, `accept/t84_impl_distinct_ifaces`. Suite green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 29 / stdlib 809 / types 163). **Deferred to follow-ons (empirically-motivated):** DECIDE-1 (reject a user impl OVERLAPPING a built-in, e.g. `impl Eq(Int)`) — built-ins are seeded into `env.impls` with `dummy_span` and SKIPPED by the check, because 6 interface-machinery test fixtures legitimately re-impl builtins on primitives; enabling the builtin-overlap error is its own change + test migration. DECIDE-3 (orphan rule) still blocked on the flat namespace. Stage 2 (parametric unifiability overlap, `List(a)` vs `List(Int)`) is DONE via `types_overlap` (witnesses `reject/t85`, `accept/t86`; corpus gate found zero legitimate overlaps). Original spec + status: **No impl-coherence check: overlapping impls of the same interface for the same type are silently accepted, and the interpreter/compiled backends disagree — deterministically, but DIFFERENTLY — on which impl's method body runs.** **SPEC'D (2026-07-17): `specs/plans/2026-07-17-interface-impl-coherence.md`** — a design + staged implementation plan that resolves the open §4.4.3 divergence via **coherence** (≤1 impl per `(interface, type-head)`, reject overlaps at declaration) rather than a shared selection policy. Grounds the fix at `register_impl_shape` (`typecheck.ml:5788`, the unconditional prepend), identifies the backend split (interp `impl_tbl` Hashtbl last-write-wins vs compiled mono), measures ZERO stdlib blast radius, stages exact-overlap (Task 1-4) then unifiability (Task 5-6), and calls out three sub-decisions (builtin override, derive-vs-manual, orphan rule — the last blocked on the same flat namespace as linear L4). Ready to execute. Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march.md` §4.4.3 (the "Known divergence: impl coherence" subsection) and `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.3's `(T-Impl)` step 1 note, widening the interface/impl declaration-checking reference (`.superpowers/sdd/interface-impl-survey.md` §4, findings D1–D3). `env.impls : ty list StrMap.t` (`typecheck.ml:455`) registers every impl by unconditional prepend (`typecheck.ml:7081`–`7084`) with no lookup-before-insert step anywhere in `(T-Impl)`'s ordered checks — two `impl Speak(Dog)` blocks for the identical `(interface, type)` pair both typecheck with **no diagnostic of any kind** (confirmed live, `--check` exit 0, only unrelated "unused variable `self`" warnings).

  **Minimal repro** (confirmed live this task, both backends, 2 runs each for determinism):
  ```march
  mod M do
    interface Speak(a) do
      fn speak : a -> String
    end

    type Dog = Dog(String)

    impl Speak(Dog) do
      fn speak(self) do
        "FIRST"
      end
    end

    impl Speak(Dog) do
      fn speak(self) do
        "SECOND"
      end
    end

    fn main() do
      println(speak(Dog("Rex")))
    end
  end
  ```
  ```
  $ march --check file.march        # exit 0, both backends' shared typechecker accepts
  $ march file.march                # interpreted: SECOND
  $ march --compile -o /tmp/ovl file.march && /tmp/ovl   # compiled: FIRST
  ```

  **Root cause, both selection sites cited live:**
  - Interpreter (last-registered wins): `DImpl`'s eval handler does `Hashtbl.replace impl_tbl (idef.impl_iface.txt, type_name) fn_val` (`lib/eval/eval.ml:8324`, mirrored at the letrec-style path `lib/eval/eval.ml:8640`); for a user interface (not on the `Show`/`Eq`/`Ord`/`Hash` allowlist) the real effect is the adjacent ordinary `env`-binding branch (`eval.ml:8309`–`8311`) prepending a fresh `("speak", v)` binding per impl, so ordinary lexical "first binding in `ρ` wins" scoping resolves to whichever impl was declared LAST (closest to the front).
  - Compiled backend (first-registered wins): TIR lowering's `collect_iface_impls` (`lib/tir/lower.ml:1005`–`1014`) reads `already = List.mem_assoc type_name l` against the accumulating dispatch table BEFORE registering, and only lowers/registers `if not already` (`lib/tir/lower.ml:1014`) — the FIRST impl for a given `(iface, type)` claims the slot; every subsequent overlapping impl is silently skipped.

  Confirmed the same divergence holds for **generic-vs-specific overlap** (`impl Speak(Box(a))` + `impl Speak(Box(Int))`, called on `Box(42)`: interpreted `"int box"`, compiled `"generic box"` — whichever backend "looks right" is accidental, since neither implements real specificity resolution) and **derive-vs-manual overlap** (`derive Show, Eq for Color` + hand-written `impl Eq(Color) do fn eq(a,b) do true end end`, `Red == Blue`: interpreted `true`, compiled `false`).

  **This is an OPEN divergence, deliberately left unfixed by the documentation slice that found it** — unlike `core-march.md` §4.2.1's `ERecordUpdate` case (investigated, adjudicated, and CONVERGED; its todos entry is closed), there is no clearly-normative backend to converge on here. Fixing this requires an actual language-design decision: add a coherence/overlap-rejection check at `impl` declaration time (Rust-style), define one deterministic selection policy shared by both backends (e.g. always-first or always-last, formalized rather than incidental), or embrace intentionally-overlapping instances with an explicit specificity order (Haskell `OverlappingInstances`-style) — each a real design trade-off (e.g. backward compatibility with any code, such as test-mocking patterns, that happens to rely on the interpreter's current last-wins behavior). Filed here in the same spirit as the existing open `hash()`/`to_string` cross-backend entries above and `test/test_oracle.ml`'s `known_divergence` list (`test/test_oracle.ml:138`–`174`) — pinned and tracked, not silently fixed or hidden. Deliberately NOT added to `specs/lang/types/{accept,reject}/` (`check_types.sh`'s single-`--check`-invocation harness can't witness a runtime interp/compiled split — both backends accept the program at typecheck time; the divergence only appears once the program is actually RUN on each backend).

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — interfaces/impls declaration checking, Task 5, 2026-07-06)

- ✅ **finding 17 (FIXED, 2026-07-07) — `derive X for UnknownType` now ERRORs instead of silently no-opping.** Fix locus: `expand_derive`'s `None` branch (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`) now emits `Err.error` at the type-name span (`` Unknown type `%s` in `derive` — is it declared in this module? ``) before returning `[]`, mirroring the sibling unknown-derive-INTERFACE case. Witness: `specs/lang/types/reject/t49_derive_unknown_type.march` (`derive Show for NoSuchType`, EXPECT-ERROR `` Unknown type `NoSuchType` in `derive` ``) — flips exit 0 → exit 1. `check_types.sh` 104 → 107 (with F6/revoke_cap witnesses). Original finding below.

  **[ORIGINAL FINDING]** Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.4 (the `derive`/`satisfy` widening section) and §4.1 finding 17, widening the interface/impl declaration-checking reference (`.superpowers/sdd/interface-impl-survey.md` §5, finding S1). `expand_derive`'s `None` branch (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml:1659`) is a bare `[]` when the derive TARGET TYPE isn't found in the module's own collected `type_defs` — no `Err.error` call, unlike the very same function's own unknown-derive-TARGET-INTERFACE case just a few lines away (`derive_impl`'s `_ -> Err.error …` catch-all, `desugar.ml:1641`–`1647`), and unlike `expand_satisfy`'s unknown-interface and missing-function checks (`desugar.ml:1687`–`1690`, `:1694`–`1699`), both of which DO reject.

  **Minimal repro** (confirmed live this task, both `--check` and RUN):
  ```march
  mod M do
    derive Eq for Ghost           -- `Ghost` is never defined anywhere

    fn main() do
      println("no error, no Ghost type defined")
    end
  end
  ```
  ```
  $ march --check file.march   # exit 0, no diagnostic
  $ march file.march           # exit 0, prints: no error, no Ghost type defined
  ```
  The `derive Eq for Ghost` line has zero observable effect — the program behaves exactly as if it were deleted. Confirmed reproducible; not test flakiness (re-run, same result).

  **Cited derive-expansion site:** `expand_derive` (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml:1651`–`1664`):
  ```ocaml
  match List.assoc_opt type_name.txt type_defs with
  | None -> []   (* type not found — silently skip *)          (* desugar.ml:1659 *)
  | Some (tparams, td) -> List.concat_map (fun iface_name -> …) ifaces
  ```

  **Why this is a real gap, not intentional leniency:** every OTHER "the target of a declaration doesn't exist" case documented in this widening slice IS rejected — `impl` of an undeclared interface (`core-march-types.md` §2.3 item 2, `` Unknown interface `NotDeclared` — is it declared above this impl? ``), `derive` of an undeclared INTERFACE (this same function, `` Unknown derive target `Frobnicate` for type `Color`. `` — confirmed live, `reject/t23_derive_unknown_interface`), and `satisfy` of an undeclared interface (`` Unknown interface `Bogus` in satisfy declaration. ``, confirmed live). The derive-unknown-TYPE case is the one asymmetric exception, and it fails silently rather than loudly — the worst direction for a typo (a misspelled type name in a `derive` line is currently indistinguishable from a no-op comment).

  Filed here in the same spirit as the impl-coherence entry immediately above (a real, pinned gap, deliberately left unfixed by this documentation-only slice) — fixing it (rejecting an unknown derive TARGET TYPE the same way an unknown derive target INTERFACE already is, i.e. an `Err.error` call in `expand_derive`'s `None` branch instead of `[]`) is a small, well-scoped compiler change, but out of scope here. Deliberately NOT added to `specs/lang/types/{accept,reject}/` as a `reject/` program — a `reject/` witness would assert behavior this finding identifies as WRONG (the program currently, incorrectly, `--check`s clean); once fixed, a `reject/derive_unknown_type`-style program should be added per `core-march-types.md` §4.1 finding 17's note.

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — actors: declaration + spawn typing, Task 1, 2026-07-06)

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18, `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml` `ESpawn` arm — `spawn` now returns `Pid[state]`).** The `ESpawn` arm resolves the plain actor name against `env.vars` directly, reaching the `Pid[state_ty]` binding the `DActor` arm makes for the actor name (previously unobservable — shadowed at every `ECon` occurrence by the nullary-constructor registration) and returning its instantiation; an unknown name (error recovery) keeps the fresh var, and a non-`Pid` vars binding (a user value shadowing an actor name) also falls back rather than mistyping. Consequences verified live: two same-actor pids share one concrete `Pid[{…}]` (`accept/t87` — pid list + `is_alive`/`kill` instantiating at the state record), and a cross-actor pid list is now REJECTED (`reject/t81`, `expected `{ x : Int }` but got `{ s : String }``) where it previously typechecked clean via opportunistic fresh-var unification. Types corpus 166 → **168** (87 accept / 81 reject, `check_types.sh` 168/168); `accept/t39`'s stale fresh-var comment updated; `core-march-types.md` §2.6.3 finding-18 text + the §2.6.4 finding-19 cross-reference rewritten (finding 19 — `send` unchecked against the target's message set — remains OPEN and is unaffected: the STATE type says nothing about the accepted-MESSAGE set). The `GlobalPid`/`Pid(T)`-annotation-impossible half of finding 18 (global type-namespace collision) also remains OPEN — untouched by this fix. Full gate green.

  ~~`spawn(Actor)` returns `Pid[<fresh var>]`, NOT `Pid[state]` — the actor's state type never reaches an observable `Pid`.~~ Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.6.3 (the actor declaration + spawn typing widening) and §4.1 finding 18. The `ESpawn` typing arm returns `TCon ("Pid", [fresh_var env.level])` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml:4203`) — a fresh, unconstrained variable computed with no reference to the actor's state type. Separately, the `DActor` arm binds the actor NAME to `Pid[state_ty]` (`typecheck.ml:6821`), but that value binding is unreachable from a bare name occurrence because the nullary-constructor registration at `:6769` (actor name ⇒ type `<Name>`) shadows it — so a bare `Counter` is typed `Counter`, not `Pid[state]`.

  **Live probes (confirmed this task):**
  - `let p = if true do spawn(Counter) else spawn(Named) end` typechecks CLEAN with `Counter`'s state `{count:Int}` and `Named`'s state `{name:String}` — the two `if`-branches unify only because each `spawn` produced an independent free var; were the parameter the state type, T-If would reject them (`Pid({count:Int})` vs `Pid({name:String})`).
  - `is_alive(Counter)` (with `is_alive : Pid(a) -> Bool`) is REJECTED `` expected `Pid(r3)` but got `Counter` `` — the bare name resolves to the nullary ctor's `Counter` type, not the `:6821` `Pid[state]` value binding.

  **Compounding gap:** no surface annotation can pin the parameter either. The built-in `Pid` is registered at arity 1 (`typecheck.ml:1849`), but stdlib `GlobalPid` declares a 0-arity `type Pid = { … }` record (`stdlib/global_pid.march:11`); because March has a single global type namespace with no per-module type identity (`core-march-types.md` §2.5), that bare `Pid` shadows the built-in in `env.types`, so `Pid(T)` annotations reject `` `Pid` expects 0 type argument(s) but got 1. `` (arity check, `typecheck.ml:2348–2351`).

  **Net effect:** the state type IS checked inside the actor decl (`init` + each handler body checked to return the state record, `typecheck.ml:6785–6820`), but it does not propagate to any observable `Pid` at a `spawn` site — the `Pid` parameter stays a free var that unifies opportunistically with whatever surrounding builtins demand (`is_alive`, `kill`, `send`, …). Tightening `spawn`'s result to `Pid[state]` (or making the actor name resolve to its `:6821` binding rather than the `:6769` nullary ctor) is a compiler change, out of scope for this documentation-only slice. Deliberately NOT added to `specs/lang/types/{accept,reject}/` as a `reject/` program — there is no *incorrect* program to pin (the current fresh-var behavior is what it is, and `accept/t39_actor_spawn_pid` witnesses it); this is a faithfulness/expectation-gap note, not a rejectable typo.

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — actors: message payload typing + actor affinity, Task 3, 2026-07-06)

- ✅ **(COMPILED-MISROUTE HALF FIXED, 2026-07-07) — the compiled memory-safety divergence is gone; the type-system gate remains deferred.** The compiled backend no longer MISROUTES a foreign message; it now DROPS it, byte-identical to the interpreter's silent drop. Fix loci: (1) `lib/tir/repr.ml` — `repr_of_ty`/`niche_repr_of_concrete`/`is_niche_shaped` now force every actor message type (`<Actor>_Msg`, via new `Tir_names.is_actor_msg_name`) to the **Boxed** representation, so a single-handler actor's message is a tagged heap cell rather than a tag-less Newtype (previously indistinguishable at dispatch); (2) `lib/tir/llvm_toplevel.ml` `build_ctor_info` — actor message ctors get **globally-unique** heap tags (base `0x01000000`), not per-actor 0-based tags, so `Logger.Log`'s tag ≠ `Counter.Inc`'s; (3) `lib/tir/lower_actor.ml` — the dispatch `ECase` gets a **dropping default arm** (`ECase(msg, branches, Some (EAtom unit))`), so a foreign message's now-distinct tag matches no branch and falls to the default, where Perceus emits the `march_decrc` that releases it (no leak, verified in the emitted IR). Witness: golden `specs/lang/golden/g40_actor_foreign_msg_drop.march` — a `Logger` message `send` to a `Counter` Pid is dropped in BOTH backends (`count=3`, exit 0, MATCH); the pre-fix compiled binary printed a garbage int (or SIGSEGV'd on the niche shape). The witness uses a single count-changing message (`Inc(3)`, then the foreign `Zlog`, then `Report`) deliberately: a foreign-drop sandwiched *between* two count-changing messages exposes an unrelated, pre-existing compiled-scheduler race (filed immediately below as finding 20) that would make the golden intermittently flaky. Regression IR test: `test/test_codegen.ml` `test_actor_foreign_msg_drop_boxed_dispatch` (asserts Boxed switch + `case_default` drop + two distinct global tags). Covers all three message shapes (single-handler Newtype, two-handler-one-nullary Niche, multi-handler Boxed), all now Boxed+global+default. **STILL OPEN (deferred):** the *type-system* half — `send` does not gate the message by the target actor's accepted-message set, so a wrong-actor send still TYPECHECKS (exit 0). Fixing that is a significant type-system design decision (typing Pids by their accepted-message set); the runtime is now memory-safe regardless. Original finding below.

  **[ORIGINAL FINDING]** `send(target, Msg(args))` does NOT check the message against the target actor's accepted-message set — a wrong-actor send typechecks (exit 0), then is silently DROPPED interpreted but MISROUTED (memory-unsafe) compiled. Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.6.4 and §4.1 finding 19. **Distinct from finding 18** (the `Pid`-is-unparameterized-after-`spawn` gap above): finding 18 is about the *type the Pid carries*; THIS is about the `send` typing arm ignoring the target regardless of what the Pid carries. The `ESend` arm (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml:4177`) infers the target Pid's type and immediately discards it — `ignore (infer_expr env cap)` (`:4178`) — so `send` never consults *which actor* `cap` is. The only send-side check is `check_sendable` (`typecheck.ml:3335`), which walks the message type and errors solely on a `RingBuf`-family constructor (`let non_sendable_types = ["RingBuf"]`, `:3331`) — NOT a message-acceptance check. The message payload *shape* IS checked (ordinary `ECon` constructor typing via `let msg_ty = infer_expr env msg`, `:4179`, witnessed by `reject/t29_actor_send_wrong_payload`: `send(counter, Inc("x"))` where `Inc` expects `Int` rejects `` expected `Int` but got `String`. ``), but *which handler the target actually has* is not.

  **Live repro (confirmed this task, BOTH backends).** `Counter` handles only `Inc(Int)`; `Logger` handles `Log(String)`. Send `Log("stray")` — a `Logger` message — to the `Counter` Pid:
  ```
  mod Main do
    actor Counter do
      state { count : Int }
      init  { count: 0 }
      on Inc(x : Int) do
        println("Counter.Inc -> " ++ int_to_string(state.count + x))
        { count: state.count + x }
      end
    end
    actor Logger do
      state { seen : Int }
      init  { seen: 0 }
      on Log(m : String) do
        println("Logger.Log -> " ++ m)
        { seen: state.seen + 1 }
      end
    end
    fn main() do
      let counter = spawn(Counter)
      send(counter, Inc(3))
      send(counter, Log("stray"))   -- Log is a Logger message, not Counter's
      run_until_idle()
      println("done")
    end
  end
  ```
  - `--check` exits **0** (accepts).
  - **Interpreted** (`main.exe file.march`) prints `Counter.Inc -> 3` then `done` — the stray `Log` matched no `Counter` handler NAME (`h.ah_msg.txt = msg_tag` string equality, `lib/eval/eval.ml:7545`) and was **silently dropped** (`None -> ()`, `eval.ml:7547-7549`).
  - **Compiled** (`--compile --opt 2`) prints `Counter.Inc -> 3`, then `Counter.Inc -> <garbage int, e.g. 2796564219>`, then `done` — the stray message was **MISROUTED** into `Counter`'s first handler slot. The compiled dispatch lowers each message to a per-actor `<Actor>_Msg` variant in handler-declaration order (`lib/tir/lower_actor.ml:17`) and dispatches by an `ECase` on that variant's discriminant with **no default arm** (`ECase(msg, branches, None)`, `lower_actor.ml:256`); a foreign message's discriminant indexes into the *target* actor's branch table, so `Log`'s slot hits `Counter.Inc`, whose body reinterprets the `String` payload pointer as an `Int` (non-deterministic, memory-unsafe).

  **Why filed separately from finding 18:** finding 18 = "the Pid is unparameterized / a `Pid(T)` annotation is impossible." This finding = "`send` does not gate the message by the target actor" — and it would remain true EVEN IF the Pid carried its state type, because `send` discards `τ_cap` entirely (`:4178`). Fixing it (typing Pids by their accepted-message set so `send` can gate the message) is a significant type-system design decision — deferred, out of scope for this docs-only slice. Deliberately NOT a `reject/` corpus program (it typechecks; a `reject/` witness would codify the WRONG behavior); the correctly-typed accept path is `accept/t40_actor_send_typed_payload`. The message-name flat global namespace that underlies the compiled misroute is a DESIGN POINT (analogous to `core-march-types.md` §2.5's no-per-module-type-namespace point), documented in §2.6.4 — NOT filed as a gap.

- ✅ **Finding 20 (FIXED, 2026-07-08) — compiled actor scheduler intermittently LOST a legitimate message when a foreign message was dropped mid-drain between two count-changing messages (memory-safe, compiled-only).** Surfaced 2026-07-07 during the finding-19 fix review, while making golden `g40` deterministic. **Distinct from finding 19:** finding 19 was a memory-UNSAFE misroute (garbage int / SIGSEGV), fixed separately; this was a memory-SAFE silent message *loss* (a valid-but-incomplete count, never garbage).
  **Repro + characterization (compiled `--opt 2`; interp deterministic throughout):**
  - `send(c, Inc(3)); send(c, Zlog_foreign); send(c, Inc(4)); send(c, Report())` → intermittently printed `count=4` (the `Inc(3)` write was lost) instead of `count=7`. Rate was load-dependent and intermittent: observed **5/30 (~17%)** in one batch, **0/30** in another — an unacceptable flaky-golden trigger.
  - `send(c, Inc(3)); send(c, Zlog_foreign); send(c, Report())` (foreign NOT between two count-changing messages) → **100/100 `count=3`, deterministic.**
  - `send(c, Inc(3)); send(c, Inc(4)); send(c, Report())` (no foreign, 3 msgs) → **40/40 `count=7`, deterministic.**
  - `send(c, Inc(3)); send(c, Inc(2)); send(c, Inc(4)); send(c, Report())` (no foreign, 4 msgs) → **20/20 `count=9`, deterministic.**
  Only a single spawned actor is involved (`Logger` is defined only to bring the foreign ctor into scope; it is never spawned), ruling out multi-actor interleaving as the cause.
  **Root cause (NOT the mailbox drain — the original "drain cursor" hypothesis above was wrong):** the actor's message handler writes its new state back into the actor struct via a Perceus **`EReuse`** (in-place FBIP update). The generic `EReuse` emit path is **RC-conditional**: it loads the target's refcount and only mutates in place when `rc == 1`, else it allocates a fresh copy, writes into the copy, and discards the old one. For an actor struct this check is unsound: the actor object is a stable, long-lived singleton mutated *solely* by its own daemon green thread, but the *handle*'s refcount (how many `Pid` references exist) is concurrently, atomically incremented/decremented by the **caller thread** as it passes the `Pid` to successive `send`s. A handler observing a transient `rc > 1` (the caller mid-flight through several `send`s) takes the "fresh" branch — allocating a copy, writing the state update into it, and discarding it (the handler's result is `Unit`), **silently losing the state write**. This is a genuine data race on the RC-load vs. the caller's concurrent incrc/decrc, not a scheduler/drain bug; the foreign-drop-between-two-messages shape was incidental — it happened to be the timing window most likely to expose the existing race, not a distinct trigger.
  **Fix (`lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`, `emit_expr`'s `EReuse` case):** added a branch that for an actor struct **always** mutates in place — no RC load, no branch, no decrc, no fresh alloc (stores the tag + fields directly into the existing pointer). Non-actor `EReuse` sites are unaffected (unchanged RC-conditional path). Verified: **150/150 then a further 50/50 (200 total) compiled runs of `g40` all print `count=7`, zero `count=4`** (was ~5–17% failure); interp==compiled. Golden `specs/lang/golden/g40_actor_foreign_msg_drop.march` restored to the fuller `Inc(3)/Zlog/Inc(4)/Report → count=7` shape (the shape that originally exposed this race) now that it is deterministic; `verify.sh` MATCH. Full six-runner suite green (compiler 482 / eval 231 / codegen 392, `llvm_ir_validity_gate` clean / stdlib 804); `examples/actors.march`'s pre-existing dead-actor-drop ordering divergence (unrelated — confirmed identical on the pre-fix and post-fix binaries via file-copy A/B) is untouched.
  **Follow-up (adversarial review, same day) — the gate's first cut was a NAME-based check (`Tir_names.is_actor_struct_name`, a suffix match on the type constructor name ending in `"_Actor"`) and it was a Critical false-positive vector: an ordinary user type coincidentally NAMED `Foo_Actor` (not a real actor) would ALSO take the always-in-place branch, silently corrupting it if the value was shared (`RC > 1`) — the exact refcount check that shared-value FBIP safety depends on was skipped for a non-actor type. Live-verified: a `type Tree_Actor = TLeaf(Int) | TNode(Tree_Actor, Tree_Actor)`, aliased then `bump`ed (an FBIP-eligible recursive rebuild), corrupted the alias compiled (`shared sum=31`, should be `30`) under the name-based gate; interp was unaffected (interp has no FBIP). Fixed by making the gate STRUCTURAL instead of name-based: a genuine actor struct's field 0 is always literally named `"$d_dispatch"` (`lib/tir/lower_actor.ml`'s `TDRecord` construction), and March identifiers can never start with `$` (lexer's `ident = alpha (alpha|digit|'\'')*`), so a user type can never forge this field — `Repr.is_actor_struct_type` (`lib/tir/repr.ml`, a new `ctx.type_defs`-based lookup) checks for it directly instead of pattern-matching the type name. Re-verified: the `Tree_Actor` corruption repro now matches the interpreter (`shared sum=30`) on both backends; the genuine actor path is unaffected (still 260/260 deterministic `count=7` runs across two rebuilds). Two new NON-VACUOUS regression tests in `test/test_codegen.ml`'s `actor_dispatch_codegen` group (RED on the name-based gate / GREEN after, confirmed via file-copy A/B): the genuine-actor case asserts the emitted IR has NO RC-conditional branch for the state-update `EReuse`; the `_Actor`-suffixed-user-type case asserts the RC-conditional branch is STILL PRESENT (proving the gate does not misfire). Full six-runner suite green again (compiler 482 / eval 231 / codegen 394 / stdlib 804); `verify.sh` 40/40; `check-docs.sh` clean.

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — actors: lifecycle + epoch capabilities, Task 4, 2026-07-06)

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18, runtime + codegen wiring + typecheck — the whole plane is now byte-identical, pinned by `test/native/cap_epoch_plane.march` + oracle anchor).** Five stacked defects: (1) **`march_get_cap` was a stub returning a boxed 16-byte tag-0 cell** — under `Option(Cap)`'s NICHE encoding (None=NULL) that decoded as `Some(garbage)` for EVERY pid, live or dead; now builds the real 5-word cap (hdr, hdr, actor ptr, pid_index, epoch from the actor's meta) and returns NULL for dead/unknown. (2) **`march_send_checked` returned void** — the call site read garbage as the atom; now returns runtime-interned `:ok`/`:error` (new `march_atom_of_name`: FNV-1a 64 + bit63:=bit62, matching `Llvm_ctx.atom_hash` exactly), with the liveness check added. (3) **`revoke_cap`/`is_cap_valid` had NO codegen wiring at all** (`_revoke_cap` link error) — the C fns took (pid_index, epoch) scalars with no way to call them from March; both now take the Cap object, and are wired (llvm_builtins rows + PDeclare + defun builtin_names; preamble golden updated). (4) **runtime-produced atoms rendered as `:<atom>`** — `emit_atom_show_table` now pre-seeds `ok`/`error`. (5) **`send(dead_pid, M)` decoded `Some` compiled** — `ESend` was typed as a fresh unconstrained var (stale "returns the handler's result" comment; both backends actually return `Option(Unit)`), and the erased `Option('a)` scrutinee made emit_case's abstract-arg niche path guess NICHE for `march_send`'s BOXED cells; `ESend` is now typed `Option(Unit)` concretely AND `Repr.niche_payload_ok` marks `TTuple []` (the typechecker's `t_unit`) niche-UNSAFE (its value repr is raw 0 = the niche None). Verified byte-identical on the full plane: live cap `:ok`, revoke → invalid + `:error`, `send(dead)` → None, `get_cap(dead)` → None, stale-cap `:error`. Full gate green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 31 / codegen 421 / stdlib 810 / oracle 98 matched 0 divergences / types 166).

  ~~The capability / dead-actor `send` plane is NOT byte-identical interp vs compiled — the compiled epoch-`Cap` validation is non-functional.~~ Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march.md` §4.10.6 (the lifecycle + epoch-capability widening). The **live-actor message plane** (`spawn`/`send`/`receive`/`run_until_idle`/`is_alive`) agrees between backends (witnessed by golden `g35`–`g37`), but the dead-actor and capability paths diverge — verified live on both backends:
  - `send(dead_pid, Msg)` → interp `None` (drop) vs compiled `Some` (compiled does not implement the dead-actor drop).
  - `get_cap(dead_pid)` → interp `None` vs compiled `Some` (compiled `get_cap` does not gate on liveness).
  - `send_checked(cap, Msg)` → interp returns `:ok` for a valid live cap / `:error` for a dead/stale/revoked cap (`eval.ml:3137`); **compiled performs no epoch validation at all and returns an uninterned/garbage atom** (compares equal to neither `:ok` nor `:error`, `show`s as `:<atom>`) for EVERY cap, live or dead. So the entire epoch-`Cap` security mechanism (`VCap of int*int` `eval.ml:48`, `send_checked` `:3137`, `revoke_cap` `:3164`, epoch-staleness `:384–388`/`increment_epoch:1100`/restart-inherit `:1513–1517`) is documented for the **interpreter** only; it is not usable compiled. Because a divergent program cannot be a golden `MATCH`, no cap witness was added to `specs/lang/golden/`; the mechanism is documented in §4.10.6 prose + citations with the divergence table. Fixing it is compiled-runtime work (implement the dead-actor drop, liveness gate, and epoch validation in the compiled scheduler/runtime), out of scope for this documentation-only slice.

### Compiler / runtime (found during Core March widening slice — actors: supervision, Task 5, 2026-07-06)

- ✅ **`get_actor_field`/`pid_of_int` + compiled supervision — FIXED (2026-07-08, six-task compiled-actor-supervision plan `specs/plans/2026-07-08-compiled-actor-supervision-plan.md`).** The whole compiled supervision plane — pid encoding, external actor-state inspection, spawn-time child injection, crash isolation, and all three restart strategies — now works compiled, byte-identical to the interpreter for the deterministic single-restart witnesses. **Fixes:** (1) **`march_pid_of_int`** (`runtime/march_runtime.c`) now reverse-looks-up the actor by its sequential `pid_index` via `find_meta_by_pid_index` (a linear scan of the actor-meta table), returning a shaped **"dead actor" sentinel struct** (rc≈1e9, `$e_alive` already false) for any stale/unknown index — never the old unsafe `(void*)(intptr_t)n` cast — so `send`/`kill`/`is_alive` on a recycled pid safely hit their existing already-dead fast-path instead of dereferencing a wild pointer. (2) **`march_get_actor_field`** (relocated to `runtime/march_extras.c`, replacing the always-`None` stub) does a real partial lookup using the compiler's EXISTING runtime shape-registry (`rec_shape_of`/`rec_find_field`/`rec_field_raw` — the same mechanism `march_record_field_dyn` uses for type-erased `EField`): a per-actor-struct "shape id" (hash of `name:kind;…`) is stamped into the actor header pad word at spawn time via `emit_set_shape` (gated to actor structs by `Tir_names.is_actor_struct_name` in `llvm_emit.ml`'s Boxed-`EAlloc` branch), so the field read works regardless of the caller's static type knowledge (the earlier compile-time-string-compare design NEVER fired — nothing monomorphizes the abstract `Pid(a)` through the polymorphic `get_actor_field(sup, field)` helper). (3) **spawn-time child injection** (`lower_actor.ml`): a supervisor's `spawn` now spawns each declared child, encodes its pid into the right state-field slot, and calls `register_supervisor_child` (`march_actor_register_child`) — so the compiled supervisor DOES now run/track its declared children (the earlier "compiled supervisor doesn't run children's init" divergence is closed). (4) **crash isolation + restart** (`do_actor_death`/`march_supervisor_notify`/`march_one_for_one_restart`/`march_one_for_all_restart`/`march_rest_for_one_restart`): a supervised child's panic `longjmp`s to a per-`march_proc` `crash_jmp` trap (NOT a `_Thread_local` — this scheduler steals procs across OS threads) instead of `exit(1)`, and the supervisor respawns per its strategy within a `max_restarts`-within-window budget. Respawn unwraps the `<ActorName>_spawn`-as-value **March closure** (offset-16 wrapper-fn dance — these references are ALWAYS heap closures here, never bare C fn pointers). **6 native golden tests** (`test/native/{pid_of_int_roundtrip,get_actor_field_direct,supervisor_spawn_children,supervisor_one_for_one_restart,supervisor_one_for_all_restart,supervisor_rest_for_one_restart}.march`) pin the behavior — each stress-verified stable (0/15 flaky). See the **scheduler-race finding immediately below** for why the full 3-strategy `examples/supervision_strategies.march` demo is NOT a golden.

- ✅ **PRE-EXISTING multi-scheduler kill+respawn stack-corruption crash — FIXED (2026-07-09, single-owner run-queue plan `specs/plans/2026-07-09-scheduler-single-owner-fix.md`, commits dd9e293f/b1e050a2/9407cc6f/81adf1b1).** **Actual root cause (found via a new MARCH_DEBUG fatal-fault triage handler + disassembly of the shipped binary — NOT the deque double-dispatch the characterization below assumed):** clang -O2 inlined `march_sched_yield` into `march_sched_wait_idle`'s loop and hoisted the `tl_sched` thread-local address computation out of the loop (TLS slot cached in a callee-saved register for the whole function). After the first yield migrated the green thread to a different OS thread (work stealing), every later iteration read the ORIGINAL thread's `tl_sched`, grabbed the WRONG scheduler's `->current` (a different, possibly running proc), forced its status to RUNNABLE mid-run, saved over its live ucontext, and `swapcontext`-ed into the wrong scheduler's `sched_ctx` — two OS threads inside one `sched_loop` frame. That reproduces the exact signature below: `sched_loop`'s `sched` register reading back NULL (si_addr=0x8000 = offsetof deque `top`) and pc jumping to `&g_scheds[1].sched_ctx`. Discriminator runs pinned the preemption dependency: quantum disabled → 0/150 failures; SIGUSR1 delivered but handler no-op → 2/150; full preemption → ~20/150. **Fix:** `march_sched_yield` and `march_sched_recv` are now `noinline` MIGRATION BARRIERS (every call re-derives TLS on the current OS thread; rule documented at both sites: never touch a `_Thread_local` after a swapcontext that can migrate the green thread, never let a switch-crossing function inline into a loop that reads thread-locals); `sched_loop` also pre-materializes `march_tls_reductions` before the SIGUSR1 daemon may first-touch it inside a signal handler (Darwin materializes TLV lazily via malloc — async-signal-unsafe). **Hardening landed with it (same plan):** `march_sched_wake`'s cross-thread Chase-Lev deque push (the contract violation behind the earlier 2/40 double-dispatch detector hits) is deleted — all wakes route through a new mutex-FIFO global run queue (the plan's lock-free Treiber stack was rejected during implementation: it is ABA-unsafe once wakes re-push the same proc) drained FIRST each dispatch iteration (drain-only-when-idle livelocks at N=1: a wait_idle spinner re-pushed locally every turn starves the woken actor forever); dispatch claims procs via CAS `RUNNABLE→RUNNING` (`PROC_READY` renamed `PROC_RUNNABLE`) with a MARCH_DEBUG abort backstop, preserving `march_task_cancel_by_id`'s queued-DEAD run-anyway semantics; permanent `dbg_queued`/`dbg_running_on` MARCH_DEBUG tripwires now guard single-membership/single-dispatcher. **Evidence:** `examples/supervision_strategies.march` and the supervision-free minimal repro each **200/200 clean at N=4 AND 200/200 at N=8** (baseline ~46–52% crash/hang per run at N=4); six-runner suite green (804 tests); TSan shows only the known-benign classes. The compile-time default stays `MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=4`; the `=1` mitigation is obsolete. The demo is deliberately NOT a native golden: its output interleaves concurrent worker prints nondeterministically (30/30 runs byte-differ) — inherent to truly parallel actors, not a bug. **Historical characterization (pre-fix, kept for the record):** The full `examples/supervision_strategies.march` demo (all 3 strategies, multiple workers, one process) crashes ~50% of runs (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS 138/139, or hangs) under the default 4-OS-thread work-stealing scheduler. **PROVEN pre-existing:** a minimal repro with ZERO supervision code (`kill` two workers + immediately `spawn` two replacements + `send`) reproduces the identical crash, and a `git worktree` at commit `e355aeff` (immediately before ANY of this session's supervision work) reproduces it too. **PROVEN scheduler-count-dependent:** rebuilt with `-DMARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=1` (verified `g_num_scheds==1` under lldb) → **40/40 clean**; default 4 → reliably crashes. So the mitigation for any supervision-heavy / rapid-kill+respawn compiled program is the existing runtime env override **`MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=1`** (safe, cooperative green-thread concurrency retained; only true multi-core parallelism is lost). **Root-cause characterization (deep investigation, 2026-07-08/09):** the dominant crash faults at a fixed PC in `sched_loop` reading `sched->local_queue` off a near-NULL `sched` — i.e. `sched_loop`'s OWN spilled `sched` parameter on its native OS-thread stack gets corrupted while it is suspended in `swapcontext` running a green thread. A CAS-guarded instrumentation **confirmed DOUBLE-DISPATCH** (the same `march_proc` dispatched by two scheduler OS-threads at once, 2/40 runs) — two CPUs `swapcontext`-ing into one green thread's single ucontext/stack simultaneously, which shreds it. That is the leading (but NOT sole — see below) mechanism; the exact source of a proc landing in two deques was not pinned despite a full audit of every push/pop/steal/wake site against the Chase-Lev contract (all textbook-correct on paper). **Attempted (reverted, unverified) fix:** a `READY→RUNNING` CAS claim in `sched_loop` (replacing the unconditional `atomic_store(PROC_RUNNING)`) cut crashes ~47%→~28% but nudged hangs up (drops a needed proc in some case) — so double-dispatch is real and contributory but not the whole story, and the CAS has its own gap; reverted to keep shipped code verified. **Tool notes for the next session:** ASan was fiber-BLIND here until this session added `__sanitizer_start/finish_switch_fiber` annotations around all 5 `swapcontext` sites (+ the `proc_trampoline` first-entry `finish`) — with them, the repro runs 100/100 clean under ASan (ambiguous: redzone-catch of a real overflow, vs. ASan's overhead masking the timing race). TSan needs its own `__tsan_create_fiber`/`__tsan_switch_to_fiber` (also added this session, `MARCH_SANITIZE=thread`) but hits an INTERNAL `tsan_rtl_proc.cpp:46` CHECK-failure on this fiber pattern before cleanly reaching the core crash; the remaining TSan reports on `sched_loop` are the known benign Chase-Lev standalone-`atomic_thread_fence` false-positives TSan can't track happens-before through. **Next avenues:** valgrind/helgrind (different model, no fiber-annotation need, but slow on macOS arm64); or a focused fix for the double-dispatch double-enqueue; or committing to `MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=1` as the compile-time default (safe, opt back into multi-core via the env override). Distinct from the FIXED memory-SAFE finding 20 (message loss) above — this one is memory-UNSAFE (wild deref).

  **VERIFIED-CORRECT scheduler/supervision race fixes made this session (all TSan/ASan-confirmed, all landed):** (a) **mailbox fast-path race** — `march_sched_recv`'s unlocked `if (p->mailbox) return mbox_pop(p);` raced a sender's locked `mbox_push` on the shared list; now always takes `mbox_lock`. (b) **proc-lifecycle UAF** — `sched_loop`'s `PROC_DEAD` branch `munmap`+`free`'d a `march_proc` while other threads held unlocked `meta->green_thread` references; now leaks-instead-of-frees (a stale-but-allocated proc correctly reads `PROC_DEAD`). (c) **`meta->supervisor` unsynchronized publish** (THIS session's Task 3 code) — `march_actor_register_child` wrote `child_meta->supervisor` on the supervisor's thread while the child's already-running `actor_green_thread` read it unlocked at startup; both now go through `g_tbl_mu` (TSan-confirmed gone). (d) **ASan+TSan fiber annotations** — the sanitizer integration was fiber-blind (see above); now correct, making both sanitizers usable for future scheduler debugging.
