Cherry-picked back (`git cherry-pick 4b4c70b3`) with one reconciliation: the timed-wait Err payloads now use the interpreter's exact message ("no reply (timeout or unhandled Call)") for byte-parity. Mechanism: positive `timeout_ms` does a deadline-bounded yield-poll via `march_sched_try_recv2` (distinguishes an empty mailbox from a legitimate NULL message); `timeout_ms <= 0` keeps wait-forever; known limitation (documented in-code): a late reply after timeout still lands in the caller's mailbox. Pinned by `test/native/actor_call_timeout` (compiled golden from the restored commit + oracle both-backends anchor `timeout_ok`).

  ~~`Actor.call`'s `timeout_ms` is UNENFORCED in the compiled runtime — a synchronous call cannot actually time out.~~ `march_actor_call(void *actor, void *inner_msg, int64_t timeout_ms)` (`runtime/march_runtime.c:1809`) explicitly discards the timeout: `(void)timeout_ms; /* timeout not yet enforced; accepted for API compat */` (`:1810`). The parameter is accepted for ABI/API compatibility but has no effect — a `call` that would block indefinitely will not be interrupted by its stated timeout. Noted here for reference-completeness alongside the supervision widening (§4.10.7); it is not exercised by any golden (the actor-`call` path is not part of the operational core fragment). Fixing it is runtime work (thread the timeout through the compiled scheduler's blocking-receive so the call unblocks with a timeout result), deferred, out of scope for this documentation-only slice.

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18, `lib/eval/eval.ml` `actor_call` + the restored `4b4c70b3` compiled tag-base fix — the canonical protocol now works in BOTH backends).** Two halves: (1) **compiled** — the restored lost commit `4b4c70b3` (see the timeout item above) fixed the silent call-drop: post-F19, actor `_Msg` ctors carry GLOBALLY-unique tags (base 0x0100_0000 + declaration index) but `march_actor_call` stamped the augmented message with the sentinel's per-type 0-based tag, so every compiled call fell to the dispatch default arm; codegen now registers each actor's first-msg-ctor global tag at actor-record alloc (`march_actor_set_call_base`) and the runtime translates sentinel index → base + index (with a non-deref decode for enum-immediate sentinels). (2) **interpreter** — reconciled to the documented-canonical compiled protocol (the maintainer decision in `specs/lang/actors.md` "Synchronous Request-Reply"): eval's `actor_call` no longer wraps as a 2-arg `Call(ref, msg)` (which required an interp-only `on Call(ref, msg)` handler); it now tag-routes exactly like `march_actor_call` — a handler NAMED like the sentinel wins, otherwise the sentinel's ctor index within its own declared type (via `ctor_type_tbl` + `ffi_type_decl_tbl`) selects the actor's handler at that index, and the reply ref is injected as the handler's single argument (`Actor.reply(reply_to, x)` answers). The docs' `type GetReq = GetReq` single-ctor sentinel → index 0 → first handler, on both backends. The one interp-form corpus test (`test_actor_call_get`, `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`) migrated to the canonical form. Pinned by `test/native/actor_call_canonical.march` (the actors.md example shape; `count = 2` on both backends, oracle-anchored) + `actor_call_timeout`.

  ~~`Actor.call`'s handler-dispatch FORM diverges interpreted vs compiled — no single example works in both backends.~~ The interpreter (`lib/eval/eval.ml:6455`) wraps the call as `Call(ref, msg)` (`VCon ("Call", [VInt ref_id; inner_msg])`) and delivers it to a **two-argument** handler matching `on Call(ref, msg)`; any message value works, and dispatch is to a `Call`-named/first handler. The compiled runtime (`march_runtime.c:1809–1849`) instead reads the **tag** of a **zero-arg sentinel** `inner_msg`, builds an augmented message `{tag, field0 = caller}`, and routes it to the **handler at that tag**, binding the caller as its **single** argument (e.g. `on GetCount(reply_to)`). Consequences (verified live 2026-07-06, both forms × both backends): the interpreter form (`on Call(ref, msg)` + `Actor.call(pid, Inc(), …)`) works interpreted (`count = 2`) but **DEADLOCKS compiled** — the tag routes to a non-replying handler and the unenforced timeout (finding above) never fires; the compiled form (zero-arg sentinel + one-arg handler) works compiled (`count = 1`) but returns `Err("no reply …")` interpreted. `specs/lang/actors.md` documents the **compiled** form as canonical (maintainer decision) with an interpreter-divergence note; the `stdlib/actor.march` and `share/march/actor.march` docstrings likewise show the compiled form. Fixing it is runtime/interpreter work — reconcile the two protocols, most likely by making the interpreter tag-route and inject a single caller field to match compiled — out of scope for the doc reconciliation.

### Compiler (found during Core March widening slice — interfaces/impls declaration checking, Task 6 closeout / `interfaces.md` reconciliation, 2026-07-06)

- [x] **FIXED (2026-07-18, `lib/desugar/desugar.ml` `inject_defaults`).** Root cause: `inject_defaults` synthesized the default method as a **zero-param** fn clause whose body was the default expression verbatim — a lambda `fn (x, y) -> …`. So the default method compiled to a 0-arg function that merely *returned* a closure; a real call site `mylt(Red, Green)` then invoked that 0-arg function with 2 args, the args were silently dropped, the returned closure was never applied, and the closure pointer itself was used as the `Bool`/`Int` result — hence "always the same answer regardless of arguments." (The interpreter's application machinery tolerated the extra indirection and stayed correct.) **Fix:** when the desugared default expression is an `ELam(params, body, _)`, FLATTEN its params into the synthesized clause's own `fc_params` (wrapping each `param` as `FPNamed`) and use `body` as `fc_body`, so the default method has real parameters that flow to the call. A non-lambda default keeps the zero-param clause. Verified interp==compiled (`true false`) on the `MyOrd`/`AppColor` repro below AND the `Eq`-shaped `neqx` repro; regression fixture `test/native/default_method_args.march` + oracle anchor `true\nfalse\ntrue\n`; full gate green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 29 / codegen 421 / stdlib 809 / oracle 0 un-triaged). **NOTE — a genuinely distinct, still-OPEN compiled-only ICE was isolated while verifying this** (see the "constructor-pattern params" note at the end of this item, now generalized): any **multi-arg** function whose params are constructor patterns (`fn cmp2(N(a), N(b))`, `impl` method or plain top-level fn, no interface/default needed) hits `LLVM Llvm_ctx.emit: constructor pattern $Tuple2(…) destructures a non-pointer scrutinee` at codegen — single-arg ctor-pattern params (`fn unwrap1(N(a))`) compile fine. Filed separately below.

  ~~A user-interface default method whose body calls a sibling interface method compiled ALWAYS returns the same result, regardless of the actual call arguments — a real, previously-undocumented compiled-only wrong-answer bug (NOT a hang).~~ Found while reproducing `specs/lang/interfaces.md`'s stale "Known issue" callout (which claimed a default `neq` calling `eq` "hangs/stack-overflows at runtime"). That claim is FALSE — reproduced live, interpreted AND compiled, and neither backend hangs or overflows the stack; the interpreted backend is fully correct. But the compiled backend has a different, real bug in the same area: the default method's body (compiled to a lambda closure over the interface's own type parameter, evaluated at `impl`-application time) does not correctly re-evaluate per call — it appears to always take the same branch/answer as whichever call is compiled/inlined first, ignoring the actual arguments on subsequent (or all) calls.

  **Minimal repro** (confirmed live this task, interpreted vs `--compile --opt 2`, deterministic across reruns):
  ```march
  mod M do
    interface MyOrd(a) do
      fn mycmp : a -> a -> Int
      fn mylt  : a -> a -> Bool do fn (x, y) -> mycmp(x, y) < 0 end
    end

    type AppColor = Red | Green | Blue

    fn color_rank(c) do
      match c do
        Red -> 0
        Green -> 1
        Blue -> 2
      end
    end

    impl MyOrd(AppColor) do
      fn mycmp(a, b) do
        color_rank(a) - color_rank(b)
      end
    end

    fn main() do
      println(bool_to_string(mylt(Red, Green)))   -- expect true  (0-1 = -1 < 0)
      println(bool_to_string(mylt(Green, Red)))   -- expect false (1-0 = 1, not < 0)
    end
  end
  ```
  ```
  $ march file.march                                          # interpreted: true / false  (correct)
  $ march --compile --opt 2 -o /tmp/b file.march && /tmp/b     # compiled:    true / true   (WRONG — 2nd call should be false)
  ```
  Calling `mycmp` directly (not through the `mylt` default) is correct compiled in isolation (confirmed: printing `mycmp(Red, Green)` compiled gives `-1`, matching interpreted) — the bug is specific to the DEFAULT method's own lambda body, not to `mycmp`'s dispatch or to `<`'s codegen. Also reproduces identically for `Eq`-shaped defaults (`neq` calling `eq` via `fn (x, y) -> !eq(x, y)`) and is NOT specific to colliding with the built-in `Eq`/`Ord` interface names — renaming to a user-only `MyEq`/`myeq`/`myneq` (no built-in name collision at all) reproduces byte-for-byte identically, ruling out the `impl_tbl` dispatch-key-collision mechanism the stale doc callout blamed (that mechanism was a real, separate, already-fixed bug — see `core-march.md` §4.4.2's "context, not a rule" note on the `is_type_dispatched_iface` guard). Also confirmed the doc's claim that "`Ord`'s `cmp`-calling defaults are unaffected" is ALSO wrong — `mylt`/`mygt` derived from `mycmp` show the identical always-same-answer symptom.

  A second, textually-adjacent shape (`impl` methods with constructor-pattern params, e.g. `fn mycmp(N(a), N(b)) do … end`, as opposed to `fn mycmp(a, b) do match (a,b) do … end end`) instead hits a DIFFERENT, pre-existing ICE (`` LLVM Llvm_ctx.emit: constructor pattern $Tuple2(...) destructures a non-pointer scrutinee ... type-incorrect TIR reached codegen ``) rather than the wrong-answer symptom above — noted here because it was surfaced by the same investigation, but it is a distinct failure mode (compile-time ICE, not a silent runtime wrong-answer) and not otherwise probed or filed by this task. **UPDATE 2026-07-18 — probed, generalized, and FIXED (`lib/tir/lower.ml` `lower_to_atom_k`). This ICE was NOT impl-specific and NOT default-method-related. It fired for ANY multi-arg function whose parameters are constructor patterns** — a plain top-level `fn cmp2(N(a), N(b)) do a == b end` ICE'd identically (`$Tuple2($f…, $f…) destructures a non-pointer scrutinee`), while single-arg `fn unwrap1(N(a)) do a end` was fine. Trigger: (2+ params) × (each param a destructuring constructor pattern). **Root cause:** multi-arg fn desugaring synthesises the merged match scrutinee as `ETuple(__arg0, …, __argN)` carrying the FUNCTION span (`fn_span`); lowering bound that tuple to a fresh var typed via `ty_of_expr` (span-keyed), and `fn_span`'s `type_map` entry is the fn's RETURN type (the match RESULT type, e.g. `Bool`), not the tuple type — so codegen received a non-pointer immediate destructured as `$TupleN`. **Fix:** `lower_to_atom_k` now has an explicit `ETuple` case that types the scrutinee var from its per-element spans (`TTuple (List.map ty_of_expr es)`) whenever the tuple's own span doesn't already record a `TTuple` — each `__argN` element has its own correctly-typed synthetic span, sidestepping the collision. Verified interp==compiled for plain/impl/default 2-arg, 3-arg, and mixed ctor+var params; regression `test/native/ctor_pattern_multi_param.march` + oracle anchor `false\ntrue\n6\n15\n`; full gate green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 29 / codegen 421 / stdlib 809 / oracle 0 un-triaged).

  Root cause not pinned down (docs-only reconciliation task, `lib/tir`/`lib/eval` not modified) — plausible candidate, per `core-march-types.md` §2.3's default-method mechanics (`inject_defaults`, `lib/desugar/desugar.ml:897`–`931`, splices a synthesized zero-param clause wrapping the default expression verbatim before typecheck ever sees the impl) interacting with the compiled backend's closure/TCO lowering for that synthesized clause, but this was not investigated further. Filed here (not fixed) because it directly falsifies both halves of `interfaces.md`'s removed "Known issue" callout (see that file's reconciliation, this same commit) and is a real, reproducible, currently-undocumented compiled-backend correctness bug distinct from every other interface/impl finding filed by this widening slice (impl-coherence overlap, above, and derive-unknown-type no-op, above — neither of which is about default-method lambda bodies specifically). Deliberately NOT added to `specs/lang/types/{accept,reject}/` — that corpus is `--check`-only (typecheck-time accept/reject) and this is a RUN-time, compiled-only wrong-answer, exactly the same harness-shape limitation documented for the impl-coherence divergence above.

### Compiler (found during Differential Oracle Task 4 generator scoping, 2026-07-04)

- [x] **FIXED — cross-backend hash() equality RESTORED (2026-07-18, cherry-picked the THIRD lost commit `c30161d7`).** The merge-loss audit found that `c30161d7` ("cross-backend hash() equality — interpreter matches compiled algorithms", 2026-07-13) — a genuine FIX making `hash()` bit-for-bit identical across backends — was also dropped in the PR #27/#38 merge (the third lost commit, after `c6599af9` and `4b4c70b3`). So the divergence I initially documented here as "expected" was NOT intended: the fix reimplements the compiled runtime's hash primitives in the interpreter (splitmix64 for ints, FNV-1a for strings, both masked to 62 bits via `MARCH_HASH_MASK` so the result fits the interpreter's native int) — for ALL types, not just records (`hash(42)` diverged 395478795 vs -6387817139659442654 pre-restore). Restored via `git cherry-pick c30161d7` (eval.ml `march_hash_int64`/`march_hash_string64` + `hash` builtin rewiring, runtime `MARCH_HASH_MASK`, `test_properties.ml` un-skips the record-generator hash comparison); the golden `g51_hash_cross_backend` was dropped (golden corpus diverged to g46 in this tree) in favor of a `test/native` + oracle parity fixture. `interfaces.md`'s derive section rewritten to state the equality. **NOTE: this is the THIRD confirmed commit lost in the PR #27/#38 merge — a full merge-loss audit is warranted.**

  ~~Compiled and interpreted `hash()` use different, backend-specific algorithms with no cross-backend value equality for RECORD types — expected, but undocumented.~~ For `TDRecord`, derived `Hash`'s body (`expand_derive`, `lib/desugar/desugar.ml` "Hash" case) calls the polymorphic `hash()` builtin per field and combines the results. That builtin is genuinely backend-specific: interpreter uses OCaml's `Hashtbl.hash` (`lib/eval/eval.ml`); compiled uses a custom splitmix-style hash (`march_hash_int`/`march_hash_string`/etc., `runtime/march_runtime.c`). Confirmed by hand: `hash({x:1,y:2})` prints `28043382405` interpreted vs `6305855436935449413` compiled for the identical value — not a bug, just two independent hash implementations that were never meant to agree. (Derived `Hash` on a VARIANT type is NOT affected — its body is the bare constructor index as an integer literal, `ELit (LitInt i)`, no call to the `hash()` builtin at all, so it's trivially portable.) `syntax_reference.md`'s derived-Ord/Hash section documents the payload-ignoring semantics but doesn't mention the record-Hash cross-backend non-portability; worth a one-line addition so a future test author doesn't file it as a divergence. Differential-oracle Task 4's record derived-method generator (`gen_derived_method_record_module`, `test/test_properties.ml`) deliberately never prints `hash()`'s result for this reason (only `==`/`eq`/`compare`, all pure Int-field comparisons); the Newtype/Boxed/enum generators DO print `hash()` since those are all variant types (portable by construction, not by luck — verified by hand).

- ✅ **FIXED 2026-07-17: Tuples now have `Show` (compiled + interp consistent).** Tuples have no `Show` impl — compiled `println`/`to_string` on any tuple is broken (link failure or garbage output).** stdlib/prelude.march defines `impl Show(List(a))`, `impl Show(Option(a))`, `impl Show(Result(a,e))` but no `impl Show` for tuples. `println((1, 2))` fails to even LINK compiled (`Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: "_show"` — the bare `show` call inside `println`'s prelude body never resolves for a tuple argument type). `to_string((1, 2))` compiles and runs but prints garbage: `#<tag:0>` instead of `(1, 2)`. Interpreted mode is correct in both cases (`value_to_string`'s `VTuple` case, `lib/eval/eval.ml`, produces `"(1, 2)"` exactly — confirmed by an existing test, `test/test_eval.ml:330`). **INVESTIGATED 2026-07-17 (after item 347's to_string→Show fix):** the blocker is the DISPATCH, not a missing impl. `impl Show((a, b))` written in source PARSES, TYPECHECKS, and works INTERPRETED, but the compiled path still fails to link `_show` — `resolve_iface_method` (`lib/tir/lower.ml`) keys the Show dispatch on a NOMINAL `TCon` name, and a tuple is structural (`TTuple`) with no name to key on, so neither a user impl nor a synthesized one is found for a tuple value. Fix approach: teach the show/to_string dispatch to handle `TTuple` — synthesize a per-arity tuple `show` at lowering (`"(" ++ show(e0) ++ ", " ++ show(e1) ++ ")"`, mirroring the interpreter's `VTuple` case) so mono specializes each element's show; the runtime cannot do it (no element-type info at a raw ptr). Not a quick patch — a lowering/dispatch change. Repro:
  ```march
  mod Main do
    fn main() do
      println((1, 2))   -- compiled: link error "Undefined symbols: _show"
    end
  end
  ```
  and, compiling successfully but wrong:
  ```march
  mod Main do
    fn main() do
      print(to_string((1, 2)))  -- interp: "(1, 2)"   compiled: "#<tag:0>"
      print("\n")
    end
  end
  ```
  Fix needs either a dedicated `impl Show` for tuples (stdlib, if tuple types can be named in an `impl` head) or, more likely, a compiler-level special case in the `to_string`/`show` dispatch (`lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`'s builtin `to_string` dispatch and/or mono's interface-impl resolution) that renders tuple element-wise like the interpreter does. Differential-oracle Task 3 (`test/test_properties.ml`) deliberately excludes tuple-container generators from `gen_well_typed_module` to avoid reddening the oracle on this pre-existing bug; a tuple generator can be added once this is fixed.
- ✅ **FIXED 2026-07-18 (items 347+465, mono dangling-TVar): bare unpinned `None` link failure + `mangle_ty $V_<n>` gap.** A residual (dangling) TVar left in a specialization — the element type of a bare `None`, never pinned — made mono mint a DISTINCT `Show$Option.show$Option_V__<n>` per fresh var id, whose inner element `show` was unresolvable → `_show` undefined, link failure. Fix: `default_residual_tvars` in `lib/tir/mono.ml` rewrites any residual `TVar` (except the `"_"` lowering placeholder) to `String` in the specialization subst, at BOTH `build_subst` sites (the EApp path + `enqueue_specialized_impl`) plus a `TUnit`/`TString` type-name mapping so the iface dispatch resolves. **Why `String` and not `Int`/`Unit`:** a residual TVar can still type a REAL erased value (a boxed heap pointer whose type merely wasn't concretized); `Int`'s tagged-immediate repr made RC treat that pointer as a tagged int (incrc on even Int ≥ 4096 SIGSEGVs — the erased-int hazard; broke Vault/record_put adversarials + g44_crdt), and `Unit`'s niche repr SIGSEGV'd the `Option(Unit)` decode. `String` shares the heap-ptr repr the erased value already has with IS_HEAP_PTR-guarded dup/drop. Verified: bare `None`/`to_string(None)`/annotated/`match`/list-of-None all interp==compiled, ASAN clean; eval 233 / compiler 514 / snapshots 29 / codegen 421 / stdlib 809 / oracle 0 un-triaged / types 166. Witnesses `accept/t86_bare_none_unpinned`, `test/native/bare_none_print.march` (oracle anchor). Original diagnosis: **A bare/unpinned `None` (no `Some(_)` of the same element type at the SAME call site) fails to LINK compiled — even with an explicit type annotation.** `println(None)` fails compiled with `Undefined symbols: _show` regardless of whether `None` carries an explicit `Option(Int)` annotation (`let x : Option(Int) = None; println(x)` fails identically). This is NOT fixed by a `Some(_)` of the same type appearing elsewhere in the program (even in an immediately preceding statement) — mono resolves each `println`/`show` call site's `Show$Option` specialization independently from its own static argument type, not globally across the module, so a sibling `Some` does not "pin" the type for a separate `None` call. `None` DOES compile correctly when it appears inside a list literal alongside a `Some(_)` in the SAME call site, e.g. `println([Some(1), None, Some(3)])` (this is the exact repro `ffe6fba8`'s own regression test uses and IS green). **INVESTIGATED 2026-07-17:** the ANNOTATED case now COMPILES CORRECTLY (`let x : Option(Int) = None; println(x)` → `None`); only a truly-unpinned bare `println(None)` still fails, with `_show` referenced from `Show$Option.show$Option_V__35118` — a DANGLING TVAR in the specialization (the element type is never pinned, so mono mangles `V__<n>` and the inner element-`show` reference is unresolvable). This is the same root cause as the P1 mono item ('build_subst/match_ty can bind a type param to a dangling non-`_` TVar → mangle_ty produces a `$V_<n>` name'). For `None` the element type is provably UNOBSERVED (no value flows through it), so the safe fix is to default a dangling type argument to a canonical Show/Eq/…-having concrete type (`Unit`) at the mono specialization point — BEFORE both mangling and inner-impl enqueue, so they stay consistent — which also closes the P1 gap. Deep mono hot-path change (miscompile/golden risk); do NOT rush. **ATTEMPT 2026-07-17 (defaulting works, second gap found; reverted):** added `default_residual_tvars` in mono (TVar→Unit) applied to the specialization subst at both `build_subst` sites (the EApp `Some orig_fn` path AND `enqueue_specialized_impl`). This DOES concretize the mangle — the symbol went from `Show$Option.show$Option_V__35196` to `Show$Option.show$Option_Unit`, and `fn println$Option_Unit(x : Option(Unit))` is emitted. BUT a SECOND gap surfaced: inside the re-processed specialized body, `show(x)` with the now-concrete `x : Option(Unit)` STAYS BARE — mono does not re-resolve the iface-method call when it re-emits a specialized generic body, so `Show$Option.show$Option_Unit` is REFERENCED but never emitted (link error moves from `_show` to `_Show$Option.show$Option_Unit`). So the full fix needs (a) the residual-TVar defaulting AND (b) iface-method re-resolution on re-enqueued specialized bodies. Reverted (build cycles ~10min made iteration impractical this session); the defaulting helper is the right first half. Repro (fails):
  ```march
  mod Main do
    fn main() do
      let x : Option(Int) = None
      println(x)   -- link error: Undefined symbols: _show
    end
  end
  ```
  Likely same root cause as the two entries above (mono's interface-impl specialization needs a concrete element type to resolve `Show$Option.show`, and a lone `None` carries none at the call site — even a static annotation on the binding doesn't flow into the specialization). `test/test_properties.ml`'s new generic-container generators (Differential Oracle Task 3) deliberately never emit a bare `None` for this reason — every `Option` print is `Some(n)`, and every `None` appears only inside a mixed `[Some(...), None, ...]` list literal.

ORIGINAL FINDING (test harness gap, not a compiler bug): Found during Task 4 verification (full-suite run), root-caused, confirmed to reproduce identically on the unmodified pre-Task-4 file (a byte-for-byte copy of `git show HEAD:test/test_properties.ml` with the same probe hook reproduces it), so this is NOT a Task 4 regression and NOT caused by the derived-method generators. `pipeline_up_to_typecheck` (`test_properties.ml:32`) calls `March_typecheck.Typecheck.check_module` directly on the bare parsed+desugared module — no stdlib `.march` files are ever loaded into the typecheck env (unlike the `--check`/`--compile` CLI paths, which auto-discover and link stdlib's `prelude.march` `impl Show(List(a))` etc. via `MARCH_LIB_PATH`/default stdlib discovery). Since `prop_generated_programs_are_well_typed` runs at `~count:500` over the full `gen_well_typed_module` pool, this was latent since Task 3 landed the `println(<container>)` generators — the random draw simply didn't hit this specific interaction until now (QCheck shrinking easily finds it once triggered: shrunk to `println([0])` in 4 steps). Fix options: (a) give `pipeline_up_to_typecheck` a pre-built stdlib-loaded env (there is a `check_module_with_env` entry point in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml` for exactly this) and thread it through the no-crash/well-typed properties that use `gen_well_typed_module`, or (b) scope `prop_generated_programs_are_well_typed` to only the generator subset that doesn't call interface-dispatched builtins (`println`/`to_string` on non-primitive types), mirroring how the dedicated `prop_oracle_*` properties already avoid this by going through the full CLI (`oracle_check`) which DOES load stdlib. Not fixed as part of Task 4 (out of scope — Task 4 touches only the derived-method generators, all of which print via `bool_to_string`/`int_to_string` first and never hit this path).

### Compiler (found during Wave 4 Task 5 semantics-notes verification, 2026-07-03)

- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED for TOP-LEVEL (2026-07-15, open-items plan Phase 7.1) — a top-level default-arg function is now callable by name from March source at every arity, both backends.** Fix (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, general `EApp` arm): before inferring the callee, a call of an UNBOUND bare/qualified name `foo(args)` is redirected to its `foo$<n_args>` arity variant when that variant is in scope (matching `expand_defaults_decl`'s `%s$%d` mangling, keyed on the number of supplied args). Typing-only — the interpreter (`VMultiarity`) and TIR (`_default_dispatch`) already lower the original `foo(args)` downstream; the typechecker simply no longer errors before they run. Verified: `greet("Bob")` / `greet("Al","Yo")` / `greet("Cy","Hey","?")` all resolve and apply the right defaults on interp AND compiled. Regression: `test_compiled_default_args_parity` (`test/test_codegen.ml`, `assert_compiled_interp_parity` at all three arities). **NESTED-module default-arg fns also RESOLVED (2026-07-15, same slice) — three coordinated fixes:** (part 2) `expand_defaults_decl` now recurses into `DMod` so a nested default-arg fn gets its `foo$N` variants (was dropping defaults via `desugar_fn_def`'s tuple-UAF fast-path); (part 3a) `eval.ml`'s nested-module `eval_mod_decls` now performs the same `foo$N`→base-name `VMultiarity` reconstruction the top-level `make_recursive_env` does; (part 3b) the module-member EXPOSURE (`declared_names`) now also exports the base name of a mangled `foo$N` decl so the reconstructed `Inner.foo` is prefixed to `A.Inner.foo`. Verified `Inner.f(1)` (default) / `Inner.f(2,20)` (full) on BOTH backends at 2- and 3-deep nesting. Regression: `test_compiled_nested_default_args_parity`. ORIGINAL FINDING: A source-level call to a default-arg function's own name fails typecheck with ``I cannot find `add`.`` under `--check`, `--compile`, and plain interpretation alike — at every arity including full:
  ```march
  mod Main do
    fn add(x, y \\ 10, z \\ 20) do x + y + z end
    fn main() do
      println(int_to_string(add(1, 5, 6)))   -- I cannot find `add`.  (exit 1)
    end
  end
  ```
  Root cause: `expand_defaults_decl` (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`) deliberately emits ONLY mangled `add$1`/`add$2`/`add$3` decls — no bare-name dispatcher decl (its doc comment: the interpreter's env-builder auto-creates `VMultiarity` entries for the base name from the `foo$N` pattern, and the TIR lowering rewrites call sites via `_default_dispatch` in `lib/tir/lower.ml`). But the TYPECHECKER runs between desugar and both of those consumers, binds each `DFn` under its literal post-desugar name only (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`), and has no equivalent arity-dispatch reconstruction — so bare `add` is never in scope and every source-level call dies before eval or TIR ever run. **Test gap that hid this:** every existing default-arg test (`test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`: `test_default_arg_used`, `test_default_arg_overridden`, `test_default_multiple_defaults`) invokes the function from the OCaml harness via `call_fn env "greet" [...]`, which bypasses source-level name resolution entirely; `test_default_arg_typechecks` only checks the *definition* typechecks, not a call site. No test in the tree contains a March-source call to a default-arg function. (The `greet("World")` example in `syntax_reference.md` § Functions does not compile today.) Fix should add a source-level call-site test at every arity, top-level AND nested. Related, distinct: nested-module default-arg fns additionally DROP their default values entirely (`desugar_fn_def`'s `FPDefault` fast path — "nested default-arg dispatch was never wired up"), so even after the typecheck gap is fixed, nested reduced-arity calls will still fail. Doc note: `syntax_reference.md` § "Semantics notes → Nested-module default-arg functions".

### Runtime / stdlib

- ✅ **Signal-handler API (`Signal.watch`) — IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-16, Phase 7.2, both backends).**
  New `stdlib/signal.march`: `mod Signal do type Sig = Term|Int|Hup|Usr1|Usr2; watch(sig, handler : () -> ())`,
  `unwatch(sig)`, `raise(sig)` — `needs IO.Signal`.  Deferred green-thread dispatch: the OS handler
  only flips atomic pending flags (async-signal-safe), and a drain point runs the March closure on a
  normal stack (interpreter: `run_scheduler`; compiled: `sched_loop` body + a final drain in
  `march_sched_run`).  Term/Int suppress the default graceful shutdown on the first delivery and escape
  to shutdown (`g_http_shutdown`) on the second; Hup/Usr2 have no default action while watched.
  **Compiled caveat:** SIGUSR1 is reserved by the scheduler's green-thread preemption
  (`march_scheduler.c`), so watching `Usr1` in a compiled program is refused with a one-line stderr
  note (it works in the interpreter, which has no preemption).  New `IO.Signal` capability
  (`cap_lattice.ml` + typecheck cap table/`builtin_types`); `signal_watch`/`signal_unwatch`/
  `signal_raise_self` builtins wired through purity, defun `builtin_names`, and codegen
  (`llvm_emit.ml` extern calls + preamble declares); the watcher closure is passed OWNED so the
  runtime keeps its reference across drains.  `g_http_shutdown` moved to a weak def in
  `march_runtime.c` (strong in `march_http.c`) so the REPL/JIT runtime-only build links.  Tests:
  `test/test_eval.ml` (drain/coalesce/unwatch via a USR1 self-raise) + native goldens
  `test/native/signal_watch.march` (USR2 drain) and `signal_term_suppress.march` (watched TERM
  survives).  ASAN-clean; existing HTTP-shutdown paths unaffected (unwatched TERM still exits 143).
  Design: `specs/2026-07-02-signal-handler-api.md`; execution sub-plan:
  `specs/plans/2026-07-16-signal-watch-execution-subplan.md`.

- ✅ **`Session` stdlib middleware module** — `stdlib/session.march`: cookie-backed (`:cookie`) and Vault-backed (`:vault`) session middleware. `:cookie` stores full session data in a signed browser cookie; `:vault` stores only session ID in cookie with data in `Vault`. Signing: HMAC-SHA256 via `pbkdf2_sha256` key derivation from `Config.secret_key_base` + per-cookie-name salt; cookie format `base64(payload).base64(hmac)`; tampered cookies silently start fresh sessions. Public API: `Session.load(conn, backend)` middleware plug; `Session.save(conn)` / `Session.save_with_opts(conn, opts)` (supports `max_age`, `secure`, `same_site`, `path`, `HttpOnly`); `Session.get/put/delete/clear/all`; `Session.put_flash/get_flash` one-request flash messages (sweep on `save`, unread flash survives). Session data serialised as `key\x1Fval\x1Ekey\x1Fval` strings for storage in Conn string assigns. 49 tests in `test/stdlib/test_session.march`.

- ✅ **Shell completions + external subcommands** — `forge completions bash|zsh|fish` prints a ready-to-source completion script; `forge-<cmd>` binaries on PATH are exec'd when `<cmd>` is not a built-in (built-ins always win). `forge/lib/cli_ext.ml` (pure `completion_script`/`external_subcommand`, 6 unit tests). Item #5 of `specs/forge_tooling_roadmap.md`.
- ✅ **`forge watch`** — reruns build/test/run on source changes (polls `lib/ src/ test/ config/` + `forge.toml`); never exits on failure. `forge/lib/watcher.ml` (pure `changed`, 5 unit tests) + `cmd_watch.ml`. Item #1 of `specs/forge_tooling_roadmap.md`.
- ✅ **`forge build --target js` / `forge run --compiled --target js` (2026-06-22)** — `forge build --target js` compiles the project entry to an ES module (`.mjs`) under `.march/build/{debug,release}/<name>.mjs`; the compiler auto-copies `march_runtime.mjs` + `march_dom.mjs` alongside it. `forge run --compiled --target js` builds the `.mjs` and runs it with `node`. All other targets (`native`, `wasm*`) unchanged — `?target` defaults to `None` so existing call-sites (`forge test`, `forge release`, `forge watch`) are unaffected. `forge/bin/main.ml` + `forge/lib/cmd_build.ml` + `forge/lib/cmd_run.ml`.
- ✅ **`forge bench`** — compiles + runs `bench/*.march` at `--opt 2`, reports wall-clock times (table or `--json`), name-substring filter. `forge/lib/cmd_bench.ml` (pure `bench_name`/`matches`/`format_results`, 4 unit tests). Item #2 of the tooling roadmap.
- ✅ **`forge version` / `forge release`** — bump `[package].version` (patch/minor/major or explicit), `--tag` commits + tags `vX.Y.Z`; `release` gates clean→build→test→bump+tag. `forge/lib/versioning.ml` (pure `bump`/`rewrite_version_line`, 5 unit tests) + `cmd_version.ml`/`cmd_release.ml`. Item #3 of the tooling roadmap (fmt --check + lint CI already existed).

Item #4 of the tooling roadmap.

Three fixes in `bin/main.ml`: (1) `module_name_to_filename` extended to handle dotted names — `MyApp.Router` → `my_app/router.march`, `MyApp.Templates.Layout` → `my_app/templates/layout.march`; (2) `resolve_imports` now tracks loaded file paths (`loaded_paths` set) to prevent duplicate loads when explicit `use` and auto-discovery overlap; (3) auto-discovery: after resolving explicit imports, all `.march` files in `MARCH_LIB_PATH` dirs are loaded — sorted by module-name dot-depth (more dots = deeper namespace = fewer dependents = load first) so the evaluator sees dependencies before their users (`Templates.Page.Index` → `Templates.Layout` → `PageController` → `Router` → app root). Validated: full `Router.dispatch → PageController.index → Layout.wrap → Page.Index.render` chain works from a scaffolded `test_app_01` with `MARCH_LIB_PATH` set.
- ✅ **Forge dependency resolution and versioning system** — Full plan at `specs/plans/forge-dependency-resolution-plan.md`. Six implementation phases (Phases 1–6 complete): (1) Semver `~>` / `>=` / `<=` / `>` / `<` / exact / `AND` combinations (`resolver_version.ml`, `resolver_constraint.ml`); five dep source types (`RegistryDep`, `GitTagDep`, `GitBranchDep`, `GitRevDep`, `PathDep`); `forge.lock` TOML with manifest hash drift detection (`resolver_lockfile.ml`). (2) In-memory registry index; PubGrub greedy solver with FIFO work queue, conflict-driven incompatibility tracking, human-readable error messages (`resolver_pubgrub.ml`, `resolver_registry.ml`). (3) SHA-256 content-addressed package store — sorted canonical archive (`.git`/`.march` excluded, no timestamps), store/lookup/verify with tampering detection (`resolver_cas_package.ml`). (4) `[patch]` fork overrides — `GitBranchDep`/`PathDep` substitution before solver; extra patches for transitive deps; `forge deps` and `forge deps update`. (5) Text-based `.march` source API surface extraction (`pub fn`/`pub type`), diff (Added/Removed/Changed), MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH classification, semver enforcement in `forge publish --old-source` (`resolver_api_surface.ml`, `cmd_publish.ml`). (6) Property-based tests (QCheck, 200 cases × 3 properties), regression tests for Cargo/Hex/npm known bugs, solver performance benchmarks (chain-100: <100ms, chain-500: <1s, diamond-20×20: <500ms). Total: 132 forge tests across 6 suites.
- ✅ **Forge toolchain version manager (first slice)** — `forge toolchain install [<version>|nightly]` / `use` / `list` / `uninstall` over the shared `~/.march/{versions,current,bin}` layout (`forge/lib/toolchain.ml`), plus the `install.sh` curl installer. ## P2 — Important / Near-Term

- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15, open-items plan Wave A) — entry file self-qualifying its own top-level mod name now resolves on BOTH backends.** Fix (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`): `desugar_module` runs a new `strip_entry_self_qual` pass on the entry module before `qualify_module_refs`, stripping only the single leading `<entry_mod_name>.` segment from every `EVar` (`Foo.wrapped → wrapped`; nested `Outer.Inner.wrapped → Inner.wrapped`, so the nested `Inner.` survives to match the still-qualified nested definition). Because desugar output feeds both interp and codegen, this fixes both backends uniformly. Regression: 3 `assert_compiled_interp_parity` tests in `test/test_codegen.ml` (single-level, nested, and an over-stripping guard — `wrapped(5)`/`Inner.wrapped(5)` must still resolve). Verified: interp + compiled both print `6`. ORIGINAL FINDING (2026-07-07): found alongside the `qualify_module_refs` two-level-nesting fix (see Done section) but deliberately left unfixed there (narrower, lower-impact). Repro: `mod Outer do mod Inner do fn helper(x) do x + 1 end fn wrapped(x) do helper(x) end end fn main() do println(Outer.Inner.wrapped(5)) end end` compiled natively → `Undefined symbols: _Outer.Inner.wrapped`. TIR lowering correctly never includes the ENTRY file's own top-level mod name in emitted symbol names (it "unwraps" the entry module — `Inner.wrapped`, not `Outer.Inner.wrapped`), but the user explicitly wrote the reference WITH the redundant self-prefix (`Outer.Inner.wrapped` from within `Outer` itself), and nothing currently strips it back off before the reference reaches TIR — `Outer.Inner.wrapped` and `Inner.wrapped` never converge. A bare (`wrapped(5)`) or single-level-qualified (`Inner.wrapped(5)`) call from the same position works fine; only the explicit-self-prefix form breaks. Fix direction: either detect + strip a leading `entry_mod_name.` segment from a qualified `EVar`/call reference during desugar/lowering when it matches the entry module's own name, or (simpler, probably correct) just make TIR lowering ALSO accept/normalize the self-prefixed form as an alias for the bare one. Low real-world impact (unusual to redundantly type your own file's enclosing mod name when calling your own code), so not actioned this pass.
- ✅ **FIXED 2026-07-18 (with items 347/465): `mangle_ty` `$V_<n>` dangling-TVar gap.** mono: `build_subst`/`match_ty` can bind a type param to a dangling non-`"_"` TVar — `mangle_ty` silently produces a `...$V_<n>` "specialized" name** — latent gap in the shared specialization machinery, found in review of the Wave 2 Task 1 fix but **pre-existing**: `match_ty` will bind e.g. `a → TVar "_1456"` when the call-site argument type is itself still abstract (a real dangling var, not the `TVar "_"` lowering placeholder, which IS handled by the wildcard-preference logic), and `mangle_ty` renders it as `V__1456` — yielding a specialized name (e.g. `Show$List.show$List_V__1456`, or any ordinary generic fn's `foo$V__1456`) whose body still carries the unresolved element type. This affects the **pre-existing generic-fn EApp specialization branch** just as much as the interface-impl `enqueue_specialized_impl` path added in Wave 2 Task 1 — both feed `build_subst` output straight into `mangle_name`. Downstream consequences today: the nested method call inside such a body stays unresolvable, and (post-Wave-2) trips the loud `fail_if_unresolved_iface_method` failwith in llvm_emit rather than miscompiling; the fresh-name-derived `V_<n>` suffix is also compile-order-dependent, which could make emitted symbol names nondeterministic across compiles. **No concrete trigger program was found (reviewer tried)** — `match_ty`'s concrete-over-TVar binding preference covers the observed cases — so this is hardening, not a live bug: consider having `build_subst` (or its two consumers) drop/reject bindings whose RHS still `has_tvar`, or mangle them to a canonical erased marker instead of `V_<n>`. — RESOLVED: `default_residual_tvars` concretizes a residual dangling `TVar` to `String` in the mono specialization subst, so `mangle_ty` never emits a `$V_<n>` name; see the bare-`None` fix entry.
- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15, open-items plan Wave A) — guarded match arms now share ONE fallback join point.** Fix (`lib/tir/lower_match.ml`): the guarded-match path hoists `rest_expr` (the remaining-arms tail) into a single 0-arg join point via the extracted `hoist_fallback_jp` helper and references the SAME `EApp(clo_var, [])` in both the guard-fail default and the pattern-fail fallback (calling `compile_matrix_impl` directly so the fallback is not re-hoisted). A `needs_fallback` guard skips the closure entirely when the tail is dead (unguarded trivial final arm). The `guard_match` perceus snapshot drops from ~7 closure types / 9 fns (jp/Clo refs 35) to 2 closures (10 refs). Behavior unchanged: `classify(5/-3/0)` still prints `pos/neg/zero` on interp AND compiled (new `assert_compiled_interp_parity` guard). Snapshots regenerated. ORIGINAL FINDING: found during Wave 2 Task 5 bookkeeping, reading `test/snapshots/perceus/guard_match.expected` (the golden snapshot for `classify(x)`'s 3 guarded arms, `n > 0` / `n < 0` / fallback `"zero"`). The dump shows **7 separate join-point closure types (`$Clo_$jp11$0`, `$Clo_$jp6$1`, `$Clo_$jp1$2` through `$Clo_$jp1$6`) and 9 functions**, with `$jp1$apply$2`, `$jp1$apply$3`, `$jp1$apply$5`, `$jp1$apply$6` all being byte-identical `panic("non-exhaustive pattern match")` bodies and `$jp6$apply$1`/`$jp6$apply$4` both being byte-identical `"zero"` bodies — despite `lower.ml`'s own doc comment on the join-point mechanism claiming it exists specifically to share the fallback body "once... instead of being duplicated 4× per nesting level." The guard-desugaring path appears to re-lower a fresh join point per guard check in the chain rather than threading one shared join point through all of them. This is IR bloat, not a correctness issue (all three guard values 5/-3/0 produce correct compiled output, per Wave 2 Task 4's audit) — relates to the Wave-1 analysis §4 Medium finding "guarded matches duplicate the rest-tree per arm" (`specs/analysis/2026-07-01-pipeline-deep-review.md`), which this snapshot now gives a concrete, reproducible, human-auditable artifact for. Worth a look if TIR size becomes relevant for guard-heavy code; not fixed here (test-infra/bookkeeping task, `lib/tir/lower.ml` out of scope).
- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15, open-items plan Wave A) — `MARCH_LIB_PATH` auto-discovery now prunes unreachable modules; a broken UNRELATED module no longer blocks the build.** Fix (`lib/resolver/resolver.ml`, option (a) reachability pruning): Step-2 auto-discovery only builds a library module the entry can actually reach — directly or transitively — seeded from the entry + explicitly-imported module sources, using an OVER-approximating textual module-name reference scan (`referenced_name_tokens`, identifier/dot runs + every dot-prefix) so the only error direction is keeping an unused module, never dropping a reachable one. Modules with GLOBAL effect (`impl`/`interface`/`protocol`/`deriving`/`transitions`/`extern`, via `has_global_effect_decl`) are NEVER pruned since they can be used without being named; type names + their constructors are also reachability anchors (`provided_anchor_names`, since March registers ctors program-wide). Verified: an entry using only `GoodLib` (which transitively calls `MidLib`) builds+runs clean with an unreferenced ill-typed `Broken` present (transitive `MidLib` NOT pruned); an entry that DOES reference `Broken` still errors. Also cuts compile time on large multi-file projects. ORIGINAL FINDING: March's multi-file compilation model (see `CLAUDE.md` "Multi-file compilation") walks ALL `.march` files under every `MARCH_LIB_PATH` directory recursively and loads their modules automatically; there is no reachability analysis from the entry file, so a compile error in a module the entry never imports or calls still fails the whole build. Demonstrated harmful in practice on 2026-07-02 (the "march_bin B9-regression incident," see `specs/todos.md`'s B9-regression hotfix entry and deciduous nodes 1556–1558): an unrelated bastion module's compile error under `MARCH_LIB_PATH` blocked all `forgepm` builds even though nothing in the actual build target depended on that module. Wants either (a) reachability-based module pruning — only typecheck/lower modules transitively imported from the entry file — or (b) per-module compile isolation so one module's failure doesn't abort sibling modules' compilation/reporting. Either direction is a `bin/main.ml`/resolver-level change (`resolve_imports`, auto-discovery phase) outside this bookkeeping task's scope. **Also a compile-speed opportunity (2026-07-07):** pruning to only transitively-reachable modules would cut per-invocation compile time on large multi-file projects (fewer files parsed/typechecked/lowered per build), not just improve blast-radius isolation — surfaced while scoping a persistent-daemon perf plan (`specs/plans/2026-07-07-compiler-daemon-perf-plan.md`) as the "bigger, riskier" alternative to daemon caching.
- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15) — `opaque type`'s constructor-hiding is now enforced against a qualified constructor reference from a separate compilation unit.** Fix: gate the bare module-qualified ctor key (`add_ctor qctor ci`) on `v.var_vis = Ast.Public` at BOTH Pass-1 prebind sites (`prebind_mod_members` and `prebind_mod_members_inc` in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`), mirroring the already-gated disambiguated `Mod.Type.Ctor` key. A private opaque ctor is no longer seeded into the Pass-1 forward-reference env, so the ungated bare key can no longer survive the `StrMap.union` with the correctly-filtered Pass-2 DMod export. Regression tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`resolver` group): `OqToken.Token("direct-bypass")` from a sibling now rejects (exit 1); the `oq_entry.march` control (qualified name as a TYPE annotation + public `make`/`value` accessors) still accepts (exit 0); a PUBLIC variant's `Mod.Ctor(..)` still resolves cross-module. ORIGINAL FINDING: the SAME class of bug Task 1 fixed for `ExFn`/`ExValue`, but on a different registration path. Found while widening the modules/visibility reference (`specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.5, widening slice 2 Task 3) and verifying the opaque-type asymmetry live. Root cause: `prebind_mod_members` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml:8032–8087`, a Pass-1 forward-reference pass run for every sibling `DMod` and the entry module's own top-level types) registers each variant's qualified constructor key (`"Mod.CtorName"`) via `add_ctor qctor ci acc.ctors` (`:8056`) **unconditionally on `v.var_vis`** — only the separate disambiguated `"Mod.TypeName.CtorName"` key a few lines later checks `v.var_vis <> Ast.Public` before registering (`:8065–8070`). This Pass-1 registration runs BEFORE `check_decl`'s `DMod` arm computes its own, correctly `ci_vis`-filtered `new_ctors`/`qual_ctors` (the same `pub_set`-gated export step Task 1's `ExFn`/`ExValue` fix lives beside), and the two results are MERGED (`typecheck.ml:6963–6969`, `StrMap.union` prepending the later pass's entries onto the earlier one's) rather than the later pass's filtering replacing the earlier — so the Pass-1 ungated entry for the bare qualified key survives into the final environment regardless. Live-verified against `test/imports/opaque_qual/{oq_token,oq_entry}.march` (a genuine `MARCH_LIB_PATH`-discovered `opaque type Token = Token(String)`): `OqToken.Token("direct-bypass")` from unrelated code typechecks (exit 0) AND runs, constructing a real value that matches its own pattern and prints `"direct-bypass"` — even though `opaque type`'s grammar rule (`parser.mly:436–440`) DOES force `var_vis = Private` on the constructor (confirmed `ci_vis = Private` is correctly set at registration; the gap is that an EARLIER, ungated registration site shadows the later, correctly-gated one, not that the visibility flag itself is wrong). The PatCon (pattern-matching) side is differently, and also incorrectly, affected: matching `Mod.Ctor(…)` against a value produced by the module's own public API hits the unrelated, separately-filed qualified-type-unification gap for match scrutinees instead of a visibility diagnostic. Not fixed here — out of the docs-only widening slice's scope and beyond Task 1's `load_module_into_env` fix (a different function, a different gate). `specs/lang/modules.md`'s "Visibility" section is corrected to match the current (not the intended) behavior in the same slice. **Related but distinct (checked 2026-07-21):** a separate `pfn`-privacy audit considered whether this bug's "ungated registration path" class also covered `pfn`/function privacy — it does not. The `pfn` case that slipped through (a same-file nested-module private fn whose bare name collides with an unrelated global, e.g. the `Hash` interface's built-in `hash`) traced to a wholly different mechanism, `EVar`'s dot-suffix fallback resolver having no floor, not an ungated registration site — both Pass-1 and Pass-2 already correctly refused to register a private `pfn`'s qualified name here too. See this file's Done section ("`pfn` privacy silently bypassed...").
- [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-05, commit `7e40dc5b`) — `ELetFn` (local recursive fn) with a return-type annotation that conflicts with its self-recursion-consistent body reports the identical diagnostic TWICE.** Fix in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`'s `ELetFn` arm: measure the `env.errors` diagnostic count before/after the return-annotation `unify body_ty expected`; if it grew, run the later self-type reconciliation `unify fn_ty arrow_ty` against a scratch (discarded) error context so its type-linking side effects still happen but the duplicate report is suppressed. A genuinely distinct error from the self-reference (which grows the count on the arrow unify but not the return unify) is still surfaced. Verified via `--check-json`: the canonical `t12` witness now emits ONE diagnostic (was two); a program with two distinct errors still reports both. Unit tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`letfn_ret_annot` group). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §4.1 finding 13 (marked RESOLVED). ORIGINAL FINDING: found while building `specs/lang/types/reject/t12_letfn_ret_annot_conflict.march` for the Core March typing spec (Task 5, `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2 (T-LetFn)). Repro: `fn go(k) : Int do match k do 0 -> "done" _ -> go(k - 1) end end` nested inside another fn — `--check-json` emits two byte-identical `{"message":"expected \`Int\` but got \`String\`."}` diagnostics at the same span. Root cause: `infer_block`'s `ELetFn` arm (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml:4371–4399`) unifies the return annotation against the inferred body type once directly (`unify body_ty expected`, :4392 — reports the mismatch) and, independently, unifies the self-reference placeholder `β` against the completed arrow type (`unify fn_ty arrow_ty`, :4396) — but the in-body recursive call already bound `β` to `params → body_ty` via T-App's `TVar` case (:4253–4259), so the second unify rediscovers the SAME conflict through `β`'s arrow and reports it again. Purely cosmetic — does not affect `check_types.sh` (substring-containment + exit code both still correct) and does not reproduce for the equivalent TOP-LEVEL `fn go(n) : Int` (`check_fn`'s single `unify` against `fn_ret_ty` reports once, with a BETTER message pinpointing the offending branch: "This is the declared return type of `go`."). Fix direction: either suppress the second `unify`'s report when the first already errored on the same pair (e.g. an error-tolerant sentinel), or route `ELetFn`'s return-annotation check through the same per-branch-pointing mechanism `check_fn` uses instead of a bare post-hoc `unify`. Not fixed here (docs-only spec task).

### Stdlib hardening: Phase 5 — missing high-demand APIs

Spec: `specs/2026-04-14-stdlib-phase5-plan.md`.  These are *new
functionality* gaps left after Phase 0–4 closed every blocker, security
finding, and convention drift.  Listed in the recommended order.

- ✅ **Logger v2 — structured fields, tracing, appenders** — Replaced
  the `println`-with-severity v1 logger with: rich `LogValue` field
  type (Str/Int/Float/Bool/Atom/Null), pluggable
  appenders+formatters (`format_text` / `format_logfmt` /
  `format_json`), per-module level overrides, scoped context
  (`with_scope` with auto-pop on panic via `try_finally`), tracing
  helpers (`with_span`, `with_trace_context`,
  `current_trace_id`/`current_span_id`).  JSON formatter is
  OpenTelemetry-friendly — `trace_id`/`span_id`/`parent_span_id`
  appear at the top level; everything else under `attributes`.
  Field deduplication ensures nested scopes don't emit duplicate
  keys.  Backward-compatible with v1: existing `Logger.info`,
  `with_context`, `set_level` keep working unchanged.  Runtime adds
  11 new builtins.  4 new tests; `test_march` 1311 → 1315.  Spec:
  `specs/2026-04-14-logger-v2-design.md`.
- ✅ **Structured concurrency** — `Task.race`, `Task.any`,
  `Task.all_settled`, `Task.scope`, cancellation tokens, and
  `task_cancel_by_id`.  Runtime: signal-based preemption daemon
  (`SIGUSR1` via `pthread_kill`, 1 ms quantum), `march_cancel_token`
  ref-counted struct with `march_sched_spawn_with_cancel`.  Eval:
  `VCancelToken` value variant, `te_cancelled` flag on `task_entry`,
  five new builtins (`task_cancel_token_new`, `task_cancel`,
  `task_is_cancelled`, `task_spawn_with_cancel`, `task_cancel_by_id`).
  Typecheck: `CancelToken` type, `task_cancel_by_id` poly1 signature.
  Stdlib: `Task.race` (first wins, losers cancelled), `Task.any`
  (first Ok wins, all-Err → `Err(list)`), `Task.all_settled`
  (no short-circuit), `Task.scope` (Phase 1 pass-through; Phase 2+
  injects cancel token).  Tests: 24 in `test/stdlib/test_task.march`
  (100 % pass), 10 new alcotest cases in `test_march`
  (`test_march` 1320 → 1330).
- ✅ **`Test.assert_eq` / `assert_ne` (generic)** — `stdlib/test.march`:
  single generic `assert_eq(expected, actual, msg)` using structural `==`
  (which falls through to OCaml equality when no `Eq` impl is present).
  Works on ints, strings, bools, floats, tuples, records, ADT variants,
  lists, and arbitrary nestings.  Failure messages render both sides
  via `to_string`.  Counterpart `assert_ne`.  9 new tests in
  `test/stdlib/test_test.march` (the first test for the `Test` module
  itself).
- ✅ **`UUID.v7` / `v7_at` / `timestamp_ms`** — RFC 9562 time-ordered
  UUIDs for better B-tree locality than v4.  Runtime adds
  `uuid_v7` (CSPRNG + current unix_time_ms), `uuid_v7_at(unix_ms)`
  (pinned timestamp — useful for backfilling and deterministic
  tests), and `unix_time_ms()`.  Stdlib exposes `UUID.v7`, `UUID.v7_at`,
  and `UUID.timestamp_ms` (extracts the embedded millisecond stamp
  from v7 UUIDs, returns `None` for other versions).  Version = 7
  and variant = `10xx` bits set correctly.  String-sort order of v7
  UUIDs matches timestamp order — that's the whole point.  5 new
  tests in `test_march` `uuid stdlib` group.  1315 → 1320.
- ✅ **DateTime timezones — Phase A: fixed offsets** —
  `stdlib/datetime.march`: new `Tz(name, offset_seconds)` and
  `LocalDateTime(civil, tz)` ADTs.  Constructors:
  `utc_zone`, `fixed_zone(name, secs)`, `fixed_zone_hours(h)`,
  `fixed_zone_hm(h, m)` (auto-derives ISO label).  Accessors:
  `zone_name`, `zone_offset_seconds`, `format_offset` (`"Z"`,
  `"+HH:MM"`, `"-HH:MM"`).  Construction:
  `local_of`, `local_now`, `local_from_timestamp`,
  `local_from_utc`.  Conversion: `local_to_utc`,
  `local_to_timestamp`, `local_with_zone` (same instant, different
  wall clock).  Format extension: `local_format` adds `%z` (compact
  `+HHMM`), `%:z` (ISO `+HH:MM`/`Z`), `%Z` (zone name).  Parse:
  `parse_offset` accepts `2024-01-15T10:30:45Z`,
  `2024-01-15 10:30:45+05:30`, and the compact `±HHMM` form,
  rejecting anything without an offset suffix.  Phase B (DST-aware
  IANA zones) deferred — needs tzdata loading or hard-coded
  transition rules; the fixed-offset primitive shipping now is
  the substrate that approach will sit on top of.  11 new tests in
  `test_march` `stdlib_datetime` group; `test_march` 1330 → 1341.
- ✅ **Streams (`Seq.from_*` source constructors) — Phase A** —
  `stdlib/seq.march` gains the source-end primitives the existing
  transform/consume API was missing, all yielding the same
  church-encoded `Seq(a)` so they compose with `map`/`filter`/`take`/
  `batch`/`to_list`/`fold` exactly like `from_list`.  Adds:
  `from_string_lines(s)` (split by `"\n"`, trailing-newline-tolerant),
  `from_file_lines(path)` (lazy pull, auto-close on EOF; returns
  `Result(Seq, FileError)`), `from_file_chunks(path, size)` (lazy
  fixed-size byte chunks), `repeat(x, n)` (n copies), `iterate(seed,
  step, n)` (apply `step` n times, yielding seed first), `cycle(seq, n)`
  (concatenate seq with itself n times — re-folds source per cycle, so
  not safe for one-shot file/http sources), `batched(seq, n)` (alias for
  the existing `batch` to match the API name in the spec), and
  `unfold_until(seed, next, max)` (bounded `unfold` that stops at the
  smaller of `next=None` or `max` elements).  Documented limitation:
  because Seq is church-encoded, `take(seq, k)` reads the entire source
  to EOF (the consumer-side fold doesn't truly short-circuit); a real
  pull-stream representation (`Step(a) = Done | Yield(a, () -> Stream)`)
  is the planned Phase B follow-up, which would also enable
  `from_http` and `from_channel` streaming with proper back-pressure.
  TDD: 21 new tests in `test/stdlib/test_seq.march` exercising
  every new constructor + the lazy-take and EOF-close paths,
  added BEFORE the implementation as red-then-green.  test_seq
  101 → 122; test_stdlib_march 18 → 19 (now wires `test_seq.march`
  into the runner).
- ✅ **`Stats.quantile` / `quantiles` / `iqr` / `five_number_summary`**
  — `stdlib/stats.march`: `quantile(xs, q, method)` implements all 9
  Hyndman & Fan (1996) interpolation methods matching R's
  `quantile(type=k)` and numpy's `method=` argument
  (`InvertedCdf`, `AveragedInvertedCdf`, `ClosestObservation`,
  `InterpolatedInvertedCdf`, `Hazen`, `Weibull`, `Linear` [default],
  `MedianUnbiased`, `NormalUnbiased`).  Batched `quantiles(xs, qs,
  method)` sorts once.  `iqr(xs, method)` / `iqr_default(xs)`.
  `five_number_summary(xs, method)` returns `(min, Q1, median,
  Q3, max)`.  `quantile_default` is a `Linear` alias consistent with
  the existing `percentile`.  18 new tests in
  `test/stdlib/test_stats.march`, cross-checked against R reference
  values for each method.
- ✅ **`Random.normal` / `exponential` / `bernoulli` /
  `choice_weighted` / `choice`** — `stdlib/random.march`:
  `standard_normal(rng)` via Box-Muller; `normal(rng, mu, sigma)`;
  `exponential(rng, lambda)` via inverse-CDF; `bernoulli(rng, p)`;
  `choice(rng, xs)` uniform; `choice_weighted(rng,
  List((a, Float)))` with cumulative scan.  All samplers validate
  params (panic on `sigma<0`, `lambda<=0`, `p` out of
  `[0,1]`, negative or all-zero weights).  All return `(value,

- ✅ **Distributed algorithms — `Deque`, `VectorClock`, `Merkle`, `CRDT`, `ConsistentHash`** — Five new stdlib modules. `stdlib/deque.march`: functional double-ended queue with O(1) size tracking; banker's deque (two-list representation); `push_front/back`, `pop_front/back`, `peek_front/back`, `from_list`, `to_list`, `map`, `filter`, `fold_left`, `fold_right`, `concat`, `any`, `all`. `stdlib/vector_clock.march`: causal ordering for distributed actors via `Map(String, Int)`; `increment`, `merge` (component-wise max), `compare` → `ClockOrder = Before | After | Concurrent | Equal`, `happens_before`, `concurrent`, `advance`, `entries`, `sum`. `stdlib/merkle.march`: SHA-256 content-addressed tree; `MLeaf`/`MBranch` constructors; `leaf` (caller-supplied serializer), `branch`, `root_hash`, `build` (balanced from list), `diff` (tail-recursive work-list), `leaves`, `leaf_hashes`, `contains_hash`, `size`. `stdlib/crdt.march`: four CRDTs nested under `CRDT.*` — `GCounter` (grow-only counter, per-actor map), `PNCounter` (increment/decrement via two maps), `LWWRegister` (last-write-wins with VectorClock, left-bias on concurrent), `ORSet` (observed-remove set with UUID tags). `stdlib/consistent_hash.march`: sorted virtual-node ring with configurable replica count; `add`, `remove`, `get` (successor lookup with wraparound), `nodes`, `node_names`, `size`. 5 new test files; design spec: `specs/2026-06-20-distributed-algorithms-design.md`.

### LSP: Performance Insights

- ✅ **LSP Performance Insights — Phase 1 (AST-level)** — Three AST-only insights implemented: (1) tail call optimization — `tco_check` walks function bodies tracking tail position, emits `NonTailCall` Warning with blocking-op description and accumulator suggestion; (2) actor message copying — `send_copy_check` detects `ESend` calls with non-linear complex types, emits `ActorSendCopy` Warning; (3) closure capture size — `lambda_free_vars` + `closure_capture_check` emits `ClosureCapture` Hint when lambda closes over ≥3 values. `perf_insight` type + `perf_insights` field in `Analysis.t`. Wired into `diagnostics` and `perf_insight_at` hover query. 11 new LSP tests.
- ✅ **LSP Performance Insights — Phase 2 (AST heuristics)** — All three heuristics done: (1) memory reuse opportunities via single-use-allocation heuristic, surfaced as FBIP inlay hints (`♻ reused` / `⧉ copied` — see the "LSP semantic tokens + documentHighlight + FBIP inlays" entry below); (2) **indirect call detection** — `indirect_call_check` flags `EApp(EVar n, …)` where `n` is a parameter of the enclosing function (dispatched through a function pointer), `IndirectCall` kind, code `perf/indirect-call`; (3) **allocation in recursive arms** — `recursive_alloc_check` flags constructor/record/tuple allocations inside a match/if arm of a self-recursive function (`contains_call` detects self-recursion), `RecursiveAlloc` kind, code `perf/recursive-alloc`. Both are synchronous AST passes wired into `collect_perf_insights`, surfaced as Hint diagnostics + hover. +4 LSP tests. The `"march.inlayHints.performanceAnnotations"` client-config toggle also landed (`perf_annotations_from_settings` reads it from `workspace/didChangeConfiguration` into a server ref gating `inlay_hints_for ~perf_annotations`).
- ✅ **LSP Phase 5 — incremental typecheck engine** (`specs/plans/2026-06-13-lsp-incremental-engine.md`) — The dominant per-keystroke LSP cost was `analyse` re-running the whole-module typechecker over `stdlib @ deps @ user` on every edit. Now the stdlib is typechecked **once** into a cached base env (`lsp/lib/typecheck_cache.ml`: `base_env`/`derive`), and forge deps **once** into a deps env keyed by their content hash (`deps_env`/`clear_deps`); only the edited file's own decls are re-checked per edit, layered via the new `Tc.check_module_with_env_full` (env-returning incremental check; the REPL-JIT path now also exposes its final env). Mutable env state (`errors`/`type_map`/`pending_constraints`/`import_tracker`) is reset per analysis so the shared base is never polluted; `type_map` is copied so stdlib/dep span→type entries survive. Also: `run_tir_pass` insights memoized by source hash; `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` invalidates the workspace + deps caches; `did_change` debounced (coalesces keystroke bursts, version-guarded); JSON-RPC integration tests over stdio (`test_jsonrpc.ml`). The 159-test LSP suite stays green (identical hover/def/completion/diagnostics), proving the layered checker matches the whole-module checker. Deferred: a per-def in-file AST `sig_hash`/`impl_hash` firewall (Increment G) — needs full-AST canonical serialization and the dominant cost is already removed. 11 new tests (test_incremental + test_jsonrpc).
- ✅ **LSP parameter-name inlay hints at call sites** — `inlay_hints_for` gained `?param_names` (default on). For a call `rect(10, 20)` whose callee `rect` has params `width`/`height`, it emits `width:`/`height:` Parameter-kind inlays at the START of each positional argument. `build_param_name_map` builds a function-name → param-names table from the raw user AST (`t.decls`, recursing into `DMod`), reusing `clause_param_names`; only registers a function when clause-0 has a name for every param (avoids misaligned hints on pattern params). `callee_simple_name` resolves plain (`EVar`) and qualified (`EField`) callees; `walk_e`/`walk_decls` visit every `EApp` and pair params/args by position (arity-safe). Noise reduction (`suppress_param_hint`): single-arg calls suppressed; bare-identifier arg equal to the param name, or ending `.param`/`_param`, or a field access `x.param`, suppressed as redundant. Client toggle `march.inlayHints.parameterNames` (default ON) via `param_name_hints_from_settings` + server ref, mirroring the perf-annotations toggle. Limitation: only user-file functions; stdlib param names unavailable to the LSP. +6 LSP tests.

### Compiler: Capabilities/effects (found during Core March widening slice 5)

- [ ] **F1 — body-scanned IO caps are WARNING-only, not error; "absence of `needs` = machine-verified purity" holds only when authors thread `Cap(X)` through signatures.** Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.8.6 (capabilities widening, Task 2, 2026-07-07). Check 1b (`typecheck.ml:5588-5605`, `Err.warning_with_fix` at `:5596`) — a function BODY calling a `builtin_cap_table` builtin (`file_read`, `tls_connect`, `vault_set`, …) without a covering `needs` — is WARNING-only, not an error: `--check` exits 0. Contrast Check 1 (signature `Cap(X)`), Check 4 (transitive `use`), and Check 5 (extern `Cap(X)`), which are all true ERRORs, exit 1. So a module that calls IO builtins directly in a function body, never threading `Cap(X)` through any signature, is *warned*, not *rejected* — the guarantee "no `needs` declared ⇒ the function is pure" only holds at the ERROR-level signature/transitive/extern-cap surface, not at the body-call surface. `specs/lang/capabilities.md` overclaims this: `:69` ("The compiler enforces this transitively... the build fails"), and the prose framing around `:142`/`:312` ("There are no false positives"; "the type checker already enforces `needs` as an error") describes the body-call case as effectively error-level when it is warning-level in the actual implementation (the example text in those sections does correctly say "Warning"/"hint", but the surrounding claims overstate the guarantee). Verified live, both sides reproduced side by side: a `Cap(IO.FileRead)` signature with no `needs` rejects (`` `Cap(IO.FileRead)` used in module `Reader` but `IO.FileRead` is not declared in `needs`. ``, exit 1); a body call to `file_read` with no `needs` only emits a HINT + WARNING (`` function body calls a builtin that requires `Cap(IO.FileRead)` but `Reader` does not declare `needs IO.FileRead`. ``, exit 0). This is a design/enforcement gap, not a mechanical bug — Checks 1/4/5 themselves are sound and precise over the `builtin_cap_table` domain. - [x] ✅ **RESOLVED (2026-07-15, open-items plan Wave A) — the `--check` capability-narrowing HINT no longer fires nondeterministically.** Root cause (found empirically, differs from the original hash/traversal-order hypothesis): the `--check` CAS result cache (`bin/main.ml`) stored a "clean check" artifact after ANY successful check, INCLUDING runs that emitted warnings/hints; a later identical-source `--check` hit that cache and `exit 0` BEFORE the diagnostic-printing pass, so the HINT showed on the first (cache-miss) run and vanished on cache hits — reappearing ~1-in-N as the shared project-root CAS store was cleared. Fix: only cache a `--check` run that emitted NO user-facing diagnostics (`printed_user_diag` guard), so a cache hit provably means "clean, nothing to print" and its silent exit is byte-identical to a fresh run; files with warnings/hints are re-checked and print consistently. Plus defensive hardening: `lib/errors/errors.ml` `sorted` uses `stable_sort` with a total tiebreaker (span→severity→message); the two `fn_*capability_closures` `Hashtbl.fold`s in `typecheck.ml` are sorted by key. Verified: 5+ repeated `--check` runs of a `Cap(IO)`-hint module now produce byte-identical stderr with the HINT consistently present. ORIGINAL FINDING: found during capabilities widening Task 3 (2026-07-07), filed now. (Labeled distinctly from the sessions-slice "F7" linearity finding to avoid a shared-doc label collision.) The Check 3 narrowing HINT (emitted when a `Cap(IO)` root capability is used where a narrower sub-cap would suffice) is INCONSISTENT across repeated `--check` runs of the SAME binary on the SAME file: on `accept/t51`'s shape (a two-function `cap_narrow`-threading module) it appeared ~1 of 10 runs; a reduced repro (a single-function module with a bare unused `Cap(IO)` parameter, no `cap_narrow`) reproduces the same flakiness, so it is not `cap_narrow`-specific. Independently reproduced by the Task-3 reviewer (t51 HINT 0/80 runs vs `reject/t37` HINT 80/80 — the exact inconsistency). **The `--check` EXIT CODE is invariant** (accepts exit 0, rejects exit 1 with stable ERROR text every run), so NO corpus program depends on it and conformance is unaffected — but it is a real, previously-undocumented compiler nondeterminism (likely a hash/traversal-order dependence in the HINT-emission path). A determinism-quality follow-up. Documented in `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.8.10 + `specs/lang/types/INDEX.md` (t51 row). Not fixed here; the trigger was not isolated further.

The mechanism that DOES satisfy Check 6's return-type rule is `cap_narrow` — a call to `cap_narrow(cap)` where `cap : Cap(IO)`, at a call site typed `Cap(Db.Migrated)`, typechecks cleanly and mints the proof cap (`typecheck.ml`'s `cap_narrow` builtin is declared with a **polymorphic** return type, `Cap(IO) -> Cap(a)`, documented in `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.8.8 as "also the mechanism a proof-cap mint... uses to satisfy Check 6's return-type rule"). But `cap_narrow` is the SAME builtin used for ordinary least-privilege IO-cap narrowing (`Cap(IO) -> Cap(IO.Network)`, etc.) — nothing distinguishes "narrowing to a real IO sub-cap" from "minting an unrelated proof capability" at the type level, so the unforgeability properties `capabilities.md` documents ("only public functions of `mod Db` can mint it," "the runtime-provided `Cap(IO)` cannot produce it") do not actually hold: **live-verified**, a one-line `fn run_migrations(cap : Cap(IO)) : Cap(Db.Migrated) do cap_narrow(cap) end` — outside `mod Db`, given only an ordinary `needs IO` `Cap(IO)`, with **no `needs Db.Migrated` declared** — typechecks with `--check` exit 0 (only the unrelated Check-3 narrowing HINT fires, suggesting a narrower IO sub-cap; no error). So any code holding a plain `Cap(IO)` can mint any nominal proof capability by name, with zero declaration or provenance requirement, contradicting the tutorial's "unforgeable" claim. A genuine, narrow gap in the proof-cap mechanism (Check 6), not a doc bug — `capabilities.md` is reconciled (Task 7) to flag the documented idiom as a known mismatch pending a later proof-caps-focused slice; not fixed here (out of this docs-only slice's scope, and out of F2/F3's fix scope). - ✅ **Nested-module qualified-prebind type-erasure — a GENERAL type-soundness hole (proof-cap forge was one exploitation), FIXED (2026-07-08, `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml` `check_decl` DFn branch).** An adversarial second review of the proof-cap forge found the forge was rooted DEEPER than `cap_narrow`: `consume(id(cap))` where `fn id(x) do x end`, `cap : Cap(IO)`, `consume : Cap(Db.P) -> Int` typechecked at `--check` exit 0 with NO `cap_narrow` involved. **CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (not Cap-specific, not a `unify` bug):** `unify`'s `TCon` arm (`typecheck.ml`, `| TCon (n1,a1), TCon (n2,a2) ->`) is strict and never erases a `Cap` (or any) type argument — the forge never reaches it. The defect: an UNANNOTATED public fn defined inside a NESTED `mod` gets its QUALIFIED name (`Mod.fn`) prebound to a fresh `Mono (fresh_var 1)` by `prebind_mod_members` (`prebind_fn_scheme` returns `None` for an unannotated fn); desugar's `qualify_module_refs` (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`) rewrites every intra-nested-module reference to that qualified form (`App.id`); and `check_decl`'s DFn branch rebound ONLY the bare name — never the qualified one. So a sibling fn resolving `App.id` got the stale `Mono '_v` placeholder, which `infer_app`'s `TVar` branch turns into a decoupled `?a -> ?b`, **ERASING the type of anything laundered through it**. Proven GENERAL, not proof-cap-specific: a plain `Int` laundered through a nested unannotated `id` into a `String` parameter (`takes_str(id(12345))` with `takes_str(s:String)` calling `string_length`) `--check`ed exit 0 pre-fix — a genuine memory-safety break. Also erases ADT args (`Box(String)`→`Box(Int)`), IO-cap coercions (`Cap(IO)`→`Cap(IO.Network)`), at any nesting depth, through unannotated tuple/HOF factories. The single-module case, annotated helpers, and private (`pfn`) helpers were all already safe (no qualified placeholder / concrete prebind / no qualified prebind respectively). **THE FIX:** after `check_fn` computes the real scheme, `check_decl`'s DFn branch now also reconciles the qualified prebind — `if env.cap_qual_prefix <> "" then` rebind `cap_qual_prefix ^ "." ^ fn_name` to the real scheme, but ONLY when it is still a bare `Mono (TVar Unbound)` placeholder (an already-concrete scheme from `prebind_fn_scheme` or a default-arg sibling is left intact — mirrors `check_fn`'s pass-1 placeholder-reconciliation guard). `cap_qual_prefix` accumulates exactly as `prebind_mod_members`'s key does ("" at the entry module, then nested names, entry mod stripped), so it matches the desugared reference at every depth. The fix touches `unify` NOT AT ALL, so `cap_narrow` narrowing, the `needs` gate (`cap_subsumes`), the builtin cap schemes, and actor `Cap` dispatch are structurally untouched. **Batch-A `cap_narrow` taint machinery RETAINED (complementary, NOT subsumed):** the single-module `cap_narrow`-mints-a-proof-cap route (`consume(cap_narrow(cap))`) is rejected ONLY by Batch-A (`cap_producer_ivars` + `demote_to_monomorphic` + the `unify` proof-cap hook + gated `mint_cap`); that route is a genuine unbound-var-binds-to-a-proof-cap event a stricter `unify` cannot reject without also rejecting legit IO narrowing, so only Batch-A's proof-cap-target discriminator handles it. This fix does not and cannot replace it. **Tests:** 10 NON-VACUOUS cases in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`nested_mod_prebind_erasure` group) — 6 RED-pre-fix forge routes (Int→String, Box(String)→Box(Int), Cap(IO)→Cap(Db.P), Cap(IO)→Cap(IO.Network), 3-deep, tuple factory) all flip exit 0→1; a 7th RED case proves the fix RESTORES legit polymorphism (nested `id` at Int AND String errored pre-fix because the stale placeholder pinned to the first use — now accepts); 3 GREEN-STAYS-GREEN guards (nested `Cap(IO)` passthrough, annotated-`id`, private-`pfn`-`id`). Full six-runner suite GREEN (`scripts/run-tests.sh`, `$?=0`): run_compiler 467, run_eval 231, run_codegen 392 with the `llvm_ir_validity_gate` at 0 failures, run_stdlib full. Plan: `specs/plans/2026-07-08-strict-cap-unification-plan.md` (which, despite its filename, concludes strict Cap unification is unnecessary and the wrong fix). Report: `.superpowers/sdd/prebind-fix-report.md`. **[ROUND 2 — 2026-07-08, commit on top of 10249488]** An adversarial re-review found the round-1 `Unbound`-only guard left TWO residual erasures, both the same root (the qualified prebind must equal the fn's REAL body-checked scheme). **Critical #1 (order-dependent, forward reference):** with the unannotated helper defined AFTER its caller, the caller pins `App.id`'s prebind to its own decoupled use (a `Link`, not `Unbound`) before `id`'s DFn runs → the round-1 guard skipped, and a post-hoc rebind was too late (the caller was already checked). **Critical #2 (order-independent, distinct-tvar annotation):** `fn launder(x:a):b do x` gets a prebind from `prebind_fn_scheme` built purely from annotation SYNTAX (`a→b`, never unified against the body constraint `a~b`), which round-1 left intact (concrete-prebind skip). Both erased Int→String / Box / Cap. **The round-2 fix (two parts):** (1) `check_decl`'s DFn qualified rebind is now UNCONDITIONAL — it binds the qualified name to `check_fn`'s real body-checked scheme regardless of the prebind's shape (placeholder OR un-body-validated annotation), replacing the `Unbound`-only guard. **The round-1 guard was never actually needed for codegen safety** — the 8-fixture IR-gate regression attributed to the unguarded rebind during plan feasibility was a rsync-tree `test/native` stdlib-resolution artifact, NOT the rebind; verified in-worktree that the unconditional rebind keeps `llvm_ir_validity_gate` at 0 failures (mono/TIR key on the per-span `type_map`, not this env scheme). (2) Forward references are handled UPSTREAM in `dependency_order_dfn_run`: `free_vars_expr` now KEEPS dotted names (was dropping every `String.contains '.'`), and `deps_of`/`local_of` map a qualified body reference `App.id` to the local `id` by its suffix, so the helper is ordered BEFORE its caller and the rebind runs in time. (Both `free_vars_expr` callers are safe: `warn_unused_params` only compares against bare param names.) **Round-2 tests:** 8 more NON-VACUOUS cases in the `nested_mod_prebind_erasure` group (18 total) — C1 forward-ref (Int→String, Box, Cap) + C2 distinct-tvar (Int→String, Box, Cap), all RED on 10249488 (exit 0) / GREEN after; plus a forward-ref-legit-polymorphism guard (RED→GREEN: an unannotated forward-ref `id` used at two types spuriously errored pre-fix) and an annotated-`a→a` forward-ref guard.
