Also reproduced via a nested sibling referencing the entry module by name (`T.id` where `T` is the entry) at any depth. Bare `id` was always safe (desugar's `entry_prefix=""` never auto-qualifies bare refs); only the written `EntryMod.id` form triggered, but it is memory-unsafe when written. **The round-3 fix:** the DFn qualified-rebind now reconciles BOTH the `cap_qual_prefix`-based key (nested) AND the `current_module`-based key (`reconcile_qkey env env.current_module` when it differs from `cap_qual_prefix`) — so `EntryMod.id`, seeded under the entry module's own name with `cap_qual_prefix=""` but `current_module=EntryMod`, is now reconciled to the real body-checked scheme. **Seeding audit (close the CLASS):** every site that binds a `Mod.fn`-shaped fn key was checked — (1) `prebind_mod_members` nested prefix (`cap_qual_prefix.fn`) → covered by the `cap_qual_prefix` reconcile; (2) entry self-qualify `prebind_mod_members m.mod_name.txt` (`current_module.fn`, `cap_qual_prefix=""`) → covered by the new `current_module` reconcile (round-3 fix); (3) DMod re-export `new_names` (~:7429, re-exports the ALREADY-reconciled `inner_env.vars` keys) → covered transitively, verified a sibling-DMod `Helper.id` forge already rejects on d19dc519; (4) `prebind_mod_members_inc` (`check_module_with_env`, LSP/incremental path) seeds only NESTED DMods and never entry-self-qualifies nor sets `current_module`, so it has no entry-level erasure. NO qualified fn key can now retain a scheme decoupled from the real body-checked scheme, at any nesting level including entry. **Round-3 tests:** 7 more NON-VACUOUS cases in `nested_mod_prebind_erasure` (25 total) — entry `Main.id` (Int→String, Box, Cap), nested-sibling `T.id`, entry forward-ref `Main.id`, all RED on d19dc519 (exit 0) / GREEN after; plus an entry-`Main.id`-polymorphic guard (RED→GREEN: entry `id` at two types spuriously errored pre-fix) and a nested-sibling-consistent-type guard. (Also filed the pre-existing, unrelated `stdlib/global_registry.march:101` inline-`match`-lambda-body PARSE ERROR the review surfaced — the real cause of the `test_stdlib_march` `global_registry` failure — as its own P1 finding above; not fixed here.)
- ✅ **Container/factory `cap_narrow`-taint gap — RESOLVED (2026-07-08), with a corrected diagnosis: the historically-filed repro was actually a different, already-fixed bug, and the architectural asymmetry it was blamed on is now closed anyway as hardening.** `tag_cap_producer_result` (the tagger) was shallow — it only tagged a bare `Cap(a)`/`TVar`, while `ty_has_tagged_cap_producer` (the detector gating the call/factory taint-propagation sites) already recursed into tuples/records/`TCon` args. Filed by the adversarial proof-cap review as a live escape (a nested-module `box(x) = (x, 0)` called as `box(cap_narrow(cap))`, destructured, consumed as a proof cap).
  **Investigation (picking this finding up) found the escape does NOT currently reproduce, and traced why in full:** live-testing the exact repro plus 11 further variants (Option-wrap, forward-referenced factory, single top-level module, the exact cross-module `Db.requires_migration` shape, a closure/thunk-deferred producer, a record-wrapper, and a 3-layer tuple→Option→List wrap) — ALL reject on this tree. Tracing the mechanism: `demote_to_monomorphic` (Batch-A's value restriction) pins a `cap_narrow`/`mint_cap` result's inner var to level 0 the instant it is produced, so that SPECIFIC var is never swept into any later generalization — it is the SAME physical var wherever it flows, through arbitrary tuple/record/generic-function wrapping, because `repr` follows links transparently regardless of syntactic nesting. `unify`'s own hook additionally propagates the tag to whatever var the tainted one gets bound to (`Hashtbl.replace env.cap_producer_ivars id2 cn_sp` when the bound-to side is itself an unbound var), so the taint survives arbitrary var-to-var aliasing chains, INDEPENDENT of `tag_cap_producer_result`'s own shallow/recursive distinction. This is why even a SINGLE top-level module (never touched by the nested-module qualified-prebind bug) already rejects the container-wrap shape.
  **But the ORIGINAL repro genuinely DID forge at the time it was filed** — confirmed via a live source A/B against the actual historical commit (`66b6716a`, the commit the review was reviewing): the identical `box(cap_narrow(cap))` program forges (`--check` exit 0) on `66b6716a`'s `typecheck.ml`, and rejects (exit 1) on every later commit. The reviewer's diagnosis (blaming `tag_cap_producer_result`'s shallowness) was a plausible-looking but ultimately INCORRECT root-cause attribution: at that commit, the nested-module qualified-prebind type-erasure bug (see the Done entry above, fixed three commits later in the same line of work) was ALSO present, and `box` — an unannotated helper in a nested module — is exactly the shape that bug corrupted. Under that bug, `box`'s call resolved a decoupled placeholder scheme that bypassed normal unification entirely, so the tainted var's own tag never had a chance to reach the destructured result — a completely different mechanism than "the tagger silently no-ops on a compound shape." The qualified-prebind fix closed this as an unplanned side effect.
  **The architectural asymmetry (shallow tagger vs. recursive detector) was real regardless of exploitability, so it is fixed anyway, as hardening rather than resting on the incidental protection above.** `tag_cap_producer_result` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`) now recurses through `TCon` args, `TArrow`, `TTuple`, `TRecord`, `TLin`, `TNatOp`, and `TRefine` — identical to `ty_has_tagged_cap_producer`'s traversal — so the detector/tagger pairing at the call-propagation sites (the `ty_has_tagged_cap_producer env arg_ty then tag_cap_producer_result env ret_ty` pattern) is no longer a no-op when a call's result is container-shaped. Zero rejection risk: tagging only ever marks a still-*unbound* type variable, so any tuple/record slot already resolved to a concrete type via ordinary argument-passing unification (e.g. a legitimate proof-cap parameter passed straight through beside an unrelated tainted slot in the same tuple) is untouched — verified live with a devious combine-both-in-one-tuple probe, which still accepts.
  **Tests:** 4 new cases added to `test/test_compiler.ml`'s `proof_cap_mint` group — tuple-wrapped and `Option`-wrapped forge attempts (reject), an ordinary IO-cap narrow wrapped in a tuple factory (accept, regression guard), and the devious "tainted IO narrow tupled with an unrelated legit proof-cap passthrough" over-rejection guard (accept). Honestly documented in-line: these tests currently pass with or without the recursive-tagger change (value restriction already covers every shape tried), so they lock in the correct, currently-safe behavior rather than demonstrating the recursive fix's own independent necessity. Full six-runner suite green (compiler 486 / eval 231 / codegen 394 / stdlib 804); `check_types.sh` 120/120; `check-docs.sh` clean.
- ✅ **`root_cap()` (calling the root capability like a function) silently passed `--check` then crashed both backends at runtime — FIXED (2026-07-22).** Found auditing `specs/lang/capabilities.md`/`docs/capabilities.md` against the compiler. `root_cap` is registered `Mono (Cap(IO))` (`typecheck.ml`) — a plain value, referenced bare (`let c = root_cap`, per `examples/capabilities.march` and the docs) — but `root_cap()` (calling it with zero args) also typechecked clean, then failed at eval (`applied non-function value: ()`) or link (`Undefined symbols ... _root_cap`). Root cause: `infer_app`'s `| [], t -> t` base case unconditionally returns the callee's type for ANY zero-arg call, regardless of whether that type is actually an arrow — this is deliberate and necessary for the many builtins genuinely invoked as `name()` while declared `Mono <non-arrow>` (`pmap_threshold`, `get_work_pool`, `task_cancel_token_new`, the `logger_*`/`process_*` readers, `self`, `remote_count` — see the `pmap_threshold` comment), and for a zero-param user `fn` (whose type collapses to its bare return type, no `TArrow` wrapper), but it can't distinguish those from `root_cap`, a genuine non-function value, by type alone. **Fix (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`):** new `noncallable_builtin_values : StringSet.t` (currently just `root_cap`) plus a check in `EApp`'s handler, parallel to the existing `arity_error` check: a zero-arg call (`EVar name, []`) where `name` is in that set is rejected with `` `root_cap` is not a function — it has type `Cap(IO)`. Remove the `()` and use `root_cap` directly. `` instead of falling into `infer_app`. **Scope note (investigated, not fixed here):** the SAME hole also silently accepts calling an ordinary non-function local value with zero args (`let x = 5; x()` — no error at `--check`, crashes at runtime with "applied non-function value"). A safe general fix would need to track local-vs-global binding provenance — `env.fn_arities` only covers same-module `fn` decls, so a naive "reject unless known-callable" gate false-positives on legitimate bare-imported or cross-module qualified zero-arg calls (verified live: both `Lib.zero()` and a bare-imported `zero()` from another module must keep typechecking). Left as a documented, separately-scoped gap (`test_tc_nonfunction_local_value_call_known_gap` in `test/test_compiler.ml` pins the current behavior so it doesn't regress further un-noticed). **Tests:** 5 new cases in `test/test_compiler.ml`'s `typecheck` group — `root_cap()` rejected with a message naming both `root_cap` and "not a function"; bare `root_cap` still accepts; the legitimate zero-arg builtins (`pmap_threshold`, `get_work_pool`, `task_cancel_token_new`, `self`, …) still accept; a zero-arg user `fn` call still accepts; the known-gap characterization test above. Verified both backends: `root_cap()` now rejects at `--check` and at `--compile` (was a link error before); `examples/capabilities.march`'s bare `let cap = root_cap` still compiles and runs correctly on both. Full suite green: compiler 532/532, eval 238/238, codegen clean, stdlib `-q` clean.
- ✅ **The guarded-match exhaustiveness gap (FIXED, fix-campaign batch 3, 2026-07-07) — `cap no_panic` now rejects a guarded, genuinely non-exhaustive `match` whose GUARDLESS arms are non-exhaustive, closing the residual soundness gap F3's fix inherited.** Found during capabilities widening Task 7 (closeout, 2026-07-07) while reviewing F3's fix for completeness; filed OPEN then, fixed now. **The bug:** `check_exhaustiveness` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`) began with `` let has_guards = List.exists (fun br -> br.branch_guard <> None) branches in if has_guards then () else ... `` — if ANY arm carried a `when` guard, the function returned immediately, before computing `find_missing_mc`'s verdict and — critically for F3's mechanism — before recording the match's span into `env.nonexhaustive_match_spans`. So a `cap no_panic` module containing a guarded non-exhaustive match was invisible to BOTH the ordinary Warning AND F3's error path: `--check` exited 0 with zero diagnostics. Live-verified pre-fix: `` mod GuardGap do cap no_panic; fn classify(opt : Option(Int)) : Int do match opt do Some(v) when v > 0 -> v; None -> 0 end end end `` — guardless arms `{None}`, non-exhaustive (missing an unguarded `Some`) — typechecked exit 0; calling `classify(Some(-1))` panics at runtime, exactly the class `cap no_panic` exists to rule out. **The fix (conservative, sound, minimal blast radius, `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`):** for a guarded match, `check_exhaustiveness` no longer returns immediately — it computes coverage over the GUARDLESS branches ONLY (`guardless_matrix = List.filter_map (fun br -> match br.branch_guard with None -> Some [norm_pat br.branch_pat] | Some _ -> None) branches`). A branch reachable only behind a guard cannot be relied on to match, so it contributes nothing to GUARANTEED coverage; if the guardless branches alone are non-exhaustive, then when every guard fails at runtime no arm matches and the match panics → the span is recorded into `env.nonexhaustive_match_spans` (so `check_no_panic_module` promotes it to an ERROR) exactly as for a guard-free non-exhaustive match. If the guardless branches ARE exhaustive (e.g. a guarded arm followed by an unguarded catch-all) the match can never fall through → nothing recorded, still accepts. `find_missing_mc` already handles an EMPTY matrix (all-guarded match) correctly (`typecheck.ml:3045`, `if matrix = [] then Some [] else None`) → reports non-exhaustive rather than crashing. **Minimal blast radius / preserved global behavior:** the guarded case RECORDS the span but emits **NO global Warning** — guarded matches are common in ordinary code and get no such warning today, so only `cap no_panic` modules (which opt into strictness) are made stricter; the guard-FREE path is UNTOUCHED (still emits its Warning + records). Clean split — no non-`cap no_panic` behavior changed (regression-guarded by a new plain-module guarded-non-exhaustive unit test that stays green/silent). **Verified (live, before/after):** `cap no_panic` + guarded non-exhaustive (guardless arms non-exhaustive) → REJECT exit 1 (was exit 0, zero diagnostics); `cap no_panic` + guarded match WITH unguarded `Some(v)` catch-all → STILL ACCEPT exit 0; plain (non-cap) guarded non-exhaustive → STILL exit 0, no warning; all existing `cap no_panic` and guard-FREE non-exhaustive behavior unchanged. **Tests:** 3 new NON-VACUOUS regression cases in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`cap_no_panic` group) — `cap no_panic` + guarded non-exhaustive (RED pre-fix / GREEN after, since `has_errors` counts only `severity = Error`), `cap no_panic` + guarded guardless-catch-all (accept), and plain-module guarded non-exhaustive (accept — the record-without-warning regression guard). **Corpus:** `specs/lang/types/reject/t50_cap_no_panic_guarded_nonexhaustive.march` (type-correct, IMPOSSIBLE to reject pre-fix) + `specs/lang/types/accept/t59_cap_no_panic_guarded_guardless_catchall.march` (proves no over-rejection). `check_types.sh` 107 → **109** (58 → **59** accept, 49 → **50** reject). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.8.11 + §2.1a and `specs/lang/types/INDEX.md`.

### Runtime: compiled RC-bug family now wedges UNKILLABLY instead of crashing (found retrying the oracle sweep, 2026-07-10)

- ✅ **The known sort-RC-underflow family (`alphadev_sort`/`heapsort`/`mergesort`/`sort_nearly_sorted`/`timsort`) — ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (2026-07-17, plan `specs/plans/2026-07-17-closure-scalar-abi-uniform-ptr.md`, commits fd1e882d/0cd1d5d6/7f20bf56).** Sub-item (a) is now done: the "garbage pointer reaching `march_incrc` from a lambda apply" was an **untagged even Int in a `ptr`-typed closure slot** — the Int analog of the float register-mismatch. A generic-Int comparator's apply wrapper takes `ptr` params (erased ABI), but the call site (`heap_merge_h`) passed the element as a raw `i64`; the even raw Int passes `IS_HEAP_PTR` (even + canonical range) so `needs_rc(TVar)=true` emits `march_incrc` on it → deref of a garbage address → SIGSEGV. Fixed by a **uniform ptr closure scalar ABI** across four boundaries: (A) `ECallPtr` and (B) direct-`EApp`-to-apply-fn call sites tag ints `(n<<1)|1` / box floats before passing; (C) apply-fn scalar params are declared `ptr` and untagged/unboxed at entry; (D) `clo_wrap` decodes `ptr` scalar params before forwarding to the concrete named fn. The linchpin the earlier debug attempts missed was boundary B — apply fns are reached by BOTH indirect ECallPtr AND direct EApp calls (defun rewrites non-escaping closures), so tagging only one path left a raw odd value for the entry untag to ashr-corrupt. Verified: all 6 sort benches interp==compiled (incl. introsort), full suite green (eval 233 / compiler 514 / codegen 421 / stdlib 809 / snapshots 29), native golden `test/native/closure_scalar_abi.march` covering the failure-mode matrix, float/FFI goldens intact. **Historical context (the kernel-wedge sub-item b, fixed 2026-07-10, and the original crash writeup) follows:** the family previously hung UNKILLABLE, then crashed cleanly. Evidence (2026-07-10, `sample` on the wedged pids): the main green thread pins at `march_incrc + 48` inside a self-applying lambda (`$lam…$apply → itself → march_incrc`) — an RC op on a garbage pointer — while all scheduler workers idle in `nanosleep`; the process shows macOS `ps` state `UE` (uninterruptible + exiting), consumes ~0 CPU, and **ignores SIGKILL indefinitely** (kill -9 leaves it in `UE`; the pending signal is never acted on), consistent with the fault/Mach-exception handling wedging in the KERNEL rather than a userland loop. The `runtime/march_scheduler.c` SIGSEGV stack-growth handler's foreign-fault path (SIG_DFL + re-raise) looks correct on paper — the wedge locus is not yet pinned (candidates: the alt-stack/ucontext interaction on the main thread, or the scheduler-rewrite's preemption changes altering fault-time state). Previously this family crashed cleanly (SIGSEGV, `RunFail(crashed)`); the mode change means an affected program now hangs FOREVER and cannot be killed without a reboot (wedged `UE` zombies accumulate in the process table — several are parked on this machine now, harmless but unreapable). Two sub-items: (a) fix the underlying RC bug (garbage pointer reaching `march_incrc` from a lambda apply — the long-filed sort-RC-underflow family, `specs/progress.md` "heapsort RC underflow") — **STILL OPEN**; (b) **✅ FIXED 2026-07-10** — the kernel-wedge escalation is defused: `runtime/march_scheduler.c`'s fatal-fault path (both the non-debug tail AND the `MARCH_DEBUG` diagnostic path, which used `abort()`) now `_exit(128 + signo)` instead of re-raising the signal. Re-raise (`raise`/`abort`/`pthread_kill(self)`, even with SIG_UNBLOCK) all hang: the kernel's default terminate-by-signal action walks the thread state to build a Mach exception / core dump, and over the alt-stack + green-thread-ucontext it wedges in an uninterruptible in-kernel wait — and because the re-raise blocks in-kernel, no `_exit` backstop AFTER it ever runs, so the re-raise had to be dropped entirely. `_exit` is a single syscall that cannot fault/block/recurse. Verified: the whole family (`heapsort`/`alphadev_sort`/`mergesort`/`sort_nearly_sorted`/`timsort`/`dataframe_bench`/`dataframe_basic`) now dies in <1s with exit 138/139 (128+SIGBUS/SIGSEGV), zero survivors — was: hung forever, unkillable. Trade-off: a compiled crash now arrives as a clean `128+signo` EXIT rather than `WIFSIGNALED` (no core dump); the oracle's `is_divergence` was updated to treat 139/138/134/132/136 as crash divergences so a NEW segfault is still caught. The underlying RC bug (a) remains — these programs still crash, just cleanly now. **Harness fallout, both fixed 2026-07-10 in `test/test_oracle.ml`:** (i) the sweep's timeout path used a BLOCKING `waitpid` after SIGKILL — an unkillable child froze the entire 105-program sweep at [1/105] for hours, twice; now a bounded WNOHANG reap that leaks-and-warns. (ii) known_divergence staleness WARNs treated a RUN_TIMEOUT as "no longer reproduces / consider pruning" — a known-broken program that times out is still broken; RunTimeout/RunFail/CompileTimeout verdicts no longer mark an entry prunable.

### Compiler: Name resolution (found reconciling the corpus after the order-independent-resolution merge, 2026-07-10)

- ✅ **Sibling-module constructor shadowing (FIXED 2026-07-10) — a module can again use its OWN constructor when a sibling declares a same-named one; introduced by `d95fe942` (order-independent multi-module name resolution).** Root cause: Pass-1 prebind seeds every nested module's bare ctor keys in declaration order (so a later sibling's `Mk` sat at the candidate-list head), and Pass-2's own-module re-registration (`check_decl` DType → `add_ctor`) was a STRUCTURAL-DEDUP NO-OP — both `lookup_ctor` (head pick) and `lookup_ctor_in_type` (first `ci_type` match; both candidates carry the bare type name) then committed to the sibling's ctor inside the declaring module's own body. Fix: `add_ctor` dedup now MOVES the re-registered entry to the FRONT — the definer's Pass-2 registration runs right before its own bodies are checked, restoring declaring-module recency (the pre-`d95fe942` semantics) while keeping the Pass-1 seeds and therefore the cross-module order-independence `d95fe942` exists for (its three regression tests stay green). Witnesses: `accept/t69_sibling_own_ctor` (the ORIGINAL `t35` shape, restored — typechecks AND runs, prints `7`) + unit `test_tc_sibling_ctor_own_module_wins`; `t35` keeps its reconciled distinct-ctor form pinning the type-identity design point in isolation. Original filing below.** Caught by the types corpus at merge time: `accept/t35_no_per_module_type_namespace` (same-named `Mk` ctors in sibling `mod A`/`mod B`) went red — `A.make`'s own `Mk(1)` now resolves against B's `Mk(String)` and rejects `` expected `String` but got `Int` `` pointing INSIDE `A`. Minimal repro: two sibling modules each declaring `type Foo = Mk(...)` with different payloads; the FIRST module's own `fn make() : Foo do Mk(1) end` fails. Pre-`d95fe942`, a module's own ctor won inside its own body (t35 passed for months). The no-per-module-TYPE-identity design point (§2.5) is UNCHANGED (verified: the same program with distinct ctor names still accepts the cross-module substitution); only ctor-name resolution changed. Wants a declaring-module-wins rule for ctor lookup (own module's ctor before siblings'), or an explicit duplicate-ctor diagnostic instead of silent shadowing. t35 reconciled to distinct ctor names 2026-07-10 with a pointer here; §2.5 carries the reconciliation note.

- ✅ **Compiled-only MessagePack miscompile from the same ambiguous-bare-constructor issue — closed as a side effect of the sibling-ctor-shadowing fix above, no separate compiler change needed (found 2026-07-10 investigating three failing distributed native dune rules).** `Msgpack.Value` and `Json.JsonValue` (both stdlib) share `Null`/`Bool`/`Str`/`Array` at DIFFERENT tag positions (`Array` = tag 5 in `Value`, tag 4 in `JsonValue`). Pre-fix, a bare `Array`/`Int`/`Map` inside `mod Msgpack`'s own `encode_val`/`decode` could resolve to `JsonValue`'s variant: `encode_val`'s mistyped scrutinee produced a non-exhaustive LLVM `switch` that dropped the Msgpack-only arms — `Msgpack.encode(Msgpack.int(42))` panicked "non-exhaustive pattern match" when compiled (interpreter was correct throughout) — and `decode` built `alloc JsonValue.Array` with the wrong tag. This broke every compiled program that MessagePack-encodes anything, including `native_node_call_loopback`/`native_node_discovery`/`native_rpc_auto_enroll` (`dune build` failures). Verified fixed by the `add_ctor` move-to-front change: all three native rules now pass, and new regression `cross_module_ctor_resolution` (`test/test_codegen.ml`) exercises the Msgpack-only arms through encode + a decode round-trip.

- ✅ **`bench/tree_transform.march` / `bench/binary_trees.march` typecheck failure (RESOLVED 2026-07-10, by the sibling-ctor shadowing fix `3caa0d1b` — same root mechanism).** The benches' private `ptype Tree` collided with the parameterized `Tree` types the merged stdlib work added (`stdlib/ordered_map.march:14` `Tree(k, v)`, `stdlib/sorted_set.march:12` `Tree(a)`) — whose `Leaf`/`Node` CONSTRUCTORS also collide with the benches'. The `` `Tree` expects 1/2 type argument(s) but got 0 `` errors pointing inside the bench's own declaration were downstream of the same add_ctor dedup-no-op that caused the sibling-ctor shadowing: the bench's own `Leaf`/`Node`/type re-registrations could not reclaim head position from the Pass-1 stdlib seeds. **A/B-verified**: fails at `b8858ffe` (pre-ctor-fix, temp worktree build), passes at `3caa0d1b` — no separate fix needed. Both benches now compile AND run correct: `tree_transform` prints `104857600` (= 2^20 leaves × 100 passes, 8.9s user), `binary_trees` prints the correct check triple (0.15s). The Perceus/FBIP and allocation benchmark rows of `specs/benchmarks.md` are runnable again. **Residual harness gap found while closing this (fixed alongside):** the oracle full-corpus sweep could never have caught this class — a clean typecheck rejection is backend-symmetric (`InterpFail`, not a divergence), so a corpus program regressing from working to NOT-COMPILING passed the sweep silently; `is_divergence` now treats a clean `InterpFail` on a swept corpus program as a failure requiring triage.

- [ ] **The tutorial's dedicated "`let?` cannot have a type annotation" parser error production was never implemented — `let? x : T = e` is rejected by the GENERIC missing-`=` recovery instead.** `let-propagation.md` §5.2 shows a planned `LET; QUESTION; simple_pattern; COLON; error` production emitting "`let?` bindings cannot have a type annotation — the type is inferred from the Result:". NOT a soundness issue.

### Compiler: Parallelism + Clustering (found during Core March widening slices 9 + 10, 2026-07-10)

Reference accounts: `core-march.md` §4.14 (parallelism determinism) + §4.15
(distributed CRDT convergence + scope boundary); `core-march-types.md` §2.11 +
§2.12 (both add no new typing rules). Goldens `g43_parallel_determinism`,
`g44_crdt_convergence`. Accept witnesses `t73`/`t74`. Both slices are primarily
docs+golden (no new typing rules) — but the clustering slice UNCOVERED a serious
compiled memory-safety bug (C1) that makes the whole distributed CRDT path
compiled-unsafe.

- ✅ **C1 (P0, memory-safety) — FIXED (2026-07-11).** The read-then-update map idiom `Map.insert(m, k, f(Map.get_or(m, k, ...)), cmp)` compiled to a use-after-free: `Map.get_or(m, k, ...)` **then** `Map.insert(m, k, ...)` on the *same* `(m, k)` left the resulting map's keys refcount-deficient, surfacing as a use-after-free hashing a freed `String` key (SIGSEGV 139, sometimes a hang) in runtime `march_hash_string` whenever the map was later read via `List.fold_left(Map.keys(a), z, fn(acc, k) -> ... Map.get_or(a, k, ...) ...)`. **Root cause (found via `--dump-tir` + manual TIR tracing, not the bisection's original per-primitive guesses):** `lib/tir/llvm_case.ml`'s `strip_scrut_decrc` — the codegen helper that detects a dying match-arm scrutinee and replaces its plain `dec_rc` with a runtime shared/unique check (`march_decrc_freed`; on the shared path, `IncRC` each extracted heap field to compensate for the alias that survives) — required the scrutinee's own `EDecRC` to be the LITERAL head of the branch body. But Perceus's `add_cross_decrcs` can prepend OTHER cross-branch-dead variables' `EDecRC`s in front of it: `Map.node_insert`'s `HLeaf` arm emits `dec_rc eq; dec_rc node; ...` (an unused comparator closure `eq` dec'd before the scrutinee `node`). The exact-head match failed on this shape, silently falling through to a plain unprotected `dec_rc node` — so whenever `node` (or, at the outer level, the map itself) was actually SHARED (which `vinc`-shaped helpers using `m` at both a borrowed `get_or` position and an owned `insert` position routinely produce, via the `inc_rc m` needed to hand `get_or` a temporary copy), the extracted String key field's refcount went uncounted. **Fix:** generalized `strip_scrut_decrc` to scan a leading run of bare `EDecRC`/`EAtomicDecRC` ops for the scrutinee's own (wherever it falls), preserving the others in their original order — a single-function change in `lib/tir/llvm_case.ml`, identical behavior for the original literal-head case (zero intervening ops). **Verified:** the minimal repro and the original `VectorClock.compare` disjoint-clock scenario both go from 100%-crash to byte-identical-with-interpreter (0 crashes across repeated runs); `MARCH_SANITIZE=1` clean on both; TIR snapshot suite UNCHANGED (pure codegen fix, no TIR-emission change); full six-runner suite (808 tests) and `tree_transform`/`binary_trees` benchmarks unaffected; oracle sweep `UN-TRIAGED FAILURE: 0` before and after. Golden `g44_crdt_convergence` now includes the disjoint-key `VectorClock.compare`/`.concurrent` case unconditionally (previously excluded). Full account: `specs/perceus-invariants.md` §9. Memory: `project_map_read_then_update_uaf.md` (should be updated to note FIXED).

- [ ] **P1 — `Parallel.psum_float` is not backend-portable and must not be golden-compared.** IEEE-754 `+.` is not associative, so `preduce`'s differing chunk counts (the interpreter's worker count comes from `Domain.recommended_domain_count`, the compiled runtime's from the physical CPU count, and both differ across machines) can reorder the additions and change the last bit. The same caveat applies to any `preduce` with a non-associative `merge`. `psum_float` has no doc comment flagging this; the existing `test_rrb_vec.march` unit test happens to use binary-exact inputs (`[1.0,2.5,3.5]==7.0`) so it passes, but that is luck, not a guarantee. Deliberately EXCLUDED from golden `g43` (documented in `core-march.md` §4.14 + the golden's header). Fix options (optional): add a doc-comment warning on `psum_float`, or pin it to binary-exact float inputs. NOT a soundness bug — a documented non-portability. See §4.14.

- ✅ **L7 (FIXED 2026-07-10) — COMPILED-ONLY, memory-unsafe-class: escape analysis stack-promoted ERASED-repr (Newtype/Niche) allocs, so any non-escaping construction consumed under the erased convention read nondeterministic GARBAGE.** The original filing said "TyLinear-annotated" — the annotation was a RED HERRING (the survey never ran the plain control): the unannotated `let c = R(22); let b = match c do R(n) -> n end` was equally broken. TRUE boundary: an `EAlloc` of a Newtype- (or Niche-) repr type bound to a var that never escapes (ECase scrutinee/EField/EDecRC are non-escaping positions) was promoted by `escape.ml` to `EStackAlloc`, whose emission builds an unconditional BOXED stack cell — while every consumer decodes the erased convention, so the ECase untag took `ashr(stack_address, 1)` = the varying garbage. The helper-call shape only worked because a call argument ESCAPES (no promotion → the EAlloc arm emitted the proper `(22<<1)|1` immediate). Root-caused by IR diff (boxed `alloca [24 x i8]` construction vs `ptrtoint`+`ashr` consumption in one function). **Fix (`lib/tir/escape.ml`):** `alloc_emits_heap_cell` gates promotion candidacy — Newtype/Niche-repr allocs (which emit NO heap cell; promotion was also a strict pessimization) are no longer candidates; mirrors `llvm_emit`'s own alloc_type_name derivation + separate `is_niche_shaped` guard. **Defense (`lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`):** the `EStackAlloc` TCon arm now FAILS LOUDLY on an erased-repr type instead of silently corrupting. **Tests:** two pre-existing `escape_analysis` unit tests used `Box(Int)` — a Newtype — as their vehicle and were asserting the broken behavior (invisible to them: they inspect TIR only, never emitted IR); re-vehicled to `Box(Int, Int)` (Boxed), plus new `test_escape_newtype_not_promoted` L7 pin. **Witness:** golden `g41` now consumes its affine binding via a DIRECT match (the shape that caught the bug on g41's first-ever run), 41/41 MATCH, stable 10/10. Full six-runner suite green; snapshots unchanged; `bench/list_ops` perf sanity normal. Found 2026-07-10 while authoring golden `g41` (the witness caught it on its first run — interp `42`, compiled `2156423140`). Minimal repro: `type Res = R(Int)` (single unary ctor → Newtype/erased repr); `let c : affine Res = R(22)` then `let b = match c do R(n) -> n end` — interp prints `22`, compiled prints garbage that VARIES per run (e.g. `2169571280`, `2187519952` — an uninitialized/mis-repr'd read, not a stable mis-tag). **Boundary, all live-verified:** BOTH annotation flavors diverge (`: linear Res` identically); `: affine Int` (primitive) fine; `: affine Pair` with `P(Int, Int)` (Boxed repr) fine; `linear let c : Res` (keyword form, PLAIN type annotation) fine; and — the sharpest datum — passing the SAME annotated binding to a helper `fn get(q : Res)` that matches internally is byte-identical (`22`). So the corruption is specific to lowering a **match whose scrutinee's typecheck-type carries `TLin` over a Newtype-shaped ADT** — `lower_types.ml` strips `TLin` at both its entries (`:51` surface, `:92` typecheck-ty), so the scrutinee's ECase/repr classification must consult an UNSTRIPPED type through some other path (suspect: the ELet annotation type flowing into the case-lowering/`emit_case` newtype-recovery, cf. the Bytes/newtype classification history). Golden `g41` deliberately consumes its affine binding via a call, not a direct match, and documents the exclusion (`core-march.md` §4.12) — same pattern as the MPST exclusion. Fix is TIR/repr work: find the ECase scrutinee-type path that misses the strip; regression = the g41c/g41d probe shapes as a new golden or codegen test.

- **Cross-ref:** session-channel linearity's own gaps (parameter-endpoint reuse; unclosed-`SEnd` drop) are the pre-existing **F7**, filed under "Compiler: Session types" below — the generic tracker documented in §2.9 is the ONLY session-linearity enforcement, so F7's shapes are exactly the shapes this tracker cannot see.

### Compiler: Session types (protocols/channels)

- ✅ **F4 — the MPST merge rule leaked into binary duality: a `choose` with two structurally-identical-type branches was wrongly rejected as "not duals of each other." — FIXED 2026-07-07 (fix-campaign pilot, `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`).** The `ProtoChoice` merge-rule branch is now gated on `multiparty` (one added conjunct): a binary protocol's non-chooser always projects to `SOffer{…}` (it observes the choice); only a true MPST (>2-role) bystander merges. Verified live — identical-`Int`-branch binary protocol now `--check`s exit 0 (was "not duals"); MPST 3-role bystander merge byte-identically preserved; types corpus 78/78 (+`accept/t44_binary_choice_identical_branches`); regression tests `test_session_binary_choice_identical_branches` + `test_session_mpst_bystander_still_merges`. Original analysis retained below for history. Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.7.5 and §4.1 finding 20 (session-types widening, Task 2, 2026-07-06). Cause: `project_steps`'s `ProtoChoice` arm (`typecheck.ml:5906–5919`) applies the standard MPST mergeability rule — "if all branches project to the exact same local type for a non-chooser role, collapse them into that one type (the role need not observe the choice)" — UNCONDITIONALLY, including when `multiparty = false` (an ordinary 2-role binary protocol). For a binary protocol the "non-chooser" role is the chooser's ONLY peer, not a bystander the merge rule was designed to exempt. When both `choose` branches happen to carry an identical payload type (`session_ty_exact_equal`, `typecheck.ml:2058`), the peer's projection collapses from `SOffer {...}` to that single shared type, which is then no longer the dual of the chooser's `SChoose {...}` — so `project_protocol`'s binary duality check (`:5972–5986`) rejects a perfectly legal protocol. Minimal repro (verified live):
  ```march
  protocol Decision do
    choose by Client:
      ok  -> Server -> Client : Int
      err -> Server -> Client : Int
    end
  end
  ```
  `march --check` on this exits **1**:
  ```
  Protocol `Decision`: the projection onto `Client` and the projection onto `Server` are not duals of each other.
  dual(Client) = Offer{ok: Send(Int, End), err: Send(Int, End)}
  but Server has: Send(Int, End)
  ```
  (The printed `Server` projection is already the MERGED `Send(Int, End)`, not a `Choose{...}` — the tell that the merge rule fired.) Making the branches type-distinct (`err -> Server -> Client : String`) typechecks clean (exit 0) with no other change — confirmed live. **Impact:** any binary protocol author whose two `choose` branches happen to share a payload type (a common, unremarkable shape, e.g. two branches both replying with a plain `Int` status code) hits a spurious rejection whose message talks about "duals" rather than anything resembling the actual cause. Fix direction: gate the merge-rule branch in `ProtoChoice` on `multiparty`, only merging for the true MPST non-chooser case (a binary protocol's peer role should always get `SOffer`, never a collapsed type). Filed here (not fixed — docs-only widening slice, out of scope for a reference-widening task); a `reject/` corpus program was deliberately NOT added for this repro (it currently, incorrectly, typechecks as accepted when branches differ, and incorrectly rejects when they match — a `reject/` witness for either behavior would codify the bug as intended). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.7.5 for the full writeup and both live-verified repros (reject + accept sides).

A companion `iter_arms_linear` treats match arms as mutually-exclusive paths so a linear channel consumed once per arm is not a false double-use. Witnesses: `specs/lang/types/accept/t79_offer_branch_dependent_continuation` (correct branch-dependent drive — IMPOSSIBLE to accept pre-fix) and `reject/t74_offer_wrong_branch_drive` (wrong-branch drive still rejected). `check_types.sh` 155/155. ORIGINAL FINDING: **F5 — `Chan.offer` always returns the FIRST branch's continuation type, regardless of which branch the peer actually chose at runtime.** Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.7.9 and §4.1 finding 21 (session-types widening, Task 3, 2026-07-06). Cause: `Chan.offer`'s arm (`typecheck.ml:3614`, requiring `SOffer branches`) computes its result continuation as `match branches with (_, sty) :: _ -> TLin (Linear, TChan (ref sty)) | [] -> TError` (`:3624–3627`) — always the FIRST entry of the branch list, never indexed by the `Atom` label the op also returns. The arm's own comment (`:3607–3613`) is explicit that this is deliberate: "the exact continuation is not known statically without dependent types, so we return the first branch's continuation type as a conservative approximation." **Impact — a real, narrow soundness gap:** for an `SOffer` whose branches lead to DIFFERENT continuations (e.g. `Decision`'s `ok -> Send(Int, End)` vs `err -> Send(String, End)`), the returned channel's static type is simply wrong whenever the peer actually picked any branch other than the first — a program that pattern-matches the returned label and then tries to drive the channel per-branch (e.g. `Chan.send` a `String` after matching `:err`) is rejected at typecheck time even though it is exactly what the *runtime* session requires, because the type never left the first branch's continuation. Repro (live-verified, `specs/lang/types/accept/t43_choose_offer_roundtrip.march` sidesteps this by having the chooser always pick the first-listed branch, so the approximation happens to be exact there — this is not a counterexample, just a witness that doesn't trigger the gap):
  ```march
  protocol Decision do
    choose by Client:
      ok  -> Client -> Server : Int
      err -> Client -> Server : String
    end
  end
  ```
  `Chan.offer(sc)` on the `Server` endpoint is typed `(Atom, Chan(Server, Send(Int, End)))` unconditionally — even on a run where the peer chose `:err` and the true session is at `Send(String, End)`. Fix direction: branch-indexed / dependent typing of the returned continuation on the returned `Atom` value (refine the tuple's second component per `match` arm over the first). Filed here (not fixed — docs-only widening slice); no `reject/` corpus program added (it typechecks — wrongly permissively — today; a `reject/` witness would codify the gap as intended). See `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.7.9 for the full writeup and worked example.

Fixed by returning a flat N-tuple (mirroring `march_chan_new`). (2) *role name/index skew* — endpoints carry positional role indices in tuple-position (role-name-SORTED) order, but send/recv route by role NAME via `mpst_resolve_role`, which assigned names first-encounter → misroute. The in-repo compile tests (`test_session_compile_*`, `test/test_compiler.ml:2350–2434`) only assert `march_mpst_*` symbols *appear* in the emitted IR; none of them run the resulting binary, so this segfault is invisible to the existing green suite. **Impact: MPST is interp-only in practice — no MPST program can be a `golden/` witness** (a crashing compiled binary can never produce byte-identical output). - [ ] **F6 — SEMANTICS (scope boundary, not a bug to fix): the channel runtime has no scheduler, so a `recv` called before its matching `send` in program order typechecks cleanly but deadlocks/aborts at runtime on BOTH backends.** Found and pinned by `specs/lang/core-march.md` §4.11 and §4.1 finding 23 (session-types widening, Task 4, 2026-07-06). The channel runtime is synchronous, single-threaded, non-blocking: `chan_recv` (`eval.ml:2655`) does not suspend when its `ce_in_q` queue is empty — it raises a hard error immediately (`eval.ml:2660`, `"Chan.recv: channel %s#%d has no pending value — did you run the sender first?"`); there is no coroutine/actor-mailbox integration for channels, so both endpoints of a session must run in the same straight-line thread with every `send` textually ordered before its matching `recv`. Verified live (this task): a program calling a `server_side` function (whose FIRST op is `Chan.recv`) before a `client_side` function (whose `Chan.send` would have satisfied it) — a protocol that typechecks (`--check` exit 0, session-state advancement is purely a static per-op check, oblivious to call order) — dies at runtime on both backends: interpreted, `Chan.recv: channel Echo#0 has no pending value — did you run the sender first?` (exit 1); compiled, `march: Chan.recv on empty channel queue (role 1)` then abort (exit 134). Neither the type system nor any runtime scheduler prevents the ordering mistake; both backends simply agree it is a fatal error once it happens. **This is a documented scope boundary, not a defect to fix:** session types here are a linear protocol-*conformance* checker layered over a same-thread mailbox, not a concurrent-session / coroutine system — the type system guarantees "the protocol steps you take advance a valid session state," not "your calls into that protocol are scheduled in the order the protocol requires." Filed here for reference-completeness (no fix proposed; a scheduler/coroutine integration would be a substantial feature, out of scope for a docs-widening task). See `specs/lang/core-march.md` §4.11 for the full writeup and both live-verified backend error messages.

This is DELIBERATELY narrower than full linear consumption so a mid-protocol create-and-drop stays legal (the out-of-scope F6 direction; preserves `accept/t42`/`t44` and the `test_session_chan_type_annotation` unit test). (2) **reusing a linear *parameter* endpoint whose session state coincidentally still matches** — a function `use_twice(ch : Chan(Client, Two))` for a `Two`-role protocol `Client -> Server : Int; Client -> Server : Int` that calls `Chan.send(ch, 1)` and THEN `Chan.send(ch, 2)` — reading the *original* parameter binding `ch` twice rather than threading the first call's returned continuation — typechecks and runs cleanly, because both calls independently see `ch`'s *parameter-declared* type (`Send(Int, Send(Int, End))`) rather than the advanced-by-one-step type the first `Chan.send`'s result actually carries; the generic linear tracker only rejects re-*use* of a `let`-bound name that was already consumed, and a function parameter is not re-bound by a `let`, so this reuse is invisible to it. **Net: the "consume each channel exactly once, at the exact advancing state" guarantee that session types are supposed to provide only actually holds for `let`-bound continuations threaded through in the same scope** — parameter reuse and unclosed-drop both slip through. Any construct minting a SECOND, unmarked `TChan` ref at the same session state therefore laundered the mark away. Four live shapes reproduced at branch HEAD, all `--check` exit 0: **(a)** a type annotation, `let ch : Chan(C, E) = cc2`, where `E` is exactly the offer's guessed first branch — compiled, this printed `40852523489`, the `String` payload's heap pointer read as an `Int`; **(b)** an `if`-join with an ordinary channel at that same state, `let ch = if false do ec else cc2 end` — no annotation needed, so this is the shape a user hits by accident; compiled, `4315028705`; **(c)** passing the channel to a function with an annotated parameter, `drain(cc2)`; **(d)** storing it in a record field declared `Chan(R, P)`. Propagation was rejected: it cannot close shape (c), because a callee's annotated parameter mints its own ref and the callee body is checked against THAT ref — a mark propagated at the call site arrives after the body is already checked and diagnoses nothing. Reporting at the unify chokepoint closes all four shapes at the point of laundering, one diagnostic each, at a fraction of the durable option's blast radius. **What it does NOT cover:** enforcement now rests on two chokepoints — every `Chan.*` op, and every `TChan`/`TChan` unification — not on the session type itself. Those are the only ways a `TChan` is consumed or copied today (`instantiate`/`subst` return `TChan` unchanged; the only fresh-ref mints are `Chan.new`, the `Chan.*`/`MPST.*` continuations, and `surface_ty`'s `Chan(R, P)`), so there is no KNOWN remaining route — but it is a checked invariant, not a structural impossibility. See the OPEN follow-up below. **[Corrected later the same day: the "no KNOWN remaining route" clause was false when written — an annotated LAMBDA / nested-`fn` parameter reached neither chokepoint. See the entry immediately below.]** New witnesses `reject/t98_offer_unrefined_laundered_annotation`, `t99_offer_unrefined_laundered_if_join`, `t100_offer_unrefined_laundered_fn_param`; five new unit tests including a SILENCE companion (an ordinary channel-to-channel unification and a properly match-refined continuation must both stay clean).

- [ ] **Session types: make "awaiting `offer` refinement" a session STATE rather than a side table (durable form of the Finding 1 fix above, OPEN).** Today `env.offer_unrefined` is a physical-identity list guarded at two chokepoints. The structural fix is a new `session_ty` constructor — `SOfferPending of (string * session_ty) list` — that `Chan.offer` puts the returned ref at when the branches diverge, and that only `with_offer_refinement` strips. It would then survive unification, annotations, and function boundaries BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a checked invariant, and would need no `unify` special case at all. Deferred because it touches `pp_session_ty`, `session_ty_equal`, `session_ty_exact_equal`, `dual_session_ty`, `unfold_srec`, `subst_svar`, and every `match` over `session_ty` — many of which have `_` fallbacks, so OCaml's exhaustiveness warnings would NOT enumerate the sites for you. Do it with a survey of every `session_ty` match first, not by chasing compiler errors.

### Runtime: Hot Code Reloading

Spec: `specs/hot-code-reload.md`. Erlang-style live code swapping for deployed Bastion apps. **Two key findings from the design review:** (1) March's whole-program optimization (mono, defun, Perceus/borrow, LTO) is in tension with module isolation — hot reload must *forfeit* those at the boundary; two execution models, **Model A (interpreter trampoline)** shippable now, **Model B (native JIT)** research gated on a spike. (2) The CAS (`lib/cas/`) is the natural HCR substrate — per-SCC granularity, dual `sig_hash`/`impl_hash`, compiler/runtime identity already in the artifact key, two-tier content-addressed store — so it replaces the bespoke ABI table, source-diff, shipping protocol, and integer-ID scheme **once `did_hash` is Merkle-populated**. Phasing is CAS-prerequisite-first, then trampoline. **(RESOLVED prerequisite: the `impl_hash` Merkle-root population is DONE — see Phase 1 below and `progress.md` 2026-06-21 "Hot Code Reload — Phase 1". The CAS substrate is now available; remaining HCR work is Phases 2–7.)**

- [ ] **Phase 0 — Spike (MANDATORY before any Model B work)** — Throwaway prototype proving native code can be swapped across a boundary without memory corruption: two app modules with a `Conn`-style borrowed-record boundary call, frozen RC/borrow ABI, hot-swap callee, run under ASan → zero double-frees/leaks; introduce a new closure shape flowing through the boundary → prove a no-defun-at-boundary scheme works (no defun fault) or conclude Model B can't defunctionalize the boundary; measure the boundary deoptimization on `bench/list_ops.march` + a Bastion request bench. Deliverable: go/no-go on Model B with real numbers. (Model A needs no spike.)
- ✅ **Phase 1 — CAS prerequisite (highest leverage; also fixed a real stale-cache bug)** — `impl_hash` is now a true Merkle root: `hash_module` (`lib/cas/pipeline.ml`) folds, into each definition's hash, both (a) the `impl_hash`es of its earlier-SCC callees (walking SCCs dependencies-first) and (b) the base hashes of every named type it *transitively* references. A callee body change propagates into every direct/transitive caller; a record/variant layout change propagates into every definition that uses the type directly or through another type. This closes the cross-SCC stale-cache hole (`known_call` inlines across SCCs, so `compile_scc`'s key was serving stale inlined callees) **and** the type-layout hole (TIR references types by name, so a layout change moved GEP offsets while leaving the user's bytes/hash unchanged) — the latter is HCR Part 5's shared-type soundness gate, now a hash comparison. **Implementation notes:** threaded callee/type hashes into the hash computation rather than *emitting* `ADefRef` nodes or adding types to `compute_sccs` (same Merkle guarantee, no TIR mutation; per-def callee sets via `Scc.deps_of`, type refs via a TCon walk over sig+body; types are folded by transitive closure of their base hashes, so no type-SCC machinery is needed and recursive types are cycle-safe). Externally-defined types (stdlib/deps) have no base hash and are simply not folded, mirroring the cross-SCC callee rule. Intra-SCC refs (self-recursion, `Group` members) are excluded from the fn fold (covered by the group hash). Regression tests in `test_cas.ml` `def_id` group (6 new): direct + two-hop transitive call propagation, unrelated-def isolation, direct + transitive type-layout propagation, unreferenced-type isolation (cas suite 44→50; compiler/codegen/eval/stdlib all green).
- ✅ **Phase 2 — Boundary + versioned dispatch (compiler + main-build)** — Boundary classifier, NAME_ID interning, runtime dispatch table (`march_dispatch.{c,h}`), `Llvm_emit` dispatch-call emission (enter/leave wrapping), inliner no-inline guard, real `impl_hash`es in `publish`, and runnable end-to-end test all complete. Known limitation: bare entry-file fn names in the single-file compiler path (`@b` not `@App.b`) — `forge build` qualifies by package name so real multi-file builds work; single-file `--hot-reload` only matches nested/library modules.
  - ✅ **Boundary classification** (`lib/tir/hot_reload.ml`, `is_reloadable`): a module is reloadable iff it is app code (under the package module prefix) or force-included, and not force-excluded (excludes win); module-path-aware prefix match (`MyApplication` is not under `MyApp`), so stdlib/deps/lookalikes are excluded. Pure, 6 TDD cases (`test/test_hot_reload.ml`).
  - ✅ **NAME_ID interning** (`Hot_reload.Name_table`): dense `name ↔ id` map with ids assigned in sorted-name order, so the mapping is a deterministic function of the boundary name set (not a source-order int that shifts on unrelated edits). Cross-build reload activation is keyed by name, so dense per-build ids suffice. 5 TDD cases.
  - ✅ **Runtime dispatch table** (`runtime/march_dispatch.{c,h}`): dense slot array indexed by `NAME_ID`, each slot a per-version ring (`MARCH_MAX_LIVE_VERSIONS`=2) of `{fn_ptr, atomic refs, impl_hash, kind, live}`. `march_dispatch_enter(name_id, &v)` pins the current version and reports its ring index so `leave(name_id, v)` unpins *that* version even after a concurrent `publish` advanced `current`; `publish` advances current and reclaims a non-current slot only when its refs have drained (else returns -1 → purge needed, a later phase). Release/acquire ordering on `current`. 7 TDD groups / 23 checks in `test/test_dispatch.c` (wired into `dune runtest`). (Epoch/grace reclamation for the enter-vs-reclaim race is deferred — noted in `march_dispatch_enter`.)
  - ✅ **`Llvm_emit` dispatch-call emission** — `emit_module ?hot_reload:Hot_reload.config option` (default `None` → existing codegen byte-identical). `ctx` carries the config, a `Name_table` of reloadable fn names → NAME_ID, and the current caller module; a `module_of_name` helper derives a fn's module from its qualified name. At a `Tir.EApp` call site, when `Hot_reload.needs_dispatch` holds (caller+callee both reloadable, callee a known top-level fn with a NAME_ID), the direct `call @callee(..)` is replaced by `alloca i32`; `%fp = call ptr @march_dispatch_enter(i32 NAME_ID, ptr %ver)`; indirect `call %fp(..)`; `load %ver`; `call @march_dispatch_leave(NAME_ID, %ver)`. Dispatch externs declared in the preamble. IR-level TDD in `test/test_hot_reload.ml` (`llvm_emit` group): with the flag the boundary call emits enter/leave and drops the direct call; without it the direct call is preserved. **Regression-clean: compiler 296, codegen 320 green** (the real compile path is unchanged with the flag off).
  - ✅ **Inliner no-inline guard** — `Inline.boundary_config` (set by `Opt.run ?hot_reload`) excludes reloadable fns from the inline-candidate set so a boundary→boundary call survives `Opt.run` as a real call site (small boundary callees would otherwise be inlined away before codegen). `module_of_name` promoted to `Hot_reload` as the single source of truth. 2 TDD cases (`test_hot_reload.ml` `inline_guard`): boundary callee not inlined under a config, inlined when off. Regression-clean (compiler 296, codegen 320 with the flag off).
  - ✅ **Runnable end-to-end — first hot-reload binary runs and genuinely dispatches.** Startup registration (`@main` emits `march_dispatch_init(n)` + a `march_dispatch_publish(NAME_ID, @fn, ptr null, NATIVE)` per boundary fn before user main spawns; impl_hash is null baseline, reload server stamps real hashes on activation — IR-tested). `march_dispatch.c` linked into the compile path (`bin/main.ml` `extra_c_files` — note there are *two* runtime-source lists; the `--compile` clang path uses `extra_c_files`, not `extra_files`). `--hot-reload <Prefix>` flag in `bin/main.ml` builds `Hot_reload.default_config Prefix`, threaded into both `emit_module` calls + `Opt.run`, and added to **both** `cas_flags` sites. **Verified:** a nested-module program (`Core.a`→recursive `Core.b`) compiled with `--hot-reload Core` emits the full dispatch sequence (init/publish/enter/leave), `Core.a`/`Core.b` survive the inliner (guard works in the real pipeline), the binary runs and prints identical output to the plain build. Regression-clean (compiler 296, codegen 320).
  - [ ] **Remaining (smaller follow-ups):** **boundary-naming for the entry module** — a single-file program's *top-level* functions are emitted bare (`@b`, not `@App.b`), so `--hot-reload <Prefix>` only matches *qualified* (nested/library) modules; the real `forge build` path qualifies modules by package name so this is the right model there, but the raw single-file compiler can't reload bare entry-file fns. ✅ **Real `impl_hash`es threaded into `publish`** — `emit_module` takes an optional `~impl_hashes:(name → 64-hex)` map; `bin/main.ml` builds it from the same `Pipeline.hash_module` SCC hashing that keys the artifact cache (`hd_impl_hash` per `FnDef`, across `HSingle`/`HGroup`), in both the `--compile` and `--emit-llvm`-only paths. In `hr_setup` each boundary fn's hash is emitted as a private NUL-terminated string global (`@.hr_hashN = [65 x i8]`) and passed to `march_dispatch_publish` as `ptr @.hr_hashN` instead of `ptr null` (null fallback retained for non-CAS paths). ✅ **Automated end-to-end test** (`test_stdlib_suite.ml` `adversarial-regressions`, Slow): compiles the nested-module `Core.a`→`Core.b` program with `--compile --hot-reload Core`, asserts it prints `dispatch works`, that the plain `--compile` build prints identically, and that `--emit-llvm --hot-reload Core` IR contains a real `call ptr @march_dispatch_enter` (not just the preamble `declare`). `--hot-reload` plumbed through `forge` + `config` from `forge.toml [hot-reload]`. Main-build symbol export (`-rdynamic`/un-stripped) — only needed for Model B (Phase 6) JIT resolution, not Model A; defer.
- ✅ **Phase 3 — Native reload server + `--compile-so` (shippable milestone, `dlopen` variant)** — Background pthread on a Unix-domain socket (`MARCH_HOT_RELOAD_SOCKET`). Text protocol: `PING → PONG`, `ABI_QUERY → SLOT id hash...END`, `ACTIVATE name impl_hash so_path → OK impl_hash | ERR reason`. Name registry (`march_dispatch_register_name`) maps human-readable function names to dispatch slot IDs at startup. `--compile-so` compiler flag produces a patch shared library (no `@main`, `-shared -fPIC`, `-undefined dynamic_lookup` / `--allow-shlib-undefined`): boundary functions exported as named symbols (`Server.square`, etc.). ACTIVATE: `dlopen(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_GLOBAL)` + `dlsym(handle, name)` + `march_dispatch_publish` — atomically replaces the function slot at runtime. `scripts/march-reload` client script: `--src` auto-compiles, `--so` uses pre-built. Verified end-to-end: `square(7) = 49 → 343` with live server, zero downtime. Works on Linux + macOS. `-Wl,-rdynamic` (Linux) / `-Wl,-export_dynamic` (macOS) export server symbols for patch resolution. `--compile-so` keyed into both `cas_flags` sites so cache can't silently ignore the mode. Demo: `demo/hcr_server.march` + `demo/hcr_client.march` + `scripts/rpc/hot-deploy.sh`. **Key design finding:** boundary functions must be in NESTED modules (`mod App do mod Server do fn square...end end`) — top-level module names are dropped in TIR, so `--hot-reload Prefix` only matches qualified (`Prefix.fn`) names. Remaining: Model A interpreter trampoline (zero-downtime without pre-compiling a patch); actor state migration (Phase 5); fleet tooling (Phase 7).
- ✅ **Phase 4 — `forge deploy hot` (CAS-native)** — Reload set = `impl_hash` set-diff vs the running process's active set (via `ABI_QUERY`), NOT a source diff. Safety gate = per-changed-def `sig_hash` comparison (ABI break rejected). Distribution = inline CAS over the SSH-tunneled Unix socket (`CAS_CHECK`/`CAS_PUT`). `VERSIONS` for crash-restart drift detection. Ed25519 signing: `march_deploy_hot keygen`/`show-pubkey` (`lib/ed25519/` OCaml library wrapping vendored `runtime/tweetnacl.c`); `--signing-pubkey` embeds the public key in the server binary; `ACTIVATE <name> <impl_hash> <cas_hash> <sig64>` verifies before dlopen. `--compile-so` emits a `.hcr_manifest` sidecar (cas_hash + per-fn impl_hash/sig_hash). `bin/main.ml`: fixed `remote_sig_hashes` (now passed to emit_module for all fns, not just RPC), manifest writing, `tweetnacl.c` linked with main binary for server-side verify. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-24-hcr-phase4-design.md`. Implementation: `runtime/tweetnacl.{h,c}`, `runtime/march_dispatch.{h,c}` (sig_hash, baseline_impl_hash, id→name), `runtime/march_reload.c` (CAS_CHECK/CAS_PUT/VERSIONS/signed-ACTIVATE), `forge/lib/cmd_hot_reload.ml`, `forge/lib/cmd_deploy_hot.ml`, `forge/lib/project.ml` ([hot-reload] section), `lib/ed25519/`.

ACTIVATE extended with `migrate_required` flag; `march_reload.c` dlsyms `__migrate_<actor>` and calls `broadcast_migrate`. ### Compiler Backend

- [ ] **Query-based/demand-driven compiler architecture** — Current pipeline is linear (parse → desugar → typecheck → eval/TIR). Design goal is a query-based architecture (like `rustc`'s `salsa`) for fine-grained incremental recompilation. Deferred post-v1.
- ✅ **Constraint solver for type-level naturals (v1)** — `normalize_tnat` reduces concrete arithmetic (`2+3 → 5`, `(1+2)*3 → 9`) and applies identity/annihilation laws (`n+0 → n`, `n*1 → n`, `n*0 → 0`). `solve_nat_eq` in `unify` solves linear equations (`a+2=5 → a=3`). Parser extended: `INT` as `TyNat`, `+`/`*` in type position via `ty_nat_add`/`ty_nat_mul` levels. 9 new tests in `type_level_nat` group.
- ✅ **Record field auto-satisfy (Feature 2)** — Zero-declaration rule: when discharging `CInterface(Iface, TRecord[...])`, auto-satisfy single-method accessor-shaped interfaces (`a -> T`) when the record has a matching field. Applies only to anonymous `TRecord` types (not named aliases), single-method interfaces, and exact field name+type match. 9 tests in `record_auto_satisfy` group. Spec: `specs/structural-interface-satisfaction.md`.
- ✅ **`satisfy` declaration (Feature 1)** — New `satisfy Iface for T` keyword that generates an `impl` block from matching functions already in scope. `SATISFY` lexer token, `DSatisfy` AST node, `expand_satisfy` desugar expansion, passthrough in eval/lower/typecheck/format/LSP/coverage/refactor/span_remap. 10 tests in `satisfy_decl` group. Spec: `specs/structural-interface-satisfaction.md`.

### Compiler Optimizations (Planned)

See `specs/optimizations.md` for full catalog with effort/impact/dependency details.

- ✅ **Borrow inference and elision (P7)** — `lib/tir/borrow.ml` + `lib/tir/perceus.ml` integration. Pre-Perceus analysis marks TCon/TString/TPtr params as borrowed when they are only read (pattern-matched, field-accessed) and never stored, returned, or passed to owning positions. Fixpoint inter-procedural: params passed only to other borrowed positions remain borrowed. RC elision: (a) call sites skip EIncRC for borrowed args still live after the call; (b) callee suppresses scrutinee EDecRC for borrowed params; (c) last-use borrowed args get caller-side EDecRC instead of callee-side. Eliminates 100% of RC overhead for read-only middlewares (HTTP Conn pattern). 10 new tests in `borrow_inference` group.
- ✅ **Known-call optimization** — `lib/tir/known_call.ml`: replaces `ECallPtr` with direct `EApp` when the closure allocation is visible in scope. Runs between Defun and Perceus + in Opt fixed-point loop. Inline threshold raised 15→50. Struct update fusion (`Fusion.run_struct`) fuses chains of `EUpdate` operations into a single update. 8 new tests (known_call × 4, struct_fusion × 4).
- ✅ **Mutual TCO** — Shared loop with dispatch: `find_mutual_tco_groups` (Tarjan SCC + qualification), `emit_mutual_tco_group` (combined dispatch fn + thin wrappers), `EApp` back-edge for mutual calls. 5 tests in `mutual_tco_codegen` group. `bench/mutual_recursion.march`.
- ✅ **Case-of-known-constructor / Beta-ADT (P11)** — `lib/tir/beta_adt.ml`: matches `let r = EAlloc(tag, args) in ECase(r, [{tag; vs; body}], default)` and reduces to `let v0=args[0] in … in body`, dropping the dead EAlloc (DCE removes it). Run pre-Perceus (before RC insertion); safe post-Perceus only in the matching branch when the scrutinee is not referenced in the branch body. `tags_match` handles qualified (`Result.Ok`) vs bare (`Ok`) tag naming via `short_name`. 3 new tests in `beta_adt` group. See `specs/optimizations.md` §P11.
- ✅ **Variable copy propagation (P12)** — Extended `lib/tir/cprop.ml` with `avar_env : (string * Tir.var) list` to propagate `let x = y` variable aliases in addition to `let x = literal`. Excludes closure types (`TFn`/`TVar`) to protect ECallPtr dispatch (llvm_emit is name-sensitive for closures). Uses `~allow_avar:false` for ECallPtr's function argument. 3 new tests in `cprop` group. See `specs/optimizations.md` §P12.
- ✅ **FBIP cross-tag constructor reuse (P8)** — Extended Perceus FBIP to reuse heap cells across constructors with the same field count (not just the same constructor name). `add_scrutinee_free_for` encodes the consumed ctor's arity as dummy `TUnit` type-args in the DecRC var's type (`TCon(qualified_tag, [TUnit; …])`). `same_arity` replaces `shape_matches` in `try_fbip_sink` and `fbip_expr`, comparing `List.length dummy_args = List.length new_alloc_args`. Cross-ctor reuse is safe: March allocates `[tag + nfields × ptr]` blocks so same-arity ⟺ same block size; the new tag is written into the reused cell by llvm_emit. 5 new tests in `fbip_p8` group. LLVM *cannot* do this — these lower to opaque `call @march_*` instructions, not arithmetic, so the fold must happen at TIR level where the builtin's semantics are known. **Safe set (exact results, zero cross-libm bit-drift):** `int_pow`, `int_abs`, `float_abs`, `int_to_float`, `float_to_int` (truncation), `floor`, `ceil`, `round`. **`int_pow` must reuse the 63-bit range guard** from the `string_to_int` overflow fix — `int_pow(2, 100)` stays a runtime call rather than baking in a corrupt constant; likewise skip negative exponents and `/0`/`%0`. **Defer `sqrt`/`pow`** on non-trivial inputs: compile-time OCaml `libm` and runtime C `libm` aren't guaranteed to agree on the last ULP, so folding could embed an off-by-one-bit value. Each fold must bit-match the interpreter oracle. Lift: ~1 session (~50 lines + ~10 tests), low risk, additive — no new pass or pipeline wiring. Payoff: modest (only fires on builtins over literal constants, e.g. `let max_val = int_pow(2, 31) - 1`) but correctness-clean and removes work LLVM provably can't.

No measurable wall-clock win in a bandwidth-bound map-then-sum benchmark (expected — the array traffic dominates, not the now-vectorized per-element compute), but the codegen is genuinely cleaner (no allocation, no indirect call) and pays off for compute-heavier element bodies. Capturing/reused/RC-entangled closures fall back to the unchanged, correct general path — never a correctness risk. New regression test `test/native/native_arr_map_inline_vectorize.march`. See `specs/optimizations.md` §P10 "Phase 2b".

- ✅ **P10 Phase 2b fix — inline path now fires when the mapped array is reused afterward** — `lib/tir/native_map_inline.ml`'s `strip_alias_chain` only pattern-matched a bare `let f = clo in ...` alias hop immediately after the closure alloc; whenever the mapped array is used again afterward (e.g. a self-recursive loop function mapping `arr` and then passing `arr` on to its own tail call), Perceus inserts an unrelated `inc_rc arr;` (`ESeq`) between the alloc and the alias-let, and the pass silently bailed out to the slower closure-call path for this extremely common shape. Fixed by having `strip_alias_chain` return the list of wrapper expressions peeled through (in original order), which `rewrite_expr` re-wraps around the rewritten body afterward — the RC op is relocated, never dropped or reordered (dropping one would be a UAF/premature-free bug). Guard: a wrapper mentioning the alias name itself stops the walk instead of risking a miscounted "used exactly once" check. New regression test `test/native/native_arr_map_inline_reuse.march`, asserting both correctness and (via `--emit-llvm` grepped for the `nmap_pre`/`nmap_cond` block labels) that the inline path actually fires. See `specs/optimizations.md` §P10 "Fixed (2026-07-26)".
- ✅ **P10 Phase 2c — inline CAPTURING NativeArray.map closures** — extends Phase 2b to the common `stdlib/dataframe.march` shape (`fn x -> x +. f`/`fn x -> x *. f`, capturing a scalar) that non-capturing-only Phase 2b couldn't reach. `lib/tir/native_map_inline.ml`: new `rewrite_expr` arm for `EAlloc` with one-or-more captured free vars — leaves the allocation and everything around it untouched (the struct is a real value the apply body reads from) and rewrites only the terminal call to a 3-arg form (`[arr; apply_fn; clo]`) keeping the real closure pointer. `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`: loop codegen factored into a shared `emit_native_map_inline_loop` helper parameterized on the `$clo` register (`"null"` for Phase 2b, the real coerced pointer for Phase 2c) — no duplicated loop logic between the two. ## Done (recently completed)

- ✅ **`Json.parse` allocated ~2 heap strings per INPUT BYTE; rewritten as a byte-index scanner, plus a new `string_byte_at` builtin (2026-07-27, `stdlib/json.march`, `runtime/march_runtime.{c,h,mjs}`, `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `lib/eval/eval.ml`, `lib/tir/{defun,borrow,llvm_builtins,js_emit}.ml`).** `parse` opened with `string_split(src, "")` — one heap string per input byte — then rebuilt every token by consing those single-byte strings and `string_join`-ing them, so cost scaled with the SIZE of the document rather than with the number of strings in it; `to_string`/`escape_str` did the same on the output side. On a 239-byte document containing ~20 distinct strings, compiled `--opt 2` over 20,000 iterations: **261 → 21 allocations per parse** (21 is the number of strings the document actually holds, the floor for a parser returning owned `String`s), 486 → 58 for a parse + serialize round trip, `hist_le7` share 90% → 31%, wall clock 0.67 → 0.14s parse-only and 1.10 → 0.24s round-trip (same-session interleaved A/B, 4 rounds, identical to 0.01s). **The enabling primitive was missing:** before `string_byte_at(s, i)` (byte value `0..255`, `-1` out of range, allocates nothing) March had NO way to inspect one character of a string without allocating — both `string_split(s, "")` and `string_slice(s, i, 1)` allocate a heap string per character — so "just don't split up front" does not work on its own, because the scanner still must inspect essentially every byte to find token boundaries. **Dead end worth recording:** the first rewrite walked `string_to_codepoints` (a `List(Int)`) alongside a byte offset, passed the full 825-test stdlib suite, and then failed to LINK when compiled — `string_to_codepoints` and `string_from_codepoint` are interpreter-only, with no entry in `llvm_builtins.ml`/`defun.ml`/`js_emit.ml`/the C runtime, and nothing rejects them at typecheck time. **A green stdlib suite does not establish that stdlib code compiles** (those tests run interpreted). The final version scans BYTES, which is safe because every JSON structural character is ASCII and every byte of a UTF-8 multibyte sequence is `>= 0x80` — and which avoids the codepoint version's real hazard, that `string_to_codepoints` emits a raw byte and advances ONE byte on a truncated multibyte sequence, silently desyncing a width-derived offset and slicing at the wrong boundary. Behaviour verified identical over a 48-case corpus (all escape forms, 2/3/4-byte UTF-8 in keys and values, nesting, whitespace, 16 error cases), old-vs-new and interpreted-vs-native, error text included; two deliberate improvements: a non-ASCII character in an error message prints as itself instead of mojibake, and a keyword mismatch names the keyword (`expected 'null'`) not the byte (`expected 'l'`). **Found and fixed in passing:** `march_string_slice` in `runtime/march_runtime.mjs` was `s.slice(start, len)`, treating arg 3 as an END index rather than a LENGTH, so every JS-backend slice with a non-zero start was wrong (`String.slice("abcdefgh", 5, 3)` → `""` on JS vs `"fgh"` elsewhere) — load-bearing here because the new parser slices at non-zero offsets constantly where the old one never called `string_slice` at all; the three checked-in `march_runtime.mjs` copies that were byte-identical to canonical were re-synced. **Three pre-existing bugs found and deliberately NOT fixed**, to keep this a pure performance change: a qualified constructor PATTERN whose bare name is shared by another stdlib ADT silently takes the wrong branch when COMPILED (`Ok(Json.Array(_))` and `Ok(Json.Null)` fall through to `_` compiled but match interpreted — `Array` is declared in both `json.march` and `msgpack.march`, `Null` in `dataframe`/`json`/`msgpack`, so the qualification is dropped and the pattern is compiled against another ADT's tag; it fails OPEN, with no error or warning, and reproduces identically pre-rewrite); `Json.to_string` crashes on any Object on the JS backend (`TypeError: f._0 is not a function` from the match-lambda passed to `map_list`; reproduces identically pre-change, and the JS *parse* path is verified correct), and the number scanner rejects a signed exponent like `1e-5` (preserved verbatim from the old `json_is_num_char`, flagged in a comment at `is_num_byte`).

- ⏳ **`toml.march`, `yaml.march`, `xml.march` have the same per-byte allocation profile** — all three still open with `string_split(s, "")`. `string_byte_at` is the primitive they need and it now exists; the `json.march` rewrite is the template.
- ✅ **Interpolating a String no longer costs an atomic refcount pair per operand (`lib/tir/lower.ml`, 2026-07-27).** `"a${s}b"` desugars to `to_string(s)`, which Show-dispatches to `Show$String.show` — a synthesized IDENTITY (`fn x -> x`, emitted by `emit_builtin_impls`, because a string already is its own representation). That call was *emitted* and then inlined away in the post-Perceus opt loop; since Perceus runs FIRST, it saw a live owned-argument call and bracketed it with `inc_rc`/`dec_rc`, and the later inlining removed the call and stranded the pair around a bare alias. `string_concat3` borrows all three arguments (`lib/tir/borrow.ml`), so the extra reference bought nothing, and it was charged to every interpolated String operand in every March program. **Two fixes, both at the source rather than downstream:** lowering elides the `Show$String.show` call outright (so Perceus never sees a call), and `lower_to_atom_k` no longer binds a fresh temp when the lowered RHS is already a *variable* atom — `let v = EAtom (AVar x) in k (AVar v)` ≡ `k (AVar x)` in ANF, but the alias reads to Perceus as a second owned reference, so eliding only the call just moved the pair onto the alias. **The `AVar` restriction is load-bearing and was found by test, not by inspection:** the first attempt passed *any* `Tir.EAtom` through, which drops the binder's `ty_of_expr` ascription — a literal atom carries no type of its own, so `println(:hello)`/`show(:world)` fell back to the untyped path and printed `()` instead of `:hello` (caught by `iface_impl_mono_codegen` cases 17-18, compiled Show$Atom parity). Measured on arm64, `"w${a}x"` vs hand-written `"w" ++ a ++ "x"`, 3M iterations: **181/173ms → 137/133ms**, with the two now lowering to byte-identical TIR; `MARCH_STRING_STATS=1` histograms unchanged, confirming refcount traffic and not allocation. `bench/tree_transform` and `bench/list_ops` unchanged. Pinned by the `interp_string_operand_rc` TIR golden snapshot, **verified to FAIL on the unfixed compiler** at both the lower and perceus stages. **Two traps worth recording.** (1) *Benchmarks of this shape have a ~25% first-position warmup penalty*: in an A/B where both halves compile to identical IR, whichever ran first measured 173ms against the second's 137ms — so the original report's "interp 358ms vs chain 285ms" was itself partly warmup, and any before/after claim here must hold the benchmark slot fixed. (2) *Two previously-attempted fixes were reported as "did not work" on a mistaken premise* — that `to_string` was already gone before pre-Perceus simplify. `MARCH_DUMP_TXT` (added in this pass) shows `Show$String.show(a)` alive and well at the `tir-simplify-pre` checkpoint; the call survives all the way into Perceus. `--dump-tir` is post-Opt and therefore cannot distinguish a pass that CREATED a construct from one that merely preserved it.
- ✅ **`MARCH_DUMP_TXT=<stage>` prints pretty-printed TIR at any pipeline checkpoint (`bin/main.ml`, 2026-07-27).** `--dump-phases` serialized every `snap_tir` stage to JSON but there was no readable text view of the intermediate stages, so diagnosing "which pass introduced this?" meant reading `--dump-tir`, which only shows the post-Opt end of the pipeline. `MARCH_DUMP_TXT` prints `Pp.string_of_fn_def` for every function at each checkpoint whose label contains the given substring (`all` matches every stage) — e.g. `MARCH_DUMP_TXT=tir-simplify-pre`. This is what localized the interpolation refcount bug above.

- ✅ **Many-part string interpolation desugars to a single `string_join` call instead of a `++` chain (`lib/parser/parser.mly`, 2026-07-26).** `desugar_interp` folded interpolation parts (`"${a}${b}"`) into a left-deep chain of `++` (`prefix ++ to_string(e1) ++ s1 ++ ...`); each `++` (`march_string_concat`) allocates and copies the whole growing prefix again, so a k-part interpolation copied O(k²) total bytes. Past `interp_join_threshold` (3) segments it now builds a `Cons`/`Nil` list of the parts and emits one `string_join(parts, "")` call — `march_string_join` already does a proper two-pass O(n) join (sum lengths once, allocate once, copy once), so no runtime change was needed, and `string_join` is registered as a bare global builtin identically to `++` (typecheck/eval/codegen all key it by name with no module qualification). Short interpolations keep the `++` chain: materializing the list costs more than the extra copy at that size, measured on arm64 over 2M iterations with short segments at 231ms (`++`) vs 303ms (`string_join`) for 2 segments, 307 vs 356 for 3, and 589 vs 564 for 5 — crossover just under 5. Because both shapes now reach downstream passes, the two consumers that pattern-match the desugared interpolation had to learn the join shape: `try_collect_interp` (`lib/format/format.ml`), which reconstructs `"${...}"` source — without it the formatter emitted a literal `string_join([...], "")` call and the stdlib formatter-idempotency tests failed — and `decompose_concat` (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`), which splits a `~H` sigil into per-part IOList segments. The `~H` path was the dangerous one: `html_interp_to_iolist` matches `to_string(e)` *per part* to decide what to wrap in `html_auto_escape`, so an unrecognized shape collapses the template into one opaque part and silently stops HTML-escaping interpolations — reproduced with `~H"<p>${evil}</p>"` emitting raw `<script>` tags, escaping restored by the `decompose_concat` fix. `test/test_eval.ml` now asserts both desugarings (`parse interp`, `parse interp many`). `specs/lang/surface-syntax.md`'s operator table gained a note that `++` itself is still O(n) per call — so `acc = acc ++ x` in a loop is still O(n²) — pointing at `IOList` (`stdlib/iolist.march`) for that case, matching the note `String.concat`'s doc already carried. **Not done in this pass** (deferred): a memchr-based prefiltering pass for `march_string_contains`/`index_of`/`split`/`split_first`/`replace`/`replace_all` (`runtime/march_runtime.c:2550-2760`), which currently do a naive byte-by-byte `memcmp` scan.
- ✅ **String performance phase 2, tasks 1-3 (2026-07-27).** Three landed against the phase 1 profile, each verified by same-session A/B (absolute timings on this machine are not comparable across runs). (1) **`String.index_of_from`** — offset-aware search, removing the O(n²) trap in tokenizing: without a start offset, finding the next separator means slicing off the tail and searching again, re-copying the remaining bytes every step. Two phase 1 benchmarks had to be written around its absence. Counting 150K fields in an 800KB buffer: `String.split` + `List.length` 975ms vs an `index_of_from` walk at 267ms — **3.7× with effectively zero allocation**. (2) **memchr-based substring search** — a shared two-stage helper (memchr finds candidate first bytes, memcmp confirms) routed through `index_of`, `index_of_from`, `contains`, `split`, `replace`, `replace_all`; `last_index_of` stays scalar as it scans backwards. `bench/string_scan` **809ms → 20.8ms (39×)**, `string_parallel_scan` 390 → 171ms, `string_split_large` 1108 → 928ms; unchanged where no search is involved.
