- ✅ **js_emit: statement-position match arms fell through the emitted switch — FIXED (`lib/tir/js_emit.ml`, 2026-07-10).** `emit_case`'s constructor-switch path emitted `break;` only for value-position arms (`result_var = Some`); statement-position arms (`None -> emit_stmts`) relied on the body ending in `return`, but a trailing Unit-typed call emits as a bare statement — so after it returned, execution FELL THROUGH into the next case or the non-exhaustive-match default throw. Shape that hits it: any recursive list walk whose `Cons` arm ends in the recursive call (e.g. a Canvas draw loop over entities) — every frame threw "non-exhaustive pattern match" on unwind even though every arm matched correctly; diagnosed via a headless node probe walking `Game.stars` (all elements printed, `Nil` arm printed, THEN the throw). Fix: unconditional `break;` after `emit_stmts` in both the branch arms and the default arm (unreachable and harmless when the body did return). Golden `test/native/js_match_stmt_fallthrough.{march,expected}` + `test/dune` rule pins the shape; all 18 JS-target goldens + quick alcotest suites green.

- ✅ **`Dom.set_timeout`/`set_interval`/`on_frame` callbacks had a never-satisfiable extern signature — FIXED (`stdlib/dom.march`, `runtime/march_dom.mjs`, 2026-07-09).** Resolves the zero-arg-lambda follow-up filed by the Canvas 2D API entry below (`task_f422fd93`). The three externs declared `cb: Unit -> Unit`, but a zero-arg March lambda (`fn -> body`, the documented idiom for a 0-arg callback) types to its body's result DIRECTLY with no arrow wrapper (T-Abs, `specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2; `List.fold_right (fun pt acc -> TArrow (pt, acc)) param_tys body_ty` in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`'s `ELam` inference arm returns `body_ty` unchanged when `param_tys = []`), so it can never unify with a declared arrow type — `call_it(fn -> once())` against a `Unit -> Unit` param failed with "expected `() -> ()` but got `()`" both at the call site and inside the callee. This means the three callbacks were never actually callable from real March source; no existing test exercised them end-to-end. Root cause confirmed via `--check` repro; the bidirectional checker's `check_expr`'s `ELam` arm (`peel` helper) is not buggy — it faithfully implements the same direct-body-type rule in checking mode. **Fix:** followed the codebase's own established idiom for this exact shape (`task_spawn`'s thunk param, `pmap_threshold`, `task_cancel_token_new` all avoid arrow types for 0-arg-like values) — changed all three `cb` params to `Int -> Unit` (a dummy, ignored Int argument), so callers write `fn _ -> body` instead. Updated `runtime/march_dom.mjs`'s `march_dom_set_timeout`/`set_interval`/`request_animation_frame` to call `cb._0(cb, 0)` (was `cb._0(cb)`), matching the `f._0(f, args...)` closure-call ABI (`lib/tir/js_emit.ml`) for a 1-declared-param closure. Documented the limitation in `stdlib/dom.march`'s module doc and each wrapper's `doc` string. Regression: `test/native/js_dom_timeout_callback.{march,expected}` + `test/dune` rule compiles `--target js` and runs under `node`, verifying the callback both typechecks with `fn _ -> ...` and actually fires via the `cb._0(cb, 0)` ABI (prints "fired"); a `march_dom.mjs` copy-rule was added to `test/dune` alongside the existing `march_runtime.mjs` one since this is the first JS test to actually invoke a `Dom` extern (previous `js_dom_available` test only referenced `Dom.body()` in dead code, so `march_dom.mjs`'s import was never exercised). Full suite green (`scripts/run-tests.sh`, 807 tests) plus all `test/dune` JS-target golden tests (`js_dom_available`, `js_dom_timeout_callback`, `js_extern_import`, `js_ffi_async`, `js_ffi_blocking_raises`, `js_ffi_raises`, `js_ffi_cbacked`) diff-clean.
- ✅ **Self-referencing block-`let` shadowing miscompiled on the native + JS backends — TWO bugs, both fixed (2026-07-10).** `let x = 10 / let x = x + 5 / …x…` printed 15 interpreted but a silently-wrong **10** compiled (and TDZ-crashed or mis-folded on `--target js`). The idiomatic `let x = x + 1` rebinding pattern, so high severity despite the narrow trigger (RHS must reference the binder being shadowed). Root-caused to TWO independent defects, each with a regression test/golden. **(1) `lib/tir/cprop.ml` (shared TIR, hit native + interp-constant-fold + JS):** the `ELet` arm extended the literal/alias/field env with the new binding but never REMOVED the outer binding's stale mapping when the shadowing RHS was not itself a literal/alias/record (e.g. `let x = x + 5` lowers to an `EApp`). So the outer `x -> 10` literal survived into the body and the body's uses of the NEW `x` were const-propagated to the OLD value; a later Fold baked in the wrong constant. Fix: drop `name` from all three envs (`env`/`avar`/`fenv`) before conditionally re-adding the new binding — mirrors the shadow-filtering the `ECase` arm already did for branch-bound vars; RHS look-ups still use the pre-removal envs so a self-alias can inherit outer field shape; `remove_assoc` on an absent name is a no-op so non-shadowing lets are unchanged. Regression: `test_compiled_let_shadowing_parity` (`test/test_codegen.ml`, `iface_impl_mono_codegen`) — chain `((10+5)*2)=30` (buggy=10). **(2) `lib/tir/js_emit.ml` (JS only, surfaced once cprop couldn't fold to a constant, e.g. a param-driven `mix32`):** a shadowing `let x = <expr using x>` emitted `const x = (…x…)` inside a fresh `{ }` block, and the RHS's `x` resolved to the block-HOISTED inner `const x` in its temporal dead zone → `ReferenceError`. Fix: thread a `name_env` (source name → current JS id) through emission; a binding that shadows an in-scope name is emitted under a fresh unique id (`x$sN`), the RHS is emitted BEFORE the new id is installed (so it reads the outer binding), and pattern-variable bindings in `emit_case` are registered the same way (a scrutinee/branch var on a renamed local now resolves correctly — also fixed `scrut_name` to use the rename). `name_env` is saved/restored around nested (`ELetRec`) fns. Golden: `test/native/js_let_shadowing.{march,expected}` (self-ref chain, a binding read before it is shadowed, and a match arm whose pattern var shadows an outer local — `29/129/101/8`, identical on all three backends). With both fixed, `stdlib/random.march`'s `mix32` was restored from the distinct-name workaround (`a`/`b`/`c`) to the classic self-shadowing splitmix32 idiom (`let x = f(x)` chain) and `seed`'s workaround comment corrected; the `js_random_determinism` golden stayed byte-identical. Full suite green: **451 compiler / 231 eval / 396 codegen / 807 stdlib**; all 10 JS goldens pass. Filed by the Random-on-JS work; a dedicated background session (`task_259907b1`) was also spun up.

- ✅ **Random + int builtins on `--target js`; portable sfc32 Random core (2026-07-10).** Resolves the 2026-07-09 Starfling P1 ("`Random` unusable on `--target js`"). Three parts. **(1) JS mappings for the int builtins** — `int_and/or/xor/not/shl/shr/popcount/mod/div/mod_euclid/div_euclid` now delegate to new checked implementations in `runtime/march_runtime.mjs` that mirror the INTERPRETER's semantics (`int_shr` is a logical shift of the 63-bit pattern; `int_popcount` flips the sign bit before counting) exactly within the double-exact range ±(2^53−1) and **throw RangeError rather than silently round** beyond it; fast paths (int32, and non-negative split into 2^32-radix words) keep hot code off BigInt entirely (~35 ns/op vs ~53 ns/op BigInt path, node 25). Also mapped: `int_abs`, `unix_time`, `float_abs/floor/ceil`, and `float_round` (half-away-from-zero via `march_float_round` — JS `Math.round` differs on negative halves). First-class `$clo` wrappers added for all of the above. **(2) Unmapped builtin = compile error** — a direct call that resolves to no user fn, letrec-local fn, or extern now raises `Js_emit_error` (sorted, one diagnostic per name) instead of bare-emitting a guaranteed runtime `ReferenceError`; `int_max_value`/`int_min_value` get a tailored message (their value ±2^62 is fundamentally unrepresentable in the JS target's double-backed Int — the reason a "BigInt-backed xoshiro" fix was rejected). Negative golden `test/native/js_unmapped_builtin.{march,expected}` pins the diagnostic. Note: `test/whole_program/zoo.mjs` is now a frozen pre-change artifact — the zoo deliberately exercises tcp/tls/actor/process/file builtins, so its whole-program JS emission now (correctly) fails with 98 unmapped-builtin errors. **(3) `stdlib/random.march` core rewritten from 63-bit xoshiro256\*\* to sfc32 on 32-bit words** (state record shape `{s0,s1,s2,s3}` and the whole public API preserved; `Gen`/`Check`/`SwimDriver` untouched): every intermediate stays below 2^53, so sequences are exact — and IDENTICAL — on the interpreter, native, and JS backends (verified: same 200k-draw checksum on all three; ~0.10 µs/draw native `--opt 2`, ~0.70 µs/draw node). `next_int` is now uniform in [0, 2^52) (was full-63-bit signed) — the widest portable width; `next_float` builds from 52 fresh bits; seeding is splitmix32-style over the seed's base-2^32 digits (extracted without shifting negative words — `int_shr` is logical interpreted but arithmetic native, a pre-existing divergence the old xoshiro silently suffered). Golden `test/native/js_random_determinism.{march,expected}` wired into `test/dune` (three-rule pattern): self-checks range/distinctness, diff pins determinism, and the .expected equals the interpreter/native output byte-for-byte. Full suite green: **451 compiler / 231 eval / 394 codegen / 807 stdlib**; `test/stdlib/test_random.march` 169-test file green (4 pre-existing unrelated doctest failures unchanged). Two new compiler bugs found while building this, both since FIXED (see Done entries): the self-referencing `let`-shadowing miscompile and the `int_div_euclid` native link gap (`main` `cf604dcd`). **Starfling note:** `demo_app/starfling`'s Level generator (on branch `claude/doom-like-browser-game-82db28`) can now swap its module-local 31-bit LCG fallback back to `Random` — Random is portable and exact on JS as of this change (and sfc32 is the better generator); not swapped here per instruction, and note the LCG's sequences differ from Random's, so the swap changes generated levels.
- ✅ **`int_div_euclid` native codegen — the last of the four `int_div`/`int_mod` family missing from the LLVM backend (2026-07-10).** The builtin existed in the interpreter (`lib/eval/eval.ml`, Euclidean quotient) and had a JS-target mapping (`march_int_div_euclid` in `runtime/march_runtime.mjs` via `lib/tir/js_emit.ml`), but had **no native codegen mapping**: compiling any caller failed at link time with `Undefined symbols: _int_div_euclid`. It was already correctly listed in `defun.ml`'s `builtin_names` (and `policy_dce.ml`/`purity.ml`), so it stayed an `EApp`/`ECallPtr` rather than being defunctionalized — the gap was purely the emit + runtime symbol. Fix mirrors its siblings `int_mod`→`march_checked_imod`, `int_div`→`march_checked_idiv`, `int_mod_euclid`→`march_checked_umod`: (1) new `march_checked_ediv(i64,i64)` in `runtime/march_runtime.c` implementing eval.ml byte-for-byte (`q=a/b; r=a-q*b; if r<0 then (b>0 ? q-1 : q+1) else q`), with the same `march_div_by_zero("int_div_euclid")` panic on a zero divisor; (2) the mapping added to **both** `llvm_emit.ml` call-path sites (the `EApp` guard/helper ~1600-1613 and the `ECallPtr` twin ~2090-2103, per the "builtin multi-site" gotcha); (3) the `declare`/`PDeclare` added to `lib/tir/llvm_builtins.ml`'s preamble (string table + `PDeclare` list). Named `march_checked_ediv` (Euclidean) rather than a "u"-prefixed sibling of `umod` because it is signed throughout — commented as such at the def. New parity test `test_compiled_int_div_euclid_parity` (`test/test_codegen.ml`, `iface_impl_mono_codegen` group) exercises all four sign quadrants (`[3, -4, 4, -3]`) via `assert_compiled_interp_parity`. Verified manually: interpreter and compiled both print `[3, -4, 4, -3]` and both panic `int_div_euclid: division by zero` on a `/0`.

Full 2D surface: state stack, style, rects, paths (including quadratic/bezier curves), text, and `load_image` as a `blocking raises` extern (`Result(Image, String)`, no callback API needed). `Dom` gains `event_x`/`event_y` canvas-relative pointer accessors. New `demo_app/canvas_demo/` verified live in a browser (preview tools): all shapes render, click lands a marker at the exact clicked coordinate, zero console/network errors. New `test/native/js_canvas_available.march` golden fixture (dead-code compile coverage, no real DOM needed); `js_dom_available.march` extended similarly for the new Dom accessors. Docs: `docs/stdlib.md` Canvas section + table row, stdlib count 108 → 109 across `docs/stdlib.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`SKILL.md`. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-09-canvas-api-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-09-canvas-2d-api.md`. Deliberately **not** wired into `test_oracle.ml`/`@oracle` — that suite diffs interpreter vs. native compile and cannot exercise `--target js`-only code, confirmed with the user during planning rather than added as a no-op. **Found and filed, not fixed here:** `Dom.on_frame`/`set_timeout`/`set_interval` are uncallable from March source with a zero-arg lambda (a zero-arg lambda types to its body's result directly, per `core-march-types.md`'s T-Abs rule, and never unifies with the externs' declared `Unit -> Unit` arrow type) — a pre-existing latent bug, not introduced by this change; `canvas_demo`'s originally-planned animation loop was replaced with a static rotated shape as a result. See P1 section / spawn_task `task_f422fd93` for the follow-up.

- ✅ **Order-independent multi-module name resolution — bare/qualified type & constructor references resolve the same regardless of compile entry (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`, 2026-07-08).** A `mod A.Sub` referencing a sibling `mod A`'s constructors/types by BARE name (or the `Type.Ctor` disambiguation form) with no `import`/`use` previously resolved only when `mod A` was Pass-2-checked first — so on a **cyclic** module graph (impossible to topologically order; real case: the `conduit` package, `Conduit` ↔ `Conduit.API`) `forge check` passed or failed depending on which file was the entry (`conduit/lib/conduit/backoff.march` entry → 59 errors, `api.march` entry → 0, identical sources). Root cause: nested-module public types were seeded in Pass-1 prebind under their module-QUALIFIED key only, while the top-level path and records already seeded the bare name; bare cross-module resolution then depended on Pass-2 order, which a cycle makes nondeterministic. **Fix, all in Pass-1 prebind (`prebind_mod_members` + the `_inc` LSP/REPL twin + the unwrapped-entry top-level fold):** (1) seed a nested public type's bare name and bare constructor keys, plus the bare `Type.Ctor` disambiguation key, mirroring the top-level path (`:8929`); (2) the module-qualified constructor now carries `ci_type = <bare type>` (was the qualified `qname`) to match `check_decl` — the lone site emitting a qualified nominal, cause of "expected `Mod.T` but got `T`"; (3) `prebind_fn_scheme` declines to build a scheme from a QUALIFIED type name (falls back to the fresh-var placeholder) instead of emitting a qualified nominal it can't canonicalize env-lessly — fixing an order-dependent signature/argument mismatch without over-canonicalizing distinct same-suffix types (`Conduit.Config` vs stdlib `Config`); (4) bare-constructor seeding is SUPPRESSED for types a sibling `sig` exports opaquely (opacity filter threaded through prebind via an `~opaque` set built from sibling `sig` decls at both nested and unwrapped-entry levels), preserving opaque-type constructor hiding. All ~40 `conduit` files now `--check` clean as the entry, in any order. **Full six-runner suite green modulo the pre-existing baseline (15 Slow compiled adversarial-regressions + 1 codegen IR-gate — all present on `origin/main` before this change, verified by a file-copy baseline diff).** New regression tests `test_tc_cyclic_bare_ctor_order_independent` and `test_tc_qualified_sig_type_order_independent` (`test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`, module-system group) pin the cyclic-bare-ctor and qualified-signature cases; `test_tc_sig_opaque_hides_ctors` guards the opacity carve-out. Directly closes the "whole-program type resolution must be order-independent" constraint (`forge build` typechecks each lib file as its own entry).

- ✅ **Tetris live-compile browser playground + 3 JS-backend/typecheck bug fixes (`docs/tetris-playground/`, `js/march_browser_compile.ml`, `lib/driver/js_pipeline.ml`, `demo_app/tetris{,_logic}/`, 2026-07-08).** New browser demo: edit March source, hit Run, watch the real compiler (parse → typecheck → lower → optimize → js_emit) run entirely in-browser and produce a playable Tetris game in a fresh iframe. New `lib/driver/js_pipeline.ml` extracts the `--target js` TIR pipeline as a standalone library (verified to link under js_of_ocaml — the LLVM-only native-triple C stub dead-code-eliminates); a new `js/march_browser_compile.ml` entry point wraps it for the browser. Game: `demo_app/tetris_logic/` (pure rules, 14 forge unit tests) + `demo_app/tetris/` (Dom wiring, path-deps on `tetris_logic` so `forge test` stays native-safe — Dom externs have no native symbols, discovered the hard way when the first combined project failed to link natively). State lives in the DOM (`#game-state` data-* attrs) since March has no mutable-cell primitive reachable across independent event callbacks. Along the way, found and fixed three real, general compiler bugs (all pre-existing, not introduced by this feature): (1) `lib/tir/js_emit.ml` had no case for `int_div`/`int_mod`/`int_mod_euclid`/the bitwise family/`unix_time`/`int_pow`/`int_abs`/`int_max_value`/`int_min_value` — any `Array` growing past 32 elements, or `Random`, hits this; (2) `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml` never registered `string_from_codepoint`/`string_to_codepoints` at all, breaking any strict typecheck of `stdlib/string.march`; (3) `stdlib/random.march`'s `mix()` had an integer literal exceeding the March lexer's `max_int` — but only when the compiler ITSELF runs as js_of_ocaml-compiled browser JS (32-bit `int` representation there vs. native's 63-bit) — rewritten as an exactly-equal product+sum, a real fix for the pre-existing interpreter REPL playground's `Random` support too. Filed, not fixed: `check_module_full`'s pass-1 flat-merges bare names across many sibling stdlib modules, letting a same-named function in two modules (`fold_left`, in `prelude.march` and `list.march`/`array.march`) shadow across module boundaries — worked around narrowly in the playground bundle. Full suite green throughout (451 compiler / 231 eval / 398 codegen / 773 stdlib quick). See `specs/progress.md`'s matching entry for the full writeup; plan at `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-08-tetris-playground.md` (gitignored).

- ✅ **`march check`/`forge check` seed pass 1 from a cached, already-typechecked stdlib env instead of re-typechecking stdlib from scratch every invocation (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `bin/main.ml`, `specs/plans/2026-07-07-compiler-daemon-perf-plan.md`, 2026-07-07).** Follow-up to a compile/typecheck-speed opportunity sweep: `--timings` showed stdlib typecheck alone is ~68% of `forge check`'s wall time on a small (10-file) real project (`~/code/march_doc`), ~19% on a 16-file one, down to ~5% on an 80-file outlier — a large, avoidable, constant cost paid on every invocation of `run_check_cmd` (the `march check f1 f2 ...` subcommand `forge check`/`forge build` batch onto). **Investigated a persistent-daemon design first (see the plan doc's superseded "REVISED" section) but found it unnecessary:** `Typecheck.check_module_core` gained an additive `?seed_env` parameter — when given, pass 1 starts from it instead of `base_env`, with NO other change to pass 1/1b/2's structure, so every existing caller (passing `None`) is byte-for-byte unaffected. `bin/main.ml`'s `run_check_cmd` now builds (or loads from an on-disk Marshal cache, `get_stdlib_tc_env`, keyed by a content hash of `stdlib_decls`) a `stdlib_tc_env` via `check_module_core` on stdlib decls ALONE, then typechecks just the user's own files seeded from it — UNLESS a user file shadows a stdlib module name (rare; falls back unchanged to the original from-scratch combined check rather than parameterizing the cache key on the shadow set). Verified byte-identical diagnostic output against the unmodified compiler across `march_doc`/`marathon`/`scroll`/`bastion` plus synthetic error/warning fixtures. Measured: `march_doc` `forge check` 0.86s → 0.20s (~4.3x) on a warm cache, `marathon` 0.51s → 0.16s (~3.2x); `scroll`/`bastion` (both shadow a stdlib name via a transitive `depot` dependency) see no change, by design. **A real regression was found and reverted before shipping:** an earlier version also wired `compile` (`--compile`) the same way, but `compile`'s `desugared` value is ALSO used for TIR lowering (which needs stdlib's function BODIES, not just types) — skipping the stdlib prepend there silently dropped stdlib from what gets lowered, breaking every compiled program touching real stdlib internals. Caught by the full test suite (24 codegen + 6 stdlib failures, all "type-incorrect TIR reached codegen" ICEs) before being reported as done; `compile` was reverted to its original always-prepend behavior. Caching stdlib's LOWERED TIR for `--compile` is explicitly out of scope (a separate, riskier follow-up — `lower.ml`'s heavy use of global mutable `Hashtbl` refs makes this a bigger undertaking, not justified by `--compile`'s smaller measured lowering-cost share vs. typecheck's). - ✅ **`dependency_order_dmod_run` mixed hard (bare ctor/type) and soft (qualified-reference) dependency edges into one DFS, letting a soft-edge reference cycle silently reorder a hard edge — FIXED (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, 2026-07-07).** Found checking a real downstream project (`conduit`) whole-program: `Conduit` qualified-delegates to `Conduit.API`, which qualified-calls `Conduit.Worker`, which bare-pattern-matches `WorkerError` — a constructor `Conduit` itself declares. `march check` reported `` I don't know a constructor called `WorkerError` `` despite the declaration being correct. **Root cause:** `dependency_order_dmod_run` topologically orders sibling DMods over the UNION of `module_refs_in_decls` (qualified `Mod.fn`/`Mod.Ctor` references) and `unqualified_module_deps` (bare ctor/type references) — but the two are not equally load-bearing. Qualified references are pre-bound as pass-1 Mono placeholders regardless of check order (`prebind_mod_members`), so ordering by them is a precision nicety only (the rationale `0799c745` introduced this edge kind for — avoiding a caller pinning an under-generalized placeholder). Bare references have no such placeholder — the name is only visible once the defining sibling's DMod is actually processed by `check_decl` — so ordering by them is a hard correctness requirement. Real modules commonly form legitimate reference cycles through qualified calls alone (a facade delegating to an internal module that calls back into a module the facade depends on) — previously harmless, since qualified refs tolerate any order. Mixing both edge kinds into one DFS meant a soft-edge cycle could non-deterministically reorder a hard edge: whichever edge type the traversal reached an already-in-progress ancestor through "won", independent of which one actually mattered. **Fix:** compute the existing combined-edge DFS order unchanged (zero behavior change for the common case — every existing regression fixture, including the `0799c745` "dotted sibling module order" precision test, still passes byte-identically), then validate it against the hard edges alone; only when a hard edge is actually violated does it fall back to Kahn's algorithm restricted to hard edges, using the original order purely as a tie-break. New regression test `test_check_qualified_cycle_does_not_break_bare_ctor_ordering` in `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, minimized to the same three-module facade/worker/core shape (file naming is itself load-bearing there — `Cmd_build.find_march_files` walks sorted-ascending but prepends, so the actual file list handed to `march check` is sorted DESCENDING; the hard dependency's definer has to be discovered first through the real `forge check` path for the bug to reproduce, hence `zcore.march`). Verified against the live repro: `conduit`'s `WorkerError` error is gone; standard runners unaffected (424 compiler / 231 eval / 391 codegen, all exit 0; `forge/test/test_build_check.exe` 12/12).

- ✅ **Compiled `Task.await` on a heap (ptr) result crashed at runtime (`march: out of memory` / SIGSEGV) — FIXED (2026-07-06, `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml` `task_await` case).** The thunk trampoline stores `task[3] = (apply_ret << 1) | 1` — the apply-wrapper's uniform-slot return tagged exactly once. `march_task_await` wraps `task[3]` straight into `Ok(...)`, but a boxed-ADT field must hold the *uniform value* `apply_ret` verbatim: an `Ok(x)` destructure loads a **ptr** field **raw** (no untag, since a normal `Ok(heap_ptr)` stores an even raw pointer), so the Ok payload carried the wild `(addr<<1)|1 ≈ 2*addr` pointer — `march_incrc`/`march_decrc` no-op'd on it (odd ⇒ `IS_HEAP_PTR` false) and the payload deref (`march_string_concat`/`List.length`) hit garbage → OOM/SIGSEGV. Interpreter was always correct; `await!`/`task_await_unwrap` were fine (they use `march_task_await_value` + a type-directed untag). This is the ptr sibling of the i64 double-tag bug fixed on main in `f89b8711` — whose commit message *wrongly assumed* the ptr path was already correct. **Fix:** extend `f89b8711`'s guard from `inner_ty = "i64"` to `"i64" || "ptr"` and `ashr` the freshly-allocated Ok payload field (offset 16) once. `task[3]` is always odd, so a single arithmetic shift is the exact inverse for **both** reps — `4*n+3 → 2*n+1` (i64: the destructure's one conditional untag then yields `n`) and `(addr<<1)|1 → addr` (ptr: the raw pointer the destructure loads directly). `"double"` (Float, ABI-broken through the `void*`-returning trampoline — separate) and other reps left byte-identical. Covers every combinator funnelling through the `task_await` builtin (`await_many`, `async_stream`/`_n`, `all_settled`, `race`). Verified compiled == interpreter for String/List/tuple/ADT/list-of-string payloads and `await_many` over Strings; clean under ASAN (no UAF/overflow); the i64 path (`6*7 → 42`) is fixed as a side effect on this branch, which lacks `f89b8711`. Regression: `test/native/task_await_ptr.{march,expected}` + a `test/dune` native compiled-run golden (String/List/i64, `MARCH_NUM_SCHEDULERS=1`). **391 codegen / 231 eval pass.**

Corpus: `reject/t26_cross_module_private_fn` pins `Array.lst_rev(...)` now rejecting with `` is private to module `Array` ``; `accept/t31_cross_module_public_and_opaque_ptype` proves the gate is narrow — a PUBLIC cross-module call (`Array.length(Array.empty())`) still resolves, and the opaque-type pattern (a private `ptype`'s bare name usable in a cross-module annotation) still holds. `check_types.sh` green with the additions. - ✅ **Core March widening slice 1 — interfaces/impls declaration checking, dispatch, and `derive`/`satisfy`, CLOSEOUT (`specs/lang/core-march-types.md` §2.3/§2.4, `specs/lang/core-march.md` §4.4.2–§4.4.4, `specs/lang/types/{accept,reject}/t23`–`t30`/`t18`–`t24`, `specs/lang/types/INDEX.md`, `specs/lang/interfaces.md`, 2026-07-06, `specs/plans/2026-07-06-widening-interfaces-impls-plan.md`, six tasks).** Widens the two conformance-tested core-language references past the core expression fragment to cover user-defined `interface`/`impl` DECLARATION checking (`(T-Interface)` registration, `(T-Impl)`'s seven ordered checks including MANDATORY superclass/`requires` enforcement, `impl_matches_ty` named as its own rule `(T-ImplMatch)`, default methods), the operational method-DISPATCH split (built-in `Show`/`Eq`/`Ord`/`Hash` via a runtime `impl_tbl` hashtable vs. user interfaces via ordinary lexical `env` shadowing), and `derive`/`satisfy` as `DImpl` generators (the closed five-interface set, `Json`'s pseudo-interface special case, `satisfy`'s all-or-nothing name-matching wiring) — the roadmap's stated "natural next widening slice" after constraint-discharge. Corpus grew from 39 to **54 programs** (30 accept / 24 reject); `check_types.sh` 54/54, exit 0, no new CI wiring (rides the existing `types-check` dune alias). **Two real gaps found and FILED (both deliberately left OPEN, not fixed — this is a documentation-only slice):** (1) no impl-coherence check anywhere — two overlapping impls both typecheck silently, and the interpreter (last-registered-wins) and compiled backend (first-registered-wins) disagree at runtime, confirmed live for plain/generic-vs-specific/derive-vs-manual overlap; (2) `derive X for UnknownType` silently no-ops (exit 0, no diagnostic, on both `--check` and RUN) — the one asymmetric exception among every other "declaration target doesn't exist" case in this slice. **Bonus finding while reconciling `specs/lang/interfaces.md`'s stale "Known issue" callout:** that callout (claiming a default `neq`-calling-`eq` "hangs/stack-overflows," blamed on a now-fixed `impl_tbl` dispatch-key collision) was reproduced live and found FALSE — neither backend hangs, and the interpreter is fully correct — so the callout was corrected to a historical note. But a DIFFERENT, real, previously-undocumented bug was found in the same area while reverifying it: a user-interface default method whose body calls a sibling interface method (`neq` calling `eq`, `Ord`'s `lt`/`gt` calling `cmp`) compiles to a lambda that returns the same answer regardless of the actual call arguments — compiled-only, interpreter correct; also FILED (open), not fixed. `interfaces.md`'s "Interface Dispatch" section's over-strong "no vtables or runtime type lookups" claim was also softened/scoped to the compiled backend's statically-resolved common case, with a cross-reference to `core-march.md` §4.4.2's full account. See `specs/progress.md`'s "Core March widening slice 1" entry for the full writeup and `.superpowers/sdd/widening-task-6-report.md` for this closeout task's own report. **Next queued widening slice:** modules or actors (roadmap Phase-2b/3 phasing).
- ✅ **`run_check_cmd` never stripped a stdlib module shadowed by a user file, silently corrupting unrelated typecheck state (`bin/main.ml`, `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Found while trying to fully clean up a real dependency (`depot`) via the batched multi-file `march check`: two of depot's constructors (`PgTarget`/`SqliteTarget`) resolved fine when depot was checked alone, but became unresolvable — with no diagnostic pointing at the real cause — as soon as a large downstream consumer project's files were checked alongside it. Bisected (by halving the file set repeatedly) down to a single trigger file whose ONLY relevant property was declaring `mod Crypto do`, shadowing stdlib's own `Crypto` module by name. **Root cause:** the single-file `--check`/`--compile` path (`compile` in `bin/main.ml`) already strips a stdlib module from the combined declaration list when a project file shadows it by name (`extern_mod_names`, added specifically for this exact `mod Crypto do` scenario per its own doc comment) — but the multi-file `check` subcommand (`run_check_cmd`, batched onto by the `forge build`/`forge check` fix above) never had the equivalent guard, so two DMods both named `Crypto` ended up in the same combined module, corrupting unrelated global typecheck state badly enough to make a completely different file's own constructor unresolvable. **Fix:** `run_check_cmd` now filters `stdlib_decls` against the set of module names the checked files actually define (already computed by the dedup pass added in the fix above), mirroring `compile`'s existing `extern_mod_names` logic. New regression test `test_check_stdlib_shadow_does_not_corrupt_unrelated_module` in `forge/test/test_build_check.ml` — minimizing the real repro down to a 3-file case was itself informative: a same-file constructor build+match didn't reproduce it, only a shape where a separate file builds the value via a qualified call and a third file consumes it via a bare (unqualified) constructor pattern, exactly mirroring the real `depot_url.march`/`depot_db_repo.march` shape. Verified against the live repro: fixing this made BOTH `depot`'s `PgTarget`/`SqliteTarget` errors AND several of the downstream consumer's own unrelated errors (`ActionResult`/`ActionOk`/`ActionError`/`PathDep`, previously misattributed as real bugs in that project) disappear — they were all downstream victims of the same stdlib-shadowing corruption, not independent bugs.

- ✅ **A broken constructor field type was re-reported once per instantiation instead of once (`lib/errors/errors.ml`, `test/test_compiler.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Found while triaging the diagnostic output from the `run_check_cmd` fix above on the real ~85-file bastion project: one genuine typecheck error (`type Fallback = Fallback(Conn -> ActionResult -> Conn)` where `ActionResult` doesn't resolve) was printed 4 times, all citing the exact same file/line/column. **Root cause:** `instantiate_ctor` (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml:2464`) re-resolves a constructor's stored surface argument types via `surface_ty` on every instantiation (needed for fresh per-use type variables on polymorphic constructors) — but when one of those argument types fails to resolve, `surface_ty` re-emits the identical `(span, message)` diagnostic on every instantiation (pattern match, constructor call) instead of just the first. **Fix:** `Errors.report` (the single choke point every diagnostic passes through) now skips a diagnostic that exactly matches an already-reported `(severity, span, message)` triple — a byte-identical repeat at the same source location can only be the same fact re-derived, never two independent issues coinciding. New regression test `test_broken_ctor_field_type_reported_once` in `test/test_compiler.ml` (a 3-instantiation repro asserting the bogus-type error is reported exactly once). Verified against the live bastion repro: `router.march:46:35`'s `ActionResult` error dropped from 4 occurrences to 1; project-wide diagnostic count dropped from 54 to 46.

- ✅ **`march check`'s multi-file combined typecheck re-embedded shared/auto-discovered modules once per input file — confirmed superlinear blowup on a real ~85-file project, fixed (`bin/main.ml`'s `run_check_cmd`, `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Found immediately after landing the `forge build`/`forge check` batching entry below, by measuring real compile/typecheck time on an external ~85-file project (`~/code/bastion`): the combined `march check f1 f2 ... fn` never finished in 4+ minutes, versus the old per-file behavior completing the whole project in seconds. **Root cause:** `run_check_cmd` called `resolve_imports` once per input file, and each call's `auto_discover` step unconditionally re-walks and re-parses the ENTIRE library search path with dedup tables scoped to that one call only — but the resulting `extra_decls` were then merged INTO that file's own wrapper `DMod`'s body instead of emitted as flat top-level siblings, hiding any cross-file duplicate from a name-based dedup pass and (independently) giving auto-discovered modules the wrong qualified name (`EntryFile.Module.name` instead of `Module.name` — the exact hazard `resolve_imports`'s own doc comment warns nesting causes). Confirmed empirically before the fix: checking N files together, the SAME diagnostic (same file/line/message) appeared exactly N times, and total time compounded far worse than linearly (1 file: 0.97s, 2: 2.10s, 5: 23.71s). **Fix:** `extra_decls` are now returned as flat siblings (`extra_decls @ [own DMod]` instead of merged into the own DMod's `mod_decls`), plus a dedup-by-module-name pass over the combined top-level decl list (first occurrence wins — safe since one-mod-per-file means a shared module name is always the same file). Post-fix: error/warning counts stay flat regardless of file count, time scales roughly linearly (1→20 files: 1.0–1.7s, no blowup), and the full 85-file bastion project completes in ~4.3s (previously never finished). New regression test `test_check_does_not_duplicate_shared_module_diagnostics` in `forge/test/test_build_check.ml` asserts a shared warning is counted exactly once across a 4-file combined check, calling `Cmd_build.check_all` directly to inspect its returned warning count. **Unrelated finding surfaced along the way (not fixed, out of scope):** bastion's own code used `write(path)(content)`-style curried calls (~36 call sites across 3 files) that the recently-landed `f(1)(2)`-is-a-parse-error change now rejects — fixed in bastion itself (a separate project), not in this repo.

- ✅ **`forge build`/`forge check` batch library typecheck into one `march check` subprocess instead of one-per-file (`bin/main.ml`, `forge/lib/cmd_build.ml`, `forge/lib/cmd_check.ml`, `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Second half of the compile/typecheck-speed opportunity sweep. `Cmd_build.check_all` previously invoked `march --check <file>` as a separate subprocess per `.march` file in a library project, each independently re-parsing and re-typechecking the whole ~108-module stdlib plus any shared imports (e.g. a `common.march` imported by two sibling files got parsed/typechecked twice). Batched onto the compiler's existing combined-module `march check f1 f2 ...` subcommand instead — one process, one stdlib load, one typecheck across all files. Two wrinkles handled: (1) that subcommand (`run_check_cmd`) silently dropped warning diagnostics (only printed errors) — fixed to print both, in the same `file:line:col: <severity>: msg` format `count_diagnostics` already parses; (2) the single-file `--check` path had a compiler-side CAS cache making a repeated no-op rebuild near-instant, which the batched subcommand lacks — added a small forge-local cache (`.forge/check-cache/<hash-of-sorted-file-contents+lib_path_env>.clean` marker files) so an unchanged repeat `forge build`/`forge check` short-circuits before invoking `march` at all, rather than regressing relative to the old per-file behavior. Known limitation (documented in code): the cache key does not hash the *contents* of `MARCH_LIB_PATH` directories, only the env-var string, so editing a local `path = "../foo"` dependency in place without touching forge.toml/forge.lock won't invalidate it. 2 new Alcotest cases in `forge/test/test_build_check.ml` (warning surfacing from the combined module; cache-marker existence + mtime-unchanged-on-repeat-check).

- ✅ **`forge deps`/`forge build`/`forge check` now walk transitive dependencies instead of only a project's own direct `[deps]` (`forge/lib/project.ml`, `forge/lib/cmd_deps.ml`, `forge/lib/cmd_build.ml`, `forge/test/test_build_check.ml`, 2026-07-07).** Found while running a `forge build`/`forge check` timing analysis against a real external project (`~/code/scroll`, depends on `bastion` via path): `forge check` failed with `` Unknown module `Pool` `` (a module belonging to `depot`, which `bastion`'s own `forge.toml` depends on) — scroll never declared `depot` itself. **Root cause:** both `Cmd_deps.run` (installs deps + writes `forge.lock`) and `Cmd_build.lib_path_env` (builds `MARCH_LIB_PATH`) iterated only the current project's own flat `deps` list — neither recursed into an already-installed dependency's own `forge.toml` to discover ITS dependencies. (Note: `Archive_store.dep_lib_paths_for_archive`, used by the separate `forge publish`/archive-packaging path, already walked transitively — this gap was specific to the live dev-build/check path.) **Fix:** new `Project.dep_root_dir` resolves an installed dependency's own root (a `PathDep`'s target, or a git dep's CAS clone under `~/.march/cas/deps/<name>`) so its `forge.toml` can be read. `Cmd_build.collect_transitive_deps` recursively expands `MARCH_LIB_PATH` through every dependency-of-a-dependency, carrying each entry's own declaring root (a nested dep's `PathDep` is relative to ITS root, not the top-level project's). `Cmd_deps.bfs_install` installs wave-by-wave, discovering the next wave from each just-installed dep's own `forge.toml` `[deps]` (must run AFTER install since a git dep's `forge.toml` doesn't exist until cloned) and records every transitively-discovered dep in `forge.lock`. Both dedup by name with nearest-wins semantics and a `visited` set guards against dependency cycles. Verified live against the real scroll → bastion → depot chain (workaround of adding `depot` directly to scroll's `forge.toml` reverted first): `forge deps` now records `depot` in scroll's own `forge.lock`, and `forge check` passes cleanly with no direct scroll→depot dependency declared. New Alcotest case `test_lib_path_env_walks_transitive_path_deps` in `forge/test/test_build_check.ml` (a 3-project A→B→C path-dep chain where A's own code calls a C module directly).

- ✅ **Native codegen: bare sibling calls 2+ levels deep inside a stdlib/imported file mis-qualified — undefined symbols at link time (`lib/desugar/desugar.ml`, `lib/resolver/resolver.ml`, `bin/main.ml`, `test/native/nested_mod_qualcall.march`, `test/dune`, 2026-07-07).** Found trying to get `~/code/march_doc` to `forge build` cleanly: stdlib's `CRDT.PNCounter` (`mod PNCounter do ... end` nested inside `mod CRDT do ... end`) failed to link — `Undefined symbols: _PNCounter.map_inc, _PNCounter.map_sum, _PNCounter.map_max_merge`, referenced from the correctly-named `_CRDT.PNCounter.increment`/`.value`/etc. **Root cause:** `desugar.ml`'s `qualify_module_refs` (rewrites a bare intra-module call to its fully-qualified form so TIR's `rename_tir_vars` has something to match the definition's name against) always started its prefix accumulation at `""`. Since `March_ast.Ast.module_` splits a file's sole top-level `mod X do ... end` into separate `mod_name`/`mod_decls` fields (`mod_decls` is already the unwrapped body — no `DMod` node exists for the file's own name inside it), a stdlib/imported file's OWN top-level mod name was silently missing from the walk: `map_inc`'s bare call site inside `PNCounter.increment` got qualified as only `PNCounter.map_inc` (one level) instead of `CRDT.PNCounter.map_inc` (the true two-level nesting), while TIR lowering (which has direct access to the re-wrapping `DMod` auto-discovery produces) correctly named the DEFINITION `CRDT.PNCounter.map_inc` — reference and definition diverged and the linker rejected the binary outright. **Fix:** `qualify_module_refs` takes an `~entry_prefix` seed; `desugar_module` gained `~is_entry` (default `true`, preserving every pre-existing caller), computing `entry_prefix = if is_entry then "" else m.mod_name.txt ^ "."` — the entry file's own top mod name correctly stays OUT of the prefix (TIR unwraps the entry module; mirrors `Typecheck.cap_qual_prefix`'s existing, correct convention on the typecheck side), while a non-entry file's own name is now correctly folded in. `resolver.ml`'s two auto-discovery desugar call sites and `bin/main.ml`'s `load_stdlib_file` (for every stdlib file except `prelude.march`, which is unwrapped into global scope exactly like an entry module) now pass `~is_entry:false`. Verified: the real `CRDT.PNCounter` shape compiles+links+runs correctly standalone; `~/code/march_doc`'s `forge build` no longer errors on `_PNCounter.*` undefined symbols (only the separate, pre-existing, documented native `http_fetch`/`http_fetch_available` gap remains — eval/browser-only builtins, see the 2026-06-18 entry above). New native golden test `test/native/nested_mod_qualcall.march` (real `CRDT.PNCounter` shape, diffs against `.expected`). **NOT fixed (filed, narrower, lower-impact — see the "self-qualifying entry module" P2 item below):** an entry file explicitly writing out its OWN top-level mod name when self-qualifying a nested call (e.g. `mod Outer do fn main() do Outer.Inner.wrapped(5) end end`) still produces undefined symbols, since nothing strips that redundant self-prefix back off before TIR lowering (which never includes it in the first place).

- ✅ **`--timings` now covers parse/desugar/import-resolution/stdlib-load, not just typecheck-onward (`bin/main.ml`, `test/test_properties.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Investigated as part of a compile/typecheck-speed opportunity sweep: the `--timings` flag's clock (`t_compile_start`) was only started after the frontend (parse, desugar, cross-file import resolution, stdlib load) had already finished, so the cost of re-parsing/re-typechecking the ~108-module stdlib on every invocation — often the dominant cost for small user programs — was invisible. Moved the timer to start right before parsing and added `"parse"`/`"desugar"`/`"resolve-imports"`/`"stdlib-load"` stamps ahead of the existing `"typecheck"`-onward ones (which are unchanged, just now measured from an earlier, more accurate start point). New unit test `test_timings_covers_frontend` in `test/test_properties.ml`.

- ✅ **Resolved surface grammar reference v1 — `specs/lang/grammar.md`, `specs/lang/grammar/{parse,reject}/*.march` (27 programs), `check_grammar.sh`, `INDEX.md`, `grammar-check` CI lane (2026-07-06, `specs/plans/2026-07-06-resolved-grammar-plan.md`, six tasks).** Satisfies roadmap §6's "surface grammar (resolved)" Level-1/2 acceptance criterion for the **core** grammar. Reconciles the three-layer parse pipeline (lexer → `token_filter` → menhir) `lib/parser/parser.mly` leaves implicit into one normative, cited-by-line reference: §2 lexical layer (incl. string-interpolation brace-depth tracking, the one non-context-free lexer behavior); §3 the `token_filter` pre-pass (soft-keyword demotion, `choose…by` disambiguation, and the core newline-glom/match-arm-boundary lookahead — the genuinely non-context-free layer — plus the `is_pattern_start` hand-maintained-shadow-of-the-pattern-grammar hazard, cross-checked live and found in sync as of this pass); §4 the expression precedence ladder (10 strata, associativity witnessed by value-producing corpus programs, not merely transcribed from `parser.mly`); §5 blocks/statements/significant-newline semantics; §6 patterns (incl. the `PatRecord`/`PatAs` unreachable-from-surface-syntax finding, cross-referenced with `core-march.md`/`core-march-types.md`'s prior operational/typing-side notes of the same fact); §7 types; §8 core declaration forms (`mod` one-per-file, `fn`/`pfn` multi-head merge via `group_fn_clauses`, `type`/`ptype`, `use`/`import`/`alias`, `interface`/`impl`, `derive`/`satisfy`, no-`pub`-keyword visibility); §9 a deliberately lighter DSL appendix (actors/`app`/supervision/protocols/transitions/capability directives — shape+citation only, explicitly not fully resolved). Backed by a 27-program `parse/`/`reject` conformance corpus (17 parse + 10 reject, `specs/lang/grammar/INDEX.md` maps every program to the rule it anchors) run via `specs/lang/grammar/check_grammar.sh` (**27/27 passed**) and wired into CI as its own `grammar-check` dune alias (`test/dune`, mirroring `specs/lang/types/`'s `types-check` exactly — a separate slow lane, `dune build @grammar-check`, NOT folded into `runtest`/`oracle`), verified green (exit 0) via the exact command CI runs. Two findings surfaced by the corpus work, both collected in the chapter's own new "Known parser findings" section: (i) the `f(1)(2)`-chained-call position-dependence doc-precision gap (see the "Grammar / lint contradictions" entry above — **left OPEN**, not fixed by this closeout); (ii) the `is_pattern_start` shadow-grammar drift hazard (found in sync this pass, no automated guard against future drift — documented, not fixed). **Follow-up (not done in this pass, tracked here):** full resolution of §9's DSL forms (per-form EBNF, every error-recovery message captured live, dedicated parse/reject corpus programs) to the same depth as §4–§8.
- ✅ **Multi-arm `with ... else` failed to parse entirely (`lib/parser/token_filter.ml`, `test/test_compiler.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Any monadic `with pat <- e do body else ... end` with **two or more** else-arms was a hard parse error — the caret landed on the second arm's `->` — no matter the arm shape (nullary ctors, payload ctors, infix-operator bodies); a single else-arm always worked. This made the entire multi-arm error-handling form documented in `docs/pattern-matching.md`'s "With (Monadic Pattern Matching)" section (including its 3-arm `Err(AuthFailed)`/`Err(NotFound(kind))`/`Err(Timeout)` example) unwriteable. **Root cause:** the grammar parses else-arms with `separated_nonempty_list(arm_sep, branch)` — the same rule as `match` branches, needing NL/PIPE arm separators — but `token_filter.ml` only emitted arm-separator newlines inside a `Match` context. A monadic `with`'s `do` pushed a plain `Block`, so the newlines between else-arms were swallowed as insignificant whitespace (a single arm needs no separator, hence only multi-arm broke). **Fix:** a new `With` context variant marks the with-block — recorded when a `do` follows a `<-` (`GETS`, unique to with-bindings; multiple bindings of one `with` dedup to one pending entry keyed by paren-depth, mirroring `pending_match_depths`) — and at the `else` keyword the `With` context is promoted to `Match`, so the arms are newline-separated exactly like a `match` body; the single `end` pops it. Composes cleanly with the same-day cond-form/when-guard token-filter change (the promoted arms are ordinary pattern arms → `ms_is_cond = false`; verified `match do` boolean-operator arms still parse). The with-body itself stays block-style. `if ... else`, record-update `{ e with ... }` (uses `WITH` but no `GETS`), and `else if` chains are untouched (their `do` pushes `Block`, not `With`, so the `else` handler is a no-op for them). **Known pre-existing limitation (verified identical on base via file-copy revert — NOT a regression; mirrors the `match`-scrutinee case):** a *bare* unparenthesized `do`-block expression (`if`/`with`) as a with-binding RHS steals the pending marker — parenthesize the RHS (a bare `match` RHS works, since `match` has its own pending mechanism). 4 new parser regression tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (single-arm guard, two nullary-ctor arms, three payload/nested-payload arms, infix-operator arm bodies). **Verification (six runners):** 420 compiler (+4) / 231 eval / 391 codegen / 804 stdlib (full, with Slow) / 29 snapshots exit 0; `test_stdlib_march`'s `global_registry` group (18/18) fails **pre-existing on clean main** (unbound `GlobalRegistry.*`, a module-resolution issue unrelated to this parser-only change — that module has zero `<-` tokens; confirmed by reverting the change and re-running). The `docs/pattern-matching.md` 3-arm example now compiles and runs.

- ✅ **`derive` on a variant type whose name collides with a stdlib RECORD type silently failed to typecheck — "`T` does not implement interface `Eq`/`Show`" (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `test/test_codegen.ml`, 2026-07-06).** Found verifying `docs/interfaces.md`'s canonical `type Color = Red | Green | Blue` / `derive Eq, Show for Color` example live: it failed to compile with "`Color` does not implement interface `Eq`", while renaming the type to `Status` made the identical program work. **Root cause:** record types register in `env.records` under their BARE name globally (both `name.txt` and the qualified `qname`), so a user's variant `Color` collides in that flat namespace with stdlib `Plot.Color = { r, g, b }` (always auto-loaded). Both `surface_ty` (the `Ast.TyCon` record-expansion at the impl-type conversion in `check_decl`'s `DImpl`) and `register_impl_shape`'s `lenient_ty` (pass-1 pre-registration) then structurally expanded the variant's derived `impl Eq(Color)` to the record's `TRecord{r,g,b}` shape — confirmed by a structural dump of `env.impls["Eq"]`: `target=TCon(Color/0)` vs `impls=[TRecord{b,g,r}; …]`, `impl_matches_ty` false, so the derived impl was invisible and the type read as "does not implement". (The trigger is purely the type-NAME collision with a stdlib record; the `Plot.Color` fields even leaked into a two-*variant* repro, proving stdlib Plot — not any nested type — was the corruptor in every case.) **Fix:** a new `name_is_variant env name` helper (checks whether any constructor in `env.ctors` has `name` as its parent `ci_type`, bare or `.name`-suffix) now guards all three record-expansion `when` clauses (the two in `surface_ty` — direct + module-registry — and the one in `register_impl_shape`): a name that also denotes a variant is kept nominal (`TCon`) instead of being expanded to a same-named record's structure. A variant is never itself a record, so this only removes incorrect expansions — genuine record impls (`type Point = {x,y}` / `derive Eq, Show for Point`) still expand and dispatch structurally (verified). **Regression tests:** 2 compiled-interp-parity cases in `test/test_codegen.ml`'s `newtype_derived_method_crash` group — a variant colliding with stdlib `Plot.Color`, and a self-contained variant colliding with a *local* nested record (distinct `hue/sat/lum` fields, so it guards the fix even if `Plot.Color` is renamed/removed); both RED pre-fix (verified via file-copy swap to `git show HEAD:…typecheck.ml`), GREEN post-fix. **Gates (six runners):** 400 compiler / 230 eval / 391 codegen / 804 stdlib (full, with Slow) / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots — all exit 0. The `docs/interfaces.md` example needs no change (it now works as written; the suggested `Status` rename was only a stopgap for an unfixed compiler).

Compiler internals grouped into a sibling implementation reference (`specs/impl/index.md`) over 9 docs, referenced-not-merged. Superseded docs redirect via stubs; `scripts/check-docs.sh` now globs `specs/lang/` + `specs/impl/`. See `forgepm/specs/forge-publish-client.md` for the full client-registry contract.

- ✅ **`Cli` stdlib module — Task 2: `Cli.parse` flag/value/positional parsing loop + basic accessors (`stdlib/cli.march`, `test/stdlib/test_cli.march`, 2026-07-05).** Second task of the argument-parsing `Cli` module plan (follows Task 1's types/constructors). New in `stdlib/cli.march`: `Cli.parse(specs, argv) : Result(ParsedArgs, CliError)` — a single left-to-right recursive `parse_loop` that classifies each token via `flag_name` (strips a leading `--`/`-`; `None` means positional), resolves it against `specs` by long or short name (`resolve_spec`/`find_by_long`/`find_by_short`), consumes a following value for `ValueFlag` specs (`Err(MissingValue(long))` if none), records `"true"` for `BoolFlag` specs, accumulates unmatched tokens as positionals, and at end-of-input checks every `required: true` spec got a value (`Err(MissingRequired(long))` via `find_missing_required`) before returning `Ok({values, positional})` (both accumulators reversed once, not consed in output order). (2) the brief's `flag_name` used a 2-branch `if/else if/else` chain closed with a single `end` — March requires one `end` per `if` in an `else if` chain (each `else` branch is a `block_body` that can itself contain a full nested `if...end`, so an N-`if` chain needs N `end`s; confirmed against `stdlib/base64.march`'s existing 3-way `else if` chain) — added the second `end`. (3) the brief's `find_missing_required` and `get_string` used `pair.0`/`pair.1` tuple-index field access on a `(String, String)` tuple — March's grammar has no numeric tuple-index production at all (`lib/parser/parser.mly`'s `expr_field` only accepts `DOT lower_name`/`upper_name`; no `DOT INT`), so `pair.0` fails to parse in any context, not just this one — rewrote both as `match pair do (name, value) -> ... end` pattern destructuring instead (the established March idiom per `stdlib/array.march`/`stdlib/bigint.march`'s existing `let (a, b) = tuple` usage). **All three are language-level constraints, not implementation choices** — the parsing/accessor *logic* itself (loop structure, error cases, accumulator order) matches the brief exactly. **Doctest note (pre-existing, not a regression):** `Cli.parse`'s own one-line doctest passes; but the 6 doctests using the brief's two-line `let parsed = Cli.parse(...)` / `match parsed do ... end` pattern (`Cli.get_string`, `Cli.get_string_or`, `Cli.get_bool`, `Cli.positional`, plus Task 1's carried-over `Cli.flag`/`Cli.value_flag`/`Cli.flag_with`) fail with "doctest parse error" — confirmed identical to the pre-existing `RRB.fold`/`RRB.chunk` doctest failures on a clean checkout of Task 1's commit (`f16cecf2`, via an isolated `git worktree add`), i.e. the doctest runner's single-expression `expr_eof` parser cannot handle a bare `let` as one `march>` line, regardless of module. - ✅ **`Cli` stdlib module — Task 1: `FlagSpec`/`ParsedArgs`/`CliError` types + spec constructors (`stdlib/cli.march`, `test/stdlib/test_cli.march`, `bin/main.ml`, 2026-07-05).** First task of the argument-parsing `Cli` module plan. New `stdlib/cli.march`: `FlagArity = BoolFlag | ValueFlag`, `FlagSpec` record (`long`/`short`/`arity`/`default`/`required`/`help`), `CliError = UnknownFlag | MissingValue | MissingRequired | InvalidValue` (parse-time errors for later tasks), `ParsedArgs` record (`values`/`positional`). Three constructors: `Cli.flag(long, help)` (boolean, no short form, optional), `Cli.value_flag(long, help)` (value-taking, optional, no default), `Cli.flag_with(long, short, arity, default, required, help)` (full constructor). Registered `"cli.march"` in `bin/main.ml`'s `stdlib_file_list` (required for `Cli` to resolve at all via eager stdlib loading — the module-registry lookup by itself only kicks in for explicitly-imported/lib-path modules, not the built-in stdlib set). 3 tests in `test/stdlib/test_cli.march` (spec-constructor field checks), all green. **Doctest note:** the module's three `doc` blocks originally used a call-then-field-access one-liner (`Cli.flag(...).long`) — March's parser does not support field access directly on a call-expression result (`mk().x` fails to parse; confirmed as a general grammar gap, not doctest-specific). Rewritten as two-line `let`-then-field doctests, matching the pattern in `stdlib/rrb_vec.march`; those `let`-as-doctest-line examples are known to fail the doctest runner's single-expression `expr_eof` parse (pre-existing gap — `RRB.fold`/`RRB.chunk` doctests fail identically on unmodified `main`), so `Cli.flag`/`Cli.value_flag`/`Cli.flag_with`'s doctests currently report as failing for the same pre-existing infra reason; not introduced by this task and out of scope to fix here. — `let ((a,b),(c,d)) = ...` emitted references to undefined global functions (`lib/tir/lower.ml`, `test/test_codegen.ml`, `specs/lang/golden/`, `specs/lang/core-march.md`, 2026-07-05).** Found by the Core March golden corpus (Phase 1 Task 2, tuples). A nested tuple destructured in a block-`let` — e.g. `let ((a, b), (c, d)) = ((1, 2), (3, 4))` — ran correctly interpreted (prints `10`) and compiled fine as the equivalent `match ((1,2),(3,4)) do ((a,b),(c,d)) -> … end`, but `--compile` on the `let` form emitted `%gl = call ptr @a()` for every leaf var and clang rejected the module (`error: use of undefined value '@a'`, exit 1). **Root cause:** the block-`let` `PatTuple` lowering (`EBlock (ELet … :: rest)` arm) bound only *direct* `PatVar` tuple elements — its inner fold had `| Ast.PatVar n -> …bind field… | _ -> inner`, so any non-var element (crucially a NESTED `PatTuple`) hit the `| _ -> inner` catch-all and was **silently dropped**. The nested tuple's leaf vars (`a`/`b`/`c`/`d`) were therefore never bound; later uses fell through `resolve_use_alias` and were rewritten into global function references (`@a()`), which don't exist → clang error. (`collect_pat_names` DID recurse — so the names were registered in `_fn_param_types` and typechecked — but the value-binding fold flattened only one level, which is why the failure surfaced at codegen, not typecheck.) **Fix:** replaced the one-level fold with a recursive `bind_subpat scrut scrut_ty pat inner` helper (local to the `PatTuple` arm) that mirrors the match path's `compile_matrix` decomposition — it handles `PatWild` (skip), `PatVar` (bind field directly, preserving the original RC-friendly single-level shape when the element is a leaf), `PatAs` (bind outer name + recurse), and nested `PatTuple` (bind a fresh var to the field via `EField`, then recurse into it, threading each element's concrete type from the parent tuple type so nested scalar fields untag correctly). Records / refutable sub-patterns keep the prior no-decompose behaviour (unchanged; they fall to the outer catch-all `let`). Interpreter and flat-tuple / direct-`PatVar` lowering are unchanged (flat `let (a,b) = …` produces byte-identical TIR — the 29 TIR snapshots stay green with no regeneration). **Regression:** new `nested_tuple_let_codegen` group in `test/test_codegen.ml` (2 compile-and-run tests: the exact repro → `10`; a deeper 3-level-nesting + wildcard-element + interior-nested-tuple program → `15`) — both RED pre-fix with the `@a` clang error, GREEN post-fix. - ✅ **`==` operator gave the WRONG answer (silent, not a crash) compiled on a `Newtype`-repr type with a heap payload (`lib/tir/llvm_eq.ml`, `test/test_codegen.ml`, `test/test_properties.ml`, 2026-07-04).** Found by the differential oracle (Task 4 / Phase 2b) while scoping the derived-method generators; distinct from the named-method fix `6cc676fc` (that fixed the NAMED `eq()`/`compare()` path via desugar span-uniquification + `emit_case` Newtype TVar-recovery; this is the `==` OPERATOR path). For `type W = W(String)` (Newtype repr — single ctor, single field — so the value IS its raw payload, no wrapper cell), compiled `W("x") == W("x")` returned `false` while the interpreter correctly gave `true`. **Root cause:** `ensure_adt_eq_fn` special-cased the Niche (Option-shaped) repr but never consulted `Repr.repr_of_ty` for `Newtype`, so a single-ctor single-field `TCon` fell to the generic Boxed ctor-table strategy, which reads a "ctor tag" at `payload_ptr + 8` and a "field" at `payload_ptr + 16`. For a Newtype the "payload_ptr" IS the raw payload (the String's own heap cell / a Boxed ADT cell), so those offsets land inside the payload's layout and the comparison is garbage. Confirmed by `--emit-llvm`: pre-fix `__march_eq_W` took the full boxed tag-load path; post-fix it is `%ok = call i64 @march_string_eq(ptr %a, ptr %b)  ret i64 %ok`. Affects any heap payload (verified: a Newtype over a Boxed 2-field ADT returned `true` for two DISTINCT values pre-fix); an Int/Bool-payload Newtype is a tagged scalar (`i64`, not `ptr`) and never enters `ensure_adt_eq_fn` (the `==`-lowering site gates on `ty_a = "ptr"`), so it was always correct. **Fix:** a `Repr.Newtype payload` arm in `ensure_adt_eq_fn` (checked before niche detection — the shapes are mutually exclusive, and `repr_of_ty` already routes Float-payload single-ctor types to Boxed) that compares the unwrapped operands directly per the payload's repr: `march_string_eq` for String, `fcmp` for a generic-Float payload, tagged-bits `icmp` for `payload_needs_tag` scalars, recursive `ensure_adt_eq_fn` (called on the raw operands) for a nested heap ADT/tuple/record, and `march_poly_eq` as the erased-`TVar`-payload fallback — no tag/field offset load. Generic newtypes get the concrete payload via the same `type_params` substitution the Boxed arm uses. Interpreter semantics unchanged. **Regression:** 4 compiled parity tests in `test/test_codegen.ml`'s `newtype_derived_method_crash` suite (String-payload `==`/`!=` — RED pre-fix; Int-payload control — green before and after; Boxed-ADT-payload `==` exercising the recursive arm — RED pre-fix; a generic `type Wrap(a) = Wrap(a)` at String+Int exercising the `type_params` substitution branch — the only test that drives a non-identity subst). Differential-oracle `gen_derived_method_newtype_string_module` (`test/test_properties.ml`), previously scoped to named `eq()`/`compare()` only to stay in the working subset, was widened to also exercise the `==` operator (oracle index 12 green, 50/50 matched interp = compiled). **Compiler builds clean; `newtype_derived_method_crash` 10/10 green; newtype-string oracle 50/50.**

- ✅ **Compiler robustness: an unreadable sibling directory crashed `--compile`/`--check` with an uncaught `Sys_error` (`lib/resolver/resolver.ml`, `bin/main.ml`, `test/test_codegen.ml`, 2026-07-04).** Found while running the differential oracle for real (Task 1 of the differential-oracle work; design at `specs/2026-07-04-differential-oracle-design.md`). The compiler auto-discovers sibling `.march` modules in the entry file's OWN source directory (`resolve_imports` plus the early-CAS sibling hash both walk it via `March_resolver.Resolver.collect_lib_files`). That recursive walk classified a subdirectory with `Sys.is_directory` (which stats fine on a permission-denied dir → `true`), recursed into it, and then called `Sys.readdir` on it **with no exception guard** — so a permission-denied sibling directory raised `Sys_error` uncaught to `bin/main.ml`'s top level, killing the compile (exit 2, no output binary) on an otherwise well-typed program. The trigger is real on stock macOS: `$TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/.../T/`) contains a Spotlight-managed `TemporaryItems` directory that is `Operation not permitted`, so any well-typed program placed directly in `$TMPDIR` failed to compile. Fixed by guarding the recursive `Sys.readdir` in `collect_lib_files` (`try … with Sys_error _ -> [||]` → an unreadable directory is treated as empty and skipped, never aborts the walk). Hardened the parallel unguarded walk `march_files_in` in `bin/main.ml` (the `--check <dir>` path — same latent bug, plus its `Sys.is_directory` is now exception-safe) and the `march test` auto-discovery `Sys.readdir "test"` (permission-denied `test/` now skipped like a missing one). The two other `Sys.readdir` sites (`cache_dir`, `runtime_dir`) were already guarded; the remaining `Sys.is_directory`-in-predicate sites are each short-circuited by a preceding `Sys.file_exists` and never readdir, so they can't hit this class. Regression: new `compiler_robustness` group in `test/test_codegen.ml` (`test_unreadable_sibling_dir_does_not_crash_check`) — a well-typed entry beside a 0000-perm sibling dir must `--check` at exit 0 (`--check` shares the exact crashing early-CAS/resolver walk with `--compile` but needs no clang, so it runs everywhere; perms restored via `Fun.protect`). RED→GREEN verified (unfixed binary: `Sys_error(... TemporaryItems ...)` EXIT:2 → fixed: EXIT:0). **Note:** this was independently worked around in the oracle harness itself (`test/test_properties.ml` isolates each generated program in its own dedicated temp dir), but the compiler must not crash on it — that is what this fixes. Six-runner gates: **392 compiler / 230 eval / 381 codegen (+1 new) / stdlib / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots**; the 14 `adversarial-regressions` (stdlib `Unknown module IO/BigInt`) and 1 `llvm_ir_validity_gate` (distributed-program TIR-typing) failures in this worktree were verified **pre-existing on the base commit** (identical failures with the fix reverted) — unrelated to this change and out of scope.

- ✅ **Interpreter: named `eq`/`compare`/`hash` misdispatched with 2+ impls of the same interface in scope (`lib/eval/eval.ml`, 2026-07-04)** — `DImpl` eval (two sites: the module-level `eval_decl` handler and the top-level-let `make_recursive_env` handler) bound each impl method's bare name directly into the env in addition to `impl_tbl`, so a second `derive Eq`/`derive Ord`/`derive Hash` for a different type shadowed the first — `eq(Wrap(1), Wrap(1))` returned `false` (ran the wildcard `_ -> false` arm of `WrapS`'s derived Eq) and `compare(Wrap(1), Wrap(2))` panicked with a non-exhaustive match (`WrapS`'s per-constructor match had no arm for `Wrap`). The infix operators (`==`, `<`) and `Show.show` were unaffected — `cmp_op` always dispatches via `type_name_of_value` + `impl_tbl`, and `Show.show` was already the one method excluded from the env-binding. Compiled mode was unaffected (`lib/tir/lower.ml`'s `resolve_iface_method` resolves per-type mangled impls by argument type). Fix: generalized the `Show.show` special-case into `is_type_dispatched_method` (`Show.show | Eq.eq | Ord.compare | Hash.hash`) at both DImpl sites — these now bind as a plain closure registered only in `impl_tbl`, never as a shadowing bare env binding. Regression tests: `test_eval_eq_multi_type_dispatch`, `test_eval_compare_multi_type_dispatch`, `test_eval_hash_multi_type_dispatch` in `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`'s `interface_dispatch` group. - ✅ **`spawn(<computed expr>)` crashed `--compile` with an uncaught `Failure` on a well-typed program — shape restriction now enforced in the typechecker (`lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`, `test/test_compiler.ml`, 2026-07-04).** Found during Task 1 of `specs/plans/2026-07-04-differential-oracle-plan.md` (differential-oracle `classify_compile` work). A well-typed program that spawns a *computed* actor expression — e.g. `spawn(if true do Counter else Counter end)` — passed `--check` with exit 0 but, when compiled, escaped to OCaml's top-level handler with `Fatal error: exception Failure("TIR lower: ESpawn argument must be a plain actor name")` (exit 2, no binary produced). Distinct from the known "Monomorphization limit reached" P0 above: this is compiled-backend-only and specific to the `spawn` argument shape. **Root cause:** the parser (`lib/parser/parser.mly:1222`, `SPAWN LPAREN expr RPAREN`) and the typechecker (`ESpawn` arm) accepted `spawn(e)` for *any* expression with zero shape restriction, but `lib/tir/lower.ml`'s `ESpawn` lowering only handles a bare actor name (`ECon(_,[],_)` / `EVar` — it dispatches by *name* to a statically generated `<Actor>_spawn` function) and hit an unguarded `failwith` for anything else; `bin/main.ml`'s compile path runs the TIR pipeline with no enclosing `try/with`, so the `Failure` propagated straight to the top level. **Why "reject earlier" and not "support it":** there is *no runtime actor-descriptor value* in either backend — the interpreter (`lib/eval/eval.ml:7122-7127`) *also* requires a plain actor name (`eval_error "spawn: expected actor name (got complex expression)"`), so "spawn a computed actor" is a feature that exists in neither backend, not merely a lowering robustness gap. **Fix:** the `ESpawn` arm in `typecheck.ml` now checks the argument is a plain actor name (`ECon(_,[],_)` / `EVar`, mirroring exactly what `lower.ml` accepts) and otherwise emits a structured `Err.error` pointing at the argument span, so `--check` / `--compile` / interpret now all reject the program uniformly with the same clean diagnostic before it can reach the internal `failwith` (which is retained as a now-unreachable invariant backstop). Valid `spawn(Counter)` is unaffected (compiles + runs). **Regression:** 2 new `test/test_compiler.ml` typecheck cases — `spawn computed actor: rejected` (asserts `has_errors` + the diagnostic mentions "spawn" and "plain actor name") and `spawn plain actor name: ok` (no false positive on the valid form). Six runners green: **394 compiler (+2) / 230 eval / 380 codegen / 799 stdlib / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots** — zero `.expected` diffs; the lone stdlib "failure" (`test_compiled_actor_program_exits_without_kill`) was a load-induced 60s-watchdog timeout during a 109s heavily-loaded run and passes 3/3 in isolation.

- ✅ **`is_lib_file` off-by-one dead-coded the `_test.march` exclusion in `safety/no-panic-in-lib` (`lib/lint/lint.ml`, `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml`, `test/test_helpers.ml`, `docs/coding-standards.md`, 2026-07-03)** — the test-file guard compared the 11-char literal `"_test.march"` against only the last **10** characters (`String.sub base (len-10) 10`), so the equality was always false and every `*_test.march` file was classified as library code — making `safety/no-panic-in-lib` fire on test files that legitimately `panic`/assert (e.g. via `stdlib/test.march` helpers). New `lint/safety/no-panic-in-lib` test group in `test/test_stdlib_suite.ml` (4 cases, via a new filename-taking `lint_check_named` helper since `lint_check` hardcodes `"test.march"`): panic in `foo_test.march` and under `test/` must NOT be flagged; the same source in `foo.march` and under `lib/` MUST be (RED 2/4 → GREEN 4/4, proving the positive cases still detect real lib panics). `docs/coding-standards.md` detection note corrected to match (also fixed its pre-existing "module with no `fn main()`" imprecision — the check is basename `main.march`).
