Desugar normalization already existed in `desugar.ml:474-494`: `EField(ECon(mod,[]),name)` → `ECon("Mod.Name",[])` for uppercase (constructors) or `EVar("Mod.name")` for lowercase (functions); `EApp(ECon(qualified,[]),args)` folded into `ECon(name,args)` at lines 432-443; record field access (`EField(EVar(...),...)`) correctly left untouched. 7 new tests: 2 module_registry (register+lookup, is_known_module), 5 desugar_qualified (Module.Ctor(args)→ECon, Module.Ctor→ECon, Module.func(args)→EApp, record.field not rewritten, Module.func ref→EVar). Spec: `specs/qualified-modules.md`.

- ✅ **Perceus RC leak fix for C extern / TIR builtin functions** — `lib/tir/borrow.ml`: added `extern_borrow_table` (hardcoded list of C extern and TIR builtin function names with per-parameter borrow flags) and `is_extern_borrowed` helper. `is_borrowed` now falls back to this table when the function name is absent from the March borrow map — covering `march_string_eq`, `march_string_concat`, `march_string_byte_length`, `march_string_is_empty`, `march_string_to_int`, `march_string_to_float`, `march_print`, `march_println`, all extended `march_string_*` ops, `march_compare_string`, `march_hash_string`, and their TIR builtin-name aliases. Previously, borrow inference treated every parameter of unknown callees as owned, causing Perceus to insert spurious IncRC with no matching DecRC for string arguments — a silent RC leak on any string comparison, concatenation, or print call in compiled mode.

- ✅ **Actor + HTTP scheduler integration fix** — `runtime/march_runtime.c`: two bugs fixed that caused actors to be silently ignored in compiled HTTP servers. (1) Background scheduler thread: `march_spawn()` now calls `march_ensure_sched_started()` which launches a background pthread running `march_sched_run()` alongside the kqueue/epoll HTTP event-loop threads; for non-HTTP programs `march_run_scheduler()` joins the background thread instead of running inline — no observable change for non-HTTP programs. (2) `actor_get_int` field offset: corrected from raw word index to `index + 4` (skipping the 4-word header: rc, tag+pad, $dispatch, $alive) so index 0 returns the first state field instead of rc=1.

- ✅ **`--dump-phases` + phase viewer (Phases 1–4)** — `march --dump-phases --compile file.march` serializes each IR stage to `march-phases/phases.json`. **Phases 1–2**: JSON graph (`{ phase, nodes, edges }`) with `id`, `label`, `type`, `metadata` (calls, RC ops, arity); Cytoscape.js viewer with diff mode. **Phase 3**: `lib/tir/opt.ml` now accepts `~snap` callback emitting a snapshot after every individual opt pass (`tir-opt-{iter}-known-call`, `-inline`, `-cprop`, `-fold`, `-simplify`, `-fusion`, `-dce`). **Phase 4**: stable name-based node IDs (`fn_<name>`, `type_<name>`) so the same logical entity keeps its ID across passes; `body_hash` djb2 fingerprint detects body changes in diff. `tools/phase-viewer.html`: opt passes grouped under "Opt iter N" section headers, per-pass colour coding, diff summary bar (`+X added ~Y changed -Z removed`). `forge build/run --dump-phases` pass the flag through.
- ✅ **GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows** — `.github/workflows/build.yml` (reusable matrix build: macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, Linux x86_64 static); `.github/workflows/release.yml` (tag-triggered release: builds all platforms, uploads binaries, generates SHA256 checksums, creates GitHub Release with install instructions); `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` (scheduled 02:00 UTC nightly build with Slack/artifact notifications); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (PR/push CI on macOS + Ubuntu). `scripts/marchup` — POSIX shell installer: detects platform, downloads matching binary from GitHub Releases, installs to `~/.march/bin`, updates PATH in `.bashrc`/`.zshrc`. Spec: `specs/github_release_builds.md`.
- ✅ **Module load-order independence (global module registry)** — `lib/eval/eval.ml`: `module_registry` hashtable (64-slot) populated as each `DMod` is evaluated. `EField` qualified lookups check the registry at call time (after the lexical env), so closures captured in one module can call functions from another module even if that module is evaluated later in the file. `lookup` fallback also checks the registry for dotted names not found in the lexical env. Registry cleared at the start of `eval_module_env` to keep runs isolated. Tests added in `test/test_march.ml`.
- ✅ **Event-loop HTTP server (Phases 1–2)** — `runtime/march_http_evloop.c` + `march_http_io.{c,h}` + `march_http_internal.h`: kqueue/epoll event loop replacing thread-per-connection model. One event-loop thread per CPU core with SO_REUSEPORT (kernel-distributed accept). Non-blocking I/O: `conn_state_t` per-connection state with inline 64 KB read buffer, `march_recv_nonblocking` / `march_send_nonblocking` state machines, per-thread free-list pool. Edge-triggered events with accept batching. Compile flag: `-DMARCH_HTTP_USE_EVLOOP` (auto-enabled when `march_http_evloop.c` exists). Thread-per-connection fallback retained. Plan: `specs/event_loop_plan.md`. Phases 3–4 (per-thread arena, io_uring) remain optional future work.
- ✅ **Zero-copy response builder (section 4.5 Response Pipeline)** — `runtime/march_http_response.{h,c}`: pre-serialized status lines for all common codes (200/201/204/301/302/304/400/401/403/404/405/500/503) as const globals; `march_response_t` with 160-slot fixed iovec array; `march_response_init/set_status/add_header/add_date_header/set_body/send` API; `_Thread_local` 16 KB scratch buffer (no malloc on hot path); double-buffered Date header cache refreshed ≤once/second (atomic fast-path, mutex slow-path); `march_response_send_plaintext(fd)` sends "Hello, World!" in 4 iovecs (zero per-request allocation); `march_http_response_module_init()` called at server startup; `march_http.c` wired. 20 C tests (76 checks) in `test/test_http_response.c` covering init, status lines, unknown-code scratch, header iovec layout, Date cache freshness, thread-safety (8 threads), socket-pair round-trips for 200/404/plaintext.
- ✅ **SIMD HTTP parser** — `runtime/march_http_parse_simd.c` + `.h`: SSE4.2 PCMPESTRI fast path (16 bytes/cycle for delimiter scanning); scalar fallback via `#if defined(__SSE4_2__)`; `march_http_parse_request_simd()` single-request API; `march_http_parse_pipelined()` for pipelined requests; `march_http.c` updated to use SIMD fast path by default (disable with `-DMARCH_HTTP_DISABLE_SIMD`); 20 C tests in `test/test_http_simd.c`; dune rule compiles with `-msse4.2` (harmless on ARM64).
- ✅ **Per-process heaps + message passing (Phase 5)** — `runtime/march_heap.{h,c}`: per-process bump-pointer arena allocator with O(1) arena death (`march_heap_destroy`), arena growth by doubling (64 KiB → 4 MiB blocks), fragmentation tracking via `live_bytes`/`used_bytes`; `runtime/march_message.{h,c}`: cross-heap deep copy (`march_msg_copy` with forwarding table for DAG sharing), zero-copy linear move (`march_msg_move`, updates heap accounting only), `march_send_linear` (compiler-generated for linear messages), MPSC mailbox with selective receive and save-pointer (`march_mailbox_t`); `runtime/march_gc.{h,c}`: semi-space copying collector — walk from-space, copy RC>0 objects to to-space, fix up intra-heap pointers using forwarding map, free from-space blocks; `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`: special `EApp` case emits `march_send_linear` instead of `march_send` when message argument has `v_lin = Lin` (zero-copy linear optimization), LLVM preamble declares `march_send_linear`, `march_msg_copy`, `march_msg_move`, `march_process_alloc`. 7 C test groups: bump alloc+growth, msg copy (nested 3-level), linear move (zero-copy), non-atomic RC, semi-space GC, MPSC mailbox+selective receive, ≥1M msg/s throughput.
- ✅ **Green thread scheduler (Phases 1-4 + stack growth)** — Phase 1-3: ucontext_t stackful coroutines, mmap'd stacks, reduction preemption, per-process FIFO mailboxes, M:N multi-thread with Chase-Lev work-stealing deques. **Phase 4 (reduction counting)**: Thread-local `march_tls_reductions` counter + `march_yield_from_compiled()` in `runtime/march_scheduler.{h,c}`; `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml` emits inline load/decrement/store/icmp/br reduction check at every non-leaf function prologue (non-TCO) or TCO loop header; `is_leaf_callee` skips checks for builtin-only and `march_`-prefixed C-runtime calls; budget = 4000 reductions/quantum. 4 new `phase4_reduction_codegen` IR tests. **Phase 4 (stack growth)**: Lazy virtual-memory growth — each green thread reserves `MARCH_STACK_MAX` (1 MiB) + guard page as `PROT_NONE`, makes top `MARCH_STACK_INITIAL` (4 KiB) read/write; `SIGSEGV` handler (`SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK`) calls `mprotect` on the faulting page and returns for CPU retry; per-thread 64 KiB `sigaltstack` set up in `sched_loop()`; `p->stack_base` tracks current usable bottom. 2 new C tests: `test_stack_growth_deep`, `test_stack_growth_many` (50 concurrent deep-recursion processes). Plan: `specs/plans/green-thread-scheduler.md`.
- ✅ **Mutual TCO (P3)** — `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`: Tarjan's SCC on the tail-call graph (`tarjan_sccs`, `find_mutual_tco_groups`); combined dispatch function emitter (`emit_mutual_tco_group`) that generates one `@__mutco_f_g__` function per qualifying group with shared `mutual_loop`, `switch` dispatch, and back-edge `br` for mutual tail calls; thin wrapper functions preserve original names; `emit_module` wired to detect groups before normal `emit_fn` iteration; `EApp` case in `emit_expr` handles mutual back-edges. 5 new tests in `mutual_tco_codegen` group (even/odd, three-way, state machine, non-tail guard, self-TCO unaffected). `bench/mutual_recursion.march` added. 1061 total tests, 14 pre-existing failures unchanged.
- ✅ **Borrow inference and elision (P7)** — `lib/tir/borrow.ml`: pre-Perceus optimistic fixpoint analysis over the whole module. TCon/TString/TPtr params inferred as borrowed when never stored/returned/passed-to-owned. Inter-procedural: param passed only to borrowed positions stays borrowed. RC elision integrated into `lib/tir/perceus.ml`: (a) call sites skip EIncRC for borrowed args still live after; (b) callee's `~borrowed` set suppresses scrutinee EDecRC; (c) last-use borrowed arg → caller inserts EDecRC after call instead. 10 new `borrow_inference` tests.
- ✅ **Known-call optimization + struct update fusion** — `lib/tir/known_call.ml`: converts `ECallPtr(AVar clo, args)` to `EApp(apply_fn, clo :: args)` for statically-known closure allocations; runs between Defun and Perceus and in the Opt fixed-point loop. `inline.ml` threshold raised 15→50. `lib/tir/fusion.ml` extended with `run_struct`: merges chains of single-use `EUpdate` operations into one `EUpdate` (later fields win on conflicts). Wired into `opt.ml` coordinator (Known_call + Fusion.run_struct in passes list). 8 new tests: known_call×4, struct_fusion×4.
- ✅ **Optimization spec + constant propagation** — `specs/optimizations.md`: comprehensive catalog of all 12 implemented and 4 planned optimizations with effort/impact/dependencies. `lib/tir/cprop.ml`: new constant propagation pass that substitutes literal-bound variables at their use sites, enabling cascading folds; wired into `opt.ml` coordinator between Inline and Fold. 6 new tests in `cprop` group (1056 total). **Bugfix (2026-03-30)**: cprop was propagating literals into `EDecRC`/`EIncRC`/`EFree` arguments, turning `DecRC(m)` into `DecRC("POST")` — LLVM emit would allocate a fresh string to immediately free it while the original allocation leaked at RC=1. Fixed: RC and Free nodes are now left unchanged by cprop. 3 new regression tests (`no_propagate_into_decrc`, `no_propagate_into_incrc`, `no_propagate_into_free`). (1188 total)
- ✅ **LSP ~H unclosed-tag detection + close quickfix; AnnFnReturn arrow→colon fix** — (1) **~H HTML linting**: `scan_html_unclosed` (stack-based tag balancer — skips `${…}` interpolation, `<!-- … -->` comments, `<!doctype>`, void elements, self-closing tags; respects quoted attribute values) runs over each `~H` sigil's content (`extract_h_content` handles `"…"` and `"""…"""`, recovered textually from source since string spans only cover the opening quote). Emits `html/unclosed-tag` Warning diagnostics at each open tag + a "Close unclosed tag(s)" quickfix inserting closers innermost-first at the closing quote. New `html_issue` type + `html_issues` field; `collect_html_issues` wired into `analyse`; mismatched closes (`<div><p></div>`) flag the skipped `<p>`. (2) **Fix**: `AnnFnReturn` emitted `-> T` but March return syntax is `: T` (`fn f() -> Int do` is a parse error) — now emits `: T`; this (with the record-render bug) was the real cause of the earlier "annotation seems wrong" report. Combined with the record-naming change above, named-record returns now annotate as `: R` and parse. +8 LSP tests (236 LSP, 1442 main, all green).
- ✅ **LSP "Introduce parameter object" code action (data clump → record)** — surfaces the `forge refactor bundle` ("values that travel together → struct") refactor in the editor. `Analysis.bundleable_fn_at` (pure) detects when the cursor is on a single-clause function with ≥2 fully-annotated params; `Server.bundle_actions` then runs `March_refactor.Refactor.bundle_fn ~dry_run:true` (computes without writing) and converts the engine's per-file `fc_new` results into a **multi-file `WorkspaceEdit`** — so accepting the action rewrites the signature, body, and every call site project-wide. `march_refactor` added to `lsp/lib/dune`; action appended in `code_actions_for`. This corrects the earlier assumption that the cross-file rewrite "can't be done in the LSP" — LSP `WorkspaceEdit` supports multi-file edits. (The "values traveling together" phrasing the user saw is the separate `ClosureCapture` advisory hint at `analysis.ml:1229`, which remains advisory-only.) +3 LSP tests (229). Smoke-tested: `forge refactor bundle area --dry-run` reports the rewrite the action would apply.
- ✅ **LSP bugfixes: record-type annotation + missing-case arm syntax** — two code-action bugs that produced source the parser rejects. (1) **Add type annotation** rendered an inferred *record* return as `{ a : Int, b : Int }` and inserted `fn … -> { … } do`, which is a parse error — `Tc.TRecord` is purely structural (no nominal name), so `pp_ty` cannot print a valid annotation and March has no anonymous-record type syntax. Fix: `annotatable_ty_str` guards all three annotation kinds (`AnnLet`/`AnnFnReturn`/`AnnFnParam`) and skips the action when the rendered type contains `{`. (2) **Add missing case** generated `| Ctor -> ?` with a leading `|`; March match arms separate on `NL | PIPE`, so a `|` after the existing newline is a double separator → parse error. Fix: `arm_text_for_case` drops the leading `| ` (the `?` hole body is valid). Two existing tests that asserted the buggy `|` format were corrected. +3 LSP tests (226). Note: records printing structurally (e.g. hover shows `{ … }` not the type name) is an upstream `Tc.pp_ty`/type-rep matter, out of LSP scope.

Both are `QuickFix` actions tagged with their originating diagnostic and `isPreferred`, so they surface as a lightbulb directly on the warning. `backtick_name` helper added. +3 LSP tests (223). - ✅ **LSP DAP inline values (`textDocument/inlineValue`)** — the LSP side of the DAP debugger: while the debugger is stopped at a breakpoint, the editor requests inline values for the visible range and the server returns the in-scope locals so the editor renders their live values next to the code. Capability `inlineValueProvider = Some (\`Bool true)` in `config_modify_capabilities`. Handler in `on_unknown_request` parses `range` + `context.stoppedLocation` from the raw JSON params defensively (missing/garbled → empty list, never throws) and serialises `InlineValue.t list`. Computation in `analysis.ml`: `inline_values_at ~range_start_line ~range_end_line ~stopped_line` walks the scoped, shadow-correct symbol tables (`sym_defs`/`sym_name`/`sym_id_uses`) — each binder's definition span plus all its use spans are candidate occurrences — keeping those whose 0-indexed start line is within the requested range **and** at/above the stopped line; de-duplicated by variable name (the occurrence nearest the stopped line from above wins) so the editor draws one value per variable; underscore-prefixed and non-user-file names skipped. Emitted as `InlineValueVariableLookup` (`caseSensitiveLookup:true`, name + span range) for the debugger to resolve. UTF-16 wrapper `query_inline_values` remaps outbound ranges (line band is encoding-independent). +5 LSP tests (246 total): locals-in-range, names+positions (case-sensitive, stopped-line use chosen for `a`), below-stopped-line exclusion, de-dup of repeated `x`, no-crash on error buffer.

- ✅ **Doctest fix: chained `march> let x = ...` / `march> ...x...` sessions (2026-07-05)** — the extractor previously flushed and started a brand-new example on every `march> ` line, so a `let`-bound variable on one `march>` line was unreachable on the next: `lib/doctest/doctest.ml`'s `parse_expr` (via `bin/main.ml`) fed each line to the parser's `expr_eof` in isolation, which can't parse a bare `let` binding (block-`let` requires `do...end` or a following statement) — this raised `doctest parse error in: let parsed = ...`, then a spurious `unbound variable` failure on the next line's independently-evaluated example. Fixed in `lib/doctest/doctest.ml`'s `extract`: a `march> ` line arriving while the buffered example still starts with `let `/`let? `/`linear let ` (no expected-output line has closed it yet) now appends onto the SAME example instead of flushing, so the binding stays in scope. `bin/main.ml`'s `parse_expr` now wraps every doctest source in `do ... end` before calling `expr_eof` so multi-statement chained sessions parse as a block body (transparent no-op for the single-expression case). Fixes `Cli.get_string_or`/`get_bool`/`positional`/`get_int` (branch-only module, not on this branch) and the already-present `RRB.fold`/`RRB.chunk` doctests in `stdlib/rrb_vec.march`; verified via `test/stdlib/test_rrb_vec.march --verbose` (both now pass as a single doctest each) and a full stdlib-doctest sweep (`test/stdlib/test_*.march`, 91 files) showing zero `doctest parse error` occurrences. `Path.assert_no_traversal`'s two independent (non-`let`-headed) examples in `stdlib/path.march` are intentionally left un-merged and its pre-existing panic-vs-`ExpectNothing` failure is unrelated/unchanged.

- ✅ **Bare (non-`let`) statements before a final expression in an inline-lambda call argument (2026-07-21).** Found auditing `docs/cookbook/dom.md`/`concurrency.md` — two independent subagents each hit the same parser bug and worked around it (wrapping the bare statement as `let _ = ...`) rather than filing it. Root cause: `lambda_body` (`fn params -> ...`) only accepted `LET`/`linear let`/`let?` bindings before the final expression (unlike `block_body`, which accepts any bare expression statement via `block_expr`'s `e = expr` fallback) — so `fn x -> let a = 1  println("hi")  if a > 0 do 1 else 2 end` swallowed `println(...)` as the lambda's whole body and left `if ... end` as unparsed trailing tokens ("I got stuck here" at `if`). A naive fix (make `lambda_body` a general `nonempty_list` of `let`-or-bare-expr statements, mirroring `block_body`) is UNSAFE: unlike `block_body` (always bounded by a matching `END`), a bare arrow-form lambda body has no closing delimiter, so when the lambda appears anywhere the enclosing statement sequence is *also* still open (e.g. `let f = fn n -> n` as one statement of a bigger `do...end` block), the parser cannot tell where the lambda's body ends and the enclosing sequence resumes — it silently swallows subsequent statements into the lambda (confirmed regression: `let f : (Int)->Int = fn n -> n` followed by more code became mis-typed, caught by the pre-existing `test_let_annot_poly_instance_accepts`). Fixed by scoping the relaxation to call-argument position only, where the argument is always unambiguously bounded by `,`/`)`: new `call_arg` / `call_arg_lambda_body` / `call_arg_lambda_stmt` nonterminals used only in `expr_app`'s two call-argument-list productions (function calls and `Con(...)` constructor calls), with a companion `expr_no_bare_lambda` (a copy of `expr` minus its own top-level bare-lambda alternatives) as `call_arg`'s fallback so there's exactly one way to parse a bare lambda argument — avoiding ambiguity with `expr`'s own (unchanged, still LET*-then-final-expr) lambda-body rule used everywhere else. Zero new parser conflicts beyond the grammar's pre-existing 7 states / 59 shift-reduce (one of the same pre-existing kind — a match/if-scrutinee-vs-`WITH` ambiguity — now also reachable through constructor-call args). 2 new parse tests in `test/test_compiler.ml` (`test_parse_lambda_bare_stmt_before_if`, `test_parse_lambda_consecutive_bare_stmts`); full suite green (453 compiler / 231 eval / 396 codegen / snapshots unaffected).

- ✅ **JIT REPL type_map fix — 14 pre-existing test failures resolved** — Root cause: `run_expr`/`run_decl`/`precompile_stdlib` in `lib/jit/repl_jit.ml` received empty `type_map` from tests, causing `ty_of_span` to return `TVar "_"` for all variable references during TIR lowering. With `TVar "_"`, `build_subst` in mono returned `[]` for polymorphic calls (e.g., `List.reverse` inside `range_step`), preventing specialization. The unspecialized function was absent from `tm_fns` → not in `top_level` → defun treated it as a free variable → spurious closure capture → invalid LLVM IR (load from non-existent alloca) → clang error. Fix: `run_expr`, `run_decl`, and `precompile_stdlib` now compute `type_map` internally via `March_typecheck.Typecheck.check_module m` (ignoring the passed `~type_map`), ensuring all expression spans have proper types before TIR lowering. Fixed 10 `repl_jit_regression` + 3 `repl_compiler_parity` + 1 `jit_eval_simple_expr` boolean-display failure = 14 tests. Also reverted debug code from `compile_fragment` that copied failing .ll files to `/tmp/march_debug/`.
- ✅ **REPL JIT parity — 5 remaining test failures resolved** — Three root-cause bugs fixed: (1) `ptr 0` in LLVM string equality call (`march_string_eq`) — occurs when one operand is an i64 literal (e.g. bool false as `"0"`); fix: coerce both operands to `ptr` via `coerce ctx` before formatting the call instruction in `llvm_emit.ml`. (2) `%List.length.addr` undefined — polymorphic REPL globals (free vars with `TVar "_"` type) caused `build_subst` in `mono.ml` to return `[]` for `EApp` calls, silently skipping worklist addition; the function was never emitted, defun converted it to `ECallPtr`, and LLVM emitted an invalid alloca load; fix: in the `EApp` branch of `rewrite_calls`, when `subst = []` add to worklist (matching the existing `ECallPtr` behavior). (3) Bool `v` displayed as `"1"` — when evaluating a REPL global with `TVar "_"` return type, the `Int64.to_string` path was used instead of the bool formatter; fix: added `global_tir_tys : (string, Tir.ty) Hashtbl.t` to `repl_jit` context, populated on each global store, and used in the `TVar _` display branch to look up the actual TIR type via body inspection. Also added `string_length` to `is_builtin_fn`, `mangle_extern` (→ `march_string_byte_length`), and `builtin_ret_ty` in `llvm_emit.ml` — it was registered in typecheck and defun but missing from LLVM emit, causing `@string_length` undefined errors.

- ✅ **Uniform low-bit integer tagging (Phases 1 + 2)** — Fixed SIGSEGV when integers pass through polymorphic ADT fields (e.g. `List(Int)` with n ≥ 4096). Tag scheme: immediates stored as `(n << 1) | 1` (low bit 1); heap pointers remain even (always aligned). Changes: (1) `IS_HEAP_PTR` macro in `runtime/march_runtime.c` extended with `((uintptr_t)(p) & 1u) == 0` as first clause (short-circuits before page/sign guards on hot RC path). (2) `coerce ("i64", "ptr")` in `lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml` now emits `shl i64 %v, 1` + `or i64 %s, 1` + `inttoptr` to tag; `coerce ("ptr", "i64")` emits `ptrtoint` + `ashr i64 %i, 1` to untag (sign-preserving). (3) All three closure-wrapper emitters (top-level fn ref, AVar cross-module ref, REPL closure wrap) tag i64 return values before `inttoptr`. (4) `march_value_to_string` checks low bit first and calls `march_int_to_string((intptr_t)p >> 1)` for tagged immediates (Phase 2 fix, lands with Phase 1). Spec: `specs/plans/2026-04-16-uniform-integer-tagging.md`. Regression tests: `test_int_tag_coerce_ir` (shl+or+ashr appear in IR for `List(Int)` code), `test_int_tag_wrapper_ir` (wrapper emits tagged return). `test_march.exe` 1342 → 1358 (+2 new llvm_emit tests, +14 previously covered by tag-dependent paths now exercised).
- ✅ **Perceus RC crash fix: `TFn` ownership tracking + cross-branch EDecRC** — Fixed a `march_decrc` crash where a `.text-segment address` was being passed to the RC system during `Map.fold` with a `Bytes` accumulator. Two interlocking bugs in `lib/tir/perceus.ml`: (1) `needs_rc (TFn _)` was `false` — Perceus generated zero RC operations for function-typed parameters (e.g. `f` in `Map.node_fold`), causing no EIncRC when `f` is captured into the `go` closure and no EDecRC in the HEmpty arm where `f` is unused; the closure's code pointer slot was then misidentified as a Bytes payload pointer. Fix: changed to `needs_rc (TFn _) = true` with a guard comment explaining that post-defun any `AVar` with `TFn` type is a heap-allocated closure struct (never a raw code pointer — those are `ADefRef` and are never in AVar liveness; `llvm_ty (TFn _) = "ptr"` so RC ops emit correctly at the LLVM level). (2) ECase handler was discarding `live_before_br` for each branch — variables live in some branches but dead in others never got `EDecRC` in the dead branches (a second class of RC leak). Fix: collect `live_before_br` per branch, compute their union (`union_live_br`), and insert `EDecRC v` at the head of any branch where `v` ∈ `union_live_br` but `v` ∉ branch's `live_before_br` (excluding closure FVs, arm-bound vars, and vars live after the case). New `_var_ctx` global (`Tir.var StringMap.t ref`) maps names to their typed `Tir.var` records for emitting correctly-typed EDecRC ops. `_var_ctx` is seeded from function params in `insert_rc` and extended via ELet with save/restore semantics to avoid stale cross-branch interference. All tests pass.
- ✅ **JIT REPL `println(42)` segfault fix** — `println(42)` (and any prelude fn called with a non-string literal) caused SIGSEGV in JIT. Root cause: `lower_module`'s Pass 2 iterated only `m.mod_decls`, so top-level `DFn` declarations from `stdlib_context` (prelude fns like `println`, `str`, `map`) were never lowered into `fn_table`. With no `fn_table` entry, mono could not specialize `println$Int`; the LLVM emitter fell back to `mangle_extern` and emitted `call void @march_println(i64 42)` — a C runtime call with wrong arg type — causing SIGSEGV. Fix: added a pre-pass before Pass 2 in `lib/tir/lower.ml` that lowers `DFn` from `stdlib_context` (excluding `DMod`/`DImpl`, which are handled lazily). Also fixed four `EApp` sites in `lower.ml` that used `unknown_ty` instead of concrete `TFn` types for builtin operator references, and added `march_compare_*/march_hash_*` to `builtin_ret_ty` in `llvm_emit.ml`.
- ✅ **Generic `to_string` / polymorphic `println` via Show interface** — `stdlib/prelude.march`: `impl Show(List(a)) when Show(a)`, `impl Show(Option(a)) when Show(a)`, `impl Show(Result(a,e)) when Show(a), Show(e)` added; `println(x)` now delegates to `show(x)` making it polymorphic over all Show types; `str(x)` alias for `to_string`. `lib/eval/eval.ml`: `show_dispatch` helper routes `show` / `to_string` / `println` through `impl_tbl` keyed by `(interface_name, type_name)`; builtin constructors `Ok/Err/Some/None/Cons/Nil` pre-populated in `ctor_type_tbl` (in both `reset_scheduler_state` and `eval_module_env`) so `type_name_of_value` resolves `VCon("Err",…)` → `"Result"`; Show impl methods stored as plain `VClosure(env, params, body)` (not self-referential) so `show` inside an impl body calls the dispatcher, not itself. `lib/tir/lower.ml`: `Show$Unit.show` synthetic builtin added. 7 new tests in `test/test_march.ml` (`show List eval`, `show Option Some eval`, `show Option None eval`, `show Result Ok eval`, `show Result Err eval`, `show nested list eval`, `println polymorphic typecheck`). `test_march.exe` 1358 → 1365.
- ✅ **Record field auto-satisfy for single-method interfaces (Item 3)** — When discharging `CInterface(Iface, TRecord[...])` with no explicit `impl`, the typechecker now auto-satisfies if the interface has exactly one accessor method (`a -> T`) and the anonymous record has a matching field with the correct return type. `discharge_constraints` checks `env.interfaces`, inspects the single method's surface type, converts the return type with `surface_ty`, and uses `impl_matches_ty` for a pure structural comparison. Named types (`TCon`) never auto-satisfy — they require explicit `impl` declarations. 9 new tests in `record_auto_satisfy` group covering: matching field (ok), wrong type (error), missing field (error), multi-method interface (no auto), binary method (no auto), named type (no auto), named type + explicit impl (ok), when-constraint (ok), two record shapes (ok).
- ✅ **Capability Phase 1 — IO.Random/IO.Database in hierarchy + stdlib `needs` annotations (Item 1)** — Added `IO.Random` and `IO.Database` to `io_cap_hierarchy` in `lib/typecheck/typecheck.ml`. Added `needs` capability declarations to 8 stdlib modules: `stdlib/io.march` (`needs IO.Console`), `stdlib/file.march` (`needs IO.FileRead`, `needs IO.FileWrite`), `stdlib/dir.march` (`needs IO.FileRead`, `needs IO.FileWrite`), `stdlib/system.march` (`needs IO.Process`, `needs IO.Clock`), `stdlib/csv.march` (`needs IO.FileRead`), `stdlib/uuid.march` (`needs IO.Random`), `stdlib/random.march` (`needs IO.Random`), `stdlib/crypto.march` (`needs IO.Random`). These declarations make stdlib module capability requirements machine-checkable and self-documenting.
- ✅ **Capability Phase 2 — body-scan enforcement for builtin calls (Item 2)** — Added `calls_in_expr` AST walker (collects `(fn_name, span)` from EApp nodes), `builtin_cap_table` (~65-entry association list mapping runtime builtins to IO capabilities), and a body-scan pass inside `check_module_needs`. The pass walks each DFn clause body and DLet bind_expr, looks up each call in `builtin_cap_table`, deduplicates by cap name, and emits `Err.warning` (not error) for each implied capability not covered by a declared `needs`. Check 2 (unused `needs`) now also counts body-inferred calls as usage, preventing false "declared but not used" warnings. 14 new tests in `cap_body_enforce` group covering: happy path, missing console/fileread/filewrite/random/clock/process, warning-not-error, no-dup-warning, parent-cap umbrella, two missing caps, DLet body scanning, body satisfies declared needs, pure module silence.
- ✅ **Cap(IO.Spawn) — task-spawning capability** — `IO.Spawn` added as a new leaf under `IO` in `io_cap_hierarchy`. Five builtins mapped in `builtin_cap_table`: `task_spawn`, `task_spawn_link`, `task_spawn_steal`, `task_spawn_with_cancel`, `get_work_pool`. The body-scan pass (Phase 2) automatically enforces the new cap: modules that spawn tasks without `needs IO.Spawn` get a warning; `needs IO` (or any ancestor) satisfies it. 3 new tests in `cap_body_enforce` group: missing spawn warns, declared spawn suppresses warning, parent `IO` covers spawn.

Declaring this cap without IO.NetConnect proves a module uses only encrypted connections. 3 new tests.

Declaration-only (no builtins in body-scan table yet — telemetry module lives in the bastion repo): modules declare `needs IO.Telemetry` as a semantic annotation; transitive enforcement (Check 4) propagates it to importers. 1 new test. `docs/capabilities.md` updated with sections for all three new caps and a corrected hierarchy tree.

Only top-level `pfn`/`fn` self-recursion is eligible for TCO. Not blocking (stdlib call sites were rewritten to top-level `pfn` helpers instead), but worth a compiler warning if a future change reintroduces the pattern in a hot path.
- ✅ **B5 — `EUpdate` on a type-erased record wrote past the allocation (llvm_emit.ml + runtime)** — when `get_record_fields` returns `[]` (record shape unknown at compile time — e.g. `record_from_list`/`record_put` results flowing through generic code), the old codegen still allocated a header-only cell (`emit_heap_alloc ctx 0 0`) and wrote every update at `field_index_for`'s `(0, TVar "_")` fallback offset, corrupting memory past the cell. Fixed with a new variadic runtime function `march_record_update_dyn` (`runtime/march_extras.c`, modeled on `march_record_field_dyn`): ONE call per update expression, one allocation, base fields copied, named fields overwritten, and a **runtime panic on any update name missing from the base shape** — the typechecker cannot validate names against an erased base (its TVar branch builds a partial record constraint from the update's own names), so `{ record_from_list([("a",1)]) with z: 99 }` typechecks; routing through `march_record_put` would have silently fabricated field `z`, and a per-field put-chain would have leaked N−1 intermediate cells (invisible to Perceus). Surface trigger confirmed reachable. 10 new checks in `test/imports/record_native/rn_entry.march` (compile-and-run fixture, now 28 checks) + 3 tests in `test/test_codegen.ml` (`erased_record_update_codegen`: IR asserts exactly one `march_record_update_dyn` call and zero chained `march_record_put` calls; compiled missing-field update panics with "no field" and exit 1; compiled 3-field update values match interpreter). Known divergence (documented): the interpreter's `ERecordUpdate` still silently appends missing update fields (eval.ml) — compiled fail-loud is the safer contract; aligning eval is a follow-up.

## Wave 1 — pipeline deep review P0 fixes (2026-07-01/02, `specs/analysis/2026-07-01-pipeline-deep-review.md`)

- ✅ **B3 — guard exhaustion returned literal `0` instead of panicking (lower.ml)** — commit `11925401`. Exhausted match guards now hoist the existing `nonexhaustive_panic` into both `compile_matrix_impl` fallbacks instead of fabricating a pointer-unsafe `LitInt 0`.
- ✅ **B4 — `PatRecord` and float-literal match arms silently dropped from match compilation (lower.ml, llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `e8a43b7b`. `pat_tag_and_subs` now handles both shapes; the swallowing `None -> ()` in the grouping loop fails loudly on any future unhandled kind instead of discarding the arm.
- ✅ **B9 — off-by-one in the `march_` runtime-extern prefix guard (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `cd0770d9`. `String.sub n 0 7` (7 chars) vs the 6-char literal `"march_"` made the runtime-extern-as-first-class-value arm dead; fixed to match the three sibling `0 6` checks.
- ✅ **B10 — RC ops (`EIncRC`/`EDecRC`/`EFree`) skipped by name against top_fns/builtins with no shadow guard (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `b98115da`. A local binding named `link`/`send`/etc. now gets correct RC ops; the five RC arms gained the `var_slot` shadow check `emit_atom` already applied twice.
- ✅ **B5 — `EUpdate` on a type-erased record wrote past the allocation (llvm_emit.ml + runtime)** — commit `0d1a829e`, see full entry above (Task 5).
- ✅ **B15 — raw newline inside a string literal desynced all subsequent diagnostic line numbers (lexer.mll)** — commit `f169070c`. `read_string`/`read_string_interp` now call `Lexing.new_line` on an embedded raw `\n`, matching the triple-quoted-string path.
- ✅ **FLOAT-filter — float-literal match arms failed to parse without a leading `|` (token_filter.ml)** — commit `6e376e4d`. Added `Parser.FLOAT` (and audited sibling literal tokens) to `is_pattern_start`.
- ✅ **B6 — pipe into a parenthesized `match` silently discarded the scrutinee (desugar.ml)** — commit `b579f848`. `x |> (match scrut do ... end)` now errors with a positioned diagnostic instead of matching on `x` and dropping `scrut`.
- ✅ **B14 — interleaved same-name fn clause groups silently shadowed the earlier group (parser.mly)** — commit `4cdc65de`. `group_fn_clauses` now rejects a fn name recurring in a non-adjacent group at the same level instead of leaving the first group as dead code.
- ✅ **B16 — `~H` sigil CSRF auto-injection referenced a free variable `conn` (desugar.ml)** — commit `f39a5c49`. Removed the unconditional CSRF-tag injection on `<form method=post/put/patch/delete>`, which broke every non-Bastion `~H` user (worse with bastion leaving the stdlib) — see `project_bastion_removal` context.
- ✅ **B7 — mutual-TCO back-edge dropped the Perceus dec-chain (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `05d9e46b`. Added mutual-group twins of the self-TCO `ELet`/`ESeq` interception arms so the dec-chain emits before the back-edge instead of landing in a dead block (was an RC leak every loop iteration).
- ✅ **B8 — mutual-TCO loops had no reduction check, could starve the scheduler (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `bc5b0e22`. `emit_reduction_check` now runs after the `mutual_loop` label, mirroring the self-TCO path.
- ✅ **B12 — `cur_type_defs` global left stale for every REPL/fragment emitter (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `53c70a0e`, see full entry above (Task 8). Type defs are now a `ctx` field; the global is deleted.
- ✅ **B11 — REPL closure wrapper missed the uniform ptr-ABI fix (llvm_emit.ml)** — commit `b32d8569`, see full entry above (Task 9). The inline wrapper is gone; `emit_repl_fn_with_closure_slot` calls the canonical `clo_wrap_define`.

## Wave 2 — Task 1: interface-impl monomorphization fix (2026-07-02, `.superpowers/sdd/sortby-diagnosis.md`)

- ✅ **Historic "`List.sort_by` 100+ element compiled crash" formally closed — root cause was never sort_by.** Diagnosis (`.superpowers/sdd/sortby-diagnosis.md`, 95% confidence, evidence chain): compiled `println`/`show` of ANY generic container (`List`, `Option`, `Result`) whose `Show` goes through prelude's constrained impls (`impl Show(List(a)) when Show(a)`) was type-confused and had **never worked in compiled mode**, since the feature's introduction (`df3b1e44`, 2026-04-20). `lib/tir/mono.ml`'s three interface-impl-resolution enqueue sites (EApp direct-dispatch, EApp name-collision branch, ECallPtr twin) rewrote a call like `show(xs : List(Int))` to the mangled impl `Show$List.show`, but enqueued that impl with an **empty substitution** — so the impl body stayed generic, and its nested element-level `show(x : a)` call survived to `llvm_emit.ml` as an unresolved bare reference. `llvm_emit.ml`'s `unqualified_fns` dot-suffix fallback (built for legitimate cross-module unqualified refs like `base64_encode` → `Crypto.base64_encode`) then resolved the bare `show` to whatever `*.show`-suffixed impl was registered first — typically `Show$List.show` itself, applying the LIST impl to a raw element. Symptom varied by element type and impl-registration order (Int → SIGSEGV on a match-tag load against an erased-int treated as a heap pointer; String → non-exhaustive-match panic; Option → SIGSEGV/SIGBUS) — explaining the years of shifting "sort_by crash" symptom reports. sort_by itself is and was bit-for-bit correct compiled (1000-int checksum parity, 500-tuple stability parity, heap-capturing-comparator parity, all confirmed identical interpreter vs. compiled in the diagnosis). Fix (`lib/tir/mono.ml`): all three enqueue sites now compute a substitution from the resolved call's concrete argument types (`build_subst`, reusing the exact machinery the ordinary generic-fn EApp branch already used) and enqueue the impl specialized under it — mangling a further-specialized name (e.g. `Show$List.show` + `List(Int)` → `Show$List.show$List_Int`) when the substitution is non-empty, so the nested `show(x)` resolves through mono's normal rewrite-calls machinery to the concrete element impl. Recursion (`List(List(Int))` etc.) terminates via the existing worklist `done_set` dedup — verified explicitly: a 2-level and 3-level nested-list `println` both compile in ~2s with no runaway specialization loop. Defense-in-depth (`lib/tir/llvm_emit.ml`): `unqualified_fns` population now EXCLUDES interface-impl-mangled names (detected as "contains `$` before the last `.`", e.g. `Show$List.show$List_Int` — ordinary qualified names like `Crypto.base64_encode` are unaffected since they never contain `$`), so a bare interface-method name recurring unresolved can never again be silently rebound to an arbitrary same-named impl; the ECallPtr catch-all fallback additionally `failwith`s by name (listing candidate impls) if it ever sees an unresolved bare name matching a registered impl's suffix, converting any future regression into a loud compile-time failure instead of a silent miscompile. Four RED/GREEN regression tests added in `test/test_codegen.ml` (`iface_impl_mono_codegen`): `println([1,2,3,4,5])` (pre-fix: SIGSEGV 139), `println(["a","b"])` (pre-fix: non-exhaustive-match panic, exit 1), `println([Some(42), None])` (pre-fix: SIGSEGV 139), `println([[1,2],[3]])` (pre-fix: SIGSEGV 139, also the mono-termination/recursion-guard check) — all assert compiled stdout == interpreter stdout AND exit 0. The original 150-element `List.sort_by` + `println(List.take(sorted, 10))` repro (`/tmp/sortby-kapitsa-baseline.march`) now produces byte-identical output in interpreter and compiled mode, exit 0 both — closing the saga end-to-end. **384 compiler / 227 eval / 341 codegen (+4 new, 337 pre-existing) / 791 stdlib / 53 stdlib_march all pass, all exit 0.** RC benchmarks (compiled, `--opt 2`): `tree_transform` = `104857600`, `list_ops` = `333333666666`, `binary_trees` standard Benchmarks-Game output, `bench/mutual_recursion.march` (even/odd, 3-state machine, collatz) all correct — no regressions.

## Wave 2 — Task 3: W2.1 — LLVM IR validity gate (2026-07-02, `specs/plans/2026-07-02-wave2-testing-infra.md`)

- ✅ **Emitted LLVM IR is now verified for the whole native fixture corpus — new `test/test_ir_verify.ml`, wired into `run_codegen.exe`.** Previously nothing ever ran an LLVM verifier over emitted IR; an ill-typed emission (the `coerce` catch-all class, or any other emitter bug producing textually-plausible-but-type-incorrect LLVM assembly) only ever surfaced as an opaque `clang` parse/verify failure at `--compile` time, with no locatable `.ll:line:col` pointer at TEST time. **Tooling probe:** Xcode's Command Line Tools clang does NOT ship `opt`/`llvm-as` (`xcrun -f opt` fails) — the verifier had to come from Homebrew LLVM (`brew --prefix llvm`, not linked onto PATH to avoid shadowing Xcode's clang). `find_llvm_verifier_tool` (`test/test_helpers.ml`) probes, in order: `opt` on PATH, `opt` at the brew keg, `llvm-as` on PATH, `llvm-as` at the brew keg; `` `None `` is a legitimate, counted skip (`record_jit_skip`, same ledger as the W2.0 clang-absence skips) — never a silent pass. This machine has `opt` at `/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/opt` (Homebrew LLVM 22.1.1); the gate ran for real, not skipped. **RED:** a hand-crafted `.ll` with an `i64`/`double` type mismatch (`%r = add i64 %x, %f` where `%f` is `fadd double`) is asserted REJECTED by `verify_llvm_ir_file` (`opt -passes=verify -disable-output`, rc≠0 with a locatable `file.ll:line:col` error) — proven to actually matter by temporarily sabotaging the helper to always return `` `Ok `` and confirming the RED test then fails (restored clean afterward); a converse sanity test confirms well-typed hand-crafted IR is accepted, so the gate isn't just "reject everything." **Gate:** one aggregated Alcotest case (`test_native_corpus_ir_is_verifier_clean`) emits IR via `--emit-llvm` (bypasses the CAS artifact cache entirely, unlike plain `--compile`, so the gate always inspects freshly emitted text) for every `test/native/*.march` fixture and runs the verifier, collecting every failure before asserting (a full run names every bad fixture in one shot rather than stopping at the first). **Finding, disposition = scope exclusion, not a loud skip:** of the 43 `test/native/*.march` fixtures, the 6 `js_*` ones (`js_dom_available`, `js_extern_import`, `js_ffi_async`, `js_ffi_blocking_raises`, `js_ffi_cbacked`, `js_ffi_raises`) are compiled ONLY with `--target js` anywhere in `test/dune` (producing a `.mjs`; the JS backend never touches `Llvm_emit` at all — confirmed in `bin/main.ml`'s JS-target branch, which returns before the LLVM/clang path). Compiling them natively instead (no `--target js`, what a naive "gate everything in test/native/" would do) DOES produce a `.ll` that fails verification — the emitted `declare` for a JS-side extern keeps its raw JS-style name verbatim (e.g. `@node:path_dirname`, `@./foo.mjs_bar`), and `:`/`.`/`/` are invalid characters in an LLVM identifier — but this is a probe artifact, not a real bug: no existing test ever exercises these 6 fixtures as native IR, only as `.mjs`. `list_native_fixtures` (`test/test_ir_verify.ml`) therefore excludes any `js_`-prefixed fixture, mirroring actual `test/dune` usage rather than inventing a loud skip for a scenario the corpus never puts them in. **GREEN on the real corpus:** all 37 gated (non-`js_`) fixtures emit verifier-clean LLVM IR as of 2026-07-02 — zero emitter bugs found, no `specs/todos.md` entries needed for this task. **Design: new file, not a growth of `test_codegen.ml`** (already ~6400 lines) — a distinct corpus-scanning concern (walk a directory, shell out to an external tool, aggregate a failure list) vs. `test_codegen.ml`'s single-source-snippet IR assertions; wired into the EXISTING `run_codegen.exe` runner per the task brief (`Test_codegen.codegen_suites @ Test_ir_verify.suites`), not a 6th dune test executable, so the mandated five-runner invocation recipe is unchanged. **Review hardening (same commit):** (1) the `js_` exclusion is loud, not silent — an `at_exit` note names every excluded fixture in the terminal (same mechanism as the W2.0 skip ledger), plus a misclassification invariant: the gate FAILS if `test/dune` ever contains a `native_<fixture>` compile rule for an excluded `js_` fixture (`assert_excluded_are_js_target_only`). (2) A real temp-dir leak found and fixed: even `--emit-llvm` drops a `.march/cas/vc/` verdict-cache tree in its CWD, so the original flat remove+`rmdir` cleanup silently ENOTEMPTY'd on every fixture (~240 leaked dirs observed); replaced with `rm_rf_temp_dir` (`test/test_helpers.ml`) — recursive, lstat-based (symlinks removed as links, never followed), and SELF-CONFINING: refuses `""`/`"/"` outright and refuses (`Alcotest.failf`, deleting nothing) any existing path that is not a strict realpath-resolved descendant of the realpath-resolved system temp root (realpath on both sides neutralizes the macOS `/var`→`/private/var` `$TMPDIR` spelling mismatch); the unconfined walker is local to the function so it cannot be called unguarded. Confinement unit test (refuses `""`, `"/"`, and an existing outside-temp-root dir, with a sentinel file asserted to survive) proven load-bearing by sabotage (guard arm removed → test fails exit 1; restored byte-identical). **384 compiler / 227 eval / 346 codegen (+4 new: RED-rejects, valid-IR sanity, delete-confinement, corpus gate) / 790 stdlib (789 pass + 1 pre-existing documented skip from W2.0) / 53 stdlib_march all pass, all exit 0.**

- ✅ **Added `Tir.fn_kind` (`FnNormal | FnLambda | FnJoinPoint | FnApply | FnFused`) as a mandatory field on `Tir.fn_def`, set honestly at all 21 synthesis sites in `lib/tir/*.ml`** (lower.ml ×15 covering parsed user/stdlib fns, `ELam`/`ELetFn` lambda-creation sites, the `compile_matrix` hoisted-fallback join point, actor handler/dispatch/spawn glue, module-level-`let`-as-zero-arg-fn, builtin Eq/Ord/Show/Hash iface shims, and `__march_test_N__`/`__march_setup__`/`__march_setup_all__`; defun.ml ×1 for the closure apply wrapper; fusion.ml ×3 for the map/filter/fold loop-fusion helpers). ADAPTED the plan's suggested kind list: dropped `FnTryThunk` (no synthesis site exists — `__try_call`/`__try_call_val` are typecheck/eval builtins, never lowered to a TIR `fn_def`; the thunk passed to them is an ordinary `FnLambda`), added `FnFused` (fusion.ml's generated loop helpers — a real synthesis site the plan's list missed; no consumer currently sniffs these names, so the kind exists purely for honest labeling, not yet load-bearing).
  - **Consumers converted with transitional flag-vs-sniff asserts (mandatory this chunk, removed in Chunk 2):** all three `Tir_names.is_apply_fn` call sites — `perceus.ml`'s post-call EDecRC/closure-consumes-`$clo` gating (via a new `_fn_kinds` module-level lookup table, mirroring the existing `_borrow_map`/`_type_defs` convention), `llvm_emit.ml`'s `emit_fn` (direct — the `fn_def` is already in scope), and `llvm_emit.ml`'s general `EApp` case (via a new `ctx.top_fn_kind` Hashtbl populated once from the top-level module's `tm_fns` at `emit_module`'s entry; deliberately NOT populated at the ~10 scattered REPL/JIT incremental pseudo-module registration sites — those callees have no table entry and the assert is skipped there, not treated as a mismatch). Zero assert firings across the full six-runner suite (1851 tests) — every synthesis site agreed with the pre-existing name-sniffing logic it replaces.
  - **Two named consumers left unconverted, by design, documented in place:** `borrow.ml`'s `is_clo_struct` checks a `Tir.ty` (closure-struct TCon name from an EAlloc), not a `fn_def` — there is no `fn_kind` to assert against without re-deriving the lambda's `uid` back out of the type name, which would be a new fragile re-derivation, not a fix. `borrow.ml`'s `is_try_call` checks a call-target name against the hardcoded `__try_call`/`__try_call_val` builtin names — since those are never TIR `fn_def`s, a `fn_kind` lookup by that name would always miss; this is builtin call-target dispatch, not synthesis-role classification (same shape as the `"task_spawn_steal"` check elsewhere).

  - **Critical finding, flagged not fixed:** `lib/cas/serialize.ml`'s `write_fn_def`/`write_letrec_fn`/`write_fn_sig` (feeds `impl_hash`/`sig_hash` — cross-binary RPC admission + the CAS artifact cache key) likewise write fields by name and so did NOT start hashing `fn_kind` — verified explicitly and documented with an in-code warning that `fn_kind` must NEVER be added there (it would silently invalidate every cached artifact and change RPC admission the day it was hashed — `fn_kind` is a same-binary compiler-internal role tag, not part of a function's externally observable identity).
  - **Test-file mechanical fallout:** adding a mandatory record field forced every `Tir.fn_def` literal across the repo to set it (`bench/bench_opt.ml`, `test/test_cas.ml`, `test/test_codegen.ml`, `test/test_compiler.ml`, `test/test_eval.ml`, `test/test_helpers.ml`, `test/test_hot_reload.ml`) or the build would not compile — OCaml has no default field values. This unavoidably included **`test/test_properties.ml`** (on the plan's "do not touch" list); applied the plan's own `bin/`-exception precedent ("except if a moved module forces a reference update — flag it") since there is no way to make one field mandatory-everywhere-except-one-file in OCaml.
  - **Proof of behavior preservation:** zero TIR snapshot churn (29/29 `run_snapshots` green). Same-machine A/B against a detached-HEAD `git worktree` built from `0cd6b627`: all four `specs/benchmarks.md` benchmarks produce identical outputs with timings within noise (tree_transform ~8.0s both; list_ops/binary_trees/mutual_recursion sub-second, both sides matching to within measurement noise). **384 compiler / 230 eval / 364 codegen / 791 stdlib / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots — all six runners exit 0 (1851 tests total).**

## Wave 3 — Task 4: Perceus env-record threading — retire module-level mutable state (2026-07-03, `specs/plans/2026-07-03-wave3-chunk1-refactors.md`)

- ✅ **`lib/tir/perceus.ml`'s nine module-level mutable refs replaced by one immutable `env` record threaded as an explicit parameter through `insert_rc_expr` and every helper it calls** (`incrc_for`/`decrc_for`/`wrap_incrcs`/`find_inc_vars`/`scrutinee_shares_payload_storage`). In-place refactor only — no file split (that's Task 5). Ref inventory and classification (full table in `.superpowers/sdd/w3-task-4-report.md`):
  - **Module-scoped → env fields, set once per `perceus` run, read-only for the whole traversal:** `_borrow_map`, `_type_defs`, `_fn_kinds`, `_extern_names`.
  - **Function-scoped → env fields, set once per `insert_rc` call, constant across that function's traversal (including nested `ELetRec` closures, which reuse the ambient env exactly as the old refs were never reset for them):** `_current_fn_name`, `_closure_fvs`, `_actor_sent`.
  - **Subtree-scoped → env fields, updated via `{ env with field = ... }` on descent into `ELet` bindings / `ECase` branches** (the functional equivalent of the old hand-rolled `let prev = !r in r := x; ...; r := prev` dance — the "restore" is now implicit because the caller's own `env` binding is never mutated): `_borrowed_field_vars`, `_var_ctx`.
  - **Left as a ref, by design (accumulator, not env-shaped):** `_rc_fresh_ctr` — mutated without restore across the whole module traversal (monotonic fresh-name counter, reset to 0 once per `perceus` call), not scoped to any subtree.
  - **`insert_rc`'s nested `result_is_borrowed_field` lookahead** (inside the `ELet` case) previously did its own manual save/restore of `_borrowed_field_vars` around a purely-lexical recursion with no early-return/exception escape; converted to a plain immutable parameter threaded through its own recursion — behaviorally identical, and now impossible to get wrong via a missed restore.
  - **Restore-gap audit: none found.** Every save/restore site in the pre-refactor file was on a plain functional-recursion control path (verified: zero `try`/`with`/`raise` anywhere in `perceus.ml`), so no non-lexical escape could have made the old mutable-ref version diverge from the new immutable-env version. No `specs/todos.md` entries filed for suspicious sites — there were none to find.
  - **Proof of behavior preservation (strongest gate of the chunk):** (1) all six runners exit 0 (`run_compiler` 384, `run_eval` 230, `run_codegen` 364, `run_stdlib` 791, `test_stdlib_march` 53, `run_snapshots` 29 — zero `.expected` diffs, the theorem prover for this task). (2) `MARCH_DEBUG_PERCEUS=1` before/after on three snapshot-corpus programs (`scrutinee_borrowed_conservatism.march`, `borrowed_field_escape.march`, `closure_hof.march`) — inc/dec/free/reuse counts byte-identical in all three. (3) Baseline IR diff against a clean build of base commit `c28ff465` in a temporary worktree: all four `specs/benchmarks.md` benchmarks (`--emit-llvm --opt 2`) produced **byte-identical** `.ll` files (0 diff lines each) — the strongest form of this chunk's evidence bar. ## Wave 3 — Task 5: Perceus file split — pure moves (2026-07-03, `specs/plans/2026-07-03-wave3-chunk1-refactors.md`)

- ✅ **`lib/tir/perceus.ml` (1937 lines post-Task-4) split into four focused modules via verbatim cut-paste moves**, leaving `perceus.ml` (1594 lines) as the pass orchestrator (`env` type, `insert_rc_expr` core, the public `perceus` entry point — external callers in `bin/main.ml`/`lib/jit/` unchanged): `lib/tir/perceus_liveness.ml` (162 lines: `live_before`/`name_free_in`/`vars_of_atom(s)`, self-contained, matches the plan exactly), `lib/tir/perceus_elide.ml` (87 lines: `elide_expr`/`elide_cancel_pairs`), `lib/tir/perceus_fbip.ml` (135 lines: `same_arity`/`args_alias_reuse`/`try_fbip_sink`/`fbip_expr`/`insert_fbip`), `lib/tir/perceus_scrut.ml` (151 lines: `scrut_escape_field_atoms`/`rewrite_scrut_tail`/`preprocess_scrut_escape`/`preprocess_fn`, Phase-0.5). `perceus.ml` re-exports every moved name as a one-line alias (`let elide_cancel_pairs = Perceus_elide.elide_cancel_pairs`, etc.) so existing `Perceus.foo` call sites and greps are unaffected.
  - **Two dune dependency-cycle deviations from the plan's literal module assignment, both pure direction fixes forced by a real build error (not scope creep):** (1) `fbip_arity_marker`/`is_fbip_encoded` moved into `perceus_fbip.ml` alongside their consumer, rather than staying in `perceus.ml` as the plan's wording implied — the producer (`insert_rc_expr`'s `add_scrutinee_free_for`) is in the orchestrator and the consumer (`same_arity`) is in the FBIP module; putting the marker in `perceus.ml` would have made `Perceus_fbip` depend back on `Perceus`, cycling against the orchestrator's own `Perceus -> Perceus_fbip` call. `perceus.ml` re-exports `fbip_arity_marker` so the producer keeps its unqualified reference. (2) `Perceus_scrut.preprocess_scrut_escape` calls `Rc_types.needs_rc` directly instead of through `Perceus.needs_rc`'s re-export, for the identical reason (`Perceus.needs_rc` is itself just `let needs_rc = Rc_types.needs_rc`, so routing through it would create `Perceus_scrut -> Perceus -> Perceus_scrut`). Zero behavior difference in both cases — same function, different module path. Full dependency map (built before moving anything, confirming no candidate function needed to move to a different module than planned beyond these two) in `.superpowers/sdd/w3-task-5-report.md`.

Nothing on the `env` type itself documents that (1) subtree-scoped fields must start neutral at function entry, or (2) `var_ctx`'s "neutral" is defined relative to `module_env.var_ctx` rather than a hardcoded empty — a future caller that threads a non-empty `module_env.var_ctx` (e.g. to seed some future cross-function fact) would silently leak that fact into every function's params unless this is spelled out. One-line doc-comment candidate on the `env` type definition (or on `insert_rc`'s `fn_env` construction): state the invariant explicitly and note the asymmetry between the two subtree-scoped fields' reset mechanics.

## Wave 3 Chunk 2 — Task 1: FnFused coverage test + known_call/mono name-contract stragglers (2026-07-03, `specs/plans/2026-07-03-wave3-chunk2-emit-lower.md`)

- ✅ **FnFused reachability verdict: COVERED, not unreachable.** fusion.ml's stream-fusion pass (`gen_map_fold`/`gen_filter_fold`/`gen_map_filter_fold`) IS already exercised by test-corpus programs — `test/test_eval.ml`'s pre-existing `test_fusion_map_fold`/`test_fusion_filter_fold`/`test_fusion_map_filter_fold` (via `Test_helpers.fusion_module` + `has_fused_fn`) prove all three synthesis sites fire from ordinary March source. The actual gap (per Wave 3 Task 6's filed item (c)) was narrower than "is fusion reachable": it was "does anything cross-check the `FnFused` FLAG against the name-sniffing REALITY" — nothing did. New `fnfused_coverage` suite in `test/test_codegen.ml` (4 tests: map+fold, filter+fold, map+filter+fold, and a non-fusible negative control) reuses the same reachable pipeline and asserts the bidirectional cross-check the gate required: every fn_def named like fusion.ml's `"$fused_<mf|ff|mff>_N"` gensym convention must be tagged `Tir.FnFused`, AND every `Tir.FnFused`-tagged fn_def must be named per that convention — plus an explicit "at least one FnFused fn_def exists post-fusion" existence check and a negative control proving the existence check isn't vacuously true for every module. Gates Task 2's retirement of the transitional `fn_kind` asserts (perceus.ml/llvm_emit.ml) as intended.
- ✅ **`known_call.ml`'s `is_clo_name` converted to `Tir_names.is_clo_struct`** — the 4-char `"$Clo"` inline check is one character short of `Tir_names`'s 5-char `"$Clo_"` (the underscore is part of the producer's format string). Proved behavior-narrowing is safe rather than assumed: grepped the whole tree for every `"$Clo`-shaped string literal — the ONLY producer of any `TCon`/`TDClosure` name in this shape is `Tir_names.clo_struct_name` (`"$Clo_" ^ fn_name ^ "$" ^ lam_uid`), called from exactly defun.ml's two lambda-lifting call sites (already routed through `Tir_names` per Wave 3 Task 1's report). `fn_name`/`lam_uid` can never make the underscore disappear, so the divergent shape ("$Clo" + non-underscore) is unreachable in this compiler — the 4-vs-5-char widening is unobservable. New `known_call` suite test (`is_clo_name matches Tir_names.is_clo_struct (W3C2.1)`) pins behavioral equality on every producible name plus the documented unreachable divergence case (`"$Clox"`).
- ✅ **New `Tir_names.specialize_mangle : string -> string -> string`** centralizes the "$"-glue half of mono.ml's specialization-suffix mangle (`mangle_name`'s `base ^ "$" ^ mangled_ty_suffix`, e.g. `"map$Int"`, and the W2 double-mangle case `"Show$List.show" + [List(Int)] -> "Show$List.show$List_Int"`). `mangle_ty` (the type→string algorithm) deliberately stays in mono.ml — it's a monomorphization-specific computation, not a cross-pass name CONTRACT — so `specialize_mangle` only owns the shared separator convention, mirroring the existing `iface_mangle`/`default_arg_mangle` split. Doc comment proves why this can never trip `is_iface_mangled` (the `$`-before-last-`.` predicate from Wave 2 Task 1): `specialize_mangle` never introduces a `.` or moves a `$` to before an existing `.`, so a produced name is-iface-mangled iff its `base` already was — citing the existing `is_iface_mangled` doc's own `"List.map$Int"`-must-be-FALSE example as the concrete instance of this general rule. Fixed the stale `enqueue_specialized_impl` comment ("no shared Tir_names-style helper exists yet — that's Wave 3") to point at the new helper. New `tir_names` suite test (`specialize_mangle`) pins byte-equality against the OLD inline expression shape (`base ^ "$" ^ mangled_ty`) plus the W2 double-mangle round-trip and the `is_iface_mangled` non-interference proof.
- ✅ **Standard gates, all green:** six runners exit 0 at 384 compiler / 230 eval / 370 codegen (368 base +2: `specialize_mangle`, `is_clo_name` equivalence — plus the 4 new `fnfused_coverage` tests already counted in the 368) / 791 stdlib / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots — zero `.expected` diffs. ## Wave 3 Chunk 2 — Task 4: `llvm_builtins.ml` — declarative builtin table (2026-07-03, `specs/plans/2026-07-03-wave3-chunk2-emit-lower.md`, HAZARD H2)

- ✅ **New `lib/tir/llvm_builtins.ml`** replaces llvm_emit.ml's four historically-unsynchronized builtin structures (`is_builtin_fn`'s 272-name `List.mem` list, `builtin_ret_ty`, `mangle_extern`, and the ~400-line hand-written preamble `declare` blob — source of ≥5 "missing builtin" fix commits per `specs/analysis/2026-07-01-pipeline-deep-review.md` §5) with one ordered table (`builtin` record: `march_name`; `c_name : string option`; `ret_ty : Tir.ty option`; `in_is_builtin : bool`; `declare_sig : string option`), 318 rows, in the preamble's real declaration order (286 rows with a preamble presence, then 32 declare-less rows — arithmetic/comparison operators and `int_and`/etc bitwise ops emitted as native LLVM instructions, `task_spawn`/`task_await`/etc and `pmap_threshold`/`get_work_pool`/`remote_ref_hashes` synthesized/constant-folded by dedicated `EApp` match arms — appended in their original `is_builtin_fn`-list order since they have no preamble position). All three consumers (`is_builtin_fn`, `builtin_ret_ty`, `mangle_extern`) are hashtables built once from the table at module load, answer-identical to the deleted functions (verified against a throwaway probe executable calling both old and new implementations over the full 318-name universe plus negative-control names: 0 mismatches). `Llvm_emit.mangle_extern` stays re-exported (lib/jit/repl_jit.ml references it as `March_tir.Llvm_emit.mangle_extern`); `Llvm_emit.emit_preamble` becomes a thin wrapper translating `target_config` to the `is_wasm`/`triple` values `Llvm_builtins.emit_preamble` needs (kept decoupled from `target_config` to avoid a module cycle, since `bin/main.ml` depends on `Llvm_emit.target_config`/`Native`/etc extensively and moving those was out of this task's scope).
- ✅ **HAZARD H2 (byte-identical preamble): satisfied by construction, not by a formatting function.** The original blob's per-line whitespace is hand-tuned and inconsistent (e.g. `declare i64  @foo` vs `declare i64    @bar` — return-type column padding varies within the same block to visually align with neighboring `double`-typed lines), so a generic `declare_sig`-from-fields formatter would risk silent reformatting drift. Instead each row's `declare_sig` holds the EXACT historical `declare ...` line text (copied verbatim); `Llvm_builtins.emit_preamble` replays a fixed per-target list of `preamble_item`s (`PComment`/`PDeclare`/`POther`/`PBlank` markers mirroring the original blob's line-by-line structure 1:1, including its native/WASM/REPL conditional branches) and resolves each `PDeclare` marker's text via a C-symbol lookup across the table + a 57-entry `runtime_only_declares` table (RC ops, Hot-Code-Reload/dispatch machinery, the test harness, LLVM intrinsics, task/scheduler internals — preamble declares with no March-callable name at all, hence no `builtin` row). Verified byte-identical for all three target/repl combinations (native non-REPL, native REPL, WASM) against the actual pre-refactor `emit_preamble` output via a throwaway probe executable, AND pinned as a permanent regression test: `test/test_codegen.ml`'s new `llvm_builtins_preamble_golden` suite (4 tests) embeds the four deleted `Buffer.add_string buf {| ... |}` literals verbatim as goldens and diffs `Llvm_builtins.emit_preamble`'s actual output against them byte-for-byte (confirmed the test actually catches drift, not just passes vacuously, by transiently corrupting one declare line's text and observing 3 of 4 sub-tests fail, then reverting).
- ✅ **Membership drift FILED, NOT repaired (Step 3 — the drift the table now makes visible):** two drift classes found, both preserved exactly as historical behavior via the table's optional/bool fields (no behavior change in this task):
  - **38 names have a `builtin_ret_ty` + `mangle_extern` + preamble entry but are ABSENT from `is_builtin_fn`'s recognition set:** `chan_new`/`chan_send`/`chan_recv`/`chan_close`/`chan_choose`/`chan_offer`, `mpst_new`/`mpst_send`/`mpst_recv`/`mpst_close`, `record_keys`/`record_values`/`record_entries`/`record_get`/`record_has_key`/`record_put`/`record_from_list`, `ws_handshake`/`ws_recv`/`ws_send`/`ws_select`, `http_parse_request`/`http_serialize_response`/`http_server_listen`, `tcp_recv_http`/`tcp_send_all`, `html_auto_escape`, `panic`, `send_linear`, `sha1_bytes`, `stdlib_gzip_encode`/`stdlib_gzip_decode`/`stdlib_deflate_encode`/`stdlib_deflate_decode`/`stdlib_zstd_encode`/`stdlib_zstd_decode`/`stdlib_brotli_encode`/`stdlib_brotli_decode`. Consequence: `is_leaf_callee` (`is_builtin_fn name || Tir_names.has_runtime_prefix name`) treats a direct call to any of these BY ITS MARCH NAME as non-leaf, forcing an unnecessary reduction-check emission (`emit_reduction_check`) in any caller whose body is otherwise leaf — a missed optimization, not a correctness bug (the reduction check is always safe to over-emit). Likely explanation: these names are dispatched through dedicated non-generic `EApp` match arms (session-typed channels, MPST, record introspection, WS/HTTP, compression) that never needed `is_builtin_fn`'s "is this a no-op-for-RC-purposes operator/value" check, so nobody noticed the recognition-set gap. Repair (if ever done) is a `is_builtin_fn` membership fix, tested via `expr_has_call`/reduction-check IR assertions — out of scope here.
  - **7 names (`march_compare_int`/`march_compare_float`/`march_compare_string`/`march_hash_int`/`march_hash_float`/`march_hash_string`/`march_hash_bool`) have a `builtin_ret_ty` + preamble entry but NO `mangle_extern` case and are ABSENT from `is_builtin_fn`:** these are already-mangled C-runtime names used directly as March-level call targets (no renaming needed, so `mangle_extern`'s identity fallthrough naturally does the right thing) — the reduction-check gap above doesn't apply to these specifically since `Tir_names.has_runtime_prefix` (the `is_leaf_callee` OR-clause) already recognizes the `march_` prefix. Recorded here only because the table's per-structure membership flags make the `is_builtin_fn`-absence visible; no known consequence.
  - Separately noted (NOT drift, verified as intentional dedicated-codegen design, no filing needed): arithmetic/comparison operators (`+`/`-`/`==`/etc, native LLVM instructions), `int_and`/`int_or`/`int_xor`/`int_not`/`int_shl`/`int_shr`/`int_popcount` (native bitwise instructions), `native_int_arr_*`/`native_float_arr_*` (18 names, `mangle_extern`-bypassing direct-emit arms), `task_spawn`/`task_await`/`task_await_unwrap`/`task_yield`/`task_spawn_steal`/`task_reductions`/`pmap_threshold`/`get_work_pool`/`remote_ref_hashes` (constant-folded or synthesized by dedicated `EApp` arms), and `main` (the user's own compiled entry point, not a runtime builtin).
- ✅ **Performance side-effect (the one permitted non-cosmetic change):** `is_builtin_fn` was `List.mem` over a 272-element list on hot paths (`emit_atom`, `is_leaf_callee`/`expr_has_call`'s reduction-check analysis, the `EIncRC`/`EDecRC`/`EFree` shadow guards) — O(n) per call. Now backed by a `Hashtbl.t` built once at module load — O(1) per call, answer-identical (verified above). No other behavior change.
- ✅ **Standard gates, all green:** six runners exit 0 (isolated `HOME=.w3home`) at 384 compiler / 230 eval / 374 codegen (370 base +4 new `llvm_builtins_preamble_golden` tests) / 791 stdlib / 53 stdlib_march / 29 snapshots — zero `.expected` diffs. Baseline IR diff: `--emit-llvm` on all four benchmarks (fib, binary_trees, tree_transform, list_ops) against a clean sibling-worktree build of base commit `50c30f18` — byte-identical `.ll` in all four (0 diff lines) — the preamble is part of every `.ll`, so this is the loudest possible H2 check. Compiled (`--compile --opt 2`) benchmark outputs byte-identical to expected values (fib=102334155, tree_transform=104857600, list_ops=333333666666, binary_trees check=65535); timings within noise (largest delta tree_transform +4.6%, no regression >10%). `scripts/check-docs.sh` passes clean. Full report: `.superpowers/sdd/w3c2-task-4-report.md`.
